title: Pillar 2 – Address unmet multi-sectoral WASH, Food, Nutrition and Health needs in areas with high health and protection risks in Baalbek-El Hermel for the most vulnerable 37,245 people in need.
description: ltpgtltbrgtThe project aims to address the critical needs of 37,245 vulnerable individuals in Baalbek-Hermel, Lebanon, by providing comprehensive WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) services, health care, food security, and nutrition support in Aarsal, Baayoun, Bejjaje, Deir Mar Maroun, El Ain, El Qaa, Fakehe, Hermel, Laboue,Nabi Osamane, Qaa Jouar Maqiye, Qaa Ouadi Khanzir, Ras Baalbek, Zabboud. In response to the socio-economic crisis, increasing vulnerabilities and social tensions over the scarce resources and services as well as water-related challenges in the region, ACF will ensure access to safe drinking water, proper sanitation, and hygiene products, targeting 36,668 refugees, including 1,100 people with disabilities. The health component will enhance outcomes by supporting 70 refugees, including 2 with disabilities, and 18 host community members, particularly focusing on pregnant and lactating women and improving access to maternal and child health services.ltbrgtFor food security, the project aims to address the unmet, complex, and multi-sectorial needs faced by vulnerable people in Lebanon, targeting 548 refugees and 548 host community members, including 33 people with disabilities. This includes particularly vulnerable groups such as female-headed households, elderly households, and those with chronic diseases or disabilities. Food assistance will be provided based on needs identified under ACF’s WASH, Nutrition, and Health response, ensuring complementary activities to support the most vulnerable in Baalbek, Qaa, and Aarsal. The project will provide unrestricted cash-based food assistance to 120 vulnerable households living outside Informal Tented Settlements (ITSs) and in-kind food support to 75 vulnerable households within ITSs. Collaboration with sector stakeholders like WFP, UNHCR, and MOSA will ensure coordinated support and deduplication of beneficiaries.ltbrgtWith Health intervention, the proposed project aims to provide equitable, high-quality, safe, and respectful health services to women with high-risk pregnancies. The primary objective is to eliminate the economic barriers that disproportionately affect these vulnerable women. The project's implementation is expected to lower the rates of mortality and morbidity among expectant mothers in the targeted areas, while linking to further integral nutrition and health post-delivery mother and baby follow-up.   ltbrgtNutritional support will focus on 3,517 refugees and 393 host community members, including 117 people with disabilities, ensuring timely detection and treatment of malnutrition, distribution of nutrition supplements,  supporting vulnerable pregnant and lactating women (PLW) and caregivers of children 6-23 months with resources for care with infant and young child feeding (IYCF) one-on-one counselling and health, nutrition and care practices (including hygiene) awareness sessions.ltbrgt By integrating these sectors, the project seeks to respond to critical needs of targeted vulnerable groups in high-risk protection areas and improve the overall well-being of the affected population and foster community resilience amidst ongoing crises and escalating social tensions. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtAM2: Following the collapse of the Assad regime in January 2025, approximately 16,000 individuals relocated from Aarsal ITSs back to Syria. As a result, the needs for water trucking and RTERs decreased. ACF will reallocate the budget initially planned for these activities to rehabilitate a water reservoir in Nahle village and a water transmission line serving 11 locations. Besides, ACF will conduct cash-for-food assistance instead of the initially planned modalities. This reprogramming enables ACF to adapt its intervention to the evolving context, with the aim of covering the most acutee needs of affected populations. lt/bgtlt/pgt

title: Water Quality MonitoringStations Litani River and Ultrasonic algae control devices inLake Qaraoun
description: The Litani River is the longest river in Lebanon and a major source for drinking and irrigation water for the Bekaa and the South and an important source for hydropower. The river debouches into Lake Qaraoun and is heavily polluted by municipal waste, waste water and excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides in agriculture. It also suffers from the overabstraction of groundwater through many unlicensed wells in the basin. Large fi sh kills in Lake Qaraoun have triggered large media attention. The project will supply Water Quality Monitoring Stations and Ultra sonic algae control devices to the Litani River Authority (LRA), contributing to the wider Business Plan for Combating Pollution of Lake Qaraoun. This will be complemented by capacity building in water quality monitoring and data management, and good governance. | Activities • Installation of equipment and related software for algae monitoring and Ultra sonic algae control in Lake Qaraoun • Advising in real-time automatic water quality monitoring stations in the Litani River • Installation of database • Integration of data system in LRA’s wider data management system • Training data series and data management • Training of laboratory staff in improving the quality of analysis of results • Training of staff in maintenance of monitoring equipment • Development of actions to address pollution causes | Inhabitants of Bekaa Valley and displaced persons.

title: Netherlands Water and Agriculture Expert Support Facility
description: The programme Strenghthening the Lebanese Water and Agriculture Sector has been designed to deliver specifi c results by bringing in advanced Netherlands expertise in priority areas. In addition, a facility has been created to be able to respond quickly to further requests for advanced Netherlands expertise by institutions and organizations active in the Lebanese water and agriculture sector. This facility will also provide access of Netherlands expertise to the Lebanese water and agriculture Sector. Who can apply? The facility is open to requests from Lebanese institutions and international organizations working to improve the water and agriculture sector in Lebanon that would like to enhance the impact of their activities and interventions by making use of advanced Netherlands expertise. It is expected that the facility will be used for limited interventions - not requiring personal contribution of more than two months, and not requiring substantial investments. Moreover, the facility will be put to the attention of the Lebanese Ministry of Energy and Water, the Ministry of Environment, the Council for Development & Reconstruction, the World Bank and other partners the programme is working with. | How it works? An institution that would like to make use of the facility can contact the Programme’s permanent presence in Lebanon to discuss the possibilities. If the request meets the criteria of the facility then a Terms of Reference will be drafted. In the Terms of Reference activities, outputs and level of effort as well as counterpart input are specifi ed by the institution and World Waternet’s permanent presence in Lebanon. The Embassy will be provided with the opportunity to comment and/or make suggestions. The facility cannot be used for expertise readily available within Lebanon, or on the global market. World Waternet will consult the Netherlands Water Partnership to identify persons and/or organizations that can provide the requested services before it will solicit proposals. World Waternet will be the contracting entity and their procurement regulations will apply. The benefi ciary institutions and Waternet’s permanent presence will support the implementation of activities.

title: Project Strengthening the Lebanese Water and Agriculture Sector
description: The Syrian crisis has had serious consequences for Lebanon. More than 1.5 million refugees have found refuge in the country. Meanwhile, the Bekaa Valley, to the east of Lebanon, is experiencing a shortage of drinking water and sanitary facilities. Local agriculture is also suffering from drought conditions. In these challenging circumstances, however, it is of crucial importance that the region be able to achieve good harvests, provide employment and grow its economy. World Waternet, Acacia Water and Wageningen University & Research are working together to support Lebanon using Dutch water and agricultural expertise. The two-year programme was launched in February 2017, with the aim of improving the provision of drinking water, purifying waste water, increasing water availability and boosting farmers’ production by encouraging better, more economical water use. | The programme’s specifi c components are: 1. Water Operator Partnership (WOP) with Bekaa Water Establishment (BWE). Bringing the Netherlands approach in water governance, expertise in utility management and support to take on waste water treatment as a new task; 2. Water Quality Monitoring Stations Litani River with the Litani River Authority (LRA). Also bringing the Netherlands approach in water governance together with advanced monitoring and data management technologies and in support of the wider Lake Qaraoun Pollution Abatement Project supported by the World Bank; 3. Feasibility mapping small scale storage/ artifi cial recharge and pilot projects with Water Establishments, Ministry of Energy and Water (MoEW) and Green Plan/Ministry of Agriculture. Utilizing advanced Netherlands expertise in artifi cial recharge – a technique that is receiving increased attention in the search for additional water sources in Lebanon – and making it available to Water Establishments; 4. Innovations for investment security in land reclamation and water reservoirs with Green Plan/ Ministry of Agriculture and the Lebanese Agriculture Research Institute (LARI). Bringing advanced Netherlands expertise and technologies in water and agriculture to small scale farmers and their communities; 5. Adaptable greenhouses with the Lebanese Agriculture Research Institute (LARI). Bringing advanced Netherlands expertise in the use of greenhouse techniques adapted to local circumstances and making it available for the broader farmers’ community; 6. The Netherlands Expertise Facility will provide ad-hoc (on-demand) advanced expertise in water and agriculture to Lebanese authorities and international institutions to strengthen the impact of their interventions. | The programme is part of a larger support programme by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs for the reception of Syrian refugees in Lebanon as well as the host communities concerned. In addition to activities related to water, the Ministry also supports projects for the improvement of the agricultural sector and the promotion of work opportunities. The aim of this programme is to improve the prospects of both the refugees and their host communities in the region.

title: Quick Impact Projects in Lebanon
description: The purpose of the Lebanese Quick Impact Project (QIP) is to support the development of local communities in southern Lebanon and thereby increase trust between the UNIFIL crisis management and the local population, which is essential for securing its operation. The objective of UNIFIL is to maintain stability in the region. South Lebanon is facing an even more challenging situation following the escalation of the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah. The situation in Lebanon is affected by the economic crisis and persons in vulnerable position have suffered from increased poverty and restrictions on access to basic services. As a result, it is estimated (UNHCR) that more than half of Lebanon's population lives below the poverty line and 9/10 Syrian refugees need humanitarian assistance to meet their basic needs. There are approximately 1.5 million Syrian refugees and more than 872,000 IDPs in the country. According to UNHCR statistics, around 475,000 people have fled to Syria since the current conflict escalated. In 2023, the Finnish crisis management force in Lebanon carried out a total of 277 CIMIC missions, including 34 projects/donations and 91 OUTREACH activities. Due to the highly volatile security situation in southern Lebanon in 2024, the focus of CIMIC activities has been on supporting rescuers and critical public infrastructure. By the end of July 2024, SKJL completed a total of 167 CIMIC missions, including 23 projects/donations and 27 OUTREACH activities. Experiences of the activities are positive. The projects have increased trust between peacekeepers and the local population, while improving access to clean water and waste management, as well as supporting persons in vulnerable position. Project activities strengthen good governance and sustainable public procurement locally. Support for 2025–2026 will be directed especially at supporting health care and infrastructure. In addition, education and cultural activities, environmental management, agricultural activities and renewable energy systems will be supported. The Finnish crisis management force identifies and implements projects in accordance with the QIP guidelines prepared by the Ministry for Foreign Affairs. In 2025–2026, the budget of the projects will be 100,000 per year, totalling 200,000. | Libanonin Quick Impact Project (QIP) –pienhankkeiden tarkoituksena on tukea Etelä-Libanonin paikallisyhteisöjen kehitystä ja siten lisätä UNIFIL-kriisinhallintajoukkojen ja paikallisen väestön välistä luottamusta, mikä on olennaista joukkojen toiminnan turvaamiseksi. UNIFIL-joukkojen tavoitteena on ylläpitää alueen vakautta. Etelä-Libanon on entistä haastavammassa tilanteessa konfliktin eskaloiduttua Israelin ja Hizbollahin välillä. Libanonin tilanteeseen vaikuttaa maata kurittanut talouskriisi ja  haavoittuvassa asemassa olevat henkilöt ovat kärsineet köyhyyden lisääntymisestä sekä peruspalvelujen saatavuuden rajoituksista. Tämän seurauksena arvioidaan (UNHCR), että yli puolet Libanonin väestöstä elää köyhyysrajan alapuolella ja 9/10 syyrialaispakolaisesta tarvitsee humanitaarista apua perustarpeidensa tyydyttämiseksi. Maassa on noin 1,5 miljoonaa syyrialaispakolaista ja yli 872 000 sisäisesti siirtymään joutunutta ihmistä. UNHCR:n tilastojen mukaan noin 475 000 henkilöä on paennut Syyriaan nykyisen konfliktin eskaloiduttua. Suomalainen kriisinhallintajoukko Libanonissa toteutti vuonna 2023 yhteensä 277 CIMIC-tehtävää sisältäen 34 projektia/lahjoitusta ja 91 OUTREACH-aktiviteettia. Etelä-Libanonin erittäin epävakaan turvallisuustilanteen myötä vuonna 2024 CIMIC-toiminnan painopisteenä on ollut pelastajien ja kriittisen julkisen infran tukeminen. SKJL toteutti vuonna 2024 heinäkuun loppuun mennessä yhteensä 167 CIMIC-tehtävää sisältäen 23 projektia/lahjoitusta ja 27 OUTREACH-aktiviteettia. Kokemukset toiminnasta ovat myönteisiä. Hankkeilla on lisätty rauhanturvaajien ja paikallisväestön välistä luottamusta ja samalla on parannettu mm. puhtaan veden saantia ja jätehuoltoa sekä tuettu haavoittuvassa asemassa olevia henkilöitä. Hanketoiminta vahvistaa paikallisesti hyvää hallintoa ja tukee kestävien julkisten hankintojen toteuttamista. Vuosien 2025-2026 avustusta suunnataan erityisesti terveydenhuollon ja infrastruktuurin tukemiseen. Lisäksi tuetaan koulu- ja sivistystoimea, ympäristöhuoltoa, maataloustoimintaa ja uusiutuvan energian järjestelmiä. reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Protection of Jeita-spring
description: The main problems of the water sector in Lebanon are the lack of management and insufficient protection of groundwater resources. In the Beirut metropolitan area, around 1.9 million residents depend on the drinking water supply from the approximately 13 km northeast of the city center  from Beirut located karst spring Jeita.  The aquifer in the Jeita Spring catchment is at risk from numerous sources of pollution, particularly sewage.  The measure planned by BGR is carried out in parallel with a KfW measure of the same name, which is to build sewage treatment plants and collectors in the catchment area of the Jeita spring. Both projects serve to reduce the entry of pollutants into surface and groundwater. The main source of Jeita Spring pollution is the unregulated sewage collection and treatment in the Jeita Spring catchment area. As part of the TC measure, an attempt should be made to include aspects of water resource protection in the planning of projects  wastewater treatment as well as in other areas of land use planning.  The competence of the CDR as the Lebanese partner organization of all FC donors active in the project area is to be expanded to the extent that they can decide on investment plans for sewage disposal, taking into account geoscientific aspects of water resource protection. The WE-BML, as the main water supplier in the region, is supported in extending and expanding its competencies to core and intermediary functions of water management and protection. In this respect, the definition of protected areas serves as a key instrument for reducing groundwater pollution. The installation of a water quality information system is intended to enable WE-BML to react in good time to pollution peaks with regard to drinking water treatment and supply. | Hauptprobleme des Wassersektors im Libanon sind das mangelnde Management und der un zureichende Schutz der Grundwasserressourcen. Im Großraum Beirut hängen ca. 1,9 Mio. Einwohner von der Trinkwasserversorgung aus der ca. 13 km nordöstlich des Stadtzentrums   von Beirut gelegenen Karstquelle „Jeita“ ab.   Der Grundwasserleiter im Einzugsgebiet der Jeita-Quelle ist durch zahlreiche Verschmutzungs quellen gefährdet, insbesondere durch Abwasser.   Die von BGR geplante Maßnahme erfolgt parallel zu einer gleichnamigen Maßnahme der KfW, die im Einzugsgebiet der Jeita-Quelle Kläranlagen und -sammler bauen soll. Beide Projekte dienen der Verringerung des Schadstoffeintrags in das Oberflächen- und Grundwasser. Haupt ursache für die Verschmutzung der Jeita-Quelle ist die bislang nicht regulierte Abwassersamm lung und –behandlung im Einzugsgebiet der Jeita-Quelle. Im Rahmen der TZ-Maßnahme soll versucht werden, Aspekte des Wasserressourcenschutzes in die Planung von Projekten zur   Abwasserreinigung wie auch in andere Bereiche der Landnutzungsplanung zu integrieren.   Die Kompetenz des CDR als libanesische Partnerorganisation aller im Projektgebiet tätigen FZ Geber soll dahingehend erweitert werden, Investitionsabsichten zur Abwasserbeseitigung unter Berücksichtigung geowissenschaftlicher Aspekte des Wasserressourcenschutzes zu entschei den. Das WE-BML als Hauptwasserversorger in der Region wird dabei unterstützt, seine Kompetenzen auf Kern- und Mittlerfunktionen des Wassermanagements und -schutzes auszudeh nen bzw. auszubauen. Als wesentliches Instrument zur Verringerung der Grundwasserver schmutzung dient in dieser Hinsicht die Festlegung von Schutzgebieten. Durch die Installation eines Wasserqualitätsinformationssystems soll erreicht werden, dass WE-BML hinsichtlich der Trinkwasseraufbereitung und -versorgung rechtzeitig auf Verschmutzungs-Peaks reagieren kann. | Major Risks for the Drinking Water Supply in the greater Beirut Area are reduced by implementing measures to protect the groundwater catchment basin of the Jeita Spring from pollution. | Wichtige Risiken für die Trinkwasserversorgung im Großraum Beirut sind durch die Maßnahmen im Einzugsgebiet der Jeita-Quelle vermindert.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Management der Grundwasserressourcen, Libanon
description: Das Vorhaben „Management der Grundwasserressourcen“ im Libanon unterstützt die libanesischen Bemühungen um ein verbessertes Wasserressourcenmanagement und einen verbesserten Schutz der Grundwasserressourcen.  Vor dem Hintergrund der sich drastisch verschärfenden Situation im Wassersektor u.a. auch durch die politischen Umstände in der Region ist eine Stärkung der nationalen Behörden in der Bewertung der landesweit verfügbaren Wasserressourcen erforderlich, um eine Versorgung mit Trinkwasser dauerhaft sicher zu stellen. Das Vorhaben trägt zu einer verbesserten Bilanzierung der verfügbaren und, unter Einschluss der Betrachtung der Wasserqualität, nutzbaren Grundwasserressourcen bei, um eine effektivere Planung der Wasserversorgungsinfrastruktur, der Bewirtschaftung der Wasserressourcen und des Wasserressourcenschutzes für die mandatierten Ministerien und Institutionen zu ermöglichen. Dadurch können diese besser den aktuellen Herausforderungen, die sich u.a. auch durch den Zustrom von Flüchtlingen für den Wassersektor ergeben, begegnen. Ebenso werden durch geowissenschaftliche Beratung und die Bereitstellung geowissenschaftlicher Informationen die Standortauswahl und respektive Entscheidungsprozesse und Beteiligungsmaßnahmen mit Betroffenen und der Zivilgesellschaft für potenziell wassergefährdende Aktivitäten wie z.B. Kläranlagen, Abfalldeponien, Industriestandorte verbessert.  Das Ziel des Vorhabens lautet: Ausgewählte staatliche Wassersektor-Institutionen haben weitere Voraussetzungen für eine nachhaltigere Nutzung der Grundwasserressourcen geschaffen. Das Vorhaben arbeitet mit dem Ministerium für Energie und Wasser (Ministry of Energy and Water, MoEW) bei der Abstimmung von übergeordneten sektorpolitischen Fragestellungen zusammen. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf der Stärkung der Expertise und der Kapazitäten der lokalen öffentlichen Wasserversorger Beirut + Mount Lebanon Water Establishment (BMLWE) und South Lebanon Water Establishment (SLWE). | The Management of Groundwater Resources project in Lebanon supports Lebanese efforts to improve water resource management and protection of groundwater resources.  Against the background of the drastically worsening situation in the water sector, among other things due to the political circumstances in the region, the national authorities need to be strengthened in the assessment of the water resources available nationwide in order to ensure a permanent supply of drinking water. The project contributes to an improved balancing of the available and usable groundwater resources, including the consideration of the water quality, in order to enable more effective planning of the water supply infrastructure, the management of the water resources and the water resource protection for the mandated ministries and institutions. As a result, they can better meet the current challenges that arise for the water sector, among other things, from the influx of refugees. Likewise, through geoscientific advice and the provision of geoscientific information, the site selection and decision-making processes and participation measures with those affected and civil society for potentially water-polluting activities such as sewage treatment plants, waste dumps, industrial sites are improved.  The aim of the project is: Selected state water sector institutions have created further prerequisites for a more sustainable use of groundwater resources. The project works with the Ministry of Energy and Water (MoEW) to coordinate overarching sectoral policy issues. The focus is on strengthening the expertise and capacity of the local public water utilities Beirut + Mount Lebanon Water Establishment (BMLWE) and South Lebanon Water Establishment (SLWE). | Ausgewählte staatliche Wassersektor-Institutionen (MoEW, BMLWE, SLWE) haben weitere Voraussetzungen für eine nachhaltige Nutzung der Grundwasserressourcen geschaffen. | Selected governmental water sector institutions have the necessary knowledge for a more sustainable management of groundwater resources.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Verbesserung des Wasserressourcenmanagements
description:
Ausgangssituation: 

Die wirtschaftlichen und politischen Krisen sowie bewaffneten Konflikte im Libanon haben die Wasserwirtschaft des Landes stark getroffen: Die vier regionalen Wasserbetriebe, die für die Wasserversorgung und Abwasserentsorgung der Bevölkerung verantwortlich sind, leiden unter unzureichender Infrastruktur, Personalmangel, knappen Finanzen und fehlender Technik. Dies wird durch eine unzuverlässige Stromversorgung und einen niedrigen Wasser- und Abwassertarif verschärft, der die Betriebskosten nicht deckt.
Die libanesische Regierung, vertreten durch das Ministerium für Energie und Wasser (MoEW), hat die Herausforderungen dabei erkannt, eine angemessene Wasser- und Abwasserversorgung bereitzustellen. Sie hat in ihrer „Nationalen Strategie für den Wassersektor Maßnahmen festgelegt, um vor allem die Steuerung, Verwaltung und Infrastruktur im Bereich zu verbessern.

Ziel: 

Bessere finanzielle und organisatorische Voraussetzungen tragen dazu bei, dass die regionalen Wasserunternehmen die Wasserversorgung und Abwasserentsorgung besser organisieren können.

Vorgehensweise: 

Das Projekt arbeitet mit dem MoEW daran, seine strategischen Ziele und die „Nationale Strategie für den Wassersektor umzusetzen. Zudem bietet es maßgeschneiderte und spezifische Unterstützung für die Wasserbetriebe:
- Das Projekt trägt dazu bei, Wasserverluste zu reduzieren. Gleichzeitig baut es Kompetenzen in den Wasserbetrieben aus, um die Abwasserwirtschaft zu optimieren.
- Es verbessert, dass ausgewählte Wasserbetriebe auf Krisen und Notlagen besser reagieren können. Dabei unterstützt es die Betriebe bei der Erstellung von Notfallreaktionsplänen und dabei, die gesammelten Erfahrungen im Krisen- und Notfallmanagement in die langfristige Resilienzplanung aufzunehmen. | Context: 

The economic and political crises and armed conflicts in Lebanon have badly affected the country’s water sector. The four regional water establishments responsible for supplying the population with water and for wastewater services are suffering from inadequate infrastructure, staff shortages, severe financial constraints and lack of technical capacities. This situation is exacerbated by unreliable power supply and low water and wastewater tariff which does not cover operating costs.
The Lebanese Government, represented by the Ministry of Energy and Water (MoEW), has recognised the challenges in delivering adequate water supplies and wastewater services. In its National Strategy for the Water Sector, MoEW included measures to enhance management, administration and infrastructure in the sector.

Objective: 

Improved financial and organisational conditions help the Lebanese regional Water Establishments can better organise water supplies and wastewater services.

Approach: 

The project is working with the MoEW to implement its strategic objectives and the National Strategy for the Water Sector. It also offers a tailored support for the regional Water Establishments (WEs):
- The project is helping WEs to reduce water losses, while it is developing expertise within the WEs water establishments, with the aim of optimising wastewater management.
- It is improving the ability of selected water establishments to respond more effectively to crises and emergencies. It is supporting the targeted establishments in producing emergency response plans, while incorporating lessons learned from crisis and emergency management into a long-term resilience planning.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Blue Action Fund (BAF) III
description: Das Vorhaben dient der Intensivierung des Küsten- und Meeresschutzes in Partnerländern der deutschen EZ. Die FZ-Finanzierungsbeiträge an den Blue Action Fund (BAF) sollen diesen befähigen, die Erhaltung von Netzwerken global wichtiger Küsten- und Meeresschutzgebiete zu fördern (Programmziel). Die dafür gegründete Stiftung wird durch Kofinanzierungen internationale NRO in die Lage versetzen, das Management von weltweit wichtigen Marinen- und Küstenschutzgebieten und derer Trägerzonen in Zusammenarbeit mit relevanten Institutionen zu verbessern (Modulziel), zudem werden in der EbA-Finanzierungslinie Klimarisiken für vulnerable Bevölkerungsgruppen der Küstenregionen gemindert durch den Schutz und die nachhaltige Nutzung von relevanten Küstenökosystemen und die daraus resultierende Verbesserung von deren Umweltdienstleistungen (Modulziel FZ-R). Der Träger des Projektes ist der BAF. Die Projektgebiete in ausgewählten Regionen von Afrika, Asien/Pazifik und Lateinamerika/Karibik umfassen ökologisch besonders wertvolle Küsten- und Meeresgebiete, deren Bevölkerung die direkte Zielgruppe des Vorhabens darstellt. Auf Grundlage einer Vorratsprüfung wird ein Finanzierungsbeitrag (Zuschuss) an den BAF geleistet. Durch erste Finanzierungsbeiträge (BMZ Nr. 2016.9751.5) von insgesamt 24 Mio. EUR (1. Phase: 15 Mio. EUR, 2. Phase: 9 Mio. EUR) wurden 2016 mit 22 Mio. EUR ein Verbrauchsfonds für den BAF eingerichtet sowie 2 Mio. EUR in das dauerhaft zu erhaltende Stiftungskapital des BAF eingezahlt. Für eine dritte Phase werden 2017 weitere 20 Mio. EUR für den Verbrauchsfonds bereitgestellt, für eine 4. Phase (BMZ No. 2018 34043) 2019 11.1 Mio. EUR, und für eine 5. Phase 2020 12 Mio. EUR (BMZ No. 2020 48726). Die Mittel werden aus dem IKU Haushaltstitel 68701 entnommen. Die schwedische Regierung hat 2017-2021 insgesamt 136 Mio. Kronen (ca. 16,4 Mio. EUR) bereitgestellt, die AFD 2018-2021 10 Mio. EUR. Norwegen plant ab 2022 dem Programm beizutreten. | Blue Action Fund (Blue Action) is a conservation trust fund established to safeguard marine biodiversity by supporting non-governmental organisations in their efforts to enhance regional management and use of coastal and marine ecosystems. The programme serves to intensify coastal and marine protection in partner countries of German Development Cooperation. The FC financial contributions to the Blue Action Fund (BAF) are to promote the conservation of networks of globally important coastal and marine protected areas (FC programme objective). The BAF foundation established for this purpose will provide co-financing to enable international NGOs to improve the management of globally important marine and coastal protected areas and their buffer zones in cooperation with relevant institutions (module objective). The programme executing agency is the BAF. The programme area is located in selected regions of Africa, Asia/Pacific and Latin America/Caribbean and includes ecologically particularly valuable coastal and marine areas. The direct target group of the supported NGO projects consists of the population of the marine and coastal areas worthy of protection. The Blue Action Fund grants focus on projects in the most sensitive coastal waters of Africa, Latin America and Asia/Pacific that concentrate on the following measurable outcomes: Newly established or better managed Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) of regional importance or networks of MPAs,  Conservation of or increase in biodiversity, Recovery of fish stocks, Enhanced livelihood conditions and food security, and Positive attitude of people affected by the project towards protection of marine biodiversity. Through initial financing contributions (BMZ No. 2016.9751.5) totaling EUR 24 million (1st phase: EUR 15 million, 2nd phase: EUR 9 million), a sinking fund of EUR 22 million was established for the BAF in 2016, with EUR 2 million disbursed into the BAFs endowment capital, which is to be maintained permanently. For a third phase (BMZ No. 2017 97521), an additional EUR 20 million was provided for the BAF reserve in 2017, for a fourth phase (BMZ No. 2018 34043), an additional EUR 11.1 Million in 2018, and for a fifth phase in 2020, an additional EUR 12 million (BMZ No. 2020 48726). The Swedish government has provided a total of EUR 16.4 million (SK 136 million) 2018 - 2021, and the French AFD EUR 10 million in 2018 - 2021. Norway plans to join the BAF from 2022 on. | Die Finanzierungsbeiträge der FZ an den Blue Action Fund (BAF) sollen diesen befähigen, die Erhaltung von Netzwerken global wichtiger Küsten- und Meeresschutzgebiete zu fördern (FZ-Programmziel). Die dafür zu gründende Stiftung wird durch Kofinanzierungen internationale NRO in die Lage versetzen, das Management von weltweit wichtigen Marinen- und Küstenschutzgebieten und derer Trägerzonen in Zusammenarbeit mit relevanten Institutionen zu verbessern (Modulziel).

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Abwasserentsorgung Al-Ghadir II
description: Der Libanon befindet sich seit 2019 in einem Kontext multipler Krisen. Dazu gehören unter anderem eine substanzielle Wirtschafts-, Finanz- und Staatskrise. In diesem Kontext droht die Infrastruktur vollends nach und nach zusammenzubrechen. Dort wo keine zentralen Abwasserentsorgungsnetze bzw. Abwassersammler vorhanden sind, versickert häusliches Abwasser durch undichte Klärgruben oder wird direkt in Flüsse, Bäche und Grundwasser geleitet, was sich negativ auf Umwelt und die öffentliche Hygiene auswirkt und die Gesundheitsrisiken für die Bevölkerung erhöht. In der Projektregion Al Ghadir wird dieses Vorhaben einen Beitrag zum Aufbau einer umweltgerechten und hygienisch einwandfreien Abwasserentsorgung leisten. Dies soll maßgeblich durch den Bau von Abwassersammlern erreicht werden. | Lebanon has been in a context of multiple crises since 2019. These include a substantial economic, financial and state crisis. In this context, the infrastructure is at risk to collapse one by one. Where centralized wastewater disposal networks or collectors are not in place, domestic wastewater seeps through leaking septic tanks or is discharged directly into rivers, streams, and groundwater, negatively impacting the environment, public sanitation and increasing health risks for the population. In the project region of Al Ghadir, this project will contribute to the establishment of an environmentally sound and hygienic wastewater disposal system. This is to be achieved primarily through the construction of wastewater collectors. | Das Ziel ist, einen Beitrag zum Aufbau einer umweltgerechten und hygienisch einwandfreien Abwasserentsorgung im Einzugsgebiet der Al-Ghadir Kläranlage zu leisten. | The aim is to contribute to an environmentally sound and hygienic wastewater disposal system in the catchment area of the Al-Ghadir wastewater treatment plant.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: UNOPS Libanon: Wiederaufbau kommunaler Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen Beirut und Bourj Hammoud
description: Ziel des Vorhabens ist die Wiederherstellung kommunaler Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen, um die Lebensbedingungen der Bewohner in den durch die Explosion im Hafen Beiruts am 04.08.2020 zerstörten, mehrheitlich armen Stadtteilen Beiruts und der Gemeinde Bourj Hammoud zu verbessern. Dabei soll durch partizipative Projektvorbereitung und -umsetzung sowie gezielt friedensfördernde Maßnahmen dazu beigetragen werden, soziale Spannungen zu reduzieren, die Resilienz der Bewohner und der unterstützen Institutionen zu erhöhen und das Vertrauen in staatliche Akteure zu stärken. Das Vorhaben wird durch das Büro für Projektdienste der Vereinten Nationen (UNOPS) als Projektträger umgesetzt.Das Vorhaben umfasst drei Komponenten. Im Rahmen der ersten Komponente zur Wiederherstellung von kommunaler Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen sollen ausgewählte Abschnitte des Straßennetzes und der damit verbundenen Regenwasser- und Abwassernetze, öffentliche Plätze und öffentliche Gebäude in Verbindung mit erneuerbarer Energieerzeugung (Dach-Photovoltaik-Anlagen) rehabilitiert werden. Im Rahmen der zweiten Komponente soll die Kapazität bei städtischem Personal und anderen Projektpartnern gestärkt werden. Im Rahmen der dritten Komponente sollen gezielt friedensfördernde Maßnahmen durch lokale Nichtregierungsorganisationen gefördert werden, die in einem Wettbewerbsverfahren Vorschläge beim Projektträger einreichen. | The objective of the project is to restore municipal infrastructure and services in order to improve the living conditions of residents in the predominantly poor neighborhoods of Beirut and the Bourj Hammoud municipality, which were destroyed by the explosion in Beiruts port on August 4, 2020. In doing so, participatory project preparation and implementation, as well as targeted peacebuilding measures, will help reduce social tensions, increase the resilience of residents and supporting institutions, and strengthen trust in state actors. The project is implemented by the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) as the project executing agency.The project has three components. Under the first component for rehabilitation of municipal infrastructure and services, it is intended to rehabilitate selected sections of the road network and associated stormwater and wastewater networks, public squares and public buildings in combination with renewable energy systems (rooftop photovoltaic systems). Under the second component, capacity will be strengthened among municipal staff and other project partners. Under the third component, targeted peacebuilding activities will be promoted by local non-governmental organizations submitting proposals to the project executing agency through a competitive process. | Durch die Wiederherstellung kommunaler Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen sollen die Lebensbedingungen der Bewohner in den durch die Explosion im Hafen Beiruts am 04.08.2020 zerstörten Stadtteilen verbessert werden. Dabei soll durch partizipative Projektvorbereitung u. -umsetzung sowie gezielt friedensfördernde Maßnahmen dazu beigetragen werden, soz. Spannungen zu reduzieren, die Resilienz der Bewohner u. der unterstützen Institutionen zu erhöhen u. das Vertrauen in staatl. Akteure zu stärken.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Unterstützung v. Flüchtlingen sowie kurzfrist. Verbess u Wiederaufbau v Infrastruktur in u um paläst Flüchtlingsl IV
description: Ziel des Vorhabens ist die Verbesserung der Lebensbedingungen der durch die anhaltende Krise betroffenen Bevölkerung in und um palästinensische Flüchtlingscamp im Libanon. Zielgruppe des Gesamtvorhabens ist die von akuten Krisen betroffene Bevölkerung in und um palästinensische Flüchtlingscamp im Libanon. Dies umfasst auch palästinensische Flüchtlinge aus Syrien. Auch in der vierten Phase konzentriert sich das Vorhaben auf die Unterstützung von Wiederaufbaumaßnahmen im Flüchtlingscamp Nahr el-Bared (Nahr el-Bared Camp - NBC). Die nach der Zerstörung des Camps 2007 innerhalb des Libanon geflohenen Palästinenser sollen in baulich sichere und der Familiensituation angemessene Häuser zurückkehren können. reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: LBN - UNICEF Libanon: WASH IV
description: Der Libanon steht im Spannungsfeld multipler Krisen. In Folge der Wirtschafts- und Finanzkrise und der sozio-ökonomischen Auswirkungen der COVID-19 Pandemie mangelt es an Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten für bedürftige Libanes/innen und Flüchtlinge, was zunehmend zu sozialen Spannungen zwischen den Libanesen selbst sowie zwischen ihnen und der Flüchtlingsbevölkerung führt. Der öffentliche Wassersektor des Libanon befand sich bereits vor der Flüchtlingskrise in einem desolaten Zustand. Die Infrastruktur war und ist weiterhin in vielen Gemeinden dringend rehabilitierungs- und ausbaubedürftig.Durch das Vorhaben soll eine Verbesserung der Lebensbedingungen und Perspektiven von bedürftigen Libanes/innen und Flüchtlingen in Aufnahmegemeinden des Libanon durch verbesserten Zugang der Zielgruppe zu kurzfristiger menschenwürdiger Beschäftigung und durch Verbesserung der Wasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur geschaffen werden. Als Zielgruppen profitieren von der Maßnahme sowohl die libanesische Bevölkerung in den aufnehmenden Gemeinden als auch syrische und palästinensische Flüchtlinge.Wesentliche Maßnahmen des Vorhabens sind der Bau von Wasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur zur Verbesserung der Versorgungssituation und Minderung von Umweltgefahren in sozial besonders vulnerablen Gebieten im Libanon. Weiter werden mindestens 4.000 Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten im Rahmen der arbeitsintensiven Umsetzung der Infrastrukturmaßnahmen geschaffen. UNICEF ist Träger und Empfänger der FZ-Maßnahme. | Lebanon is caught between multiple crises. As a result of the economic and financial crises and the socio-economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, there is a lack of employment opportunities for vulnerable Lebanese and non-Lebanese, increasingly leading to social tensions between Lebanese themselves and between them and the refugee population. Furthermore, Lebanons public water sector was in a desolate state even before the influx of Syrian refugees into vulnerable host communities. The infrastructure was and continues to be in urgent need of rehabilitation and expansion in many communities. The project aims to improve the living conditions and prospects of vulnerable Lebanese and refugees in host communities in Lebanon by improving the target groups access to short-term decent employment and by improving water and sanitation infrastructure. The target groups benefiting from the measure are the Lebanese population and the Syrian/ Palestinian refugees in the host communities. The main measures of the project are the construction and expansion of water and wastewater infrastructure to improve the supply situation and mitigate environmental hazards in socially particularly vulnerable areas. Furthermore, at least 4,000 employment opportunities will be created as part of the labor-intensive implementation of the infrastructure measures. The project is being implemented jointly with UNICEF. | Ziel ist die Verbesserung der Wasserver- und Abwasserentsorgung im Libanon sowie die Schaffung von positiven Beschäftigungs- und Einkommenseffekten für vulnerable libanesische und nicht-libanesische Haushalte.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Wiederaufbau kommunaler Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen Beirut und Bourj Hammoud, Phase II
description: Am 4. August 2020 erschütterte eine verheerende Explosion den Hafen von Beirut, zerstörte einen Großteil der Hafenanlagen und richtete schwere Schäden in den umliegenden Vierteln im Umkreis von mehreren Kilometern an. Die Katastrophe forderte über 200 Tote, etwa 7.000 Verletzte und ließ schätzungsweise 300.000 Bewohner mit beschädigten Wohnungen zurück. Durch die Wiederherstellung kommunaler bzw. öffentlicher Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen sollen die Lebensbedingungen der Bewohner/innen in den durch die Explosion im Hafen Beiruts zerstörten Stadtteilen sowie der Bewohner weiterer bedürftiger Stadtteile verbessert werden. Dabei soll durch partizipative Projektvorbereitung und -umsetzung sowie gezielt friedensfördernde Maßnahmen dazu beigetragen werden, soziale Spannungen zu reduzieren, die Resilienz der Bewohner und der unterstützten Institutionen zu erhöhen und das Vertrauen in staatliche Akteure zu stärken.Maßnahmen dabei sind: Schaffung von Möglichkeiten zur Bevölkerungsbeteiligung und Umsetzung der gewonnenen Anregungen, sofern realisierbar.  Entsprechend des u.a. aus der Bevölkerungsbeteiligung resultierenden offenen Programmansatzes sind Einzelmaßnahmen aus den folgenden Bereichen möglich:      oVerbesserung ausgewählter Abschnitte des Straßennetzes und der damit verbundenen Regenwasser- und Abwassernetze,       oRehabilitierung ausgewählter öffentlicher Plätze,       oRehabilitierung und Ausstattung ausgewählter öffentlicher Gebäude in Verbindung mit erneuerbarer Energieerzeugung,      oKapazitätsaufbau bei städtischem Personal und anderen Projektpartnern in Bereitstellung, Betrieb und Wartung der finanzierten Infrastruktur,       oUmsetzung von gezielt friedensfördernden, gemeindebasierten Maßnahmen durch lokale NROs. | On 4 August 2020, a devastating explosion struck the port of Beirut, destroying much of the port facilities and causing severe damage to surrounding neighbourhoods within a radius of several kilometres. The disaster killed over 200 people, injured about 7,000 and left an estimated 300,000 residents with damaged homes. By restoring municipal and public infrastructure and services, the living conditions of the residents in the neighbourhoods destroyed by the explosion in the port of Beirut as well as the residents of other neighbourhoods in need are to be improved. Participatory project preparation and implementation as well as targeted peacebuilding measures are to contribute to reducing social tensions, increasing the resilience of the residents and the supported institutions and strengthening trust in state actors.Measures in this regard are: Creating opportunities for population participation and implementing the suggestions gained, if feasible.  In accordance with the open programme approach resulting, among other things, from population participation, individual measures from the following areas are possible:      o Improvement of selected sections of the road network and the associated stormwater and wastewater networks,       o Rehabilitation of selected public spaces,       o Rehabilitation and equipping of selected public buildings in conjunction with renewable energy generation,      o Capacity building of municipal staff and other project partners in the provision, operation and maintenance of the financed infrastructure,       o Implementation of targeted peacebuilding, community-based interventions by local NGOs. | Durch die Wiederherstellung kommunaler Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen sollen die Lebensbedingungen der Bewohner in den durch die Explosion im Hafen Beiruts am 04.08.2020 zerstörten Stadtteilen verbessert werden. Dabei soll durch partizipative Projektvorbereitung u. -umsetzung sowie gezielt friedensfördernde Maßnahmen dazu beigetragen werden, soz. Spannungen zu reduzieren, die Resilienz der Bewohner u. der unterstützen Institutionen zu erhöhen u. das Vertrauen in staatl. Akteure zu stärken.

title: UNICEF Libanon WASH V
description: Der öffentliche Wassersektor des Libanon befand sich bereits vor dem Zustrom syrischer Geflüchteter in die vulnerablen Aufnahmegemeinden in einem desolaten Zustand. Die Infrastruktur war und ist weiterhin in vielen Gemeinden dringend rehabilitierungs- und ausbaubedürftig. Wasserreservoirs und -netze sowie Abwasserleitungen fehlen teilweise noch, oder sie bedürfen der Rehabilitierung, um den gestiegenen Anforderungen durch die Flüchtlingskrise adäquat gerecht zu werden. Gleichzeitig mangelt es im Libanon insbesondere in Folge der anhaltenden schweren Wirtschafts- und Finanzkrise und der sozio-ökonomischen Auswirkungen der COVID-19 Pandemie an Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten für bedürftige Libanesen und nicht-Libanesen, was soziale Spannungen zwischen Libanesen selbst sowie zwischen ihnen und der Flüchtlingsbevölkerung verschärft.Ziel des Vorhabens ist die Verbesserung der Lebensbedingungen und Perspektiven von bedürftigen Libanesen und Geflüchteten in Libanon durch verbesserten Zugang zu kurzfristiger Beschäftigung und durch Verbesserung der Wasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur.Das Kinderhilfswerk der Vereinten Nationen (UNICEF) als Implementierungspartner der KfW setzt Maßnahmen im gesamten Libanon um. Dazu gehören der Arbeitsintensive Bau von Quellfassungen, Trinkwasserreservoirs und Abwasserkanalisation. Dadurch können vulnerable Libanesen und Geflüchtete als Zielgruppe von verbesserter Wasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur sowie von kurzfristigen Beschäftigungsangeboten profitieren. | Lebanons public water sector was in a desolate state even before the influx of Syrian refugees into vulnerable host communities. The infrastructure was and still is in urgent need of rehabilitation and expansion in many communities. Water reservoirs and networks, as well as sewage systems, are still lacking in some cases, or require rehabilitation to adequately meet the increased demands since the refugee crisis. At the same time, Lebanon lacks employment opportunities for Lebanese and non-Lebanese, particularly as a result of the ongoing severe economic and financial crisis and the socio-economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, exacerbating social tensions among Lebanese themselves and between the refugee population.The project aims to improve the living conditions and prospects of Lebanese and refugees in Lebanon by increasing access to short-term employment and improving water and sanitation infrastructure.The United Nations Childrens Fund (UNICEF), as KfWs partner, is implementing measures throughout Lebanon. These include the labor-intensive construction of spring catchments, drinking water reservoirs and sewage systems. This enables vulnerable Lebanese and refugees as a target group to benefit from improved water and sanitation infrastructure as well as short-term employment opportunities. | Ziel ist die Verbesserung der Wasserver- und Abwasserentsorgung im Libanon sowie die Schaffung von positiven Beschäftigungs- und Einkommenseffekten für vulnerable libanesische und nicht-libanesische Haushalte.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: UNDP LBN - Beschäftigung im Ländlichen Raum, Phase VI
description: Der Bürgerkrieg in Syrien hat massive Fluchtbewegungen in den Libanon verursacht. Der hohe Zustrom stellt eine zusätzliche Belastung für die wirtschaftliche und sozioökomische Situation des Landes dar. Die Spannungen zwischen den Geflüchteten und der Lokalbevölkerung sind dementsprechend hoch, wobei die Konkurrenz um Beschäftigung und Verdienstmöglichkeiten in den Aufnahmegemeinden eine herausragende Rolle spielt. Durch die anhaltende Krise besteht hoher Investitionsbedarf. Viele Flüchtlinge aus Syrien sowie die aufnehmenden Gemeinden sind auf nicht absehbare Zeit auf Unterstützung angewiesen.Ziel der FZ-Maßnahme ist es daher, kurz- und mittelfristige Einkommensmöglichkeiten für Flüchtlinge aus Syrien und bedürftige Libanesen zu schaffen.Im Mittelpunkt des Vorhabens stehen dabei arbeitsintensive Maßnahmen zur Rehabilitierung bzw. zum Bau von Bewässerungsinfrastruktur (Bewässerungskanäle und landwirtschaftliche Wasserspeicher). Neben den kurzfristigen Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten auf den Baustellen soll die landwirtschaftliche Produktion in den Projektregionen gesteigert werden, was positive Beschäftigungseffekte nach sich zieht.Das Vorhaben wird durch die United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) umgesetzt.  Die Kosten dieser Phase belaufen sich auf 13,25 Mio. Euro. Die FZ-Mittel werden als Zuschuss bereitgestellt. | The civil war in Syria has caused massive refugee movements to Lebanon. The large influx places an additional burden on the countrys economic and socio-economic situation. Tensions between refugees and the local population are correspondingly high, with competition for employment and earning opportunities in the host communities playing a prominent role. Due to the ongoing crisis, there is a great need for investment. Many refugees from Syria and the host communities are dependent on support for the foreseeable future.The aim of the programme is therefore to create short and medium-term income opportunities for refugees from Syria and Lebanese people in need.The project focuses on labour-intensive measures for the rehabilitation and construction of irrigation infrastructure (irrigation canals and agricultural water reservoirs). In addition to short-term employment opportunities on the construction sites, agricultural production in the project regions is to be increased, resulting in positive employment effects.The project is being implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).  The costs of this phase amount to EUR 13.25 million. reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: UNICEF Libanon WASH VI
description: Der öffentliche Wassersektor des Libanon befand sich bereits vor dem Zustrom syrischer Geflüchteter in die vulnerablen Aufnahmegemeinden in einem desolaten Zustand. Die Infrastruktur war und ist weiterhin in vielen Gemeinden dringend rehabilitierungs- und ausbaubedürftig. Wasserreservoirs und -netze sowie Abwasserleitungen fehlen teilweise noch, oder sie bedürfen der Rehabilitierung, um den gestiegenen Anforderungen durch die Flüchtlingskrise adäquat gerecht zu werden. Gleichzeitig mangelt es im Libanon insbesondere in Folge der anhaltenden schweren Wirtschafts- und Finanzkrise und der sozio-ökonomischen Auswirkungen der COVID-19 Pandemie an Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten für bedürftige Libanesen und nicht-Libanesen, was soziale Spannungen zwischen Libanesen selbst sowie zwischen ihnen und der Flüchtlingsbevölkerung verschärft.Ziel des Vorhabens ist die Verbesserung der Gesundheits- und Lebensbedingungen sowie die Schaffung positiver Beschäftigungs- und Einkommenseffekte für vulnerable libanesische und nicht-libanesische Bevölkerungsgruppen. Dies soll durch die arbeitsintensive Durchführung von Baumaßnahmen zur Verbesserung der Trinkwasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur i.S. der Just Transition erreicht werden. Dazu gehören auch dien Installation von Photovoltaik-Anlagen in der Trinkwasserversorgung.Das Kinderhilfswerk der Vereinten Nationen (UNICEF) als Implementierungspartner der KfW setzt Maßnahmen im gesamten Libanon um. Dazu gehören der Arbeitsintensive Bau von Quellfassungen, Trinkwasserreservoirs und Abwasserkanalisation. Dadurch können vulnerable Libanesen und Geflüchtete als Zielgruppe von verbesserter Wasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur sowie von kurzfristigen Beschäftigungsangeboten profitieren. | Lebanons public water sector was in a desolate state even before the influx of Syrian refugees into vulnerable host communities. The infrastructure was and still is in urgent need of rehabilitation and expansion in many communities. Water reservoirs and networks, as well as sewage systems, are still lacking in some cases, or require rehabilitation to adequately meet the increased demands since the refugee crisis. At the same time, Lebanon lacks employment opportunities for Lebanese and non-Lebanese, particularly as a result of the ongoing severe economic and financial crisis and the socio-economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, exacerbating social tensions among Lebanese themselves and between the refugee population.The project aims to enhance health and living conditions and create positive employment and income effects for the vulnerable Lebanese and non-Lebanese population. This is to be achieved through the labor-intensive implementation of construction measures to improve drinking water and wastewater infrastructure in the spirit of Just Transition. This includes the installation of Photovoltaik in drinking water supply systemsThe United Nations Childrens Fund (UNICEF), as KfWs partner, is implementing measures throughout Lebanon. These include the labor-intensive construction of spring catchments, drinking water reservoirs and sewage systems. This enables vulnerable Lebanese and refugees as a target group to benefit from improved water and sanitation infrastructure as well as short-term employment opportunities. | Verbesserung der Gesundheits- und Lebensbedingungen sowie die Schaffung positiver Beschäftigungs- und Einkommenseffekte für vulnerable libanesische und nicht-libanesische Bevölkerungsgruppen. Dies soll durch die arbeitsintensive Durchführung von Baumaßnahmen zur Verbesserung der Trinkwasser- und Abwasserinfrastruktur i.S. der Just Transition erreicht werden. | Enhancing health and living conditions and creating positive employment and income effects for the vulnerable Lebanese and non-Lebanese population. This is to be achieved through the labor-intensive implementation of construction measures to improve drinking water and wastewater infrastructure in the spirit of Just Transition.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Unterst. v. Geflüchteten sowie kurzfrist. Verb. u. Wiederaufbau v. Infrastruktur in u. um paläst. Geflüchtetencamps VI
description: Ziel des Vorhabens ist die Verbesserung der Lebensbedingungen der durch die anhaltende Krise betroffenen Bevölkerung in und um palästinensische Flüchtlingscamps im Libanon. Zielgruppe des Gesamtvorhabens ist die von akuten Krisen betroffene Bevölkerung in und um palästinensische Flüchtlingscamps im Libanon. Dies umfasst auch palästinensische Flüchtlinge aus Syrien.Auch in der sechsten Phase konzentriert sich das Vorhaben auf die Unterstützung von Wiederaufbaumaßnahmen im Flüchtlingscamp Nahr el-Bared (Nahr el-Bared Camp - NBC). Die nach der Zerstörung des Camps 2007 innerhalb des Libanon geflohenen Palästinenser*innen sollen in baulich sichere und der Familiensituation angemessene Häuser zurückkehren können. Indirekt profitieren auch die bereits nach NBC zurückgekehrten Menschen von der Fortsetzung des Wiederaufbaus sowie palästinensische Geflüchtete aus Syrien und Bewohner umliegender Camps/Wohnsiedlungen, die durch die Rückkehr der Binnenflüchtlinge entlastet werden. Das Vorhaben kommt Familien direkt über neu geschaffene Wohn- und Geschäftsräume zugute, weitere Menschen profitieren von neuen kurz- bis mittelfristigen Jobs im Baugewerbe. Außerdem umfasst das Vorhaben einen Beitrag zur nachhaltigen Wasserversorgung sowie zum Schutz archäologischer Stätten im Rahmen der Baumaßnahmen.Empfänger und Projektträger des Vorhabens ist das Hilfswerk der Vereinten Nationen für Palästina-Flüchtlinge im Nahen Osten (UNRWA). | The aim of the project is to improve the living conditions of the population affected by the ongoing crisis in and around Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon. The target group of the overall project is the population affected by acute crises in and around Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon. This includes Palestinian refugees from Syria.In the sixth phase, the project also focuses on supporting reconstruction measures in the Nahr el-Bared Camp (Nahr el-Bared Camp - NBC). Palestinians who fled the camp in Lebanon after it was destroyed in 2007 are to be able to return to safe houses in keeping with the family situation. Indirectly, those who have already returned to NBC are also benefiting from continued reconstruction, as are Palestinian refugees from Syria and residents of surrounding camps/housing estates, which will be relieved by the return of the internally displaced persons. The project benefits families directly through newly created residential and business premises, while more people benefit from new short- to medium-term jobs in the construction sector. The project also includes a contribution to sustainable water supply and the protection of archaeological sites as part of the construction work.The recipient and implementing partner is the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). | Verbesserung der Lebensbedingungen der durch die anhaltende Krise betroffenen Bevölkerung in und um palästinensische Flüchtlingslager im Libanon

description: With GAC funding: Within the framework of the Regional Refugee and Resilience Plan 2015 (3RP), Oxfam intend to offer a comprehensive and sustainable WASH response, which includes the involvement of local municipalities in Bekaa. Besides 68 Informal settlements (IS) located in six municipalities of North Bekaa, one of the biggest IS of Lebanon (470 households), located in Bar Elias, West Bekaa, will be targeted with a comprehensive WASH intervention and a tailored solid waste management approach. In Bar Elias IS (West Bekaa), drinking water for 470 households will be provided in collaboration with the Bekaa Water Establishment. Water for domestic use will be provided using the recently built wells and pumping facilities and safe chlorination will be ensured. With ECHO Funding: This is an integrated WASH and Protection action aims at contributing to mitigating the protection risks of human -generated violence, coercion, deprivation and abuse, and to reduce public health risks for 7,080 vulnerable people affected by the Syria crisis. Specifically, the Action intends to enable vulnerable individuals and communities to reduce protection risks and safely meet basic WASH needs. Oxfam with partners (AJEM, RDFL, Najdeh) propose a combination of activities aimed at reducing the vulnerability of the population in North Bekaa and Palestinian camps in the North, to protection threats and increasing their capacity by strengthening their knowledge of legal frameworks, services available and of soft -skills to address community problems. This is combined with the establishment of solid linkages with existing services, or the provision of other specialised services that can offer redress to individuals who are victims of negative coping strategies or threats resulting from lack of legal residency and of income. title: Strengthened Protection and Resilience of Crisis-affected in Lebanon
description: Oxfam's interventions in Lebanon focus on basic service provision that grants refugees life -sustaining access to clean water and sanitation on the one hand, and empowering their communities to identify, process, and address daily protection concerns on the other, all the while highlighting those concerns and gaps in assistance and rights provision to local authorities and key international stakeholders through its advocacy efforts. In the coming years, this approach would prove even more relevant, as refugees are increasingly compelled to make radical decisions about their future  - like returning to Syria or moving to ostensibly more welcoming areas in Lebanon – with often little reliable information to guide those choices. Oxfam's interventions thus focus on equipping refugees with key information pertaining to their access to essential services, civil status documentation, and rights and protective laws against exploitation and coercion. Information shared with target population will increase the knowledge on own rights, existing legal requirements and ways to access relevant services and assistance available in a safe manner, increasing capacity to prevent and mitigate protection risks. With this knowledge, individuals are also expected to be able to contact service providers directly, through the support of a focal point, or by contacting Oxfam staff and partners. Refugee women, often more vulnerable to abuse and harassment, face unique threats that Oxfam, through its partnership with specialized local SGBV case management organizations, addresses systematically within its broader response to the needs of the community. Oxfam's protection monitoring findings, as well as feedback communicated to its staff in the field, highlight fears of forced return and eviction as being the most preoccupying for refugees. title: WASH and Protection Response to the Syrian Refugee Crisis in North Bekaa
description: Oxfam will continue to provide access to gender -sensitive latrines , adhering to a maximum of 15 persons/latrine. For every latrine, Oxfam provides a one -off cleaning kit. All construction works abide by Oxfam's Safe Programming principles, ensuring access is cleared of obstruction and that there are door handles, locks, lighting (solar) and rope handles for support. Location, design and positioning are selected in consultation with refugees, with a focus on women and girls, and persons with disabilities (PwD). • For facility (latrines and water tanks) rehabilitation, Oxfam shifted maintenance from implementation via contractors to a community -led modality. Oxfam selects Community Technical Volunteers (CTVs) and provides them with (on -the -job) training, a WASH facility toolkit  and spare parts. CTVs, supported by Oxfam engineers, monitor and document the needs of facilities. These are compiled into a Bill of Quantities (BoQ) and Oxfam reviews and authorizes the works. CTVs obtain the material from an Oxfam -contracted hardware store at an average of CAD 39.42/facility. This market -based approach greatly reduces maintenance costs compared with private contractors that charge CAD 105.12/facility, empowers beneficiaries to engage with local markets, and prevents overcharging of refugees. Once works are completed, Oxfam checks their quality before handing them over to the HHs.  • Ongoing desludging services will be maintained for existing and new latrines and septic tanks via Oxfam -contracted desludgers to ensure functionality, mitigate community tensions within the ISs that arise from sharing latrines, reduce open defecation, and prevent proliferation of hand -dug pits that expose people to health and protection risks. title: Addressing multi-sectoral needs of the most vulnerable population in the Baalbek
description: Under Lebanon Humanitarian Fund (LHF) 1st Standard Allocation(United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs  - UNOCHA project) Oxfam has two projects; LHF 1;  Oxfam will equip two boreholes in Lebanon (one in Bekaa and one in Beirut) with solar water pumping system. title: Improved Networks, Training and Jobs (INTAJ)
description: Mercy Corps proposes a 12-month, ₤5 million programme to address economic and resource-driven tensions by focusing on short to medium-term interventions to provide livelihood support and promote social cohesion within the most vulnerable host and refugee populations to help contribute to greater stability in Tripoli and Bekaa Valley. The two regions have distinctly different factors that contribute to tension between the groups. In Tripoli, economic and social factors such as job competition, increase in rents, food insecurity and gender-based violence drive tensions between refugee and Lebanese communities. While in Bekaa, community tensions are driven primarily by pressures on available resources and services, specifically in solid waste collection and removal, affordable shelter, water, and electricity, as well as jobs. These tensions were exacerbated in April by the forced movement of refugees from Arsal into West Bekaa by the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF). | Under the proposed programme, Mercy Corps will implement the following tracks:•Track 1: Private sector-led skills development training and Micro-Small-Medium Enterprise (MSME) support for vulnerable groups, including technical assistance and in-kind grant support, as well as internship and apprenticeship components for individuals; •Track 2: Design micro-interventions focused on solid waste recycling and reuse value chain, with a focus on informal collection and recycling activities, to directly target MSMEs, as well as chronically poor households who are the likely incubators of social tension within target communities;•Track 3: Market-support for women-led agricultural cooperatives to address food insecurity and livelihoods within the most vulnerable populations, while building sustainable enterprises through technical and in-kind support; and•Track 4: Regular community-level social tension perception surveys providing an effective sentinel monitoring system that generates data and evidence needed to identify, diagnose and measure changes to social tension in Lebanese host communities, thereby also affording donors an additional data stream for broader analysis and related programming.

title: Multi-sectoral Response to the humanitarian crisis in the North of Lebanon through the human security approach
description:
Lebanon is experiencing one of the worst crises in the Middle East and North Africa region. According to the latest World Bank Lebanon Economic Monitor (LEM), the economic and financial crisis is likely to rank in the top 10, possibly top 3, most severe crises episodes globally since the mid-nineteenth century. In the absence of a functional government, the UN Secretary-General expressed his deep concern in August 2021 about the rapidly deteriorating socio-economic situation while highlighting hyperinflation, acute shortages of fuel, electricity, medicine and access to clean water. The Secretary-General calls on all Lebanese political leaders to urgently form an effective government of national unity that can bring immediate relief, justice and accountability to the people of Lebanon and drive an ambitious and meaningful course for reform to restore access to basic services, restore stability, promote sustainable development and inspire hope for a better future.  
Since April 2021, the multifaceted crisis in Lebanon has significantly impacted the lives of all residents in the country, mainly the poor and vulnerable populations. With the lack of electricity, fuel, cash flow restrictions and unsubsidized medical items, the quality of life has largely decreased, and the majority of the families are not able to secure their basic needs. Unfortunately, with more Lebanese and non-Lebanese falling into poverty and the increase in the reliance on out-of-pocket expenditure, more vulnerable individuals are not having the timely access to health care, in addition, the increase in cost of the medications and medical supplies has made many patients unable to afford the procurement of essential medicines and eventually worsening of their health status and hence increase the need for secondary health care admissions. The World Bank states that the economy is likely to contract by a further 9.5 per cent in 2021 and has warned that there is “no clear turning point in the horizon”. 

To this end, the proposed Programme aims to establish a community centre in Abou Samra to assess and meet the urgent needs of vulnerable populations in response to Lebanon’s multi-layered humanitarian crisis. In doing this, the Programme aims to support affected populations to define their own urgent needs, and to engage directly with local authorities on their needs, promoting dialogue and accountability. To ensure these needs are met, given the depth of Lebanon’s current crisis, the Programme will support local service providers (government and non-government) to deliver on the assessed needs. Through this approach, the Programme will increase the resilience of at least 5280 women, men, girls and boys (1274 Lebanese and 4006 non-Lebanese) living in the most vulnerable area of the north of Lebanon. It will be implemented through a joint Programme to capitalise on UN Habitat’s expertise in areas of municipal governance and planning, on UN Women’s expertise in the delivery of protection services and gender responsive programming, and UNICEF’s expertise on integrated programming and sector leadership in child protection and education.

title: Improved access to municipal and social services through renewable energy alternatives and provision of support to Zahle basic services to enhance preparedness and crisis response capacities to protect communities and respond to conflict and natural disas
description:
The project aims to enhance the wellbeing, safety, health, and security conditions of both host and refugee populations in Zahle Beqa’a, Lebanon. This will be achieved by improving the operations of public facilities and enhancing safety in targeted communities through reliable and renewable energy supplies to these facilities and public spaces. Lebanon, hosting the highest number of refugees per capita globally, has a severely strained energy sector and collapsing social services. The project addresses urgent needs under Lebanon's Emergency Response Plan for 2021-2022, particularly in the WaSH and health sectors, by providing reliable energy to facilities like Tel Chiha Hospital and a Beqa’a Water Establishment pumping station during the first phase of the project. Renewable energy systems, designed by experts in coordination with the Lebanese Center for Energy Conservation, will ensure consistent power for essential services. A technical committee comprising UN-Habitat, local government, LCEC, consultants, and community members will oversee the project’s implementation. Given Lebanon's severe socio-economic, political, and energy crises, exacerbated by the Syrian refugee influx, Beirut Port explosion, COVID-19, and recent Gaza conflict spill-over, public sector services have drastically deteriorated.

The average salary within the public sector went down from US$ 1,000 to at most US$ 40. This has significantly impacted the quantity and quality of services provided by public institutions where public-sector employees stopped showing up to work as their wages can barely cover transportation. This comes against the backdrop of the Syrian
refugee crisis which continues to pressure existing malfunctioning and overburdened urban services and municipalities, the Beirut Port explosion, the lasting COVID-19 pandemic impact – and more recently and urgently, the drastic armed conflict spill-over effect of the war in Gaza, on Lebanon. 

The departments and branches of the Civil Defence were heavily impacted by funding cuts imposed by the central government, thus severely impacting their ability to respond and provide emergency services. Based on a UN-Habitat rapid survey, around 80% of the CD fleet is non-functional due to the lack of maintenance while the remaining 20% is not utilized due to lack of fuel. Despite all these constraints, the CD remains one of the only public institutions that still responds to emergency needs of the community, both in urban and rural settings – while other public sectors have ceased to function. However, the deteriorated ability of the CD across Lebanon, to adequately and efficiently respond to emergencies has led an increase in fatalities as well as loss of infrastructural and environmental assets across the country. 

Consequently, with the funding made available for the second phase, the project will rehabilitate and equip the Zahle District CD to strengthen its civil protection, prevention, and preparedness capacities to better respond to potential emergency needs caused by the impact of conflict, manmade and natural hazards that might turn into disasters. The need for their services is even more apparent in the preparedness context of the country and steps taken by the UN in line with the Government, to the ongoing and likely protracted spill over impact of the war in Gaza in the South of Lebanon which is already causing vast material damage and human loss. 

Thus, based on a rapid survey conducted by UN-Habitat to identify CD current urgent needs and challenges in Lebanon, the project will upgrade the building, its basic services, mainly water and sanitation, repair essential trucks and vehicles, and provide personnel firefighting/emergency response tools and equipment. 

The project approach will validate the previous assessment of the CD centre in Zahle, with additional technical assessments on urgent needs. This includes an assessment of the physical situation of the centre in terms of rehabilitation of the building, the current situation of firefighting trucks and vehicles, and the last assessment will cover the personnel protection gear needed to fight fires and respond to other emergencies in a safe and efficient way. The main expected accomplishment is a vastly improved CD centre that is better able to respond to emergencies, covering not only the large district of Zahle and neighbouring municipalities. In addition to the improved coordination mechanism created by the awareness raising workshops between the CD and the surrounding municipalities. It will also serve as a strong facility that can support the country better cope with the potential impact of a spreading conflict from the south to the rest of the country or dispatch its capacities south to support.

title: Emergency Country-Specific Funding in the Middle East - ICRC Appeals 2019-2021
description: July 2019 – Humanitarian needs stemming from the crises in Syria and Iraq remain significant throughout the Middle East. Continued violence in Syria raises little prospects for the voluntary, safe, sustainable and dignified return of over 5.6 million refugees in the region. Internally displaced persons range in the millions in Syria and Iraq, and humanitarian needs are acute for refugees facing protracted displacement in Jordan and Lebanon.  With the support of GAC and other donors, the ICRC’s humanitarian operations in Syria, Iraq, Jordan and Lebanon aim to provide protection, emergency relief, and other essential services to people affected by armed conflict and other situations of violence, as well as to promote respect for international humanitarian law. title: Bekaa Dialogue - phase 3
description: This project for continued support to the Bekaa Dialogue Group (BDG) and conflict sensitivity support and capacity development to the Bekaa Water Establishment (BWE), constitutes a third phase of the Creating Space for Peace project. This phase of work builds on the achieves and learning of the previous two phases. In Phases I and II the Bekaa Dialogue Group (BDG) was established and its capacities built on conflict-mapping, conflict-analysis, and facilitation skills. In Phase II the BDG identified as three topics which cause high conflict and tensions, these were: (a) Education, (b) Protection, and (c) Natural Resource Management. Phases I and II of this project constituted piloting and proof of concept of the dialogue model and the approach of integrating conflict sensitivity into water management in the Bekaa: developing a dialogue mechanism (facilitating dialogue, supporting initiatives and establishing a platform for increased outreach through the conference). Phase III aims at consolidating the learning and building on these results to a) further strengthen and grow the dialogue mechanism, with a focus on local ownership and sustainability, b) develop and connect up additional dialogue groups, and c) connect up the dialogue process with key institutions, such as the BWE to address tensions. Alongside this process, Alert will continue to work directly with the BWE, in partnership with SDC UNICEF and others, to develop its capacities and cultures to identify, manage and ultimately mitigate tensions related to water services in Bekaa. This third phase will focus on capitalisation of learning, scale up and replication of the dialogue mechanisms, transfer of capacities and evidencing the approach for similar dialogue and conflict mitigation projects in Lebanon. In order to mitigate the tensions due to the high concentration of refugees in some identified vulnerable areas , NRC will implement eight Community Support Projects ( 5 in the South and three in the north of the country), mainly in relation to water supply, to cope with the extra population influx and the forecasted water scarcity. The project also aims to reach a total of 154,032 beneficiaries with information, counselling and legal support, as well as providing community capacity building for refugees in urban settings.
