Les activités du projet comprennent: 1) développer une stratégie de communication pour le changement social et comportemental  sensible au genre avec les partenaires locaux de mise en œuvre et les organisations de défense des droits des femmes (ODF), pour l'adoption de comportements et de pratiques saines en matière de SDSR; 2) fournir une assistance technique aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) locales partenaires de mise en œuvre et aux ODF pour le renforcement des capacités organisationnelles et l'intégration de la dimension de genre; 3) mettre en œuvre des solutions locales aux défis en matière de SDSR et de nutrition avec les femmes, les adolescentes, les hommes et les garçons; 4) fournir des programmes complets basés sur les compétences en matière de SDSR, de bien-être, de santé et de développement aux adolescentes, aux garçons, aux parents et tuteurs d'adolescents; 5) renforcer les capacités techniques des gestionnaires et des fonctionnaires en matière de gestion, d'analyse, d'utilisation et de planification d'urgence des données relatives à la santé sexuelle et reproductive, à la nutrition et au climat des communautés et des établissements; 6) fournir une assistance technique aux fonctionnaires, aux établissements de santé et aux représentants de la santé communautaire en matière de gouvernance inclusive dans le domaine de la santé sexuelle et reproductive et de la nutrition.

reporting_org_name: Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada (DFATD)
title: Advancing gender equality, resilience, opportunity and inclusion worldwide facility
description: The Advancing gender equality, resilience, opportunity, and inclusion worldwide (GROW) facility aims to improve women’s livelihoods in developing countries by shifting corporate practices and creating economic opportunities for women. It seeks to achieve gender equality results by providing financial support and advisory services to help businesses improve gender equality through their core functions. This includes employing people, delivering goods and services, and allocating capital. The Facility aims to offer loans and other financial tools to support companies with growth strategies aligned with gender equality goals. This includes promoting women’s leadership or boosting women’s employment in under-represented sectors. Through advisory services, the Facility supports companies in adopting and implementing policies and operational practices that improve the lives of women in all their diversity.  The GROW Facility aims to support women’s leadership and inclusion in 5 priority areas: (1) accelerating access to finance for women and women-led businesses, (2) making supply chains inclusive; (3) removing barriers to employment and leadership; (4) bridging the digital divide; and (5) accelerating inclusive and gender-smart climate action. | Le Fonds de promotion de l’égalité des genres, de la résilience, des opportunités et de l’inclusion dans le monde vise à améliorer les vies des femmes dans les pays en développement en modifiant les pratiques des entreprises et en créant des possibilités économiques pour les femmes. Ce fonds vise des résultats en matière d’égalité des genres en offrant un soutien financier et des services consultatifs pour aider les entreprises à atteindre l’égalité des genres dans leurs fonctions principales. Cela comprend l’emploi de personnes, la livraison de biens et de services et l’affectation de capitaux. Le Fonds offre des prêts et utilise d’autres outils financiers pour soutenir les entreprises dont la stratégie de croissance est alignée sur les objectifs en matière d’égalité des genres. Il s’agit notamment de promouvoir le leadership des femmes et de stimuler l’emploi des femmes dans les secteurs où elles sont sous-représentées. Grâce à des services consultatifs, le Fonds aide les entreprises à adopter et à mettre en œuvre des politiques et des pratiques opérationnelles qui améliorent la vie des femmes dans toute leur diversité.  Le Fonds vise à soutenir le leadership et l’inclusion des femmes par des actions dans 5 domaines prioritaires : 1) accélérer l’accès au financement pour les femmes et les entreprises dirigées par des femmes; 2) rendre les chaînes d’approvisionnement inclusives; 3) éliminer les obstacles à l’emploi et au leadership; 4) combler le fossé numérique; 5) accélérer l’action climatique inclusive et favorable à l’égalité des genres.

title: Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI)  - NROBI - 2024 to 2025
description: The Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI) supports small projects proposed and implemented by local organizations in Burundi, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda. The CFLI contributes to the overall goal of reducing poverty by providing funding for small projects that offer direct social, economic or technical assistance to local populations.  The CFLI retains the same broad themes set out since 2016, which align closely with the 6 pillars of the Feminist International Assistance Policy. This allows flexibility to respond to and focus on themes relevant to local needs. The 6 thematic priorities include: (1) contributing to inclusive governance, including diversity and 2SLGBTQI+, democracy, human rights and the rule of law; (2) contributing to gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls; (3) contributing to peace and security, with a focus on conflict prevention and building peace; (4) contributing to growth that works for everyone, including women’s economic rights, decent jobs and entrepreneurship, investing in the poorest and most vulnerable, and safeguarding economic gains; (5) contributing to environment and climate action, focusing on adaptation, mitigation and  water management; and (6) contributing to human dignity, covering health, education and nutrition. | Le Fonds canadien d'initiatives locales (FCIL) appuie de petits projets proposés et mis en œuvre par des organisations locales au Burundi, au Kenya, en Somalie et en Ouganda. Le FCIL contribue aux objectifs de réduction de la pauvreté en finançant des projets qui offrent de l'aide sociale, économique ou technique directement à la population locale.  Le FCIL conserve les mêmes vastes thèmes définis depuis 2016, qui s'alignent avec les 6 principes de la Politique d'aide internationale féministe. Cela permet une certaine flexibilité pour répondre et se concentrer sur des thèmes pertinents aux besoins locaux.  Les 6 priorités thématiques comprennent : 1) contribuer à l’égalité des genres et à  l’autonomisation des femmes et des filles; 2) contribuer à la gouvernance inclusive, y compris la diversité et 2ELGBTQI+, la démocratie, les droits de la personne et la primauté du droit; 3) contribuer à la paix et la sécurité, avec un accent sur la prévention des conflits et la consolidation de la paix; 4) contribuer à la croissance au service de tous, y compris la promotion des droits économiques des femmes, l’accès à des emplois décents et à l’entrepreneuriat, l’investissement dans les personnes les plus pauvres et vulnérables, et la protection des progrès économiques; 5) contribuer à l’environnement et à l’action pour le climat, avec un accent sur l’adaptation et l’atténuation, ainsi que sur la gestion de l’eau; 6) contribuer à la dignité humaine, y compris la santé, l’éducation et la nutrition.

title: Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research- program 2024 to 2025
description: The Biodiversity for Resilient Ecosystems in Agricultural Landscapes (B-REAL) project aims to conserve and restore biodiversity in intensively farmed, climate-stressed regions of Colombia, Kenya and Peru. The project integrates biodiversity practices into agriculture, involving women as producers and traditional knowledge holders in the co-design of intervention. It also promotes nutritious and underutilized local crops to improve farmers’ incomes. This funding is part of Canada’s commitment made at the 15th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (COP15) in December 2022 in Montreal. It aligned with the Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils, one of the Group of Seven (G7) Apulia Food Security Initiatives. Project activities include: (1) co-creating biodiversity interventions; (2) implementing technologies through demonstration plots, tree nurseries, community seed banks, and training programs; and (3) conducting gender-responsive market assessments and using market incentives for conservation. | Le projet Biodiversité pour des écosystèmes agricoles durables (B-REAL) vise à conserver et restaurer la biodiversité dans les régions en Colombie, au Kenya, et Pérou qui sont cultivées intensivement et sous pression des changements climatiques. Dans ce projet, les approches de biodiversité sont intégrées dans l’agriculture à travers la cocréation des interventions avec les femmes productrices afin de promouvoir les espèces nutritives sous-utilisées pour un meilleur revenu des fermes. Ce financement contribue à l’engagement pris par le Canada durant la Conférence des Nations unies sur la biodiversité COP15 en décembre 2022 à Montréal et est aussi aligné avec la Vision pour des cultures et des sols adaptés (VACS), une des initiatives de sécurité alimentaire du G7 d’Apulia. Les activités du projet comprennent : 1) co-créer des interventions en biodiversité; (2) mettre en oeuvre des technologies à travers des parcelles de démonstration, des pépinières, des banques de semences communautaires et des formations; 3) réaliser des évaluations du marché sensibles à l'égalité des genres avec l'usage d'incitatifs commerciaux pour la conservation.

title: Trade for resilient, inclusive and sustainable economic growth
description: This project supports inclusive and sustainable economic growth by strengthening the capacity of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly those led by women and under-represented groups, to access Canadian and international markets. It aims to strengthen trade support institutions (TSIs) in 16 countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America to deliver inclusive, gender-responsive, and sustainable services to SMEs. The project also seeks to improve the ability of TSIs to integrate gender equality and social inclusion into their operations and to enhance the export readiness of SMEs. Project activities include: (1) training TSIs to deliver export-readiness and climate-resilient services to SMEs; (2) developing gender action plans and tools to support inclusive service delivery; and (3) coaching SMEs to improve their export offerings and connect with international buyers.  This project supports initiatives that benefit 3,200 SMEs, (2,133 led or owned by women and under-represented groups) and 16 TSIs. | Ce projet soutient une croissance économique inclusive et durable en renforçant la capacité des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME), en particulier celles dirigées par des femmes et des groupes sous-représentés, à accéder aux marchés canadiens et internationaux.  Ce projet vise à renforcer les institutions de soutien au commerce dans 16 pays d’Afrique, d’Asie et d’Amérique latine afin qu’elles offrent des services inclusifs, sensibles au genre et durables aux PME. Il vise également à améliorer la capacité des institutions de soutien au commerce à intégrer l’égalité des genres et l’inclusion sociale dans leurs opérations et à accroître la préparation à l’exportation des PME.  Les activités du projet comprennent : 1) former des institutions de soutien au commerce pour offrir des services de préparation à l’exportation et de résilience climatique aux PME; 2) élaborer des plans d’action pour l’égalité des genres et d’outils pour appuyer des services inclusifs; 3) réaliser le mentorat des PME pour améliorer leurs offres à l’exportation et établir des liens avec des acheteurs internationaux.  Ce projet soutient des initiatives qui profitent à 3 200 PME, dont les 2 tiers sont dirigées ou détenues par des femmes et des groupes sous-représentés, et à 16 institutions de soutien au commerce.

description:
PELUM Kenya has been participating in Climate Change COP discussions and has a key thematic area on climate change in its current strategic plan 2021 to 2026. PELUM Kenya works closely with climate change actors in Kenya, regionally and continental and is a member of PACJA, AFSA among other like-minded organizations. PELUM Kenya has been participating at national level COP 27 preparatory meetings and is a member of the agriculture sector working group. PELUM Kenya has also been participating in the Africa caravanners online planning meetings and therefore well connected with like-minded partners.

This is an initiative to mobilize Kenya citizenry voices to demand climate justice and more so in the areas of agriculture and climate change investments. Food security is a key sector in Africa’s zeal for climate adaptation, resilience and mitigation and therefore need for crucial attention. This will include a focus on the principles and practices of agriculture that are adaptive to climate change among small holder farmers. The initiative is aimed at influencing COP 27 decisions and will include a series of activities in Kenya such as media influencing, workshops, press releases, and will culminate in participation in COP 27 side events. The initiative will be well aligned and coordinated with a similar approach of COP 27 Africa caravanners.

Despite an insignificant responsibility for climate change, African communities bear a disproportionate burden of its impacts compared to most regions of the world.While COP 26 in Glasgow failed to recognize Africa as a region with special needs and circumstances, and adaptation still remains marginal in global efforts to combat climate change, Africancommunities and their representatives intend to seize the opportunity of COP 27 to continue their fight for climate justice.

PELUMKenya in its mandate works with small scale farmers who form a large portion of population in African context to defend the rights of communities in the face of the climate crisis, is committed to being a catalyst for the demands of African peoples on adaptation,climate finance, loss and damage, and mitigation. The caravans, which will be conducted in different parts of Kenya will constitutea unique community mobilization that will engage indigenous peoples', women's, youth and grassroots movements.

Their objectives will be to: i) Mobilize local communities -including youth and women movements -for climate justice and demand increased mobilization from African governments at COP27to address climate challenges in Africa, ii) Highlight the important role agriculture plays in addressing climate change and therefore call for attention to agro-ecology in climate change discourse and investment in African continent, iii) Highlight the impacts of climate change on African communities and their environment and livelihoods among small scale farmers, iv) Highlight agriculture related climate smart solutions integrated with their traditional and local knowledge, v) Create an inter-communitylearning chain of good practices and nature-based solutions for climate change adaptation, as well as training of youth on climate negotiations in order to prepare them for participation in COY 17 and COP 27 vi) Increase African citizen pressure on theirnational governments and on international negotiations at COP27 to better take into account their realities, priorities and aspirations.

title: FEMNET Feminist COP
description:
1.1 The African Women’s Development and Communication Network- FEMNET The African Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET) is a pan-African, feminist and membership-based network based in Nairobi, Kenya with over 800 individual and institutional members across 50 African countries and in the diaspora. FEMNET envisions a society where African women and girls thrive in dignity andwell-being, free from patriarchal and neoliberal oppression and injustices. FEMNET recognizes that the commitmentto alter relationsof power, structural injustices,and systemic oppression lies at the heart of feminism. FEMNET is therefore committed to shing towards altering power structures that perpetuate gender inequality by nurturing the Africanwomen’s movement to enable women and girls intheir diversity to effectively claim, affirm, and use their collective power to end all forms of exclusion, oppression, exploitation, and injustices against them. Founded in 1988, FEMNET exists to facilitate and coordinate thesharing of experiences,information, and strategies for human rights promotion among feminists, activists, and women’srights organizations as a strategy for collective organizing; policy influencing <(>&<)> advocacy; strategic communication; capacity strengthening as well as feminist solidarity and movement building.

1.2. Climate Justice FEMNET is implementing the climate justice work under the Africa Activists for Climate Justice (AACJ)project in partnership with Oxfam NOVIB, Natural Justice, PACJA and the Africa Youth Commission. The project is based on thepremise that women, young people, and indigenous peoples are most exposed to climate hazards and less able to adapt and/or recover.They are least positioned to cope with the effects of climate change dueto their limited access to (natural and financial) resources, networks,decision-making power, and legal systems. They are also least likely to be compensated for climate impacts, having to bear the loss and struggle to rebuild their livelihoods and properties. The theme of the Feminist COP will be "Just Transition." This theme underscores the importance of inclusive, equitable, and gender-responsive approaches to addressing climate change and its impacts.It highlights the need to ensure that the transition to a sustainable future leave no one behind,particularly women, girls, and marginalized communities. The theme will be able to link the various thematic dialogues such as Climate finance, debt, renewable energy, the extractive sector, Loss and damage, and adaptation In the face of urgent issues such as climate change, environmental deterioration, and economic disparities, it has become clear that a fair shift towards a sustainable future is not only imperative but also a chance to rectify long standinginjustices. Embracing a feminist perspective on the notion of a just transition acknowledges theinterconnectedness of environmental and social equity, emphasizing that gender equality must be a fundamental element of any transition plan.

The FeministCOP seeks to:
● To provide a safe and empowering space for African feminists to voice their concerns,aspirations, and demands related to climate change and COP 28.
● To foster solidarity and collaboration among feminists, civil society organizations,and activists working towards climate justice in Africa.
● To facilitate a deeper understanding of the COP processes and negotiations, empowering participants to engage more effectively in climate advocacy.
● To document the experiences and stories of African women in the context of climate change and share these narratives with a global audience.

title: FAIR4ALL Regional Value Chains in Africa
description:
The Power of Voices Partnership (PvP) is an influencing programme with the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The programme  FAIR for ALL led by Oxfam Novib is five year long initiative implemented jointly with consortium members Huairou Commission, SOMO and Third World Network-Africa (TWN-Africa) aimed at supporting and collaborating with people’s rightful demands towards companies, governments and multilateral organizations for economic, social and environmental justice, promoting global trade and value-chains that are fair for all. The main focus of the FAIR for ALL programme proposal is to support and strengthen CSOs to play their diverse roles; as educators, mobilizers, creators and watchdogs to make trade and value chains FAIR for ALL.
In Africa, FAIR for ALL programmeaims at Strengthened civil society and regional networks of economic and climate justice movements, human and land rights organizations, and women’s, producer and labour organizations work in partnership with the private sector to push for fairer rules, systems and institutions to promote gender, fiscal and climate justice, redistribution of power and benefit sharing within commodity value chains for more inclusive and sustainable development in Africa.
The Africa  FAIR for ALL programme will be implemented by Oxfam in Africa and partners, aiming to: 1) Transforming dominant agricultural and extractive commodity value chains and increasing the local share of value generated within these chains through: Improved respect for human, land, labour and environmental rights, including more equitable prices and improved livelihoods for women, small producers and mining-affected
communities, and better working conditions and economic returns for ASM producers; and by maximizing domestic resource mobilization, including fiscal returns for investmentin gender-responsive public services; and building natural resource-based regional economic linkages and diversification at local, national and regional levels. 2) Improving civic space for citizen groups and actors, especially those working to transform agriculture and extractives value chains.
These objectives will be achieved by Strengthening capacity to engage with the regional private sector and regional and continental processes andvalue chains on agriculture, agribusiness, climate change, extractives and trade; Improving technical knowledge on trade, tax and climate change, the extractives and agribusiness sectors, and the intersection of theseissues with gender; Expanding and consolidating alliances, networks and coalitions; Creating space for local partners including women groups to engage with regional and continental institutions, processes, fora and platforms as well as regional private sector networks and associations.
To achieve main objectives of the programme in Africa, Oxfam will collaborate with: African Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET); Réseau des organizations paysannes et de producteurs de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (ROPPA); Tax Justice Network Africa (TJNA): a member of the Global Alliance for Tax Justice (TJNA); and Fight Inequality Alliance (FIA).

title: The Feminist COP 27
description:
FEMNET and its partners are organizing the Feminist COP 27 in October 2022. This is an alternative space to COP 27 led by feministsat the frontline of the climate crisis from the global south who will gather to fulfil the main objective of the retreat which is to build solidarity and marshall support for feminist asks at COP 27. The feminist COP is an important convening as it will give feminists who will not attend COP 27 an opportunity to demand climate justice and parties’ fair share of climate action for both mitigation and adaptation.

The role of FEMNET will be fund administration as well as granting and reporting, while the role of the partnerorganization will be mobilizing the participation of frontline communities from the Niger Delta as well as from parts of Senegal. Additionally, FEMNET will be in charge of organizing the FEMINIST COP 27, co-creating with al the partner -Kebekatche Women's organization based in Niger Delta. FEMNET will co-create the Feminist COP with other partners and communities from North, South and East Africa. At least 1/3rd of the funding will be provided to the partner to mobilize participation and cater for costs associated with the mobilization.

title: AR Engendering African Social Movements
description:
Expanding the En(gender)ing African Social Movements Project to build the capacity of member movements of
Africans Rising to mainstream gender equality and its intersection with climate justice into their operations at all
levels. The project will alsoincorporatecampaigns at grassroots level, connecting movement members and building
solidarity among movements across borders to advocate for women's reproductive rights, economic rights and
climate justice. All advocacy and capacity building under thisproject will take intersectional approach especially as
climate change currently affects a greater proportion of women in Africa. This project contributesto the pathway on
building Strong, inclusive climate movements in Africa.

En(gender)ing AfricanSocial Movements has achieved greatsuccess since its inception. Through the project, we have
developed a Feminist Curriculum that outlines the feminist principles andtheir application to build an inclusive
society. It has enabled us to convene, connect, empower and support movements to build capacity as they work to
dismantle oppressive systems interlinking gender inequality, climate crisis, poverty, political and social exclusion. We
have also started training and capacity building of Africans Rising Core Team and Coordinating Collective and will
reach more movements this year through campaigns during International Women's Day, 16 days of activism, Invisible
giants recognition, movement exchange, 25th May mobilisation. The expansion of the project is a sudden
opportunity given the need to accelerate campaigns andactions against climate polluters and especially to push for
loss and damage. In communities where climate change has led to devastation of the environment or led to extreme
weatherevents, women have been the most affected. It is necessary to ensure that in tackling this catastrophe,
women's rights and inclusion are at integrated in movement work and actions.

title: Climate caravans 2025
description:
The African Climate Justice Caravan is a youth- and civil society-led movement mobilizing voices and actions for climate justice across Africa. From September to December 2025, ACJC will organize national caravans in five countries—Benin, Zambia, Chad, Nigeria, and Mali—connecting grassroots communities, women, youth, and policymakers to demand equitable climate solutions.the initiative will:
- Engage over 5,000 participants directly through caravans, dialogues, and advocacy events.
- Amplify African climate justice narratives via media campaigns and regional platforms, reaching millions continent-wide.
- Influence policy processes at national, regional, and global levels, including African Union forums and COP30.
-Strengthen women’s and youth leadership in climate governance and promote just transitions in food and energy systems.

By bridging local realities with global decision-making spaces, ACJC aims to position Africa as a united, influential voice in shaping a fair and sustainable climate future.

title: Youth-Bond-2025: Civic Innovation Hub
description:
The Youth-Bond-2025: Civic Innovation Hub is a transformative project fostering collaboration among African youth to address globalgovernance challenges and advance participatory democracy. Through capacity-building activities, the project will empower young leaders from Kenya to co-develop innovative methodologies for enhancing democratic engagement, countering threats to democracy, and advancing youth inclusion in governance, all based and scaling up from past successful initiatives and youth-led programs of WYA Africa.

Key activities include a Capacity-Building Workshop on Participatory Democracy <(>&<)> Youth Engagement in Nairobi, Kenya, where marginalized youth will collaborate with youth leaders and experts to co-create an adaptable participatory democracy methodology. This will be followed by the Human Dignity Curriculum (HDC), equipping youth with the skills to advocate for human rights, ethical leadership and promote safe digital spaces.

The project will also establish the AU Advocacy Academy and Global Governance, where youthwill analyze policies on democracy, digital transformation, human rights and climate governance, proposing solutions to global challenges. The online platform will track AU and UN governance processes, and facilitate policy tracking, youth forums, and advocacy.

A core element is the Youth-Led Civic Forums for Democratic Engagement, engaging 40 youth leaders 20 from Africa in policy dialogue and influence. These forums will focus on the African Youth Charter and local-youth-led solutions to global issues, advocating for inclusive governance and addressing threats to democracy, youth exclusion, and human rights.

The AU Youth Innovation Lab will offer a practical phase where youth design local initiatives to tackle governance challenges. The project will culminate in a hybrid conference with over 100 stakeholders, showcasing youth-led projects, the new methodology, and offering insights into AU and global governance systems.

Focusing on marginalized communities, youth-led advocacy, and institutional responsiveness, Youth-Bond-2025 is a dynamic initiative to empower youth, bridge African-youth gaps in policy development and democratic dialogue, in order to shape inclusive governance frameworks for the future.

By connecting African and global youth, it fosters collaboration and equips marginalized voices for meaningful change. Mission: WYA Africa educates, trains, andmobilizes youth to engage in advocacy, grassroots movements, and decision-making at all levels to address democracy and human rights challenges, shape policy, and promote human dignity. title: FAO HUM 2021-2025
description:
Sida’s humanitarian support to FAO enables the organisation to respond to emergencies by protecting and restoring livelihoods with a particular focus on agriculture and livestock while addressing acute food insecurity for the most vulnerable affected by conflict and climate shocks.  Through this support, FAO will focus on the phases 3-5 in the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) i.e. (3) Crisis, (4) Emergency and (5) Catastrophe/Famine. 
FAO's new strategic framework 2022-2030 places the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at the centre of its operations. In terms of programme priority areas related to humanitarian interventions, FAO will focus on agriculture and food emergencies in countries facing, or at risk of acute food insecurity, by providing urgent livelihood and nutrition assistance. The strategic framework states that by 2023 FAO aims to assist 60 million people annually with emergency and resilience interventions, and through investments in anticipatory action that will reduce humanitarian needs in the future. This is an ambitious increase from the 35 million target in 2019. 
The focus on both acute food security and livelihoods with positive spill-over effects on household and community resilience in combination with FAO’s leading technical expertise in agriculture and its focus on Anticipatory Action. FAO has a clear policy on gender equlity in crises, which include to use a gener perspective during assessment and targeting during program development. 
The above makes FAO a valuable strategic humanitarian partner to Sida. Sida will in 2022 allocate 124 million SEK to FAO’s emergency interventions in six countries: Afghanistan, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Madagascar and Somalia. This support also includes unallocated funds to emerging and deteriorating humanitarian situations through the Special Fund for Emergency and Rehabilitation Activities (SFERA) as well as a method development support to strengthening countries’ capacities for risk-informed localized humanitarian responses. | Insatsen syftar till att möjliggöra för FAO att svara upp mot humanitära behov genom att skydda och återställa försörjningsmöjligheter inom jordbruk och boskap. FAO kommer att stärka tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning för de mest utsatta som drabbats av konflikter, klimatförändringar och naturkatastrofer. Genom detta stöd kommer FAO att fokusera på faserna 3-5 i enlighet med IPC-skalan, dvs. (3) kris, (4) nödsituation och (5) svält/katastrof. 
FAO:s nya strategiska ramverk 2022-2030 utgår från de globala målen. I enlighet med ramverket kommer FAO i humanitära kontexter att fokusera på jordbruk och livsmedelskriser i länder som står inför, eller riskerar att drabbas av akuta behov inom livsmedelsförsörjning. FAO har år 2023 som mål att bistå 60 miljoner människor årligen med nöd- och resiliensinsatser, och genom investeringar i föregripande åtgärder. Detta är en ambitiös ökning från målet på 35 miljoner människor år 2019. 
FAO:s arbete i humanitära kriser svarar väl upp mot strategin för Sidas humanitära bistånd (2021-2025). FAO:s fokus på livsmedelsförsörjning i kombination med att skydda och återställa försörjningsmöjligheter inom jordbruk anses ha positiva effekter på både akuta behov och resiliens bland människor som lever i humanitära krissituationer. FAO har också en central roll i arbetet med föregripande arbete som syftar till att minska framtida humanitära behov. FAO har en tydlig policy för jämställdhet i kriser, vilket inkluderar att man använder ett gender perspektiv i sina underlag och hur man utformar sina program. 
FAO anses därför vara en värdefull strategisk humanitär partner till Sida. Med Sidas stöd på 124 miljoner SEK kommer FAO under 2022 att implementera humanitärt stöd i sex kriser: Afghanistan, Madagaskar, Mali, Niger, Nigeria och Somalia. Insatsen omfattar också oallokerade medel till nya eller förvärrande humanitära kriser genom FAO:s särskilda fond för nödsituationer och återuppbyggnad (SFERA) samt ett metodstöd som syftar till att stärka länders och lokala och nationella aktörers kapacitet för att hantera humanitära insatser. | FAOs Global Goals are:

1. Eradication of hunger, food insecurity and malnutrition, progressively ensuring a world in which people at all times have sufficient safe and nutritious food that meets their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life;

2. Elimination of poverty and the driving forward of economic and social progress for all, with increased food production, enhanced rural development and sustainable livelihoods;

3. Sustainable management and utilization of natural resources, including land, water, air, climate and genetic resources for the benefit of present and future generations.

Based on the global goals, FAO has formulated five strategic objectives:

1. Contribute to the eradication of hunger, food insecurity and malnutrition

2. Make agriculture, forestry and fisheries more productive and sustainable

3. Reduce rural poverty

4. Enable more inclusive and efficient agricultural and food systems

5. Increase the resilience of livelihoods to threats and crises

The Strategic Framework also includes a sixth, broad objective on technical quality, knowledge and services (including cross-cutting themes) that is designed to cover FAOs internal capability to deliver its strategic objectives. The objectives are in alignment with FAOs commitment to working in partnerships.

In humanitarian crises, FAOs main components are:

To help people to anticipate and prepare for crises; To respond fast to crises; To seek to reduce risks and address vulnerabilities.

The humanitarian operations are usually related to the 5th strategic objective which has the four following organizational outcomes (OO):

OO1 - countries and regions have legal, policy and institutional systems and regulatory frameworks for disaster and crisis risk management for agriculture, food and nutrition;

OO2 - countries and regions deliver regular information and trigger timely actions against potential, known and emerging threats to agriculture, food, and nutrition;

OO3 - countries apply prevention and impact mitigation measures that reduce risks for agriculture, food and nutrition;

OO4 - countries and regions affected by disasters and crises with impact on agriculture, food and nutrition are prepared for, and manage effective responses.

At the next level in the FAO Strategic Framework, there are a number of outputs pertinent to humanitarian action, such as:

Output 4.1: Humanitarian action effectively protect lives and livelihoods of farmers, herders, Fishers, forest- and tree-dependent communities and marginal groups in times of crises.

Output 3.1: Strategies and related interventions improve the resilience of livelihoods systems at risk through prevention and mitigation efforts that minimize the potential impacts of disasters and crises on agriculture food and nutrition at national, subnational and community levels.

Output 2.2: Improved capacities of countries and communities to identify monitor and evaluate risks; conduct needs assessment and response analysis; and act on impending threats to agriculture, nutrition, food security and food safety (and related public health issues).

Output 3.3: Conflict-sensitive programmes on agriculture, food and nutrition reduce the risks of localized conflicts relating to access to grazing, forest and farming lands, fishing grounds, water, trees and other natural resources.

results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | In 2023, Sida's contribution to SFERA supported responses in Bangladesh, Haiti, Myanmar, Nigeria, Syria, Türkiye and the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. The support was channeled through SFERA to these countries. Sida support to SFERA is primarily through one of the windows of the fund, the programme component, which includes the AIRC and AA windows (although the latter is a rather small contribution). The AIRC window supports rapid response by channelling pooled funds towards the immediate procurement and delivery of time-critical inputs. The AA window enables FAO to identify potential threats and act in advance to mitigate the impacts, reduce losses and safeguard livelihoods. The programmatic approach enables operations to adapt as the situation changes, streamlining activities to ensure the most appropriate assistance reaches affected populations sooner. Summary of results and performance is listed below.

Bolivia/Venezuela: Comprehensive approach, covering FSL, WaSH and AA. It was also developed in a high-priority area, which is commendable. Particularly appreciate the gender perspective and the inclusion of women in decision-making processes.

Myanmar: Critically needed and demanding continued support for Myanmar, especially given the severe floods encountered recently and throughout the year seriously affecting agriculture lives in Myanmar. One observation is that FAO has chosen to work with a single partner, AVSI, although it would have been beneficial if they could identify more relevant local partners, particularly in Sagaing, FAO has already mentioned the challenge of finding local technical partners in the report.

Afghanistan: Sida notes that the report importantly highlights how the beneficiary selection was carried out to ensure humanitarian assistance was delivered based on the principle of impartiality. FAO demonstrate how their project targeted households based on vulnerability, including by prioritising areas based on severity (the project was implemented in three provinces which were projected to be in IPC Phase 4). FAO in collaboration with the Food Security and Agriculture Cluster, developed vulnerability-based beneficiary selection criteria for emergency assistance packages, incorporating inputs from various stakeholders such as affected communities, shuras and female community members. Thereby ensuring that community members voices are heard/considered in project implementation.

The operating environment is challenging, and the burden is heavy on humanitarian actors to negotiate exemptions and maintain access to those in need. FAO demonstrate that humanitarian organisations have managed to create possibilities for principled humanitarian action by engaging and empowering women throughout the project cycle, including promoting women's opportunities to make their voices heard in society and within the home thanks to income bringing activities. 13 161 households (105 253 people), of whom 1 106 women-headed households were supported.

Niger: Sida funding was spent in 4 regions, 3 of which are priority regions for the humanitarian response. The project targeted HH in IPC3 and returnees, with a specific focus on women headed households. Activities focused on agricultural inputs and cash programming. The targets were met, with a few overachievements, and only 1 activity had a lower reach. The impact section of the report is very valuable, displaying what activities led to in the life of the persons targeted. A number of local partners were involved, from targeting to project implementation. The Sida funding was complementary to other funding. One observation is that there is no prioritization associated with conflict affected populations (apart from support to returnees), nor a focus on hard-to-reach areas. The project is a resilience strengthening programme.

Sida's assessment is that FAO has achieved results and in the majority of cases met all the targets and that the report is well-written and analytical. Observations, questions and reflections, some stated in the above, will be followed-up in the annual dialogue with FAO and also in the specific country dialouges with FAO.

In 2025, Sida will continue its contribution to the SFERA fund through the programme component, which includes the AIRC and AA windows. In total 45 million SEK will be provided to the SFERA fund, this will covers projects in DRC, Haiti, Syria and Sudan through the AIRC window and an Anticipatory project in Ethiopia through the AA window. description:
Insatsen syftar till att möjliggöra för FAO att svara upp mot humanitära behov genom att skydda och återställa försörjningsmöjligheter inom jordbruk och boskap. FAO kommer att stärka tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning för de mest utsatta som drabbats av konflikter, klimatförändringar och naturkatastrofer. FAO:s nya strategiska ramverk 2022-2030 utgår från de globala målen. title: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations
description:
Kenya's economic growth has been driven by large-scale infrastructure projects, yet small businesses and the youth continue to face challenges in accessing meaningful employment. This disparity has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and the growing effects of climate change. The country’s development plans, under Vision 2030, emphasize the need to create sustainable jobs, improve labor relations, and strengthen social protection systems to address unemployment and underemployment, particularly among vulnerable groups.

This Country Programme Outcome (CPO) focuses on enhancing the capacity of workers' organizations, particularly the Central Organization of Trade Unions – Kenya (COTU-K), to engage in policy development and social dialogue that advances the rights and welfare of workers. By providing technical assistance to COTU-K and its affiliates, the ILO aims to strengthen their ability to advocate for labor rights, social protection, job creation, and environmental sustainability. This includes supporting COTU-K in its efforts to develop strategic advocacy papers on critical issues such as workers' rights, social protection, labor laws, and climate-induced migration.

The CPO also aims to support COTU-K in promoting the ratification of key International Labour Standards, including conventions on social protection, occupational safety, and migrant workers’ rights. Through these efforts, COTU-K will be better equipped to influence national policy, including the review of labor laws and the adoption of national employment policies that benefit workers and foster inclusive development.

In addition, the ILO’s support will enable COTU-K to address gender inequality and discrimination in the workplace, focusing on issues such as gender-based violence, disability inclusion, and labor migration. title: Kenya Climate Innovation Center
description: The objective of the CIC is to support Kenyan SMEs involved in developing locally-appropriate solutions to climate change mitigation and adaptation.  The outputs produced that will achieve this result are: technical advisory services to SMEs, reports that explore and recommend government policies that will create a regulatory environment that increases the prospects and possibilities for such SMEs, provision of information helpful to the SMEs in the form of websites, written reports, and workshops/conferences that discuss the market potential of relevant technologies, the latest developments for the relevant technologies and other areas; and the provision of technical and office facilities (including communications and utilities) that selected SMEs can use. Description of the activity's expected impact and how that will be tracked (M&E): The impact of the CIC will come in the number of relevant SMEs that are assisted in their efforts to develop and deploy innovative solutions to climate change that meet local needs.  This will be assessed with measurements on the quantity of SMEs that are active recipients of the outputs described above. Description of how the knowledge generated by the activity will be disseminated (seminar, workshop, online discussion, etc.): There will be substantial knowledge generated by the activities of the CIC.  This knowledge will relate to best practices to support the development, transfer and deployment of advanced climate technologies and business models in a way that directly supports local capacity to do so, targeting the essential SME community in its key role in the innovation process and ecosystem. This knowledge will be disseminated directly through the CIC in written reports, local conferences and a website, and also internationally (via the same methods) through the planned East African regional community of CICs and related actors and globally through the network of CICs.

About 3 billion people still use heavily polluted firewood and charcoal for cooking.Therefore, the government of the Netherlands aims to give 100 million people access to sustainable energy by 2030. title: Combi Approach Toolkit (CATK)
description: The Combi Approach Toolkit (in Dutch "Combi Aanpak Tool Kit") aims to combine trade, investments and development cooperation with the aim to tackle contemporary challenges like climate change. Dutch companies, knowledge institutes and societal organisations can contribute to solutions. The innovation power, investment power and entrepreneurial spirit of Dutch companies can strengthen and complement development cooperation. This must result in win-win situations in which on the one side the policy will contribute to solving societal challenges and local economic development and on the other side enlarging the earning power of the Dutch private sector abroad.The focus will be on two transitions, the green economic transition and the digital transition, in thirteen countries:•	Bangladesh•	Colombia•	Côte d'Ivoire•	Egypt•	Ghana•	India•	Indonesia•	Kenya•	Morocco•	Nigeria•	Senegal•	South Africa•	Vietnam* Ukraine has been identified as fourteenth country, where the focus will be on reconstruction after the war.In the fourteen countries, one or two strategic combi-tracks will be selected, developed and implemented. These tracks have to contribute to the following objectives:•	Sustainable Dutch earning capacity (SDG 17);•	Local and sustainable economic development and the creation of meaningful employment (SDG 8), focussed on youth and women (SDG 5);•	The green economic transition and/or digital transition (SDG 2, SDG 6, SDG 7, SDG 11, SDG 12 and SDG 13).For more information: Combitracks (only in Dutch)Url = https://www.rvo.nl/onderwerpen/overzicht-combitracks

title: Guidance to green the Kenyan healthcare sector
description: Climate change and health are intricately linked. At the COP26, where Kenya publicly committed to delivering both net zero (by 2030) and climate-resilient healthcare, the need for the health sector to adapt to climate change, as well as contribute to climate mitigation and to make health facilities greener was undersigned by many countries.The aim of this project is to support the Kenyan Ministry of Health in drafting Green Guidelines for the Health Sector that will lead the sector into more sustainable, green and climate mitigating practices, to reduced CO2 emissions, improved health outcomes, and long-term access and cost savings for healthcare institutions. Dutch lessons learned and experience regarding the greening of the health sector, as well as Dutch green innovations and private sector solutions, will be shared. This Government-to-Government cooperation between the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport and the Kenyan Ministry of Health will on the one hand support Kenya's ambition to reduce CO2 emissions and to mitigate climate in the healthcare sector. On the other hand, Dutch innovations and solutions from the private sector will be promoted.This project is part of the Life Science and Health combi-track in Kenya, as well as the Global Health Partnership Programme of the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport.

title: Demonstrating Circular and Biobased Housing in the Kenyan Market
description: Easy Building Concepts B.V. (EBC) has developed a circular and climate-neutral housing system (for emerging economies) based on FSC-certified wood from sustainable forestry. The standardised and scalable building concept can provide a solution for the growing demand for affordable, sustainable and climate-proof housing. This concept can easily be tailored to local customs, needs and demand using local knowledge, labour and materials. This is what is demonstrated with this DHI demonstration project.ECB wants to demonstrate at Mlango Farm, an educational farm with a focus on the environment and sustainability, where a demonstration of an Easy Home as an example of sustainable and circular construction methods fits well. Here, in addition to demonstrating the technical quality of the concept, they want to show that setting up a well-functioning, local sustainable production chain for wooden houses is feasible and that one can build competitively compared to traditional construction concepts.Because sustainable forestry is still very limited in Kenya, sustainable certified wood from Uganda will be used for the time being.

title: DRRS Scoping Kenya 2025 – Remote Support 1
description: Isiolo County is facing a growing water crisis driven by increasing climate variability in Kenya’s arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs). The county experiences both prolonged droughts and recurrent flooding, which together strain water resources, livelihoods, and ecosystems. Extended dry periods have reduced flows in the Ewaso Ng’iro River, lowered groundwater levels, and degraded wetlands that support communities, livestock, and pastoralist livelihoods. Conversely, intense rainfall events trigger flash floods that erode riverbanks, damage water infrastructure, and disrupt settlements along the Lower Ewaso Ng’iro River. Flood risks are particularly acute in Merti, Gafarsa, Malka Daka, Iresaboru, Badana, and Sericho. These risks are exacerbated by the widespread invasion of Prosopis juliflora (Mathenge) in floodplains, which obstructs river channels, alters flow paths, and increases flood intensity during the rainy season while reducing water availability during dry periods. In addition, shifts in the river’s meandering channel have left some settlements without reliable and direct access to water in dry seasons.The objective of this short-term remote assignment (two working days) is to provide rapid analytical support to the Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction & Surge Support (DRRS) team in preparation for a one-week scoping deployment to Isiolo County, Kenya. The assignment will focus on a desk-based compilation and synthesis of key baseline information, drawing on readily available secondary data and geospatial datasets. The outputs will support an initial understanding of flood risk dynamics, water management considerations, and the prioritisation of field scoping activities during the in-country mission.

title: EnDev Adaptation Impact Assignment
description: The objective of this assignment is to assess and describe adaptation impact induced by EnDev interventions. The assignment would focus on four use-cases: 1) powering ventilation; 2) water pumping / irrigation; 3) powering communication; and 4) clean cooking. The assignment will include case studies in two EnDev countries that are highly vulnerable to climate change and where chances are high that measurable impact may be achieved through EnDev activities. In these countries and for these use-cases, the assignment aims at first describing the links between the activities and impacts and providing more detailed insights about the magnitude of EnDev’s contribution to adaptation to climate change of EnDev target groups. Furthermore, the assignment aims to investigate which indicators would be relevant to measure adaptation impact for these use-cases and related additional monitoring requirements. Thirdly, the assignment includes the identification of relevant partners in the climate adaptation-energy interconnection, at national and international level. Finally, the study aims to identify potential future supplementary measures of EnDev activities to augment adaptation impacts.

title: EnDev Innovation Window: Powering Resilient Agro-Pastoral Livelihoods: A Scalable Energy-as-a-Service Model for Kenya’s Arid and Semi-Arid Lands
description: ThriveAgric hypothesises that agro-pastoral systems, integrating resilient crop production with livestock, offer a viable pathway for livelihood stability in arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs) when supported by appropriate technologies. This project proposes a digitally enabled, end-to-end agricultural model powered by Productive Use of Energy (PUE) and delivered through an Energy-as a-Service (EaaS) framework. The aim is to enable pastoralist households to diversify into climate-resilient crops such as millet and sorghum, which are drought-tolerant, culturally accepted, and serve dual roles: as human food and as raw material for livestock feed. Solar-powered processing units will enable local value addition, including the production of high-energy livestock feed from crop residues, addressing seasonal feed scarcity and reducing reliance on commercial feed imports.

title: Sustainable and Secure Smallholder Systems @scale
description: This Public Private Partnership (PPP) aims to create opportunities for self-reliance and economic growth for smallholder coffee farmers in parts of Kenya and Uganda. Due to limited knowledge, limited land availability, climate change and lack of technology, the coffee production of smallholder coffee farmers is low and inefficient. Besides providing training and input materials to farmers, the project promotes and facilitates the use of Biodigesters to provide the farms with energy and better manure for the land. Hivos will be responsible for the overall project management in this PPP. Other partners include ECOM, SMS, Kawacom (all subsidiaries of Ecom) and Biogas Solutions Uganda Limited. These partners will be involved in the training, certification and other technical assistance. Ecom will also provide a credit facility for farmers to enable them to buy farming input materials and for buying biodigester. A joint learning platform will be established with Solidaridad, who has written a similar project proposal (FDOV12KE04).Both organisations have worked together on the project proposals to prevent overlap and will work together in the future to share accumulated knowledge and best practices.

title: Food for all Project in Kenya (F4APK)
description: Due to limited land availability and recurrent droughts as a result of climate change, about 75% of the inhabitants of the Eastern Kenya region are food insecure. The project wants to solve this problem by combining the production of bananas and vegetables with high-value agricultural products like milk and French beans. This project focusses on smallholder farmers since they are producing about 95% of the national volume of fruits and vegetables and many of them are located in the eastern region.Smallholder farmers lack access to quality inputs and storage and marketing opportunities. Within this project, cooling, processing and packaging facilities will be constructed. In order to increase the yields of all products, nurseries will be established and the farmers will be trained in climate-smart agriculture, livestock production practices and will be supported in obtaining certification. The certification is in order to guarantee the quality for export, but also for the local market. | The project aims to Improve the livelihoods and resilience of households, through improving access and availability of good food and livestock products, thereby reducing food and nutrition insecurity in Eastern region of Kenya. title: Study Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) Kenya
description: Climate change causes environmental problems and affects the development of the agricultural sector in Kenya. There is an urgent need to implement climate-smart solutions to help farmers adapt to a changing climate. The Netherlands can play an essential role in designing CSA plans for Kenya. The Netherlands, as an expert in the field of Smart Agriculture, can help in finding solutions for the growing climatic issues in Kenya. On the one hand, there is a need within the Kenyan agricultural sector to use climate-smart techniques to enhance climate resilience and food security and safety. On the other hand, there is a growing amount of techniques and knowledge available in the Netherlands which can provide solutions for this increasing climatic problem in Kenya. The Netherlands Embassy has proposed conducting a market study to connect the demand and supply sides. This study will investigate the business opportunities for Dutch initiatives and innovations focused on smart agriculture techniques in Kenya. It will also explore the current needs and demands of the Kenyan agricultural sector to adapt to climate change sustainably.

title: Holland Pavilion TVET conference
description: Practical skills at the Technical & Vocational Education and Training (TVET) level have increasingly become an investment climate issue because they provide an enabling environment for businesses. In the last survey conducted among the Netherlands Business Network in Kenya, lack of practical skills was one of the essential concerns in doing business in Kenya. In the Aid and Trade agenda, skills development is critical for Dutch investors wishing to establish their businesses in Kenya.To re-brand and promote the TVET sector in Kenya, the Permanent Working Group (PWG) is organizing “The Hands on the Future National TVET Conference & Kenya Skills Show” from 26th to 27th January 2017. The conference and show will focus on building upon the successes of the TVET sector in Kenya and strengthening collaboration across the ecosystem. The objectives of this conference are to:1.	Promote policy debate and dialogue on the threshold issues surrounding the implementation of reforms to the TVET sector in Kenya.2.	Strengthen collaborations among TVET partners and stakeholders in the public and private sectors.3.	Allow stakeholders from the public, private sector, development partners and other groups to showcase relevant best practices, services and innovations.4.	Improve the image and interest in TVET opportunities among students, youth and the general public.The show, which will be running parallel, will target students, out-of-school youth, parents, educators, and the general public to experience hands-on exhibits and interact with the training providers, employers, career counsellors and others to learn about the opportunities for gaining TVET skills for job readiness. In the Business Climate Strategy paper 2016, the Netherlands embassy proposes to participate in this conference to showcase what the Dutch government has been doing through Nuffic in skills development. That will also provide an opportunity for promoting the Dutch Brand through NL Branding. The Netherlands embassy would like to provide a “Holland Pavilion” where they will invite:•	some of the Dutch organizations and NGOs involved in the TVET sector•	some Dutch companies who can display practical skills like KIBO, Solinc, and BBrood to brainstorm more on this.•	the NICHE partners at the TVET level – SNV, the Kenya Water Institute (KEWI), Baraka Agric College, Bukura Agric College, Dairy Training Institute, CINOP, etc.•	Nuffic.

title: Agroforesty: Responsible Reforestation in Kenya
description: Agroforestry Project in Kenya: Addressing Deforestation and PovertyThe agroforestry project in Kenya addresses the widespread deforestation and land degradation in the country's arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL). These regions are particularly vulnerable to environmental degradation and have a high prevalence of poverty. The project aims to tackle the dual issues of environmental degradation and economic instability among local communities. The primary goal is to restore degraded landscapes while providing sustainable income-generating opportunities for local farmers and communities. By integrating reforestation with agroforestry practices, the project seeks to enhance biodiversity, improve soil health, ensure water conservation, and ultimately contribute to climate resilience and food security.This project employs a holistic approach that combines practical research on tree propagation, selection, and maintenance with innovative income-generating activities such as honey production, fish farming, and eco-tourism. By establishing demonstration projects and providing extensive training, the project empowers local communities with the knowledge and tools to adopt sustainable practices. By addressing both environmental and socio-economic challenges, this agroforestry project aims to create a sustainable model for reforestation that benefits both the ecosystem and the local communities in Kenya.

title: Breakthrough in solar energy manufacturing in East Africa
description: East Africa is a fast growing (import) market for solar energy applications and Kenya in particular is leading in this respect. However growth figures dropped over the last few years due to the particular composition of technological solutions and modules supplied and the segmentation of the consumer market. This project will contribute to the further local (and regional) development of this sector, by establishing the first production plant for high quality poly-crystalline PhotoVoltaic (PV) modules in East Africa. In addition, a low-voltage mini-Solar Home System (SHS) will be developed and introduced to the market at a revolutionary price. The project introduces high-tech laser and lamination production technology and expects to be a catalyst for further development of the solar chain. Laser technology is applied to convert rejected but reusable solar cells from European factories into mini-cells.Partners in this new venture are: applicant Ubbink B.V. from Doesburg, which is part of the Centrotec Group of companies, and local partner the Kenyan company Largo Investments Ltd in cooperation with its 100% subsidiary Chloride Exide Kenya Ltd. The project is highly innovative. There is no production of solar modules in East Africa yet; all systems are imported. The project involves a high element of technology transfer and training and will benefit urban and rural households. It is also expected to result in policy changes to arrive at a more favourable investment climate for local producers of solar energy applications, and a further deepening of the solar system producer and consumer market.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)Both partners have integrated CSR policies and an excellent reputation in this respect. As for the applicant, CSR in a wider context is – next to sound commercial interests – one of the drivers behind this project. The following aspects will be part of the project's CSR policy:•	Staff Code of Conduct, attractive salaries and sound labour standards.•	Health and safety policy (favourable package including basic medical insurance).•	Sound environmental standards, reduction of negative environmental impact.•	Human rights, anti-corruption, product quality and chain responsibility.Impact•	Employment and working conditionsDuring the project, 32 people will be employed of whom 5 are medium/higher staff. This will be respectively 48 and 9, two years after the pilot. Wages are considerably higher than the minimum for similar positions in the local manufacturing sector. Side benefits include training, lunches at work, performance related and annual bonuses, housing allowance, medical cost reimbursement, transport from home to work and a pension scheme. Working conditions are good with ample attention to occupational health and safety. The joint venture will develop a staff Code of Conduct in line with the existing Code of CEKL.•	Innovation/Transfer of knowledgeAll training related to the production process is new to the country. Modern technologies and production concepts will be introduced. The extensive training package foreseen in this project will importantly contribute to new knowledge and skills for employees across the organisation.•	Chain effectsThe establishment of a local production unit for high quality solar modules is expected to have a profound impact on this sector, both in terms of supply, but – equally important – by pushing the boundaries of the market much further. This is particularly true when the mini-SHS proves to be a success on the market and shall become in reach of new groups of consumers, who could otherwise not afford it. It is furthermore anticipated that the example of high quality local production by a professional partnership, backed by conducive fiscal government policies, will invite others to invest in the sector, thus crowding-in new players in the market and making it even more competitive and innovative. Parties benefiting in the long term are distributors/retailers, system integrators, end-users (households and small businesses, schools, hospitals who are off-grid) and local producers of components. The project expects to give structural work and income to minimal 3 sub-contractors or other suppliers of goods and services.•	EnvironmentThe project will have a positive impact on the environment as solar energy will, to an important extent, replace the use of batteries and kerosene. A limited Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) will be carried out prior to construction of the production facility. NEMA certification also includes environmental screening, next to an inventory of occupational health and safety risks.•	Position of womenThe percentage of women in almost all positions is expected to be 50% and possibly even higher at production level due to the required accuracy in this high tech environment. Women will get the same remuneration package as men for similar positions and are entitled to maternity leave.

title: Production and marketing of flower care products in the Kenyan floriculture industry
description: Kenya is the largest exporter of cut flowers to the European market. Proper post-harvest handling and treatment is a requirement to satisfy the demands of auctions, retailers and consumers. The use of products that retard deterioration and wilting of flowers directly after harvesting and during transport is essential. Besides, flower bunches and bouquets packed in Kenya need to be supplied with sachets of flower food that enhances the vase-life for consumers.The project will transfer its production and distribution/support activities for large clients in Kenya, presently served directly from Naarden in the Netherlands, to Nairobi Kenya. The production facility in Nairobi will be certified and comply with the international Chrysal Code of Practice for the manufacturing of flower care products (fluids and sachets). At the end of the pilot project the annual production will be 10,000 to 15,000 litres of liquid pre-treatment products and 50 to 60 million sachets (5 to 10 grams).Partners in the new venture are applicant Global Floral Technology Group B.V. based in Naarden, holding company of the Chrysal Group and the local partner Lachlan Kenya Ltd, a distributing agent for agricultural inputs for Kenya and East Africa.Partners will establish a joint venture private company named Flower Care Kenya Ltd.The project is innovative as there is no certified production facility in Kenya or East Africa, providing the range of products and advisory services as proposed in this project. The sector relies heavily on imports. The project involves much technology transfer and training. It will also contribute to a more competitive floriculture sector, due to cost-reduction in the supply of flower care products, and improved post-harvest management in the flower chain.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)Both partners have integrated CSR policies and so will the joint venture. The project will be in compliance with the Ethical Trade Initiative Base Code (ETI). In addition, special emphasis will be on environmental care at the production site and on environmentally sound production methods amongst its clients.Impact•	Employment and working conditionsDuring the project 24 people will be employed, of whom 8 are medium/higher staff. This will be respectively 36 and 17, two years after the pilot. Benefits for employees are: attractive and safe working conditions, above average salaries, overtime payments, lunch and basic medical insurance. Measures to safeguard sound occupational health and safety standards consist of protective clothing, industrial vacuum cleaners, exhaust hoods, climate control and ventilation, and special precautions for the storage and handling of hazardous chemicals. The project will comply with the ETI Base Code.•	Innovation/Transfer of knowledgeAll training related to production, warehousing and advisory services is new to the country. Modern technologies and concepts will be introduced across the organisation. The Chrysal Code of Practice and the ERP software will guarantee continuous quality control of production and sales. The extensive training package foreseen in this project contributes to new knowledge and skills for employees across the organisation.•	Chain effectsAt sector level, this project will contribute to an internationally competitive floriculture sector in Kenya. Besides the project will source products and services from local companies, such as part of the raw materials (chemicals), packing material, clichés. Work will be outsourced to service providers in ICT, maintenance and repair, legal and administrative services.•	EnvironmentThe production facility will have environmental protection measures equivalent to those at the production facility in Baarn. The products themselves are subjected to strict pesticide and biocidal regulatory rules, including labelling and user-instructions, guaranteeing safety for the user and the environment. Production of flower care products and advisory services near the market will lead to reduction of wastage of cut flowers up to 10% from grower to vase.•	Position of womenFlower Care Kenya will be an equal opportunity employer. Female employment is expected to be circa 25% of total staff with opportunities, especially in the administration and extension sections.

title: H2ollandwater for sustainable irrigation dosing units in Kenya
description: Note: This project has been cancelled, because the applicant has requested to prematurely terminate the project.The Kenya floriculture and horticulture sectors are amongst the most important agribusiness sectors in the country in terms of domestic employment and income generation. The sectors are characterised by relatively high capital investments in irrigation, both in greenhouses for the production of flowers and increasingly also in open fields for vegetable production for export markets.Over the last few years it has become abundantly clear that the long term sustainability of these production systems, to an important extent depends on the optimisation of water use. Not only as a result of environmental concerns in Kenya and in consumer markets abroad, but also for reasons of cost efficiency and quality of production. This project will address these concerns by setting up a local assembling and distribution facility for high-end market dosing units and related equipment (e.g. UV systems).The project's innovation is pegged on the introduction of cyclone technology and the local manufacturing of dosing units. In addition, through cooperation with Hoogendoorn B.V. as a technical partner the project will be able to design and advise upon more integrated technology packages that combine water management, climate control technologies and production advice.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)CSR themes that will get high priority in the project are: employment policy, labour standards, occupational health and safety, environment and sustainable food production, chain responsibility and corruption.Impact•	Employment and working conditionsDuring the project 28 staff will be employed (eleven are women).All employees will earn slightly above the wage level for similar positions elsewhere in the sector. They are also entitled to secondary benefits like pension fund, vacation leave, overtime payment, etc. Safety at work will be guaranteed by sound working conditions and protective clothing.•	Innovation / Transfer of knowledgeAlthough most of the training will be on-the-job, it is expected that know-ledge transfer will be high, the local assembling of dosing units will involve special skills. The project's products and the suppliers of parts are all operating in the higher segment of the market.  •	Chain effectsThe project will use a good number of suppliers of local materials and components. On the demand side the impact of the project on the sector is expected to be significant, as it introduces more sustainable irrigation and water management technologies into the market.•	EnvironmentThe project is by design geared towards more sustainable water management, reduction of fertiliser use and higher production levels per hectare.

description: The Merti Integrated Development Programme (MID-P) plans to set up and implement an RtF project – Community Led Actions On Resilience And Climate Change Adaptation (CLEAR) – in Lower stream of Ewaso Ngiro River.The CLEAR project will be implemented in 16 locations in Isiolo County, Kenya. title: Developing a low-carbon coffee value-chain in Kenya
description: Moyee Coffee, The Fairchain Foundation, Agriterra, Kipkelion District Cooperative Union (KDCU) and Kenya Agriculture Livestock and Research Organization (KALRO) have formed a consortium to develop a low-carbon coffee value-chain in Kericho, Kenya.This project consists of four main elements to support 7,200 smallholder farmers to transition from a traditional coffee farming model, consisting of mainly mono-culture coffee and the application of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides, to a low-carbon farm model.1.	Developing a bio-solutions production facility at KDCU, producing bio-compost, bio-fertilisers and bio-pesticides produced from local waste materials, to be sold as an affordable alternative to synthetic fertilisers and pesticides.2.	Implementing a Model Farm for a Regenerative Low-Carbon Coffee growing Strategy, developed by Renature.3.	Establishing a blockchain platform on which all coffee-related transactions, such as quantities of coffee bought, prices but also results from soil testing, are made transparent and available, proving low-carbon practices and higher incomes, and giving farmers access to financial services.4.	Developing a coffee roasting facility at origin in Nairobi.This should lead to: improving farmer income, improved food security and improved resilience against climate-change related shocks for 7,200 smallholder farmers in Kericho, Kenya.How will this consortium improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers in the Kericho region?•	Ban the use of fertilisers, limit the use of pesticides, farmers will get a premium based on soil samples.•	Support the cooperatives by improving their governance and financial management structures.•	Set up local bio-solutions production facility to increase the use of affordable bio-compost, bio-fertiliser and bio-pesticides to improve the soil-health and increase productivity.•	Support the implementation and roll-out of a comprehensive intercropping strategy for farmers.•	Support the hiring of Youth Extension Officers dedicated to sustainable agriculture and low-carbon farming.•	Buy coffee at a premium and decrease delivery-payment term from six months to four weeks.•	Roasting at Origin: Set up a local roasting facility in Kenya to create local job-opportunities and support structural transformation of Kenya.•	Create a transparent value-chain through Fairchain’s blockchain application.•	Actively involve women and youth in the development of this low-carbon coffee value chain.

title: SPVO – Women economic resilience in times of climate crisis
description: Kenya’s floriculture sector is a major contributor to the national economy, driving the gross domestic product (GDP) growth, exports, and employment. Women make up about 80% of its workforce, yet they remain highly vulnerable – facing low wages, insecure contracts, gender-based violence, and limited decision-making power. Climate-related crises such as floods and droughts compound these risks, disrupting food security and increasing living costs. The floods of March 2024 in Kenya highlighted critical gaps in gender-sensitive climate adaptation, crisis preparedness, and social safety nets. Despite ongoing sustainability efforts, the absence of living wages and inclusive response systems continues to leave women disproportionately exposed to economic and social shocks.The "Women’s Economic Resilience in Times of Climate Crisis" project, funded by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) under the SPVO/SSF programme (SPVO25S001), aims to address these challenges. In Phase A (June-December 2025), Women Win, Bloomon, Sian Flowers, and CIFCAD will carry out an in-depth local impact assessment and due diligence analysis. Using surveys, interviews, and participatory tools such as Drawing the Line, the project will examine how climate crises affect women workers' working conditions, wages, health, and safety, and identify adaptive strategies to strengthen their long-term resilience.The project will directly benefit more than 1,200 women employed across Sian Flowers' farms in Kenya. Additional beneficiaries include Sian male workers as allies, Sian Flowers, Bloomon, and sector stakeholders such as the Kenya Flower Council, who will gain from improved due diligence practices and shared learnings.By December 2025, the project will deliver a stakeholder-validated action plan with concrete measures to reduce identified social risks. Ultimately, this project aims to enhance women’s economic resilience, advance gender-responsive policies such as fair wages and safer working conditions, and embed social sustainability into climate resilience strategies, creating a more resilient floriculture value chain.
