title: Inclusive Refugee Response Programme (2023-2026)
description:
The objective for this specific programme is to enhance self-reliance, resilience, and long-term stability for refugees and host communities in especially Turkana County by supporting Kenya’s national and locally led development efforts to improve access to inclusive basic social services, thereby contributing to a reduction in inequality and poverty.

Overall, the Programme is organised in three thematic focus areas implemented through three different projects. The Programme is part of an alliance partnering with LEGO Foundation, Novo Nordisk Foundation and Poul Due Jensen/Grundfos Foundation working towards the same overall vision of enhancing inclusive refugee responses.  

The thematic focus areas are supported primarily through assistance to the specific area within health, education, water, self-reliance and resilience building. The projects are interlinked and contribute to the programme objective by addressing different aspects such a capacity development, services delivery, and resilience and self-reliance building.

title: Mobile payment systems to reduce rural water risks in Africa
description: This research project aims to improved handpump management by insuring payment risks. Like insurance products that pool risk of unanticipated but costly events, like a car break-down, flood damage to homes or a serious health problem, we proposed to apply the same approach to community handpumps in rural Kenya. Currently rural communities must work independently saving and paying for maintenance on a case by case basis. This is fine until an unexpected but costly repair emerges. Then the communities, which include a majority of households with low and variable income, simply can't pay to have their handpump repaired. They then turn to more distant, often dirty and costly water sources. Our approach brings these communities together in a shared financial model that reduces costs by sharing them amongst hundreds of handpumps. Earlier research suggests the majority of communities will pay into this 'insurance system' on a regular basis provided the handpumps are repaired in a couple of days. The project can guarantee this higher maintenance service which has reduced repair times from over a month to a couple of days. The communities love it the current trial of the maintenance service and now want to pay for this service through a local company to make it sustainable. This next phase of research is to introduce a fair payment system and monitor how communities pay over time. This will provide evidence for a more sustainable approach which the Government of Kenya supports and can be scaled up by our regional partner, UNICEF. | Research and development activity contributing to the UK’s strategy to address key development challenges.

title: Safe Water and Hygiene Promotion for Children of Kayole Slum
description: Access to safe, adequate and affordable water is a real challenge for people living in slums. Privately-owned boreholes can be an important supply of water but their regulation is not enforced. Recent research has found the quality of water at boreholes in three of Nairobi’s slums to be dangerously poor, containing high levels of harmful bacteria and e-coli. Also that good hygiene practice is uncommon. As a result, local people suffer, and can even die from, diseases such as typhoid fever, diarrhoea and cholera. This project aims to promote safe drinking water and encourage a more sustainable approach to water provision and hygiene. Rather than building new boreholes, the project will make existing boreholes more efficient, cost-effective and safer. Training will be provided so that facilities can be maintained. There will also be hygiene promotion in schools and the community. As a result, people in the slums will be able to source clean water more cheaply and there will be a reduction in water-related diseases contributing to better health and school attendance.

title: SHAPE 2 - Social Housing Advancement and Poverty Eradication
description: More than 60% of Kenya's urban population lives in slums, which are expected to double in size in 15 years. Slum dwellers generally do not have title to the land they occupy, and have limited access to clean water or useable toilets, or credit facilities. Without a collective voice, people living in the slums do not possess the ability to engage with the relevant authorities to change this situation. This project seeks to address some of these problems and will benefit tens of thousands of slum dwellers in 18 slums across Kenya.  It will promote community savings and make affordable loans more widely available – for both housing and small businesses. People living in the slums will learn about low-cost building technologies and improved water and sanitation facilities.  Formation of community groups will enable them to participate in urban planning and achieve better services for their communities. As a result, people will have better housing, sanitation and improved economic prospects and local government will be more responsive to the collective voice of slum dwellers.

title: Dialogue on “Research to support Africa’s agricultural transformation”
description:
In 2013, Canada’s International Development Research Centre and the Australian Centre for International Agriculture Research (ACIAR) launched the four-year, $15 million Cultivate Africa’s Future Fund (CultiAf). The fund was designed to support collaborative, results-driven and innovative research to address issues of post-harvest loss, nutrition, and water use. To date, five large applied projects and three cross-cutting projects have been funded in Zambia, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Kenya, and Uganda. These projects, due to be completed in March 2017, have generated innovations, models, and practices that are reducing post-harvest loss, increasing productivity, improving nutrition, building youth-led enterprises, and expanding public-private partnerships and communications technologies for achieving impact at scale.  

A strategic objective of CultiAf is to use results from the research to inform agriculture and food security policies and programs in the region. Events such as the 2016 African Green Revolution Forum, organized by the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa and hosted by the Government of Kenya in Nairobi, provide an opportunity to bring the projects together and engage more than 1200 policymakers, researchers, business leaders, farmer organizations and other stakeholders, including civil society and the private sector, on key results and lessons emerging from the program. 

The “Research to support Africa’s agricultural transformation” dialogue will facilitate the participation of key ACIAR staff, government representatives, heads of institutions, policymakers, and other donors and eminent persons engaged in agriculture and food security in the region. Participants will discuss the results and solutions to reduce post-harvest loss and improve nutrition, ensure research leads to development outcomes, and share experiences and resources to take innovations to scale. The general objective is to convene a dialogue to disseminate innovations from agriculture research with the potential to contribute to African agricultural transformation. 

The dialogue and related events provide a strategic opportunity to raise IDRC's visibility and position CultiAf as a strategic program for promoting agricultural growth and nutrition security in the African context. IDRC is organizing the dialogue in collaboration with ACIAR.  

This project is funded through the Cultivate Africa’s Future Fund (CultiAF), a joint program of the Australian International Food Security Research Centre of the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research and IDRC. CultiAF supports research to achieve long-term food security in Eastern and Southern Africa. | Le Fonds Cultivons l’avenir de l’Afrique (CultivAf) a été conçu pour soutenir des travaux de recherche collaboratifs, axés sur les résultats et novateurs sur les pertes après récolte, la nutrition et l’utilisation de l’eau. Cinq importants projets de recherche appliquée et trois projets transversaux ont déjà été financés en Zambie, au Malawi, au Zimbabwe, au Kenya et en Ouganda. Ces projets, dont l’achèvement est prévu en mars 2017, ont produit des innovations, modèles et pratiques qui réduisent les pertes après récolte, améliorent la nutrition, favorisent des entreprises dirigées par des jeunes et élargissent les partenariats public­privé et les technologies de communication afin d’accroître l’impact à plus grande échelle. 

L’un des objectifs stratégiques de CultivAf est d’utiliser les résultats pour éclairer les politiques et programmes sur l’agriculture et la sécurité alimentaire. Des événements tels que le Forum sur la révolution verte en Afrique sont l’occasion de réunir les projets et de mobiliser plus de 1 200 responsables des politiques, chercheurs, chefs d’entreprise, organisations d’agriculteurs et autres parties prenantes autour des résultats clés. 
Le dialogue sur la « Recherche pour soutenir la transformation de l’agriculture en Afrique » facilitera la participation d’employés de l’ACIAR, de représentants gouvernementaux, de dirigeants d’établissements, de responsables des politiques, de bailleurs de fonds et d’éminentes personnes soucieuses de l’agriculture et de la sécurité alimentaire. Les participants discuteront des résultats et des solutions visant à réduire les pertes après récolte et améliorer la nutrition, veilleront à ce que les travaux stimulent des résultats de développement et mettront en commun leurs expériences et ressources afin de diffuser les innovations à grande échelle. L’objectif général est de tenir un dialogue qui permettra de communiquer les innovations issues de la recherche sur l’agriculture pouvant contribuer à la transformation de l’agriculture en Afrique. 

Le dialogue et les événements connexes permettront de rehausser l’image du CRDI et de présenter CultivAf en tant que programme stratégique de promotion de la croissance de l’agriculture et de la sécurité alimentaire dans le contexte africain. 
Le projet est financé par le fonds Cultiver l’avenir de l’Afrique (CultivAf), un programme conjoint de l’Australian International Food Security Research Centre, qui est une composante de l’Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research et du CRDI. CultivAf finance des travaux afin d’atteindre la sécurité alimentaire à long terme en Afrique de l’Est et en Afrique australe.

title: Inclusive Growth Through Decent Work in the Great Rift Valley
description: The private company Akiira Geothermal Ltd is establishing a power plant near Naivasha, Kenya. The plant energy output will be a substantial benefit to Kenya’s growing economy. For the neighbouring pastoral communities to also benefit, conscious and pro-active measures will need to be taken to enable them to have a share of the benefits of the economic growth. Akiira Geothermal Ltd is determined that the investment will have a positive impact on the adjacent communities in terms of local content and job creation during the construction and operational phases, despite the lack of locally available skills. To this end, Akiira will use part of its revenues to support community engagement, skills development and job creation in the immediate communities surrounding the geothermal plant in response to the challenges experienced in the region – in addition to in-kind contributions. The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) offered to provide the loan guarantee as a support of generation of sustainable and renewable energy. In addition, the embassy has entered into a Public Private Development Partnership (PPDP) with the International Labour Organization (ILO) as the coordinator of this partnership. At the same time, the ILO will be entering into an agreement with ForumSyd, a Swedish Non-Governmental Organization with experience working with communities in and around Naivasha, for implementation of one of the expected outcomes. Overall, the PPDP will aim at improving the living conditions in and around the project areas, i.e. Narok and Nakuru counties, by acting as a catalyst to boost decent job creation through business development, skills development and community engagement. It is foreseen that this partnership can become a model for replication to achieve inclusive growth in the extractive industries and other industries in Kenya and beyond. The immediate objectives of the PPDP are to create decent jobs from better skills by vocational training centers; develop new and improve on growing businesses resulting from new relevant skills, business development services and access to finance, promoting the rights of workers in the local communities and increase capacity of communities to lobby for increased access to public and social services e.g. water, education, health, sanitation. While Akiira Geothermal Ltd and the Swedish Embassy agreed to jointly invest in a Public Private Development Partnership to address development challenges near the power plant, the Kenyan public partners’ involvement and commitment is vital for ownership and replication potential. As such, the total budget for the PPDP includes both the partners’ financial and non-financial contributions e.g. with time and resources.

title: PHC/CBHC/HIV/AIDS Programme
description:
The Diocesan Health and HIV and AIDS programme aims to improve the capacity of local community to enhance greater participation in health matters affecting them.  The purpose is to improve delivery of quality, affordable and accessible health care services, through community capacity building initiatives. The programme will contribute through offering complementary services in the remote areas where the Catholic Church has set up health facilities and outreaches covered by the parishes. The programme will continue to provide basic health care services. The health units provide minimum/basic health care packages for most common ailments in the catchment area.
During this implementation period, will undertake a baseline survey to provide benchmark data that will be useful in establishing the factual changes resulting from programme activities; mobilise and create awareness on the importance of home and personal hygiene, environmental management, local water treatment methods, nutrition, poor sanitation and its negative effect, gender issues, and rights of different community groups etc. 

The programme will address preventive aspect which will address cultural practices that promote liberal sexual relationship. Preventive measures will also include establishment of VCT centres, training of staff and community. Care and mitigation aspects will target the PLWHAs and the affected. Additionally, it will link and collaborate with the Diocesan Justice and Peace program and will be involved in lobbying and advocacy with and/on behalf of the PLWHAs, OVCs and the affected pastoralists. Key to the programme is internal integration, linkages and networking in order to create more synergy and efficiency in implementing diocesan programmes. Linkages with other development organisations will provide opportunity for sharing experiences and efficiently allocate resources among the organisations in the most needy localities and sectors. Networking and attending joint forums will provide opportunity to the programme to share the challenges experienced by the pastoralist groups, for national and international support. The programme will also provide an opportunity for documentation and dissemination of achievements with tangible impact to potential donors and other members of the public. 
The programme puts more emphasis on the needs of vulnerable groups such as women (including the girl child) and children, taking into account special needs of youth, orphans and vulnerable children, people living with HIV and AIDS, malnourished adults and children. The immunisation program will target a total of 2,000 children under five, 1,000 antenatal mothers, the curative services target 7,000 sick men and women. The trainings will target 160 adults, 300 youth, 80 couples and general health education targets 7,000 people.

title: Integrated AIDS Programme, Thika
description:

It does this through community sensitisation on HIV prevention and on strategies of coping with the effects of HIV and AIDS through awareness campaigns, HIV Testing and Counselling (HTC) services, Education For Life (EFL) activities, care and support for infected and affected persons. In addition, the project focuses on the needs of Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVCs), through provision of school fees and other education support; apprenticeships and training on improved farming methods; promotion of income-generating activities; monitoring and supervision, and capacity-building. 

IAP plans to empower the community in better farming methods, economic sustainability and wealth creation strategies which will equip the community with the capacity to improve their skills on soil and water conservation and planting of drought resistant crops. These strategies will ensure that households in the community have sustainable food supply. The programme will also engage the community into poverty reduction through micro finance and agri-business as a way of promoting asset acquisition for the households, increased income and sustainable financial stability.

title: Mutomo Integrated Sustainable Livelihoods Project
description:
CAFOD started funding Community for Environment forand Development (CED) in June 2007 to implement a food security project in Kenya.  The project is situated in Ikanga location of Mutomo district – in the sub-locations of Nduundune, Kiangwa, and Makele. A total of 450 households were selected to form 29 farmer field schools (FFS). The FFS groups were facilitated to identify Natural Resource Management needs in their localities and to work on their private lands and also public land to improve soil and water management, water conservation structures and stabilizing structures.

CED also aims to support the farmers in crop production and livestock production including provision of drought tolerant seeds such as cow peas, pigeon peas and beans and fruit tree seedlings of mango and avocado. The project also provides Galla goats.

In 2008, the project also supported community water projects including scooping of identified shallow wells. Connecting water to a homestead of an HIV/AIDS support group enabled the group to water their tree nurseries and Aloe Vera plants used for medicinal purpose.

title: Kajiado Pastoralists' Livelihoods and Food Security Improvement Project
description:
The pastoralist communities in Torosei and Ewuaso locations of Kajiado districts face high levels of poverty and food insecurity due to frequent and severe droughts and high levels of illiteracy in the community and therefore limited employment opportunities for earning income. Prolonged dry seasons and droughts result in acute water shortages for both humans and livestock, shortage or lack of pasture and low livestock prices due to poor livestock body conditions and to livestock losses and subsequently to food insecurity. As a result of prolonged droughts and water shortages, livestock have to trek for more than 20 kilometres one way to water sources, forcing herders to water their livestock every third or fourth day instead of daily. Women also spend a lot of hours fetching water. The communities rely on relief food during drought periods. 

The project's long term /strategic goal is to achieve sustainable livelihoods and improved food security among poor pastoralists of Torosei and Ewuaso Kedong locations in Kajiado District. The project components are geared towards disaster risk reduction, improved food security and increased household incomes. The project components include:  
+ Improved water resources management
+ Range land and pasture management through hay conservation and beekeeping
+ Improved livestock husbandry: restocking, animal health, breed improvement.
+ Income generating activities: small businesses, beekeeping for honey production and buying, fattening and selling of steers.

title: Post election violence - Mombasa
description:
The aftermath of the General Elections in Kenya on December 27th 2007 has been one of the most turbulent periods in post-independence Kenya. In particular the period just after the chaotic announcement of the winner of the election was one of intense violence in numerous parts of the country. Civilians have been beaten, homes burnt down, businesses destroyed and men, women and children killed. The Kenya Red Cross has reported that more than 500 people have been killed, and according to recent official figures released by the Government of Kenya (Jan 6th), there is officially an estimated 255,000 internally displaced people (IDPs) as a result of this violence.

A number of towns have been temporarily cut off and many major roads barricaded by various communities denying access to road users. This has affected the delivery of essential supplies to key markets and local communities. Among the most affected towns and cities are Kisumu, Eldoret, Nairobi, Nakuru, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Mombasa, Kitale and Lugari. Most of the displaced groups have been camping at police stations, district administration camps, prison compounds, church compounds, local showgrounds and other public places where they feel some security and protection is available. People in these areas are homeless as they seek security in neighbouring districts and are in desperate need of shelter, food, water, medicine, personal hygiene items and clothing items particularly for children.

Alongside national government efforts to provide relief assistance, CAFOD is responding to this situation in the slums of Nairobi with food distributions, in Eldoret and Bungoma with food and non food items and in Kericho with non food items. CAFOD is also making efforts to reach some of the displaced groups in Mombasa at the Kenyan coast where it is estimated that over 3000 people have been displaced and 10 have so far died. This request to Jersey is for support to CAFOD’s response in Mombasa, in continued partnership with the Archdiocese of Mombasa, to reach 760 people (120 men, 217 females and 423 children) who have been camping in five Catholic Parishes compounds (Likoni, Cathedral, Bomu, Mikindani and Changamwe). 

The Archdiocese of Mombasa has been providing direct assistance to these displaced people since they arrived in the parishes but are now running out of their existing resources. Shelter has been provided using existing parish facilities including meeting halls. They have also provided food such as maizemeal, rice, porridge and beans, as well as water from their existing supplies. Some additional food was provided by the Kenya Red Cross though supplies have run low. Each parish has sought to provide some basic medicines for minor ailments and refer individuals to local clinics where those services have been available. The parishes have, however, been unable to meet the growing needs of these groups and are in need of additional supplies of both food and non-food items. The Archdiocese has therefore requested support from CAFOD help reach out to these people.

title: Integrated Community Development programme (ICDP)
description:
Integrated Community Development Programme (ICDP) is an initiative of the Diocese of Marsabit resulting from consultative programme development processes that the Diocese engaged in during the last half of the year 2007. The programme focuses on justice and peace and sustainable livelihoods issues within the diocese. 

This is  a second cycle grant for  ICDP that is based on the recognition of the increasing intensity and frequency of drought and conflict in Northern Kenya. Reduced recovery periods between droughts and increased conflict that are breaking down existing coping strategies and increasing vulnerable households’ need to depend on external interventions.   Assessments conducted in affected areas in the last few months of 2010, revealed that pastoral communities have been particularly badly affected by repeated cycles of conflict and drought. The regular loss of livestock, inadequate recovery periods, poor governance, shortage of pasture and water have undermined traditional coping mechanisms and increased conflict over natural resources. Repeated humanitarian interventions have done little to strengthen affected communities’ capacity to cope with drought. An external evaluation was done for the ICDP in October 2010 with  recommendations  that  indentified gaps during the evaluation also formed the basis of this project.

title: Diocese of Maralal - Vehicle support
description:
The Catholic Diocese of Maralal covers  the entire Samburu District's administrative boundaries. Samburu District is ranked among the poorest districts in Kenya. It is affected by unpredictable climatic conditions that results in prolonged droughts.Contributing to the rising levels of poverty are the inter-ethnic cattle raids and conflicts related to access to natural resources such as land and pasture. 
The Diocese has four development programmes; pastoral, human promotion, human health and justice and peace that mainly rely on one off funding and individual donations made to the Diocese. 

The project aims to work on improving food security among pastoralist communities in Samburu district through improving access to water for livestock and domestic use, through enhancing livestock production and marketing and mainstreaming HIV/AIDS and gender.

title: Isiolo Humanitarian Assistance Project
description:
This project will expand on the current humanitarian response work undertaken by the Diocese’s Development Office and build on the ongoing response work that has been going on since December 2008 . This component is an attempt to contribute to the alleviation of the suffering as a result of the escalation of the drought situation in Northern Kenya and particularly in Isiolo District. The additional activities is in response to the continuing deterioration of the drought situation and food security situation in Northern Kenya and also an attempt to respond to the appeal by the Government of Kenya (GoK) following the declaration of the drought and food crisis a national disaster on 16th January 2009. This project component will reach an additional 400 direct beneficiaries benefiting from the “take home ration” from the previous number of 800 children  and thus totalling 1200children benefiting from the “take home ration”. Additionally, the Diocese of Isiolo will target an additional 10,000 more people in its health facilities for treatment of common drought diseases. Already, an appeal has been made to contain an outbreak of black fever in Merti and Sericho Divisions. CAFOD is increasing it s support in health care provision to correspond to the improved staff capacity of the Diocese to arrest this additional threats to the lives of the communities in Isiolo who will now benefit either directly or indirectly from improved access to essential medical assistance from clinics run by the Diocese with mobile outreach clinics, 

By working more closely with the Arid Land resource Ministry, The Diocese  will help to increase and improved access to safe water through water trucking through the provision of diesel fuel to support the Government of Kenya (GoK) carry out water tankering operations in locations hardest hit by drought.  These activities will be undertaken concurrently with the ongoing drought and food crisis response programme
participating_orgs: Catholic Agency For Overseas Development (CAFOD) / GB-CHC-285776 / 1 | Catholic Diocese of Isiolo / 4

title: Maralal Diocese Drought Assistance Project
description:
This is a 3 month emergency programme that aims to provide immediate life saving support to affected pastoral and agro pastoral households in Maralal District.  The project will prevent people from having to sell essential assets to buy extra food and drugs. The project will primarily be implemented in 4 villages of Ngilai, Bendera, Logetei and Nachola in Baragoi division. The project will be linked with a two year DRR programme whose purpose will be to build the resilience of the local communities to future droughts and related hazards.

These areas are inhabited by the Turkana, Samburu and Pokot pastoralists groups who have raided each other for years creating tensions and displacements that have never healed with time. Recurrent cattle raiding between these communities has left the communities living in fear and destituted and chronically reliant on food. The Project is based on preliminary proposals submitted to CAFOD by The Diocese of Maralal Development office to protect the most vulnerable people. The project aims to support complement and strengthen the ongoing livelihoods and Disaster Risk Reduction work already underway in the affected pastoral and agro-pastoral zones. This proposal entails providing support in the following areas; 

•	Provision of emergency water systems to communities affected by drought and without any form of water supplies to survive on.
•	Provision of take home food rations for children leaving the supplementary feeding programmes.	
The project aims to provide direct support to an estimated 1,500 people who will receive a food ration plus 3000 people will benefits from emergency water supplies over a 3 month period. Indirectly, the population to benefit is estimated at 8,432 people.
participating_orgs: Catholic Agency For Overseas Development (CAFOD) / GB-CHC-285776 / 1 | Diocese of Maralal / 4

title: Diocese of Isiolo Sustainable Livelihoods Programme
description:
The Catholic Diocese of Isiolo covers the entire area of Isiolo and Garbatulla districts and implements sustainable community development projects to help communities access essential services and reduce poverty. Over the last few decades, the Diocese through it's development office implemented integrated community development activities in micro-enterprise development, water and sanitation, agriculture and livestock development, education, community awareness and advocacy, human health and nutrition and disaster risk reduction.

As the number of disasters is on the rise, livelihoods especially in the arid and semi-arid areas have been adversely affected.  Having just emerged from a drought period resulting from failure of six rain seasons, the food security and livelihood situation of majority of the people in the region has become fragile.  This is compounded by outbreak of diseases such as cholera which claimed many lives in 2009.  Malnutrition cases have also been on the increase. According to the Famine Early Warning System information, the larger Isiolo District will continue facing food insecurity. 

There is need to develop and implement interventions that target not only the re-establishment of livelihoods but also measures that can reduce the impact of natural disasters such as drought on communities that have fragile livelihoods. CAFOD is funding livelihoods and disaster risk reduction projects in the Diocese. These projects complement each other.

The Sustainable Livelihoods project will be implemented in three divisions; namely Oldonyiro, Central and Sericho. A decision to implement livelihood activities in these divisions was arrived at through a process of needs assessment involving community opinion leaders. Needier locations and sub-locations such as Kipsing and Modogashe have been identified. Communities in these locations and sub-locations identified their needs as capacity building for community groups, improvement in animal and agricultural production, water and sanitation and access to financial services. The project will work with women and youth groups.  The rationale behind this is that women are the ones who are affected most due to lack of water and the need to put food on the table.  This will include women headed households.  Youth groups will be targeted for support in economic activities as they are most affected by unemployment. Keen interest will be given to ensure persons living with HIV/AIDS as well as other special groups like the physically handicapped are involved in the project. 

The project will target 4000 direct beneficiaries with 60% being women and 40% men and youth constituting 50%of the total number of beneficiaries.  With this coverage the multiplier effect is expected to reach a total population of 10,000.
participating_orgs: Catholic Agency For Overseas Development (CAFOD) / GB-CHC-285776 / 1 | Catholic Diocese of Isiolo / 4

description: The overall Drought and Food Crisis in Horn and East Africa is seeking to alleviate suffering among the population hardest hit by the current drought in Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia and Uganda. It will improve access to emergency food relief, safe water and sanitation facilities, fodder and water for livestock. With this extensive response, there is need to enhance partners’ capacity and make them more able to respond to the current food crisis arises.

title: Mutomo Integrated Sustainable Livelihoods Project
description:
The project aims to improve the food security of up to 450 farming households in Mutomo. Mutomo district is an ASAL district in Eastern Province. Specifically, participating farmers are located in Makele, Nduudune and Kianga sub-locations, Ikanga location, Ikanga division, Mutomo. 

The main project activities are:
1. promotion of high value drought tolerant crop species and varieties through crop production.
2. Agro-forestry by introducing tree planting and fruit tree nurseries as an income generating activity and the creation of awareness on climatic changes.
3. Promotion and/or multiplication of gala goats.
4. Enhancement of natural resource management through soil and water conservation by construction of soil structures using a catchments approach.

title: Amaiya Cholera Outbreak Rapid Reponse Project
description:
This project is a rapid response to a cholera outbreak in Amaiya Village in Samburu district which has as of 24th June 2010 claimed 14 lives and left more than 600 others hospitalized. As the situation prevails, with virtually no response from the Kenya Government and other international organizations, the outbreak has continued to spread and is now threatening to affect an increasing number of people not only in Samburu but other neighbouring district of Pokot and Baringo. 

Despite repeated press coverage, the crisis has failed to grab the attention of the Government and other aid agencies present on the ground.  CAFOD has been partnering with the Diocese of Maralal to respond to a drought that has been prevailing in the area prior to the current crisis and has now approached CAFOD to support with funding and technical support to conduct a rapid assessment and respond to the crisis.

CAFOD has already carried out preliminary appraisal of the situation through its Regional Humanitarian Coordinator and the Emergency Response Officer for the Horn and East Africa region who visited Maralal between the 18-24th of June 2010. The preliminary appraisal shows an urgent need to provide immediate assistance targeting.

At this stage, CAFOD and the Diocese of Maralal are looking at realizing the Goal of halting the spread of Cholera and safeguarding the population or Amaiya and Surrounding areas.  This will entail the twin objectives of;

a)	Case management and treatment of cholera affected people. 

b)	Protecting  vulnerable and at risk populations from public health risks associated with poor water and sanitation 

The key outcomes from this project are defined as;

c)	Cholera outbreak in Amaiya contained.
d)	
e)	Knowledge and awareness on cholera prevention amongst at risk and vulnerable population increased to over 75% of the target population.

f)	Over 75% of the at risk an vulnerable population in Amaiya using  safe water and sanitation facilities

These two objectives would be realised through both immediate short term as well as intermediate interventions lasting between 2- 12 weeks.



Immediate interventions (2-4 weeks duration) will include;
i)	Procurement and provision of essential drugs and supplies to Diocesan clinics to treat and manage the spread of Cholera.
ii)	Conduct weekly mobile clinics for disease surveillance case management in outlying areas.
iii)	Emergency Household water supplies chlorination through provision of chlorine tablets. 
iv)	Conduct hygiene education and awareness campaigns to raise public awareness on prevention and control of Cholera;

Intermediate interventions 4-12 weeks will include;
i)	Rehabilitation, construction and development of safe water supplies. 
ii)	Conduct hygiene education and awareness campaigns to raise public awareness on prevention and control of Cholera.

The project will be implemented through the Development office of the Diocese of Maralal and CAFOD will provide monitoring and technical support. The Diocese of Maralal Development Office will liaise with the Ministry of Health, WHO, UNICEF and other INGOs present in the area when carrying out this project to ensure coordination and coherence in approach. CAFOD will be monitoring and providing situation updates on the project on fortnightly for the first 4 weeks and then every month the remainder of the project.

title: Kitui Food Security Project: Mitigating Impact of Economic downturn
description:
This project falls within the DFID funded Food Security Project which aims to mitigate the impact of economic downturn for poor and marginalised people in Kenya and Zimabwe through supporting interventions that increase agricultural production and access to food.  Kenya has been selected because the economic downturn and recurrent droughts has resulted in increasing cost of agricultural inputs and food stuffs which has in turn exacerbated an already fragile food security situation. In Kenya, the project will be implemented by two of CAFOD’s partners, the Diocese of Isiolo and Diocese of Kitui. 

In Kitui, this additional funding will expand on and complement ongoing work under the East Africa Sustainable Livelihoods and DRR programme. This project will therefore support farmers in Kitui Diocese through voucher for work interventions to construct soil and water conservation structures on their farms and also through construction of metal silos for use by communities for grain storage. It is hoped that this will increase agricultural productivity, improve post harvest management and availability of food during the drought period. The voucher for work intervention will also enable farmers to earn money which they can use on their priority needs including agricultural inputs. Local communities will be mobilized to engage in these activities.

As the current programmes are funded directly by CAFOD, specific activities have been earmarked for these additional funds from DFID.

title: Kitui Community Based Green Energy Project (CB-GEP)
description:
As part of a 4 year programme, this project aims to increase access to modern, affordable and sustainable energy services for rural and peri-urban communities in Kenya. To do this, CAFOD, the Diocese of Kitui, the Diocese of Isiolo and Dupoto-e-Maa will work in partnership with CAFOD and Solar Works East Africa Limited, a private sector solar energy technology company. 

Community Based Green Energy Project (CB-GEP) in Kitui will target 138,256 households through 46 schools , 32 health centres and 32 rural community based groups in Kitui County, specifically in the districts of Kyuso, Mwingi, Mutomo and Kitui.

Income generation of women and youth groups will be facilitated through the provision of 4 ICT centres using solar-based computers and other office equipment, and commercial kiosks, all owned and managed by selected and trained youth groups. For women groups 28 green houses with solar Pumping systems will be set up for income generation.

Income generation of women and youth groups will be facilitated through the provision of ICT centres using solar-based computers and other office equipment, and commercial kiosks, all owned and managed by selected and trained youth groups.

Management of natural resources will be improved through the installation of solar water pumping systems at existing water structures, support for solar lighting systems for schools and health centres; by the use of energy saving stoves; and through community awareness raising on environmental protection.

Local partners and community groups will be trained to implement, maintain and manage the energy systems and on the benefits of sustainable environmental management, facilitating technology transfer and replication of the systems within the target areas.

title: Solar Works Community Based Green Energy Project (CB-GEP)
description:
Solar Works Community Based Green Energy Project (CB-GEP) is a 4 year project whose overall aim is to contribute towards increasing access to modern, affordable and sustainable energy services for 407,792 households through 138 schools and health centres and 69 rural community based groups in rural and peri-urban areas in Kenya. The programme will be implemented in the Eastern and Rift Valley Provinces in Kenya specifically in the districts of Kyuso, Mwingi, Mutomo, Kitui, Garbatulla, Isiolo, Kajiado North and Kajiado Central. The programme will be implemented in partnership with Dupoto-E-Maa, Catholic Dioceses of Isiolo and Kitui and Solar Works East Africa Limited which is a private Sector Company focusing on Solar Energy Technology and operating in East Africa region. 

The programme plans to address the problem of poor and inadequate access to energy in target areas by offering solar energy solutions for over 407,792 households, 138 school and health institutions, and 69 rural community based groups within 4 years. 

The programme has 4 key specific and closely interrelated objectives that include: 
1. To improve provision of energy services for schools and health centres in rural and peri-urban areas in target districts. Energy services for rural and peri-urban poor by focusing on renewable energy solutions as well as on energy efficiency measures through directly providing energy services in rural and per-urban areas in target districts. This will be achieved through installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, solar water heating systems, solar water purification plants and energy saving jikos (stoves) for rural and peri-urban institutions.
2. To increase local incomes for rural and peri-urban youth and women groups through installation of off-grid information and communication technology (ICT) centres in rural townships that will be incorporate cyber cafes, computer training and related services. The project will install solar computers, printers and photocopiers and establish solar commercial kiosks for mobile charging and barber services at strategic centres. The ICT centres and commercial kiosks will be owned and managed by selected and trained youth groups.
3. To improve management of natural resources by target rural and peri-urban communities through providing alternatives to crude sources of energy such as wood fuel, kerosene and charcoal through installation of solar water pumping systems at existing water structures, support for solar lighting systems for schools and health centres, use of energy saving jikos and community awareness raising on environmental protection.
4. To build local capacities of partners and target communities for implementing and managing modern energy systems. Solar Works E.A Limited will work in partnership with CAFOD and CAFOD Implementing partners including the dioceses of Kitui, Isiolo and Dupoto-e-Maa to train local partner staff, students and staff at target schools and health centres as well as community groups members on maintenance of energy systems and creation of awareness of the target beneficiaries on how to maintain and ensure safety of the energy systems as well as understand the benefits of sustainable environmental management. This will lead to technology transfer in rural and peri-urban areas and hence create a conducive environment for replication of the proposed actions as well as reinforced capacities at target areas.
The programme is specifically designed to offer renewable energy and sustainable decentralised solutions, giving priority to energy efficiency through use of solar for household and institutional use. The programme further offers an innovative approach to ongoing development initiatives through the inclusion of private sector in providing technical support and capacity strengthening for greater sustainability and replication.

The expected programme results include:
1. Improved school performance for marginalized children in 90 rural schools
2. Improved drug storage for 48 health institutions in rural and peri-urban areas through installation of solar refrigeration systems.
3. Increased rural incomes for 69 women and youth groups through energy systems investments.
4. Improved communication for target rural communities.
5. Reduced environmental degradation and enhanced environmental protection.
6. Reinforced capacities of key stakeholders and the development of an enabling environment for private sector investment.
7. Improved partner and community capacity in handling and maintaining energy projects through technology transfer in target areas.

Further, the action plans to replicate relevant renewable energy projects to the neighbouring regions through technology transfer and finally, the action will provide off grid power generation through renewable sources. The proposed sources of energy will supplement other major sources of energy and have high potential to contribute to social, economic and environmental dimensions of sustainable development in target areas.

title: Improving Diocesan Nutrition Management Services
description:
The Diocese of Marsabit is one of CAFOD’s strategic partners and the Diocese is located in Kenya’s arid and semi arid region where the risk of deterioration in food security frequently remains substantive particularly for the northern and north eastern pastoral areas. The area is generally food insecure and suffers from chronic food shortage for most of the year. Currently, the Diocese is not currently implementing any nutrition projects even though the malnutrition rates remain high. 
The most recent nutrition survey conducted in Marsabit showed global acute malnutrition rates of 20.4 %. The main causes of malnutrition include lack of access to food especially during dry spells, poverty and decreased food affordability due to increased food prices. According to the 2010 Long Rains assessment report, while fairly good rains have translated into substantial improvement in household food security in other parts of Kenya, less than average performance of the long rains in Marsabit has resulted in communities remaining in the acute food and livelihood crisis phase in 2011. 
The failure of the short rains in late 2010 has worsened the plight of communities with reported livestock deaths, critical shortage of water and threat of famine.

The need for this project has therefore been prompted by a need to improve the existing disaster preparedness of nutrition services provided by the Catholic Diocese of Marsabit. CAFOD’s partner has been the first port of call for local people during crises (even though the quality of services provided to the community was not up to international standards). The partner therefore has the potential to reach some of these affected beneficiaries which other actors do not have easy access to. 

The purpose of the project will be to provide an opportunity for partners to become conscious of and take measures to improve the quality of nutrition management at health facility and community levels.  
    

Whilst CAFOD is looking at possibilities of providing emergency response support to communities it would at the same time like to support the partners to upscale and upgrade their nutrition management services as part of disaster preparedness and improve quality of service to internationally acceptable standards. From this the partners can be able to support their surrounding communities effectively and reduce vulnerability to malnutrition. 

Further, by hiring a nutrition assistant, this proposal will enable the Catholic Diocese of Marsabit to benefit from the partnership between Ministry of Public Health and Sanitation, WFP and UNICEF who will provide training, food and non food supplies through the delivery of essential nutrition services, through an initiative known as High Impact Nutrition Interventions (HINI) in Kenya. HINI has proven to be cost effective and feasible in prevention and treatment of under nutrition globally. Through the HINI initiative, the community is supported in various ways including:
1. Promotion of optimal infant and young child nutrition and improved hygiene practices.
2. Prevention of micronutrients deficiencies through supplementation, de-worming and therapeutic zinc supplements for treatment of diarrhoea.
3. Food fortification using multiple micronutrient powders.
4. Integrated management of acute malnutrition.
5. Increased dietary diversity through consideration of nutrition in food and agriculture programmes, incorporation of nutrition in school curricula and pre-service education.

In addition, within this partnership, the Catholic Diocese of Marsabit will be supported with blended food for supplementary feeding, and general food distribution during times of need from WFP during times of drought.  
Money from this project will not be used to purchase food aid, but rather to provide support to the partner for on the job training, purchase of small equipments (Salter scales, height boards, MUAC tapes), acquire fuel to access project sites in the delivery of food aid and costs for supporting the hiring of a nutrition assistant for two years.
The hired nutrition assistant will be key in strengthening the partnership with stakeholders at County level, and will be the focal point in delivering essential nutrition services, high impact nutrition interventions (HINI), ensuring coordination at County level, maintaining efficient nutrition surveillance; set up of monitoring and reporting systems, monitor actions which slow down progress in critical nutrition issues, advocate for sound and sustainable nutrition policies at County level.

The failure of the short rains in late 2010 has worsened the plight of communities with reported livestock deaths, critical shortage of water and threat of famine.

The need for this project has therefore been prompted by a need to improve the existing disaster preparedness of nutrition services provided by the Catholic Diocese of Isiolo. CAFOD’s partner has been the first port of call for local people during crises (even though the quality of services provided to the community was not up to international standards). The partner therefore has the potential to reach some of these affected beneficiaries which other actors do not have easy access to. 

The purpose of the project will be to provide an opportunity for partners to become conscious of and take measures to improve the quality of nutrition management at health facility and community levels.  
    

Whilst CAFOD is looking at possibilities of providing emergency response support to communities it would at the same time like to support the partners to upscale and upgrade their nutrition management services as part of disaster preparedness and improve quality of service to internationally acceptable standards. From this the partners can be able to support their surrounding communities effectively and reduce vulnerability to malnutrition. 

Further, by hiring a nutrition assistant, this proposal will enable the Catholic Diocese of Isiolo to benefit from the partnership between Ministry of Public Health and Sanitation, WFP and UNICEF who will provide training, food and non food supplies through the delivery of essential nutrition services, through an initiative known as High Impact Nutrition Interventions (HINI) in Kenya. HINI has proven to be cost effective and feasible in prevention and treatment of under nutrition globally. Through the HINI initiative, the community is supported in various ways including:
1. Promotion of optimal infant and young child nutrition and improved hygiene practices.
2. Prevention of micronutrients deficiencies through supplementation, de-worming and therapeutic zinc supplements for treatment of diarrhoea.
3. Food fortification using multiple micronutrient powders.
4. Integrated management of acute malnutrition.
5. Increased dietary diversity through consideration of nutrition in food and agriculture programmes, incorporation of nutrition in school curricula and pre-service education.

In addition, within this partnership, the Catholic Diocese of Isiolo will be supported with blended food for supplementary feeding, and general food distribution during times of need from WFP during times of drought.  
Money from this project will not be used to purchase food aid, but rather to provide support to the partner for on the job training, purchase of small equipments (Salter scales, height boards, MUAC tapes), acquire fuel to access project sites in the delivery of food aid and costs for supporting the hiring of a nutrition assistant for two years.
The hired nutrition assistant will be key in strengthening the partnership with stakeholders at County level, and will be the focal point in delivering essential nutrition services, high impact nutrition interventions (HINI), ensuring coordination at County level, maintaining efficient nutrition surveillance; set up of monitoring and reporting systems, monitor actions which slow down progress in critical nutrition issues, advocate for sound and sustainable nutrition policies at County level.

title: Caritas Australia funded East Africa Drought Appeal Project Diocese of Marsabit 2011-2012
description:
Marsabit is a pastoral and agro pastoral zone located in upper Eastern Kenya bordering Isiolo to the South East and Wajir to the East. It is one of Kenya's Arid counties located in Eastern Province. The County has a population of 291,166. The main livelihood activities in Marsabit are Pastoral and agro-pastoral which account for 70% and 20% respectively. Livestock and livestock products are a predominant source of food and income to households. Most parts of the County other than Marsabit town chronically experience water scarcity and food insecurity due to frequent drought, recurrent livestock disease outbreaks, poor market and road infrastructure, insecurity from cross boarder raiding and resource based conflicts.  

Failure of the short rains in October 2010 and continuing La Nina induced drought has resulted in further exacerbating the situation in Marsabit. Low and erratic short rains in October last year have lead to less than 20% recharge of temporal water sources, decline in forage, breakdown of water facilities due to overuse by people and livestock. Mass death of livestock, mostly small stocks began in February, but the average daily loss of animals has risen in the last four months as crucial water sources dried up. More than 17,000 animals since January, according to officials from the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) and the governments Arid Lands and Resource Management project (ALRMP). Many of the remaining water sources are contaminated, leading to increased incidents of water-borne diseases such as typhoid, amoeba and diarrhoea.

In Marsabit, due to drought both water and grazing for animals vanished and cattle prices reduced drastically. As a result, there was deterioration of nutrition status particularly children requiring supplementation of protein rich food sources. The problem has been exacerbated by a worldwide rise in food prices. The price of grain in affected areas in Kenya generally is 30-80% above average. 

In many parts of Marsabit, up to 75 percent of their herds have already died while the remainder is either sick or dangerously underweight. The price of animals has plummeted by half while the cost of cereals has soared.Malnutrition rates stands at mean of 27 %. There is reported significant number of deaths, mainly of children, pregnant women and elderly people attributed to hunger, dehydration and water waterborne diseases. 

An increase in staple food prices, particularly in far-flung areas, has worsened, according to ALRMP: 2kg of  maize in  Hurri hills, Marsabit town  has increased from 50 shillings to 150 Kshs  (1.9 USD) and milk has risen from 40 shillings (50 cents) per liter to 80 shillings (1 USD) per liter  ( January and end may respectively). 

School attendance has greatly been affected with some schools down due to lack of  water , others experiencing low attendance while others having 2 to 3 times the number of students   as pastoralists move with their families  in search of pasture.


According to the IPC classification, many large areas of Northern Kenya such as Marsabit has now been classified as “emergency” as of June 2011. Estimates issued by the Kenya Government and the United Nations (UN) shows over 3.5 million people are affected and in dire need of humanitarian assistance in Kenya. 
The situation is changing rapidly and is now estimated that over 4 million people will be classified as “humanitarian crisis” as early as August 2011 in Kenya alone. The next rainy season is not expected before October and December 2011 and there are already indications that poor pastoral communities in large areas of Northern Kenya are already experiencing severe food stress characterised by massive crop failure, high mortality of cattle and a steep deterioration of the livelihoods assets. In the words of many commentators, this drought is being described as the worst drought to hit East Africa in 60 years. 
The encroaching drought has resulted in reduced production of livestock products for household consumption, increased pressure on pasture, death of livestock and insecurity as pastoralists continue to move in search of pasture and others immigrate from the neighbouring Wajir, Isiolo, Samburu counties and others move to the neighbouring Ethiopia.  Resource based conflict is increasing due to competition for limited water and pasture resources.
On June 1st the Government of Kenya (GoK) declared the drought a national disaster and appealed international assistance to provide support to over 3 million Kenyans affected by the drought and acute food shortages Northern, East, Coast and parts Rift valley provinces.  CAFOD through its traditional Catholic Church partners is planning to respond to the needs of the worst affected communities in 4 most affected districts of Maralal, Marsabit, Isiolo and Kitui. The assistance is meant to ensure that the livelihoods of these communities are protected and that these communities do not suffer.

Based on the findings the Diocese together with the Arid Lands and local governments have prioritized the following projects to be supported by CAFOD:

1.  Improvement of acces to safe water . This is aimed at providing Immediate relief to thirsty and hungry residents .The interventions comprise - Rehabilitation and equiping of 2 boreholes in hurii hills and Bubisa . This will involve de-silting water pans using cash transfer to households in preparation for the next rains. In addition some funds will go towards equiping and repairing boreholes in specific areas and training water management committees for sustainability.

2.  Drought stricken but potentially productive households gain access to modest cash incomes through cash for work activities/project and whose long term purpose will be to improve their resilience to future drought shocks e.g. de-silting and construction of earth dams / water pans . 

3.  Non conditonal cash grants for the most vulnerable families (elderly, disabled , HIV and AIDS affected, orphans, child head-homes) . Each vulnerable household will recieve 150 Kshs per day for a month for six months . The methods of cash transfer will be decided . Option include the use of  Mobile money transfer , mobile banking or direct transfer .

4.Additionaly the Health and hygiene promotion sessions will be provided for 600 households in the Diocese of Marsabit.This is aimed at improving the hygine quality whic suffers immensly as a  result of lack of water clean water,massive livestock deaths and low priority as search of food take priority.

5.Construction of 4 water pans in the diocese for the remaining livestocks.This will reduce the tension on the existing and/or constructed waterholes and also reduce the incidence of large movements of livestock and people in search of water.Alongside this,the diocese wil construct 8 pit latrines in the water pan zones as a means of promoting hygine.
                                             
CAFOD will also provide a grant to the Diocese of Marsabit to enable them to hire additonal staff to provide quality and effective support to the partner to enable the project to be implemnted and monitired effectively.

4) Support 5 clinics run by the Church partners are supported with the provision of essential drugs and supplies and provide free provide basic outpatient services for a period of six months to poor drought stricken families/ individuals.

title: DEC East Africa Drought Appeal Project Diocese of Maralal 2011-2012
description: Current La Nina Induced drought  and high food prices has affected over 10 million people across Horn and East Africa. In Kenya, the government and UN   indicate that over 3.5 million people are affected and in dire need of humanitarian assistance . Samburu North and East Districts are Arid areas in Rift Valley province of Kenya with  110,801 inhabitants, over 80% of the population depend on livestock as a means of livelihood and primary source of food.  Following the failure of short ( October 2010) and Long rains (March to May 2011) most of the pastrolists have lost their livestock, Distance to water points has increased  from an average of 8km to  about 40kms, the few agropastrolists in the area experienced massive crop failure. Diocese of  Maralal which has been monitoring the effects of drought in the area conducted a rapid assessment between 23 and 30th of June 2010 to prioritize intervention areas. the assessment finding show that most households do not have food 90% of 300 interviewed households had only 1 meal in the last three days , distance to water points have dramatically increased  and resource based conflict have increased. In Conjuction with CAFOD the Diocese has designed an emergency drought response project targeting 5506 households  in Wamba, Nkaroni, Naimirimo Ngilai, Waso, baragoi, Nachola, Elbarata, Nyiro Parkati and Kawop divisions in Samburu North and East district. The project aims at mitigating the effects of the current drought in Samburu East and North by promoting access to food and water  in the first 6 months followed by 18 months recovery phase that will focusing on rebuilding community resilince and reducing the impact of future drought.  The 1st phase will ensure access to safe water  to 5506 HH through construction of a borehole, desilting of 7 water pans, provision of food aid to 669 HH to ensure poor and unproductive households have access to food assistance .Recovery activities will be identified within 4 months of the start of the six months of implementation of the 1st phase relief activities.

title: CAFOD Appeal East Africa Drought Response Project Diocese of Kitui
description:
The of Diocese of Kitui covers Kitui County, an approximated  area of 30,142km2 in the Eastern Province of Kenya with an approximate population of 1.09 million people. The region is classified as Arid and Semi Arid Land (ASAL) with rainfall being recorded below 600mm per annum. The larger Kitui and Mwingi districts did not receive the long rains in 2011 and the two districts are at alert stage of drought early warning cycle and the food situation is deteriorating drastically. If immediate measures are not taken, many people are at risk of suffering and dying of hunger.

The CAFOD Appeal East Africa Drought Response Project of the Catholic Diocese of Kitui will be implemented in Mutomo and Mumoni districts. The target areas have a combined population of 25,508 people (Population Census 2011). 

The goal of the drought response project is to protect the lives and livelihoods of drought affected households in Mutomo and Mumoni districts in Kitui County. In Mutomo district, the project will be implemented in Kyatune locations targeting 262 households, Ngwani Location targeting 241 households, Ndatani Location targeting 140 households, Kathungu Location targeting 371 households and Makele Location targeting 157 households. In Mumoni district, the project will be implemented in Konyu Location targeting 214 households, Kanthungu Location targeting 201 households, Gatoroni Location targeting 145 households and Mbarani Location targeting 320 households, a total target population of 2,051 households. 

The project has 4 interrelated specific objectives that include: increased food accessibility for 2,051 most poor and vulnerable households through cash transfer, increased access to water for drought vulnerable households in Mumoni, Kyatune and Ikanga areas; increased land productivity through construction of soil and water conservation structures and organic manure application in target areas and finally improved accessibility to target  communities through construction of 3 rural access roads.

The planned activities will include construction and rehabilitation of earth pans, construction of rural access roads, construction of soil and water conservation structures and training on the same. The project plans to target 2,051 households through cash transfers. The project plans to mainstream HIV and AIDS by addressing the needs of the most vulnerable groups by setting aside 20% of the cash transfer to go directly towards supporting 410 households of the people 
living or affected by HIV and AIDS, the sick, the elderly and the weak bodied who are unable to work. The remaining 80% of the cash transfer will support the cash for work initiative targeting 1,641 households. The project plans to target 1,171 household from Kyatune, Ngwani, Ndatani, Kathungu and Makele Locations in Mutomo district and 880 households from Konyu, Kanthungu, Gatoroni and Mbarani Locations in Momoni district. The total indirect beneficiaries amount to 12,306. These include the household members who will not participate in the project activities or benefit from the direct cash transfer but will use the food bought using the money paid to project beneficiaries or benefit from the work of the beneficiaries. The project will develop a beneficiary selection criteria that will ensure that the most poor and vulnerable households are selected to benefit from the project. 

This project is going to be the first phase of project and will be implemented over a period of 6 months. It will be followed by a near-term and long-term second and third phases that will be implemented over a period of 18 months. These two phases will be recovery and reconstruction
