title: Reproductive Health and Access to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in Kajiado County, Kenya
description:
Kajiado County is a rural county in the south-east of Kenya, bordering Nairobi to the North, and Tanzania to the South. It is home to Maasai communities, including Nice Nailantei Leng’ete, Amref’s Global Ambassador to End Female Genital Mutilation or Cutting (FGM/C), who has been working for many years to reduce FGM/C across the region.
Amref has been working in Kajiado County for 11 years. Over the last three years Amref, with funding from Stitching Ondersteuningsfonds Zorg Welzijn en Sport (ZWS), has been delivering the ARPWASH Model project in Kajiado. Through integrated Alternative Rites of Passage and WASH interventions, this project aimed to improve Sexual Reproductive Health Services and Rights (SRHR) among adolescent girls and women of reproductive age. The project will end in June 2020, having reached 27,691 people. As a result of the project 23 villages have been declared Open Defecation Free (ODF) communities and 2,725 adolescent girls were trained on SRHR, life skills, and hygiene, and graduated through Community-Led Alternative Rites of Passage (C-ARP) instead of going through FGM/C.
A recent evaluation of Amref’s C-ARP programme in Kajiado County has shown that CL-ARP plays a decisive role in decreasing FGM/C, child, early and forced marriage. Since the programme started, FGM/C rates among girls in the region have declined by 24.2%, girls on average stayed in school for 2.5 years longer, and were more likely to delay marriage and childbirth, with teenage pregnancy declining by 6.3%.
Women in Kajiado County bear the greatest burden when it comes to access to healthcare and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH). Women are at risk of complications from pregnancy and childbirth, early marriages, unwanted pregnancy, and FGM/C. 
There is also increasing evidence that the reproductive health of women and girls is disproportionately affected by lack of access to WASH services, due to biological and cultural factors. Integrating WASH practices into health service delivery in health facilities and improving access to WASH within communities has been shown to decrease both morbidity and mortality of women and girls. WASH interventions are cost effective and help to improve gender equality and human rights by giving women and girls more social freedom and safety and removing inequitable work burdens.
The COVID-19 pandemic, and resulting movement restrictions and school closures, has disrupted access to critical Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) services and hampered authorities’ ability to respond to Gender Based Violence (GBV) and harmful practices like FGM/C, child, early and forced marriages and teenage pregnancies. Reports of these have risen over recent months and reduced physical interaction between health workers and community members has hampered the ability to track and monitor girls at risk of FGM/C enrolled on Amref’s C-ARP programme.

Amref's second phase of the ARPWASH model project to improve the health and well-being of women of reproductive age in Kajiado by integrating SRHR, C-ARP and WASH interventions. The second phase will address gaps that have been identified during Phase One, many of which have been exacerbated by Covid-19:
1.	Lack of online Tracking/Monitoring tool for 2,725 girls reached through the C-ARP
2.	At least 1,500 girls still at risk of FGMC, early marriage and unintended pregnancy
3.	At least 3,000 people still not reached with clean water sanitation and hygiene
4.	Seven villages (1,750 people) still practicing open defecation still practicing open defecation
5.	Limited public health infection, prevention and control measures
With funding from the Rabelais Trust, we propose to fill these gaps by:
1.	Training 90 Community Health Workers (CHWs) through our Leap digital platform on infection prevention at community and health facilities
2.	Supporting 1,500 girls at risk of FGM/C in the 7 villages
3.	Providing access to clean water for over 3,000 people in 7 villages.
4.	Supporting 7 villages (Shompole, Kilonito, Maparasha, Meto, Kiloh, Olenarau and Olgulului) to become ODF and FGM/C free communities.
5.	Attaching a trained CHW to each village to monitor and report all forms of violence against women and girls including FGM/C, domestic violence and Early Child and Forced Marriages (CEFM).
By the end of the project we aim to meet the following objectives:
1.	To improve infection prevention and control (IPC) among the target group(s).
2.	To reduce cases of FGM/C, early marriage and teenage pregnancy among targeted communities 
3.	To increase acceptance and support for the C-ARP model by cultural and political leaders.
4.	To generate evidence, share lessons learnt and best practices for ending FGM/C, early marriage and teenage pregnancy.

reporting_org_name: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.
title: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices Annual Report: October 2023 - Sept 2024
description:
The program facilitated the establishment of safe and institutionalized spaces for dialogue between youth, government institutions, and political actors through the creation of the Office of the Citizen, which worked closely with county-based youth organizations like County Rights & Voice CBO to facilitate consistent communication and improve local governance.
Additionally, supported youth-led advocacy initiatives that addressed key governance issues, such as waste management in Oyugis town (Homa Bay County) , the completion of public health facilities like the Osiepe dispensary, and infrastructure concerns like the lack of toilets at Awuoro Primary School. These advocacy efforts led to tangible improvements in public services and increased accountability from local authorities. Youth civic champions in counties such as Nairobi, Kericho, and Lamu identified and addressed local governance challenges, including waste disposal, public safety, and access to National IDs, by engaging local authorities and driving change. Their efforts included reviving stalled projects, such as the Youth Bill in Kericho, and advocating for better waste management and public infrastructure in Busia.
The program also built the capacity of youth to hold local governments accountable, with youth-led committees in Nairobi, Lamu, and Kericho successfully addressing issues such as substandard school toilets and environmental hazards like untreated sewage. Collaboration with local community-based organizations (CBOs) like the Lamu Art and Theatre Alliance further strengthened the program’s impact, enabling youth to raise issues such as delayed National ID issuance and the sale of alcohol to minors. These partnerships enhanced youth advocacy efforts and raised awareness on critical local governance issues. Regional youth forums were organized across counties such as Homabay, Busia, and Mombasa, providing a platform for youth to share concerns, build advocacy strategies, and foster stronger links between youth, government, and the community.
Youth leaders in Kericho and Busia mobilized their communities to address governance challenges, demonstrating a deeper commitment to democratic processes. The program saw a marked increase in youth engagement, with more youth leaders taking on the role of civic actors, advocating for change, and voicing concerns about issues such as water shortages, healthcare challenges, land grabbing, and unsafe infrastructure. Their ability to draft advocacy letters and engage local authorities signified their growing influence in governance. Moreover, local youth organizations like the Isangalo Art Group in Busia demonstrated increased advocacy capacity by addressing issues like healthcare service delivery and influencing local governance. Expanded dialogue platforms like town hall meetings, sports dialogues, and art expos facilitated deeper engagement with community members and local government officials. These initiatives provided youth with the tools to influence decision-making processes and allowed them to effectively advocate for their communities' needs. As a result, these youth-led organizations gained legitimacy and strengthened their capacity to advocate for long-term governance improvements, ensuring that their voices remain a key part of the development process in their communities.

title: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices Annual Report October 2024 - Sept 2025
description:

toilets in Homabay County; completion of Mlachake to Lake Kenyatta Primary school road in Bahari ward, Lamu  County; completion of Kaguria water project in South Kabuoch Ward in Ndhiwa, Homabay County; completion of construction of ECDE classroom at Waregi Primary School in Mbita, Homabay County; extension of operation of Ober Dispensary in Ndhiwa, Homabay County; repair of a sewerline in Central ward in Homabay town; supply of drugs at Sio-port sub county hospital in Funyula, Busia County; construction of a new ECDE classroom in Kedowa ward, Kericho county; murraming of chepcholoet mosomborik road in Kericho County; connection of electricity in Kapsenda Dispensary in Londiani, Kericho County; operationalization of Hongwe Market in Lamu County; construction of a pavilion in Mpeketoni, Lamu County; completion of Jericho Primary School classroom in Lamu County; murruming and grading of Kanziko - Mutha road in Kitui County. Completed projects impacted the community's lives positively by improving service delivery and increasing accountability at the local level.While the project has established better trends, youth transition and inadequate platforms for people with disability had been a challenge in the implementation of the program.In year four, the program will focus on expanding devolution of mentorship, further creation of more youth engagement platforms and supporting a series of engagements especially on the alternative platforms. The program will also expand on intergenerational dialogue forums

title: STRENGTHENING HUMAN SECURITY IN THE BORDER COMMUNITIES OF TURKANA, KENYA
description: This project addresses the human security concerns of pastoralists living in extreme hardship and vulnerability to numerous human security threats. The proposed activities aim to improve human security in a context of UN inter-agency coordination including UNDP, FAO, WHO, IOM, UNICEF, ILO and OCHA, and building on the capacities of local CBOs such as Lopedo (Loima Peace and Development organization), the Riam Riam Turkana Peace Network , local peace committees, local government and the governmental Arid Lands Resource Management Project (ALRMP). The proposed activities take into consideration the threat to the socio-economic well-being of vulnerable groups affected by food, economic and health insecurity. Activities building on local capacities are to preserve the human dignity of the target populations, reduce inter-communal, cross-border tensions and promote social and economic development through the delivery of basic health care, the stepping up crucial water initiatives for populations and livestock, the support to the pastoral production system, access to basic education for out of school and vulnerable children as well as alternative livelihood skills training. The project is focused on strengthening the resilience of the dominant livelihoods in the face of natural disasters and other shocks, while providing alternative coping mechanisms through coordinated, sustainable interventions in the livelihoods, food security, education and health sector. Considering the mobile nature of pastoral border communities, the project will target the most vulnerable of the Turkana Central population as well as selected neighbouring cross-border communities by providing opportunities to interact in a peaceful manner through joint training and the establishment of a joint markets and trade opportunities. The project activities support the MDGs by targeting poverty reduction, health and education, while being in line with the government’s objectives of poverty reduction and Disaster Risk Reduction for the region, as outlined in the National Policy for the Development of the ASALs. The activities are also in line with UNDAF outcome two on empowering people who are poor and reducing disparities and vulnerabilities. The UNTFHS offers a unique funding source that is integrated, holistic, multi-sectoral which is aptly suited to addressing the multi-facetted problem at stake. The project benefits from the input and guidance of different UN agencies, local partners and most importantly, local community beneficiaries themselves.

Activities building on local capacities are to preserve the human dignity of the target populations, reduce inter-communal, cross-border tensions and promote social and economic development through the delivery of basic health care, the stepping up crucial water initiatives for populations and livestock, the support to the pastoral production system, access to basic education for out of school and vulnerable children as well as alternative livelihood skills training. The project is focused on strengthening the resilience of the dominant livelihoods in the face of natural disasters and other shocks, while providing alternative coping mechanisms through coordinated, sustainable interventions in the livelihoods, food security, education and health sector. Considering the mobile nature of pastoral border communities, the project will target the most vulnerable of the Turkana Central population as well as selected neighbouring cross-border communities by providing opportunities to interact in a peaceful manner through joint training and the establishment of a joint markets and trade opportunities. The project activities support the MDGs by targeting poverty reduction, health and education, while being in line with the government’s objectives of poverty reduction and Disaster Risk Reduction for the region, as outlined in the National Policy for the Development of the ASALs. The activities are also in line with UNDAF outcome two on empowering people who are poor and reducing disparities and vulnerabilities. The UNTFHS offers a unique funding source that is integrated, holistic, multi-sectoral which is aptly suited to addressing the multi-facetted problem at stake. The project benefits from the input and guidance of different UN agencies, local partners and most importantly, local community beneficiaries themselves.

title: STRENGTHENING HUMAN SECURITY IN THE BORDER COMMUNITIES OF TURKANA, KENYA
description: Executive Summary This project addresses the human security concerns of pastoralists living in extreme hardship and vulnerability to numerous human security threats. The proposed activities aim to improve human security in a context of UN inter-agency coordination including UNDP, FAO, WHO, IOM, UNICEF, ILO and OCHA, and building on the capacities of local CBOs such as Lopedo (Loima Peace and Development organization), the Riam Riam Turkana Peace Network , local peace committees, local government and the governmental Arid Lands Resource Management Project (ALRMP). The proposed activities take into consideration the threat to the socio-economic well-being of vulnerable groups affected by food, economic and health insecurity. Activities building on local capacities are to preserve the human dignity of the target populations, reduce inter-communal, cross-border tensions and promote social and economic development through the delivery of basic health care, the stepping up crucial water initiatives for populations and livestock, the support to the pastoral production system, access to basic education for out of school and vulnerable children as well as alternative livelihood skills training. The project is focused on strengthening the resilience of the dominant livelihoods in the face of natural disasters and other shocks, while providing alternative coping mechanisms through coordinated, sustainable interventions in the livelihoods, food security, education and health sector. Considering the mobile nature of pastoral border communities, the project will target the most vulnerable of the Turkana Central population as well as selected neighbouring cross-border communities by providing opportunities to interact in a peaceful manner through joint training and the establishment of a joint markets and trade opportunities. The project activities support the MDGs by targeting poverty reduction, health and education, while being in line with the government’s objectives of poverty reduction and Disaster Risk Reduction for the region, as outlined in the National Policy for the Development of the ASALs. The activities are also in line with UNDAF outcome two on empowering people who are poor and reducing disparities and vulnerabilities. The UNTFHS offers a unique funding source that is integrated, holistic, multi-sectoral which is aptly suited to addressing the multi-facetted problem at stake. The project benefits from the input and guidance of different UN agencies, local partners and most importantly, local community beneficiaries themselves.

title: Inclusive Growth Through Decent Work in the Great Rift Valley
description: The private company Akiira Geothermal Ltd is establishing a power plant near Naivasha, Kenya. The plant energy output will be a substantial benefit to Kenya’s growing economy. For the neighbouring pastoral communities to also benefit, conscious and pro-active measures will need to be taken to enable them to have a share of the benefits of the economic growth. Akiira Geothermal Ltd is determined that the investment will have a positive impact on the adjacent communities in terms of local content and job creation during the construction and operational phases, despite the lack of locally available skills. To this end, Akiira will use part of its revenues to support community engagement, skills development and job creation in the immediate communities surrounding the geothermal plant in response to the challenges experienced in the region – in addition to in-kind contributions. The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) offered to provide the loan guarantee as a support of generation of sustainable and renewable energy. In addition, the embassy has entered into a Public Private Development Partnership (PPDP) with the International Labour Organization (ILO) as the coordinator of this partnership. At the same time, the ILO will be entering into an agreement with ForumSyd, a Swedish Non-Governmental Organization with experience working with communities in and around Naivasha, for implementation of one of the expected outcomes. Overall, the PPDP will aim at improving the living conditions in and around the project areas, i.e. Narok and Nakuru counties, by acting as a catalyst to boost decent job creation through business development, skills development and community engagement. It is foreseen that this partnership can become a model for replication to achieve inclusive growth in the extractive industries and other industries in Kenya and beyond. The immediate objectives of the PPDP are to create decent jobs from better skills by vocational training centers; develop new and improve on growing businesses resulting from new relevant skills, business development services and access to finance, promoting the rights of workers in the local communities and increase capacity of communities to lobby for increased access to public and social services e.g. water, education, health, sanitation. While Akiira Geothermal Ltd and the Swedish Embassy agreed to jointly invest in a Public Private Development Partnership to address development challenges near the power plant, the Kenyan public partners’ involvement and commitment is vital for ownership and replication potential. As such, the total budget for the PPDP includes both the partners’ financial and non-financial contributions e.g. with time and resources.

description:
The evaluation of legislation of ESC rights, Public interest litigation, advocacy , the organization's support . Hakijamii, in its project, focuses on the right to health, water and sanitation, and implementations of these rights. The Constitution defines 
the part of health care as a fundamental right for all citizens, but especially among the poor the unavailability of services is a major problem. The development process of the nationwide network of water distribution network, in turn, has suffered from in
efficiency, corruption and mismanagement. One of the downturn was, when  along with the Water Act in the 2002, the water privatizations occurred. From the lack of clean water and sanitation suffer both rural and urban slums, and in particular the marginali
zed groups. Kenya's estimated population of 42 million, about 30% now live in cities, and the urbanization is rapid. Slums have been incorporated into urban planning and budgeting, and residents have very little chance of the health, education and other ba
sic services. It is estimated that only 20 per cent of slum residents have the opportunity to have permanently clean water and slum residents also pay out of the water several times more compared to other residents. The project aims to promote economic and
 social rights implementation. The aim is both to improve the State's procedures for new policies and legislation, as well as through the adoption of improving the economic and social rights, the implementation of fundamental rights through the bringing of
 the action. The project beneficiaries are the most vulnerable groups whose needs are taken into account in the content promoted laws; women, the elderly, the disabled, children, young people and minorities, and other vulnerable groups. Hakijamii was found
ed in 2004 to fill the gap in Kenya to deal between the organizations, which focuses on the human rights field, and on the other hand the organizations that handle the economic and social problems in a non-legal perspective.

title: F.a: Human Rights and Forced Eviction Project
description:
Many slum dwellers are under constant threat of illegal and forced evictions and displacement. In 2004, started the Kenya Slum Upgrading Programme to improve the conditions in slums, but the slum dwellers have not been included in the program and the imple
mentation of the program involves many risks. The 1972 Public Health Act, determine the standards of living and quality of water, but authorities did not enforce the law regarding to its implementation in the slums. The draft law Eviction and Resettlement 
Bill 2012, about the forced evictions and resettlement, is approved for the Parliament processing. The bill guarantees citizens the humane treatment of such cases before the eviction, during and after it. KISORA has been involved in the preparation of the 
draft law and in its lobbing. The objective is to strengthen the community-based advocacy in the realization of ESC rights: the aim is to strengthen the capacity of slum dwellers to demand the implementation of economic and social rights, particularly the 
right to adequate housing, and lobby for the administration to run according to the requirements of the main international human rights instruments. In addition, the project aims to increase the knowledge of members of the community about the economic and 
social rights. The aim is to strengthen the cooperation in the grass-roots level and to increase the KISORAn internal capacity to take action so that it would be a strong and responsible actor. Project's direct beneficiaries are the communities living in s
lums under the threat of eviction. In addition, the project is targeted at 33 grassroots organizations in Kisumu East District. Indirect beneficiaries are the other residents in the slums of Kisumu East District. KISORA (Kisumu Social Rights Association) S
elf Help Group was established in 2007, and it is a network for human rights lobbying groups operating in grass-roots slums.http://hakijamii.wordpress.com/hakijamiis-partners/kisumu-social-rights-association-kisora

title: F.a: Meibeki Valley Area Development Project
description:
The programme works for the improvement of rural communities’ socio-economic situation and quality of life, as well for the strengthening of community capacities and enhancing children’s rights in Meibeki Valley, Western Kenya.At the beginning of the p
rogramme, water and sanitation were inadequate and the availability of clean water was weak. This was also reflected in children's health and education. One of the main goals has been the availability of clean drinking water.  At present the water supply s
ystem consists of a more than 162 km long pipeline. Clean water has permanently changed the life of more than 35 000 persons. The evaluation report shows that 89% of households have now access to clean water less than 500m from their homes during the rainy
 season and 61.7 %, respectively during the dry season . (In 2004: 1.4%)More than 7,000 children are now able to go to school and have time to do their homework, when their time is not needed for fetching water. To ensure better educational possibilities f
or the children, educational conditions have been improved with the support of the parents.  Already more than 2,500 children study in the improved classrooms. With the support of the program, two dormitories have been constructed for secondary school girl
s.  The program beneficiaries are the 54,000 inhabitants living in the area, especially women and children, who used use several hours a day to fetch water. Having clean water closer to the homes has freed time for time for other things as well as brought 
new income opportunities, like vegetable farming, agriculture and caring for livestock. A change in the women's role can be seen: there are many women as village chiefs and school attendance among girls has grown considerably. Children's participation in c
ollective decision-making is encouraged through the Children's Parliament. Children and young people are represented in the village committee and the water committee.The main partner is World Vision Kenya that runs the implementation and accounts for the u
se of funding.In addition there are many partners from different ministries, regional government officials, and religious communities.

title: F.a: Mogotio Area Development Project
description:
The programme works for the improvement of rural communities’ socio-economic situation and quality of life, as well for the strengthening of community capacities and enhancing children’s in Mogotio, Western Kenya.The 2012 evaluation showed a clear impr
ovement in key areas , though still only a fifth of the population have access to clean water (2007: 8.7%). When a child is ill, health services are now used  by 80 percent of the mothers ( 27% in 2007 ), and 92.7 %  children are vaccinated. Children's rig
hts have become known in the community, 95.5 % of the population now knows what child maltreatment means. The knowledge on how HIV infections are spread and on testing and support facilities has increased within the population of Mogotio. The evaluation re
commends that the next period of work focus would shift more and more to strengthen local capacity. In particular, access to clean water and sanitation and malnutrition among children is still a challenge.The new five -year plan has been completed and the 
first year of Implementation has started. Increasing the availability of clean drinking water has been initiated through the rehabilitation of water points. In addition co-operation with the Ministry of Health has been started to diminish water related dis
eases and diarrhea and a campaign has been launched for every household and school to get a toilet. Cooperation has also been done with the Ministry of Health through training of community health workers  on the care and follow-up of the health of children
 and expectant mothers.  In addition emphasize has been given to birth registration. Children's participation in collective decision-making is encouraged through Children's Parliament and the situation of women and girls are supported through focus on harm
ful traditions such as female genital mutilation and early marriages, as well as acts of violence against girls. The program beneficiaries are the 23,500 persons living in the programme area. The main partner is World Vision Kenya that runs the implementat
ion and accounts for the use of funding.

The programme works for the improvement of rural communities’ socio-economic situation and quality of life, as well for the strengthening of community capacities and enhancing children’s in Tinderet, Western Kenya.The main objectives of the previous pe
riod have been Children's rights and child protection. The evaluation shows that the work has been fruitful; child rights violations have decreased from 92.4% in 2009 to 34.3%. Child labor has also been halved during the same period. In addition work has b
een done to decrease waterborne diseases and improve general health. Health services are now closer. 70 per cent of the population has access to health services within a distance of less than five kilometers. Every third person is currently receiving clean
 water compared to only one in eight at the beginning of the programme.  Through renovations of water points and sanitation trainings diarrhea and waterborne diseases have been reduced. Within disability work positive cooperation has been continued with lo
cal disability institution. HIV trainings are organized through support groups and seminars. The women’s AIDS run, providing information and testing possibilities has gathered great popularity. Community members have been trained in public responsibility
 and cooperation has been established with local actors, authorities and cooperations. Children's participation in collective decision-making is encouraged through Children's Parliaments.The program covers an area of six centers with a population of about 
35 000 people. The main partner is World Vision Kenya that runs the implementation and accounts for the use of funding.

description:

e communities who are nomadic have to seek out and share limited pasture and water resources bringing them into conflict with each other. The intention is to help communities achieve their rights to security currently under threat from the proliferation an
d misuse of small arms and light weapons (SALW) by ensuring that the communities themselves are at the heart of the prioritisation planning implementation and monitoring and evaluation of the programme.  As well as being of immediate benefit to the ?target
? communities by developing credible evidence from these practical efforts the programme also intends to inform national and international processesAcross two locations in Kenya this project aims to address some of the factors contributing to insecurity wi
th a view to make a positive contribution to meeting the national development agenda under the following areas: 1.Enhancement of security along the borders to address proliferation of small arms across the borders; 2.Institutionalising national and inter-c
ommunity dialogue in order to build harmony among ethnic racial and other interest groups; 3.Deepening policy legal and institutional reform for improved enforcement of law and order. During the two yearlong project several seminars forums and workshops wi
ll be organized on security and monitoring the use of SALW for both local people and authorities. Theinteraction between local population and local authorities will be strengthened. The aim is also to develop locally ways to reduce the proliferation and mi
suse of SALW. During the program interaction between the local beneficiaries and international experts on SALW will be organized. The program will be implemented by an NGO spezialized on arms control with close cooperation with local Kenyan partners. http:

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Evaluation of Kenya Country Programme
description:
Kenya is one of Finland's long-term partner countries. There is a long-standing development partnership ? over thirty years ? between Kenya and Finland. The objectives of current country strategy of Finland in Kenya (2013-2016) are: The objectives for Finl
and?s cooperation with Kenya are: 1) Kenya?s development towards a democratic and accountable society that promotes human rights; 2) poverty reduction through inclusive green growth in the agricultural sector; and 3) improved management and use of forest a
nd water resources.The last evaluation of Finland?s development cooperation in Kenya was conducted over ten years ago in 2002. In 2009 there was an evaluation on Finnish Aid in Western Kenya to assess the impact of Finnish supported projects/programmes in 
Western Kenya and to provide recommendations for planning the new cooperation in the area.The evaluation will consist of two parts: 1) Desk review on the Finnish development cooperation in Kenya in 2003-2013 focusing on impact sustainability effectiveness 
and efficiency; and 2) Comperehensive evaluation on results of the development cooperation in 2009-2013. The purpose of the evaluation is to provide an assessment on the overall results obtained and lessons learned from the past cooperation in Kenya. The e
valuation will be forward looking and will bring forward issues lessons learned and recommendations to support planners and decision-makers in different departments of the Ministry.The tender process will be started in March so that the evaluation could be
 started in May 2014. The evaluation results are expected to be had in autumn 2014. The budget of the evaluation is 200 000 Euros. | Kenia on yksi Suomen pitkäaikaisimmista kehitysyhteistyökumppaneista. Maat ovat tehneet yhteistyötä yli 30 vuoden ajan. Suomen kehitysyhteistyön (Kenian maaohjelma 2013-2016) päätavoitteet ovat: 1) Kenian kehittäminen demokraattiseksi ja vastuullis
eksi yhteiskunnaksi joka edistää ihmisoikeuksien toteutumista 2) köyhyyden vähentäminen ympäristön kannalta kestävän ja osallistavan maataloustuotannon kasvun avulla ja 3) metsä- ja vesivarojen hallinnon ja käytön parantaminen.Kenian maaohjelma
 evaluointiin edellisen kerran vuonna 2002. Lisäksi vuonna 2009 toteutettiin Suomen kehitysyhteistyöstä Länsi-Keniassa evaluointi jonka tavoitteena oli antaa suosituksia alueella tehtävän tulevan kehitysyhteistyön suunnittelua varten.Evaluoinnin tar
koituksena on tuottaa itsenäistä ja riippumatonta tietoa siitä miten Kenian maaohjelma on saavuttanut sille asetetut tavoitteet. Evaluoinnin tarkoituksena on myös kerätä tietoa yhteistyön parhaista käytännöistä vahvuuksista ja heikkouksista. Eva
luoinnin päätavoitteena on tukea Kenian maaohjelman kehittämistyötä ja tehdä suosituksia yhteistyön jatkolle.Evaluointi koostuu kahdesta osiosta: 1) desk review ?tyyppinen arviointi kattaen vuodet 2003-2013 ja 2) laajempi toiminnan tuloksellisuuden

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Nyagowa Water Supply
description:
Kenya has approximately 40 million people and nearly half of the population lack clean drinking water. Nyagowa is situated in an area where water sometimes is found only in small water streams and where cattle and people have to share the same water source
. Drinking water is fetched from streams or from shallow wells water which is not drinkable untreated. In many cases water is collected from roofs and roofs may sometimes be carriers of various diceases spread by birds and small vector animals. Some roofin
g materials are also hazardous for peoples health. Up to 50 % of the deceases are waterborne deceases.The plan of the project is therefore to provide the health facility schools and the local community with clean drinking water which need not to be boiled 
before consumption. If the water flow is high enough the excess water will be led to water basins for the cattle.The plan of the project is to drill a hole to groundwater level in order to pump up clean drinkable water. The pumping system will be driven by
 solar energy (with an option to use landline electricity at times) which is an environment friendly sustainable and affordable way for the people to get clean water. Water will be distributed to strategically well placed water stations through a piping sy
stems and excess water will be distributed to drinking basins for the cattle. Concerning the sanitary conditions there are outdoor latrines built on a two-three meters deep wells in most of the homes. Hygiene is cared for either in streams or in private pl
aces specifically arranged for this nearby the homes. This project will therefore mostly concentrate on how to protect clean water from being contaminated and to encourage people to construct protected latrines where needed. No water flush toilets are in t
he area and the project will not build any either.The plan of the project is also to replace the water catching roofmaterial of the Health Clinic with ironsheets since water is collected from the roof to a tank. Water from the rainwater tank is today used 
for cleaning floors and for other use in the clinic but since the roof material is containing asbestos it should long ago have been replaced. If the roofmaterial is changed the rainwater tank may after a small repair serve as a water reserve for the clinic
 and be used in case of temporary absence of water from the borewell eg during maintenance of the water supply system. | Kenya har omkring 40 miljoner invånare och närmare hälften saknar rent dricksvatten. Nyagowa ligger i ett område där det ibland finns vatten i mindre vattendrag och där boskapen och människorna måste samsas om vattnet. Dricksvatten hämtas från n
ågon vattenström eller från grunda grävda brunnar och vars vatten inte kan drickas obehandlat. I många fall samlas vatten upp från tak vid regn och taken kan vara  bärare av olika smittor som sprids med fåglar och smådjur. Flera takmaterial är de
ssutom direkt hälsovådliga. Upp till 50 % av sjukdomarna i distriktet är vattenburna.Projektets plan är därför att förse byns klinik skolor och den övriga närbefolkningen med tillgång till rent vatten som inte behöver kokas före användning. Om
 vattenflödet är tillräckligt stort kan extra vatten ledas till drickhoar för byns boskap. Projektets plan är att borra ett hål till grundvattennivå för att kunna pumpa upp rent drickbart vatten. Pumpsystemet skall drivas med solenergi (med möjlig
het till nät-el vid behov) som är ett både miljömässigt hållbart och för befolkningen ett förmånligt sätt att få rent vatten. Vattnet distribueras till strategiskt välplacerade vattenstationer där befolkningen får tillgång till rent vatten. 
Vattnet kommer att distribueras till vattenstationer via ett rörledningssystem och överskottsvatten från pumpningen distribueras till vattenhoar för boskapen.När det gäller de sanitära förhållandena så har de flesta hem någon form av latriner ut
omhus byggda på ett par-tre meter djupa brunnar. Den egna hygienen sköts antingen i öppna vattendrag eller på särskilt avdelade platser i närheten av hemmet. Detta projekt kommer därför att på olika sätt förebygga att dricksvatten skulle bli fö
rorenat genom att uppmuntra befolkningen att använda skyddade latriner. Inga vattentoaletter finns i området och kommer inte heller att byggas av projektet.Planen är också att byta ut hälsostationens takmaterial till plåttak eftersom taket samlar reg
nvatten till en tank. Vatten från regnvattentanken används för att tvätta golv och för andra behov på kliniken men eftersom det innehåller asbest borde det för länge sedan har bytts ut.Om takmaterialet byts ut kan tanken efter en mindre renovering
 användas för skurning av golv samt som en vattenreserv för kliniken ifall temporära uppehåll uppstår pga tex underhåll av vatten-försörjningssystemet.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: WASH project in Turkana
description:
Turkana is in many ways the most underdeveloped area in Kenya. The proposed project aims to improve the area?s wellbeing by providing assistance in water supply and sanitation sectors in the neediest villages in northern Turkana County which have been sele
cted by the Turkana community themselves.During the project efforts are made to repair and rehabilitate dysfunctional water wells in the project area. In addition ca. 10 new wells with water pans and 10-20 hygienic latrines will be built and also the commu
nities are educated in the proper ways to operate and manage the mentioned facilitie.The Turkanas haven?t needed to pay fees regarding the use of drinkable water in the past. We have learned during our preparatory mission that most of the wells built in th
e Turkana County have not been properly handed over to the consumers/villages which has led to poor understanding on the ownership and responsibility issues. During the project WaterFinns develops together with the Turkana communities a maintenance and man
agement model which will be implemented in the use of the water points and the improved hygienic environment.The perennial boreholes will contribute to people living in stationary villages near schools increase the attendance in schools and decrease the nu
mber of people affected by using unsafe drinking water. This will provide a steady and healthy environment for the children and youth to grow up in.The Project aims to achieve its purpose through three interlinked results (outputs):1: Lessons learned from 
success and failure of long-term sustainability of rural WASH services reported and benchmarks of best practices promoted.2: Strengthened capacities of selected CBOs village spokesmen and wards in their management and efforts of further improving the WASH 
services.3: Improved WASH facilities in selected communities in order to fulfill their needs and HR requirements on a sustainable basis.A key element of the proposed project is to create opportunities for the future water sector professionals to have an in
teresting and unique possibility to participate in voluntary work which focuses on long-term learning of the sustainable schemes.The proposed project partner (GWAKO) has amble experience to carry out rural water and sanitation projects and they also have e
xperience in working in the northern Turkana County.  The proposed project would last two-and-a-half years (2015-2017) and its proposed budget is 257 200 ?. | Turkana on monin indikaattorein mitattuna Kenian alikehittyneintä aluetta. Ehdotettu projekti pyrkii parantamaan alueen hyvinvointia tarjoamalla vesihuoltoa ja sanitaatiota Turkana-yhteisön valitsemilla eniten apua tarvitsevilla kylillä Turkanan maakunn
assa.Tuetaan projektialueella olevien vanhojen kaivojen kunnostamista olemassa olevien mahdollisuuksien mukaan. Lisäksi rakennetaan n. 10 uutta kaivoa karjanjuottoaltaineen 10-20 hygieniset vaatimukset täyttävää latriinia ja avustetaan yhteisöjä opp
imaan edellä mainittujen toteutusten oikeaoppinen käyttötapa ja ylläpito. Turkanan kantaväestö ei ole joutunut maksamaan veteenliittyviä käyttömaksuja. Tiedossa on että aikaisemmin rakennettuja kaivoja ei ole luovutettu yksiselitteisesti yhteisö
ille minkä vuoksi omistajuus- ja vastuukysymykset ovat epäselviä. WaterFinns kehittää projektin aikana yhdessä vastaanottajayhteisöjen kanssa ylläpito- ja hallintomallin yhteisöjen vesipisteille ja hygieniselle ympäristölle.Ympärivuotiset kaivo
t lisäävät yhteisöjen pysyvää asumista koulujen läheisyydessä ja lastenosallistumista kouluissa ja vähentävät vesiteitse tarttuvien tautien esiintymistä. Tämä mahdollistaa lapsille ja nuorille vakaan ja terveellisen kasvuympäristön.Projekti
 pyrkii saavuttamaan tavoitteensa kolmen toisiinsa liittyvän tuotoksen avulla:1: Oppiminen sekä epäonnistumisista että päätöksistä jotka johtivat onnistumisiin ja parhaiden käytäntöjen jakaminen.2: Valittujen käyttäjäyhteisöjen ja paikallish
allintojen kapasiteetin rakentaminen maaseudun vesijärjestelmien ylläpidossa ja parantamisessa.3: Institutionaalisen kehikon voimistaminen niin että kyläyhteisöt ja käyttäjäkomiteat ottavat täyden vastuun käytöstä ja kunnossapidosta korostaen y
ksityisen sektorin osallistumista.Projektin tärkeä elementti on luoda nuoremman sukupolven vesialan ammattilaisille mahdollisuus osallistua vapaaehtoistyön kautta prosessiin jossa opitaan pitkäaikaisen työn onnistumisista ruohonjuuritasolla.Ehdotetull
a projektikumppanilla on pitkäaikainen kokemus kylätason toiminnasta FRESH-projektinsa kautta. Heillä on myös aiempaa kokemusta Turkanan alueella työskentelystä sekä hyvät keskusteluyhteydet paikallisten kyläyhteisöjen ja county-tason päättävi
en tahojen kanssa mikä mahdollistaa tehokkaan toiminnan projektialueella.Ehdotettu projekti on 25-vuotinen (2015-2017) ja sen budjetti on 257 200?.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: FLC: Strengthening local natural resources management (NRM) institutions and empowering local communities advocate for improved governance
description:
Community-based Natural Resources Management (CBNRM) is a development approach that supports natural resource conservation. More conservation-minded people will define CBNRM as a natural resources conservation approach that brings along income and employme
nt. One could also argue that conservation of natural resources and sustainable use of these resources for the benefit of the community are two sides of the same coin. The community is more inclined to conserve natural resources if is able to realize benef
its accruing form such an activity. The wise use of these resources is a precondition for sustained development. CBNRM rests on the recognition that local communities must have direct control over the utilization and benefits of natural resources - wildlif
e forests water resources - in order to value them in a sustainable manner. CBNRM is both a conservation and rural development strategy involving community mobilization and organization institutional development comprehensive training enterprise developmen
t and monitoring of the natural resource base. It therefore aims for local stakeholder participation in the planning development management and policy making for a community as a whole.In the recent past the issue of community participation has been emphas
ized in the Kenyan constitution and subsequent legislations and these present opportunities for engagement to further promote CBNRM nationally and at county level.  To optimize on the opportunities there is need to look at some core areas that support the 
participation of citizens through robust advocacy mechanisms. They include but are not limited to:  Citizen Awareness institutional strengthening and capacity building planning implementation monitoring + evaluation feedback + reporting mechanisms financia
l resource mobilization and Citizen Engagement Forums. There is therefore need for practitioners and local institutions to have a common understanding of the current opportunities understand inherent institutional weaknesses and form a strong advocacy coal
ition to tap into the few existing opportunitiesThis project therefore hopes to bring together CBNRM practitioners from different sectors (forestry and water) to share common principles and approaches informed by experiences and to ensure that their voice 
informs the County integrated development strategies and plans.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: FLC: PACODEO - Peace building and Conflict Resolution in Marsabit County
description:
The Marsabit County perceived problems in the Upper Eastern parts of Kenya are anchored in the poor participation of the communities in the developmental agendas conflicts and tensions over resources insecurity among ethnic tribes and boarder countries inf
lux of cheap and sophisticated weapons from the porous borders of Ethiopia Somalia and Sudan. These includes:-continuous aimless killings invasions poor economic infrastructure unequal or poor distribution of resources misunderstanding between inter-ethnic
 communities and conflict. This is also widely seen to be instigated by politician?s incitement lack of adequate water pasture and grazing boundaries scarcity of resources high level of illiteracy very poor cooperation and dialogue among the Sub counties a
nd regional leaders in two Neighboring Countries of Kenya and Ethiopia.All this has caused unknown number of deaths leading to displacement of people who are forced to seek for refuge in market centre?s where there is police presence closure of schools and
 public offices. There are also cases of continuous and rampant cattle raids which have left majority of the residents without a source of livelihood depending only on government and NGOs supplied relief foods. Some of the conflicts have been caused by cla
ims of some ethnic groups living in some parts of their ancestral land leading to constant retaliations and revenges. Some areas have not only had high incidences of insecurity but uncountable cases of   massacres like North-Horr and Maikona districts. In 
these areas the truth will precede the justice and reconciliation issues and many Kenyans want to know how and what happened. The invasions by groups such as Oromo Liberation Front [OLF] banditry menace[Shifta]and Ethnic Cleansing have led to high cases of
 criminality and criminal gangs unemployment with many of the young persons and the economic means have been suppressed leading to poor means of earning livelihoods. There are also cases of impunity abuse of officers and corruption with high cases of extor
tion. The ethnic communities have element of suspicions hatred strife conflict tensions dissensions and fights surface in one form or another. The communities have experienced an increased chronic banditry activity which has claimed an unimaginable number 
of human lives livestock lost to the warring groups loss of properties of unknown value and houses set ablaze from both sides.

title: Cement Your Love...Bring Clean Water To Africa
description:
Cement. It's usually not at the top of the Christmas list, but in Sub-Saharan Africa, it's a
generous gift. Cement is the main component of most of our water projects, and in many of our communities it's also one of the most expensive. Although not glamorous, $25 will buy one bag of cement. Each bag will go toward transforming the lives of our neighbors in Africa and will help us complete our future water & sanitation projects. Help us reach our goal of 4800 bags this Christmas!

title: EWB Houston - Maseno Mission Kenya Water Project
description: EWB Houston is traveling to Maseno Kenya to implement a surface water gathering project to provide a reliable water supply to the Maseno Mission Hospital.  The Hospital, operated under the auspices of the Episcopal Diocese and supported by All Souls Episcopal Church in San Diego, serves the local community with a 75 bed hospital containing mens/womens/maternity/childrens wards, seeing 5000 patients per year. Rotary is funding the construction - funds needed for travel to country.
results_text: Activity website

title: Sustainable Water Supply to 2000 Villagers
description: Current water supply problems in Gatumbi/Kiangungi village include the distance and time required to retrieve the water each day as well as the quality of water once it reaches the homes. It takes women and children many trips each day with buckets, consuming many hours of their time while pupils from neighbouring primary schools have to carry 5lts of water to school every morning for cleaning and other uses.
results_text: Activity website

title: Shining Hope for Communities
description:
Shining Hope for Communities (SHOFCO) provides free education for girls and a network of empowerment and poverty alleviation programs in one of Africa's largest slums: the Kibera slum of Nairobi, Kenya. 

SHOFCO's innovative model combats extreme poverty and champions gender equality by linking tuition-free schools for girls to desperately needed community services accessible to all-- including healthcare, clean water and sanitation, adult education, gender violence support and more. Join us!
results_text: Activity website

title: The Nobelity Project's Kenya Schools Fund
description: The Kenya Schools Fund partners with communities across rural Kenya to build libraries, classrooms and water systems. Your support for 2013 projects will help build classrooms for the 5th and 6th grade at Mutaki Primary, and needed facilities at other schools. Completed projects include Mahiga Hope High and primary school, Simbara Secondary, Mogaka and Daaba Primary, new water systems at Bondeni, Amboni, Daaba and Honi schools, and 12 school libraries
results_text: Activity website

title: Help us improve The Daos Children's Centre, Kenya
description: This project will provide improved facilities at The Daos Children's Centre in Mombasa, Kenya.  Improved facilities will include running water; 11 new classrooms; mains electricity; dormitory accommodation for orphaned children as well as a number of security improvements to ensure the children's safety.  We are also looking to provide basic scholastic equipment including pens; pencils and textbooks.

title: Provide Millions of Kenyans with Safe Water
description: The chlorine dispenser program provides safe water in Kenya through a simple, convenient, and affordable system.

title: Provide water & sanitation to 2200 pupils in Kenya
description: Nosim plans to construct rainwater harvesters and toilets to provide water and sanitation to 2200 primary school needy pupils in three primary schools in Kajiado and sensitize them on hand washing. This will help reduce hygiene and sanitation related diseases and reduce school absenteeism among young girls.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean Water for Schools in Kenya
description: In Kisii Kenya, residents are frequently stricken by life-threatening illnesses caused by water that is contaminated with feces. Children are especially vulnerable, but schools offer a solution. With their extensive roofs, they are well suited to collect water provided by irregular rains. The large, concrete tanks constructed at these sites provide water that is safe to consume, and eliminates the potential for harm to students who often travel several miles to retrieve water.
results_text: Activity website

title: Safe Drinking Water & Sanitation for Those in Need
description: Blue Planet Network brings the spotlight on communities worldwide who bear the disproportionate burden of the safe drinking water crisis. Acting as an online engine for the water sector in 27 countries and counting, Blue Planet Network connects WASH funders, organizations and grass-roots communities through its technology platform to exponentially increase the impact of safe drinking water and sanitation programs built by its implementing members.
results_text: Activity website

title: Safe Housing for Kenyan School Girls
description: Building a dormitory for 7th and 8th grade girls of Pathfinder Academy will provide a safe environment for girls who live in the most distant villages. The challenges are difficult for many girls who too often just stay home, marry early and inevitably live in poverty. Building a safe shelter for girls will transform their lives by providing  them with education, food, clean water,and shelter. With an education, these young women will return to their communities to serve as change agents
results_text: Activity website

title: Keep 627 girls in school in Siaya, Kenya
description: We want to keep all the girls at the Nina School in Siaya District of Kenya in school to get a complete education. To do that, we need two things: to supply all girls with panties and reusable sanitary napkins and build a well in their village. Girls miss one week of school each month because of their menses. They also miss school when they must walk several miles to fetch fresh water for their families. Education is power for girls in Kenya and to keep them from missing school is important.

title: CAFOD Operation Grant - DFID Match Fund 4
description:
This project covers CAFOD operational costs for the Match Fund 4, which is a three year programme. 

CAFOD is best suited to manage this internal grant for effective delivery of MF4 programme outcomes and goal.  Specifically the operational costs covered under this grant include: Travel, accommodation and Venue , Supplies, Materials and other Services CAFOD will directly pay for during the implementation period.

The aim of the Match funded project is to increase sustainable access to improved  water, hygiene and sanitation (WASH) facilities for in Kitgum district for rural disadvantaged communities. We will directly provide WASH services alongside investing in social mobilization of communities to influence local government authorities on policy implementation, and strengthen water user groups to adopt correct use and maintenance of water points. The direct beneficiaries of the project are women and men in under served villages including people with disabilities, women’s groups, school children, community water user associations and local leaders (through advocacy) in Moroto District.
The project contributes to four interrelated outputs as listed below:
1.Women and men have improved, equitable and sustainable access to safe water and sanitation 
2.Women and men are reached with better information on good sanitation and hygiene practices
3.Communities, local authorities and leaders have better knowledge, skills and relationships to engage in participatory planning, management and delivery of WASH services
4.Communities and relevant stakeholders have better knowledge and skills for management of water resources and catchment areas

title: Supporting community conservancy model in Kenya to enhance an integrated and sustainable protection of biodiversity
description: The project will contribute to the restoration of the catchment areas affecting the Sigor plain, including the WeiWei irrigation scheme. The area has been subjected to extensive deforestation and soil degradation, especially in sloping areas, due to unsustainable farming methods, excessive grazing and deforestation. As a result, floods and landslides are increasingly frequent and also jeopardize the sustainability of the WeiWei irrigation scheme. The aim of the project is to start the restoration of the most degraded areas through the introduction of soil & water conservation techniques. In addition, the initiative will promote the adoption of regenerative farming practices to improve soil productivity and enhance the sequestration of CO2​, thus contributing to the fight against climatic change. The strategy used is to reduce soil erosion in two priority areas identified as key to addressing the root causes of soil erosion and floods:1.The water catchment area that extends from Mount Korellach to the foothills; 2.The degraded riparian areas of the WeiWei River upstream of the Sigor plain. The initiative will make it possible to introduce crops and tree species capable of protecting soils but also providing new alternative sources of income to residents. | Il progetto contribuirà al ripristino del bacino idrografico che interessa la piana di Sigor e lo schema di irrigazione di WeiWei. L'area è stata oggetto di un ampio disboscamento e degrado dei suoli, soprattutto nelle zone di pendenza, a causa dei metodi di coltivazione impiegati spesso insostenibili, l'eccessivo sfruttamento dei pascoli e della deforestazione. Di conseguenza, le inondazioni e i fenomeni erosivi sono sempre più frequenti e mettono a rischio la sostenibilità del sito di irrigazione di WeiWei ed il villaggio di Sigor. L'obiettivo del progetto è quello di avviare il ripristino delle aree più degradate attraverso l'introduzione di tecniche di conservazione dei suoli e di regimazione delle acque. Inoltre, l'iniziativa promuoverà l'adozione di pratiche di agricoltura rigenerativa per migliorare la produttività dei suoli e aumentare il sequestro della CO2​, contribuendo in questo modo anche alla lotta contro i cambiamenti climatici. La strategia proposta è quella di ridurre il degrado del territorio in due aree prioritarie identificate come chiave per fronteggiare le cause all'origine dell'erosione dei suoli e delle inondazioni: Il bacino idrografico che dal Monte Korellach si estende fino alle colline pedemontane; Le aree ripariali degradate del fiume WeiWei a monte della piana di Sigor. L'iniziativa consentirà di introdurre colture e specie arboree in grado di proteggere i suoli ma anche di fornire nuove fonti alternative di reddito agli agricoltori. | aumento della protezione ambientale, della resilienza delle comunità e adattamento ai cambiamenti climatici attraverso la gestione sostenibile e pacifica delle risorse naturali nelle zone aride e semi-aride del Kenya (ASAL) | fornire incentivi per gli stakeholders volti a promuovere la gestione sostenibile delle risorse naturali attraverso la creazione di benefici per la comunità basati sulla natura e il sostegno a governance e istituzioni basate sulle comunità che promuovono inclusione e uguaglianza

title: Give 300 maasai families safe water in kenya
description:
Maasai women carry water with their backs for 20km for several months. The women and children no longer move with animals from one place to another. They now have permanency in the areas they now live. Sanitation problems in this areas is very high leading to water shortage and sanitation related illnesses in their villages due to lack of latrines.
This project will reduce the number of months that the women need to carry water with their backs through assistance with water tanks and a latrine.
results_text: Activity website

title: Show diarrhea the red card
description:
Hodari Youth Sports Foundation harnesses the enormous power of sport to catalyze social change among children and adolescents in schools and youth clubs about the importance of water, sanitation and hygiene.  

We train and inform children through the use of football-based games to raise awareness of the centrality of safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene in order to succeed in life and in sport and to facilitate life-saving behavior change.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean water for Tumaini home and the community
description: Please help us raise money to drill for fresh water for our children and our community! TMSC is located in Western Kenya, Mukhonje village which has a total population of 500,000. Each year TMSC becomes a home and a hope to a child. Our children's home  accommodates 70 children and we have 300 children in our school. Our license to drill the borehole expires in July 2015 and our goal is to begin drilling in January 2015 while the season is dry. We urgently need your help to make it possible.
results_text: Activity website

title: Provide clean & safe water for 1500 women&children
description: The project aims to develop an integrated water supply system to serve about 1500 women and children affected by an acute shortage of water and improve standards of hygiene and sanitation in Mutulani village, rural Kenya. Having already sunk a borehole, we are now focusing on completing the water supply system to ensure higher standards of hygiene & sanitation, reduced cases of school absenteeism.  We aim to construct water tanks, bio-digester system, facilitate forums on WASH.
results_text: Activity website

title: Elimination of water borne diseases in Nyakach
description: IWHA's goal: Eliminate water-borne diseases such as diarrhea, typhoid and cholera in 14,400 families, 69,000 people in Lower Nyakach, Kenya . Combining easily understood, effective and low cost community-based water testing, education, and chlorine treatment enables families to kill disease-causing germs in unsafe drinking water from streams, ponds, and wells. This project to prevent diseases and save lives can be replicated in millions of villages plagued by water-borne diseases worldwide.
results_text: Activity website

title: Empowering Rural Kenyans through Reforestation
description: Rooted In Hope promotes environmental, social, and economic development in rural Kenya through our reforestation efforts in the Aberdare National Park. In addition to restoring degraded forest areas, planting trees provides a multitude of benefits, most notably with regards to water, women, and wildlife. Our program in Kenya results in increased water table levels, employment for underprivileged women, and rehabilitation of the natural habitat of several threatened and endangered species.
results_text: Activity website

title: Nthunguni Spring Project
description: KWENCH will work with the Nthunguni Water Project self-help group to develop water from a perennial spring and distribute it to 17 water points. At present, the village of Mumani has no developed water system at all. The project will also contain sanitation, hygiene and livelihood components.
results_text: Activity website

title: Help Kenyan and Ugandan Women Provide Clean Water
description: Over 3.4 million people die per year from poor water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) conditions. Global Women's Water Initiative (GWWI) trains African women to build and sell water filters, promote good hygiene practices and become social entrepreneurs launching WASH businesses. Help GWWI support female technicians to build 200 biosand filters providing clean water and promoting good hygiene to 1000s of students and families in Kenya and Uganda, keeping girls in schools and women earning income!
results_text: Activity website

title: Educate & Empower Children from Kibera, Kenya
description: RFS provides vulnerable children from the slum of Kibera, Kenya, with the opportunity to attend a boarding school where they receive a quality education.  Here they are provided an education along with three meals a day, clean water, medical care, a bed, uniform, and safety. "Most people look at the slum of Kibera and see a huge unsolvable problem. We see huge untapped potential."
results_text: Activity website

title: Empower and Educate Phaustine!
description: In the largest slum in Africa called Kibera, near Nairobi, Kenya, live approximately over half a million people.  They are living without access to clean water, sewer system, electricity, or infrastructure.  It is unsafe at night with no lights, girls are sexually assaulted and battered. We are taking these children out of the slum and sending them on a Road to Freedom, to attend a beautiful boarding school.  There, they receive clean water, 3x meals, medical care, a bed, safety and an education
results_text: Activity website

title: Send 100 Somali PastoralGirls to school in Garissa
description: The project will support 100 Somali Pastoral girls access education in the secondary level in the arid region of Garissa, Northern Kenya. Pastoralist Girls Initiative will pay school fees for 100 girls for 1 year, procure books, uniform, sanitary towels and pants to ease the burden of the poverty stricken families who  due to harsh climatic condition and their nomadic lifestyle of moving  from one place to another in search of pasture and water can not afford to send their girls to school.

title: Clean Drinking Water for Communities in Kenya
description: We want to ensure access to clean drinking water for several Masai communities in Southeast Kenya. We will buy and install rainwater harvesting tanks in communities affiliated with Kenya Evangelical Lutheran Church. The tanks will provide water security and improve the lives of thousands of people for decades. The water tanks will serve our church communities and neighboring communities and families. Each tank will impact approximately 500 people.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean Water For 50+ Rescued Kenyan Infants
description: In Kenya, contaminated drinking water is still a reality for many people. For this reason, New Life Home Trust has installed a water tank or borehole at each New Life home over the years. With the help of these tanks, once abandoned infants are offered quality care without fear of contracting preventable diseases. Additionally, we keep our overall costs lower by relying on our water tank rather than an outside source. New life for rescued infants requires clean, safe drinking water daily.
results_text: Activity website

title: Ositeti School need a drinking water well!
description: This project will be used to help build a drinking water well in Ositeti School in Maasai Mara (Kenya) The "Amigos de Ositeti" ONGD is an organization dedicated to increasing services of the school, students and teachers. One of the most important things is to get drinking water for the community of this village. First, there were only 35 children in school but they are now than 400 and the build is very important for they.
results_text: Activity website

title: Urgent Medical Saves and Changes Lives in Kenya
description: Two month old Baby Cara lost her mom. Washing clothes in the river, she had a seizure, fell into the water and drowned. Since then, Baby Cara has been diagnosed with acute malnutrition.  Her situation is like all others, treatment begins only after paying upfront.  Malnourished babies can't wait. Their survival depends on quick treatment.  The urgent medical fund is there to get treatment of all illnesses started quickly for all children and adults.  We need your help to do that.
results_text: Activity website

title: Save a Turtle by Reducing Marine Litter in Kenya
description: Over 100 million marine animals are killed each year due to plastic debris in the ocean. Sea turtles around the world are eating plastic at an unprecedented rate, plastic bags can bear a striking resemblance to jellyfish underwater and have a tendency to confuse hungry sea turtles.  In our own little way, we would like to save turtles by cleaning up beaches along Kenya's coast while removing garbage dumps and transforming them into Mangrove forests, perfect habitats for some turtles
results_text: Activity website

title: Provide clean water for Akili Girls School, Kenya
description: Akili Preparatory School for Girls provides free quality education for underprivileged girls from Obunga Slum, Kisumu, Kenya. Deeper Missions Org, USA is matching all funds raised upto $10,000 to enable us to drill a permanent well 110 meters deep  to provide clean and safe drinking water for 30 underprivileged girls attending a boarding school in its Obambo Campus as well as over 300 households living in Obambo village, Kisumu, Kenya.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean water & Toilets to 100 Children in Nyalenda
description: SLEC will connect clean water and two 10,000 liter tanks, construct five toilets and five bathrooms for 100 children, installation of electricity,  construct three classrooms and cooking area, purchase books and furniture.  Construct a sleeping area  for 30 toddlers   The Children in Nyalenda slum will be healthier (free of water borne diseases) receive nutritious meals and quality education.
results_text: Activity website

title: Access to clean water for 2500 villagers in kenya
description: The project will install 8 water hand pumps in Tsiekuru Village. This is in addition to 5 pumps installed in phase I.   2,800 individuals plus 1,500 herds of cattle and 4,000  goats which form the prime livelihood in this arid and semi-arid region will enjoy  access safe drinking water.  Women will be saved from walking long distances, outbreaks of cholera will reduce and young girls will concentrate in their education.
results_text: Activity website

title: Operation WATSAN for 1600 Ramba School Students
description: This project will support the drilling of a borehole, construction of steel water tank and tower, providing clean water supply to over 1600 Ramba Boy's Boarding High School students. This will contribute to global sustainable development goals on " availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all" and "attain healthy life for all at all ages".

title: Increasing forest cover through play in Nairobi
description: Kick and Conserve program is tailored to provide environmental awareness, to understand how vulnerable our environment is  and the importance of protecting it through Soccer themed messages for example environmental games and activities that geared to direct the community to protect the natural resource that dictates our eco system for example water, forest, air and animals. The program involves Environmental Discussion Sessions, Environmental games and finally soccer (Fair Play)

title: To eradicate Cholera from Africa via Nadi filter
description: Contamination in drinking water is everywhere in the world, but rural areas of Africa including Kenya, Uganda, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Ethiopia, Tanzania & Malawi all facing in 2023 Cholera BREAKOUT and needs solution, AHD want to help these countries with Safe Drinking Water Nadi filter technology to help them with skills and knowledge and long term impact to get safe and clean drinking water from AHD Nadi filter solution, Nadi filter helping lifetime sustainable solution for rural communities
results_text: Activity website

title: Sondu Water Enterprise
description: Sondu water kiosk is a local enterprise situated in rural under-served area, where there is high burden of disease and poor water and sanitation infrastructure. Sondu river is highly contaminated and in absence of a reliable water source vulnerable  communities use the river water for household use. This has caused high incidence of diarrhea and child mortality. SWAP established a skyhydrant filtration unit to provide clean and safe water drinking water sold to communities at an affordable rate.
results_text: Activity website

title: Moringa for Health and Water Purification
description: Moringa for Health and Water Purification project will provide 1,000 Community Members  from Makueni with 20 Moringa  seedlings  each to plant on their farms. Planting these high yield trees will go a long way to address malnutrition and contaminated water in the Makueni Community.
results_text: Activity website

title: Water for Learning in Kenyan & Ugandan Schools
description: This project will address the lack of clean water, hygiene and sanitation facilities in EPAfrica's partner schools in East Africa through investment in facilities to collect, store, clean and distribute water. Complementary hygiene and sanitation facilities such as handwashing stations and clothes washing stations may also be installed. This funding will enable us to improve the water situation in eight schools, directly impacting the health and education of at least 4,000 students.
results_text: Activity website

title: UPCYCLING HANDMADE PRODUCTS BY 100 KENYAN ARTISANS
description: This project aims at reducing the effects of water hyacinth weed that has invaded Lake Victoria (Kenya) making fishing and water navigation impossible thereby affecting the livelihoods of families which depend on the lake. We aim to utilize the water hyacinth weeds to make functional products which we shall sell and in the process create employment for 100 artisans at the shores of Lake Victoria.
