title: Canada-South Africa trilateral research chair in nanomaterials for clean water
description:
This project aims to use nanomaterials (a nanometer is one billionth of a meter) to provide new, inexpensive techniques to purify water that also address the increasingly important issue of antimicrobial resistance. The ability of new hybrid materials to speed up reactions through exposure to light will both degrade organic pollutants and serve as an antimicrobial agent with long-lasting activity. Photoactive materials usually generate non-toxic by-products and use sunlight, which is not only cheap and harmless but also widely available in Africa. 

This project involves a trilateral partnership between lead researchers at the University of Ottawa, Rhodes University in South Africa, and the United States International University in Kenya. The project will rely on the complementary expertise of the three principal investigators in such areas as the synthesis of new complexes and nanoparticles, photochemistry, and catalysis research. The strength and novelty of the initiative lies in these trilateral links that aim to enable strong research connections within the African continent and between Canadian and African scientists. Two of the main expected outputs of this project are to establish a long-lasting world-class centre of research expertise in Kenya, and to train many graduate students from the three countries, who will benefit from mobility and exposure to a wide variety of ideas and perspectives by working with these top scientists. 

The genesis of the project is a collaborative effort to pilot a first set of trilateral partnerships between Canada, South Africa, and another country in sub-Saharan Africa, building on existing research chairs in Canada and South Africa, and supporting the role of South Africa to contribute to world-class research on the continent. The modalities were co-developed by IDRC and the National Research Foundation of South Africa. | Ce projet vise à utiliser des nanomatériaux (un nanomètre vaut un milliardième de mètre) pour créer de nouvelles techniques abordables de purification de l’eau, en tenant compte de la question de plus en plus importante de la résistance antimicrobienne. De nouveaux matériaux hybrides capables d’accélérer les réactions par l’exposition à la lumière permettront de dégrader les polluants organiques et serviront d’agent antimicrobien à effet à long terme. En général, les matériaux photoactifs génèrent des sous-produits non toxiques et utilisent la lumière du soleil, qui est non seulement gratuite et inoffensive, mais largement disponible en Afrique. 

Le projet prévoit un partenariat trilatéral entre des chercheurs principaux à l’Université d’Ottawa, Rhodes University en Afrique du Sud, et la United States International University au Kenya. Il repose sur les connaissances complémentaires des trois principaux chercheurs dans des domaines comme la synthèse de nouveaux complexes et de nanoparticules, la photochimie et la recherche en catalyse. L’initiative tire sa force et sa nouveauté de ces liens trilatéraux qui visent à tisser des rapports étroits entre les chercheurs en Afrique, et entre les scientifiques canadiens et africains. Deux des principaux résultats de ce projet seront la création d’un centre de recherche et d’expertise durable et de calibre international au Kenya et la formation d’un nombre important d’étudiants de 2e et 3e cycles dans les trois pays, qui profiteront de la mobilité et de l’exposition à des idées et à des perspectives variées grâce au travail avec ces scientifiques de haut niveau. 

Ce projet est le fruit d’une collaboration visant à lancer une première série de partenariats trilatéraux entre le Canada, l’Afrique du Sud et un autre pays d’Afrique subsaharienne, en tirant profit de chaires de recherche existantes au Canada et en Afrique du Sud et en appuyant le rôle de l’Afrique du Sud dans l’appui à des recherches de calibre international sur le continent. Les modalités du projet ont été élaborées par le CRDI et la Fondation nationale de recherche d’Afrique du Sud.

title: Mandera County Drought Appeal
description: The Horn of Africa is experiencing a severe drought due to five consecutive rainy season failures. In Mandera county, about 2.5 million livestock have died. Three-quarters of the population urgently need assistance with food and water. Unfortunately, fewer aid agencies are reaching desperate pastoralists in the hinterland. The drought has decimated their livelihoods,  forcing some families to migrate to urban centres and putting pressure on an already high level of urban poverty.
results_text: Activity website

title: Plant 50,000 Trees in Mount Kenya Forest
description: Mount Kenya Forest experienced massive deforestation starting from early 1960s to late 1990s through various illegal activities which included; unlicensed timber harvesting, felling down trees for charcoal, fuelwood, forest grazing and shamba systems. The forest is very vital to community members since they rely on it for forest products such as ; fodder ,honey,fuelwood, fruits and water . The areas which experienced deforestation never regenerated back and thus need for restoration.
results_text: Activity website

title: Providing Access to Water for 250 Kenyan Families
description: 250 Kenyan families, whose livelihoods have recently been threatened recurrently due to long periods of drought, will be provided with access to water and drinking water through this project. This will be achieved by building a well and constructing a system for filtering the water into clean drinking water on the compound of St. Monica Village, a cooperative for widows in Western Kenya. The project thus makes a crucial contribution to securing the livelihoods of these families.

title: CSF 03-21 Year 2 Payment for the Project: Transformed Communities,
description: The ‘Transformed Communities Brighter Futures’ project in Kericho County, Kenya aims to help women and girls reach their full potential leading to healthier, more resilient and productive lives through access to improved health, education and economic empowerment opportunities, together with implementing partner Brighter Communities Worldwide Kenya. The objectives of the grant are that community members particularly women and girls will have access to a strengthened and more effective and equitable healthcare system, healthier and safer school learning environments for students and teachers, and empowered equitable communities will have the ability to bring about positive change. The key activities include outreach clinics, maternal health task force events, water protection scheme, preparation meeting with Ministry of Health and Ministry of Education, teacher workshops,  the construction of latrine and washroom blocks, and the provision of resources to enable beneficiaries to engage in new business opportunities.

title: African Integrated Landscape Management
description:
Period 01.01.2017-31.03.2017:

There is an increasing acceptance that sectoral approaches to land management are no longer sufficient. An integrated place-based rather than a sector based development, the so-called Landscape Approach is broadly definedas a framework to integrate policy and practice for multiple land uses, within a given area, to ensure equitable and sustainable use of land.  An Integrated Landscape management aims to balance competing demands on land through the implementation of adaptive and integrated management systems that achieve coherence in policies and actions and maximize synergies across multiples sectors. The landscape approach combines social, ecological and economic perspectives and requires different qualities and competences.  That#s way Oxfam NOVIBjoined the Landscapes for People Food and Nature initiative (LPFN) in 2016. This initative is a leading the discussion on Integrated Landscape Approaches at the international level.  It is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Economic affairs (coordinated by EcoAgriculture) with additional funding from the Sustainable Green Growth department within the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The LPFN initiative supported the African Resilient Landscapes Initiative (ARLI), which was endorsed by the African Union in 2015 and is supported by the African Landscapes Action Plan (ALAP) and the AFR100 Initiative, provides a comprehensive framework to aggressively advance integrated landscape approaches across the continent.
The funding willcontribute to the follow-up trajectory of a 3-day knowledge-sharing event for 150 landscape practitioners, that took place in Ethiopia at the end of 2016. Knowledge sharing workshops, exchange visits, and regional knowledge-sharing events, in which to compare and contrast experiences, and innovate new
solutions to commonchallenges, have proven to be important aspects of learning and application of ILM techniques, but need a follow-up to be really effective. This grant will allow the LPFN initiative to
further advance implementation of the African Landscapes Action Plan at different country levels.

Period 01.11.2017-31.10.2018:

Traditional approaches to property rights pose a major challenge for pursuing collaborative strategies for sustainable landscape management. Familiar issues of ownership and access rights to land, water, forests and other resources affect incentives for investment in sustainable management. But other issues also arise, like competing legitimate claims by different stakeholders who are affected by resource management by other users and uses. Therefore, expanded investment in integrated landscape approaches requires more nuanced understanding of the contextual factors and policy mechanisms by which tenure security can be assured, and sets of rights renegotiated among stakeholders.

The multi-level, multi-sector, multi-actor governance required for integrated landscape management has generated a host of innovations around land and resource rights that need attention and better understanding.  New social actors are becoming involved in resource management. New types of benefits for rights-holders, such as payments for environmental services and results-based payments for REDD+, are stimulating reformulations and expansionsinthe types of property rights that matter (differentiate use rights, control rights and authoritative rights).

This initiative aims to develop a new analytical framework for understanding the issues of property and resource rights in the context of integrated landscape management, and to propose strategies to address them inform in more effective and equitable ways.

The specific objectivesare to:
1) Develop a framework for understanding and analyzing issues related to land and resource rights within landscape mosaics where there is strong interaction and interdependencies among different land uses and land users;
2) Evaluate opportunities and tradeoffs associated with evolving rights;
3) Identify innovative solutions and potential strategies foraddressing key issues;
4) Identify priority research questions that should be explored moving forward.

title: OPDP #OurLandOurRight Kenya
description:
Following an eight-year legal battle, the Court#s judgment finally provides a long awaited unique opportunity for enforcing the respect of the human rights of the Ogiek as well as other minority and indigenous peoples (MIPs) in Kenya, by securing their access to productive resources (land <(>&<)> water mainly), as well as by fostering space for their political participation.
The first ever indigenous community rights decision of 26 May 2017, the Court formally recognised the importance of respecting indigenous communities# land rights in Africa by ruling that the Ogiek's right to their ancestral lands, and linked cultural and religious rights among others, had been violated by the Government of Kenya as a result of decades of evictions in the name of conservation. As such, the ruling provides a unique opportunity for the Ogiek to secure the recognition of their rights violated until now and in partnership withother indigenous communities in Kenya and Africa to pursue changes in the law, policy and practice governing the rights of indigenous peoples and natural resources, especially when linked to conservation building upon this historical precedent.
In these favourable circumstances and within the first 12 months following the ruling, the project will ensure the rapid and effective implementation of such an exceptional decision by collectively engaging and mobilising all key identified stakeholders, to (i) facilitate and prepare the ground for the Court's forthcoming reparations order and (ii) to initiate the enforcement of the ruling, to monitor the firststeps of its implementation and pave the way for it to benefit other Minority and Indigenous communities (MIPs) in Kenya and acrossAfrica facing similar issues.

title: EWB Integrated WASH & Protection
description: EWB-USA will provide technical support for challenging locations in Imvepi, Rhino and Omugo in Arua and Kyaka II in Kyegegwa District that do not fit within the parameters of the standardized design and technical advisory as requested for engineering that lies outside of the parameters of the Ministry's current capacity. New systems installed will be assisted through the provision of this set of standards and guidelines offering design and material recommendations to all the WASH sector stakeholders that will permit consistency and reliability in the water supply. Once design standards are in place, installation guidelines will be created, a section on design variables included, and an O<(>&<)>M package in alignment with the MWE-led consultancy on O<(>&<)>M results, disseminated tofacilitate the sustainability of the systems designed. Training will be conducted across the sector and on an ongoing basis through technical support from the MoWE and partner institutions. EWB-USA has been invited in the end of 2018 by UNHCR, OPM and Ministry of Water and Environment to conduct a thorough review of existing systems in refugee settlements with a focus on optimization and standardization amongst water scheme design and installation. participating_orgs:
Oxfam Novib / NL-KVK-27108436 / 2 | ENGINEERS WITHOUT BORDERS-USA,INC | In April 2000, Dr. Bernard Amadei, professor of civil engineering at the University of Colorado Boulder, visited a community in SanPablo, Belize, to assess their water supply. He learned that the 950 Mayan Indians living in the heart of the Belize jungle lacked clean water and sanitation infrastructure, and that most of the community#s children did not attend school because their time was dedicated to collecting water from miles away.
While the community had the natural resources and motivation to build a reliable water supply system, they lacked the technical skills to design a lasting solution. Professor Amadei went home and consulted colleagues onpotential solutions, then returned to the community with a prototype and fourteen of his students to put the plan into action. The team installed a clean water system supplied and powered by a waterfall a quarter-mile from the community. This simple and low-cost solution was the first EWB-USA project!
Dr. Amadei continued to harness the power of professional and student engineers to complete similar low-tech, high-impact projects in other developing countries by officially founding Engineers Without Borders USA in 2002. Since then, EWB-USA has grown from a handful of passionate individuals to an organization of more than 14,100 passionate members working on hundreds of engineering projects across the globe.
2. ACHIEVEMENTS
What have been the principal results in the past three years that contribute to significant, structural, sustained and positive improvement in the lives of men, women, girls and boys suffering from poverty, injustice, insecurity and exclusion?
Well Repair in Arid Ethiopia
In 2016, Ethiopia#s Afar and Bale regions suffered a severe drought due to the effects of El Niño. Hundreds of thousands of livestock died from lack of food and water, leaving communities food-insecure, malnourished and vulnerable. In collaboration with Project Concern International, ESC provided technical assistance to the Ethiopia Emergency Drought Response and Rehabilitation (ENDURE) project. Over the course of one month, volunteer engineers repaired 35 wells and restored water access to more than 100,000 people.
Water Access for Expectant Mothers in Rural Malawi
It is illegal to give birth at home in Malawi -- a law that was put in place in 2007 to lower the country's maternal mortality rate. In rural Malawi, mothers-to-be spend their final weeks of pregnancy at maternal waiting shelters near health clinics. These shelters are key elements of a safer environment for women to give birth, but often lack basic infrastructure. In summer 2017, ESC partnered with Freshwater Project International to improve the water systems at six health centers. Volunteer engineers designed and implementedsustainable solutions including solar-powered pumps and new taps, providing health workers and pregnant women with reliable, easy access to life-saving water.

Building Climate Resilience Through Innovative Technology
As climate change continues to stress water tables across the world, communities in India are digging deeper wells to access water. These deeper wells are often contaminated with toxic levels of minerals, including harmful levels of fluoride. ESC has partnered with the IKEA Foundation and the Clinton Health Access Initiative on a climate adaption project. Our engineers will identify the best technology to filter out harmful levels of fluoride and assist in the construction of water ATMs. This project provides the communities of Dhar, India, with fluoride-free water and entrepreneurs with a business model to generate income.
Highlights
Household Connections in Ghana
More than 10 million people in Ghana lack access to clean water. Safe Water Network requested the technical expertise of ESC to launch a water system with household connections in the Tongor and Ashanti regions. Household connections are critical; they improve water quality for families, increase the amount of safe water consumed, and strengthen the financial proposition of water supply by increasing revenue. This collaboration will also build local NGO capacity, equipping more organizations to implement household connections across tens of thousands ofhouseholds in Ghana.

3.    INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE
Mission:

EWB-USA builds a better world through engineering projects that empowercommunities to meet their basic human needs and equip leaders to solve the world#s most pressing challenges.

Institutional objectives:

# Increase EWB-USA#s impact by increasing the number of communities served, domestically and internationally, while still ensuring quality outcomes.
# Establish lasting partnerships with the critical stakeholders in the communities where we work: community leaders, community-based organizations, local government organizationsand non-governmental organizations.
# Build collaborative relationships with the larger development and engineering communities: universities, industry professionals, corporations, donors, non-governmental organizations and governmental organizations

Field(s) of activity: What are the principal thematic and geographic areas in which the organisation works?  Who are the social actors that benefit from the work?
EWB-USA works in 47 countries around the world, with 3 established country offices in the core regions of central America and East Africa. We aim to strengthen our work in these core regions with a particular focus on East Africa over the next 3-5 years. Engineering solutions are relevant across most sectors however our work focuses on WASH, Energy, Environment, Structures and Agriculture.

title: CEFORD Integrated WASH & Protection
description: Protection Risks: The refugee influx has created pressure on existing resources and has risked co-existence between refugees and nationals. Generally, nationals view refugees as being favoured than hosts. On the other hand, there is also reluctance by refugees toshare resources. Conflicts have been registered particularly at water points. The UNHCR Joint Multi tor Needs Assessment (JMSNA, August 2018) shows that refugee households were concerned about harassment (19%) and attacks (18%) from the host community, although less than from within their own community. Amidst these potentials of conflict, support to ensure social cohesion is critical. According to the JMSNA (August 2018), households categorized as in need of protection and vulnerable were foundto be 35% and 53% in Arua (Imvepi and Rhino) for host Community and Refugee households respectively. The major indicators driving vulnerability for households categorized as PSN was having two or more vulnerable household members and being headed by a single female. Lack of access to sanitary materials for households with women and girls of reproductive age was the primary indicator driving categorisation of PSNs for both refugee and host community households. It further established that 40% and 66% of host community and refugee households categorised as in need of protection are in  39% in Arua. Community consultations and feedback meetings with Oxfam and partner's volunteers and staff in Imvepi and Rhino settlements have severally indicated lack of lighting at water points to be exposing refugee women, girls and host community to further protection risks and threats when they go for water late (avoiding queues in the day). This has increased chances of being attacked at night while especially women return from collecting firewood, water and food. Additionally, capacity to address protection mainstreaming and conflict prevention is still limited across all settlements. Local community structuresare particularly less empowered to pay attention to the risks around provision of WASH services. Such gaps do not facilitate conflict reduction initiatives. CEFORD is  the leading local actors in humanitarian protection work. They sit in sector working groups to influence the agenda. The organizations also mitigate conflicts on resource sharing by empowering community structures to address conflicts using informal justice mechanisms and peaceful conflict resolution.

Oxfam Novib / NL-KVK-27108436 / 2 | COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT FOR RURAL DEV | The history of Community Empowerment for Rural Development (CEFORD) dates back to 1993 when the Uganda government, with the financial and technical support of the Dutch government, implemented the Community Action Program (CAP) and later the Women Empowerment Program (WEP) in the West Nile region. Both programs were considered successes by the communities and district local governments of West Nile, and external evaluators and the Dutch embassy in Uganda. The focus was on community mobilisation and capacity building through service delivery and the implementation of micro-projects. CAP concentrated on the supply of social infrastructure services and the implementation of agricultural projects, while WEP concentrated on the empowerment of women and the strengthening of their capacities to participate in the development process.
Thus CEFORD was founded, to fill the gap created by the closure of these successful programs that were phased out in June 2000. CEFORD operates in parts of all the five districts of Adjumani, Arua, Moyo, Nebbi and Yumbe.
It was founded in July 2000 but the process of its formation dates back to 1998, to an internal reflection workshop of CAP staff that identified possible scenarios for the future. One scenario suggested a merger of CAP and WEP into a local NGO.
The decentralisation of government to districts in Uganda also demanded strong civil society organisations that could support local governments indelivering services.
CEFORD's major achievements in the last three years include a participatory poverty assessment in the districts of Arua and Nebbi. Through these assessments CEFORD gave objective feedback from poor women and men to the district and central governments, and to some donor.
It was also successful in supporting the Adjumani district local government in facilitating the formulation of all its sub-county development plans. This enhanced its chance of accessing funds from the central government, from which the communities would benefit.
And CEFORD strengthened the capacities of four local organisations through organisational self-assessment and the facilitation of strategic planning. The performance of these organisations has since improved. It also mobilised and linked ten community-based organisations to funding for agricultural activities; over 30 million Ugandan shillings from the German Development Services.
CEFORD's Mission is to improve the capacity of women, men, children and their organisations in the more disadvantaged communities of West Nile effectively to articulate their demands and interests, to increase their production and income in a sustainable way and to secure better access to services.
The institutional objectives of CEFORD are to contribute to the following policy and practice changes in West Nile: food and income security is guaranteed, communities have positive attitude to the enrolment and retention of girls in schools, there is active participation of the population in district and sub-county planning and policy formulation (especially around issues of natural resources, peace and security),  peace and security in the region are consolidated especially at the household level, and women are empowered to participate as equal partners to men in decision-making and control over resources at the household and community levels. / 4 | European Union / 1 | Oxfam Novib / NL-KVK-27108436 / 3

title: True Value Accounting: Making the Economic Case for Food Systems Transformation in India and Kenya
description:
The overall aim of this project aims to contribute to food systems transformation in the two countries in scope (India and Kenya) by making the economic case for pro-nature policies that provide sustainable livelihoods and for enhanced community cohesion.
UNEP has a comparative advantage in the economics of food system transformation owing to its hosting The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB) initiative launched at the G8+5 Potsdam Meeting of Environment Ministers in 2007. TEEB has developed the TEEBAgriFood Evaluation Framework that provides a comprehensive and universal approach to capture all the impacts and dependencies on nature. The Framework was recognized with the Future Policy Vision Award 2018, awarded by the World Future Council in partnership with FAO and IFOAM – Organics International. The TEEBAgriFood policy implementations (country- and firm-level) are to be included in the upcoming 2023 FAO State of Food and Agriculture (SOFA) report on True Value Accounting. UNEP has been at the forefront of both developing a Framework for assessment with the input of >100 researchers from over 40 countries, as well as showing that implementation can achieve policy impacts. For instance, the TEEBAgriFood analysis on cacao agroforestry contributed to the recent inclusion of agroforestry (for the first time) in the Five-Year Midterm Development Plan for Indonesia.
The core value hypothesis is as follows: (i) there are myriad positive and negative impacts and dependencies across the agri-food value chain that routinely and systematically are neither recognized nor captured in decision-making, and yet they contribute to the economy and to livelihoods; (ii) by evaluating and then valuing these impacts and dependencies an economic case can be made for pro-nature policy interventions.
The project will contribute to UNEP’s work on food systems transformation embedded in the programme of Mainstreaming Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Across Sectors and Systems. Specifically, with reference to PoW Indicator N.(iii), Number of countries and national, regional, and subnational authorities and entities that incorporate, with UNEP support biodiversity and ecosystem-based approaches into development and sectoral plans, policies and processes for the sustainable management and/or restoration of terrestrial, freshwater and marine areas. This project will work at State-level in India and County Council-level in Kenya to incorporate, with UNEP support, biodiversity and ecosystem-based approaches that apply economic valuation into development and sectoral plans, policies and processes for the sustainable management of agricultural landscapes. This contributes to MTS Outcome 2A: An economically and socially sustainable pathway for halting and reversing the loss of biodiversity and ecosystem integrity is established and Outcome 2B Sustainable management of nature adopted and implemented in development frameworks.
On project sustainability, UNEP would aim to incubate and foster networks/opportunities that will be complementary to the ongoing projects in the regions –implemented either by UNEP or by IKEA Foundation. In addition to that, an exit strategy will be designed during an inception phase and implemented before the end of the project in each of the project areas. An example of this comes from the recently completed IKI-funded TEEBAgriFood work in Kenya. The communities are now better organized owing to the UNEP project and are still actively involved with the County Councils in steering County Integrated Development Plans. A community-led and community-owned enterprise called the Mau Mara Natural Capital Company was established during project implementation and is still active, now working with Absa Bank in Kenya among others to secure financing.
This project will develop proof of concept of how to mainstream evidence into public and private decision making to invest on food systems to become more sustainable. This will bring lessons learned for other states and countries to replicate and hence have a bigger impact.

description: The project supports the housing restoration and re-building shelters among the families whose houses were fully submerged and or sunk by the water flooding. The availability of shelter will improve the mental health and general well-being of families supported. The children from such families will be able to attend school in peace as there will be great convenience due to enhanced social family fabrics. The project enhances participation of its beneficiaries at all stages including planning.
results_text: Activity website

title: Help 1,000 babies reach their 5th birthday - Kenya
description: This project will support women to give birth safely and have access to essential services ensuring their baby will survive and thrive to celebrate their 5th birthday.  COVID-19 has reversed progress made in supporting mothers and babies in poor and marginalised communities in Kericho County, Kenya.  Inaccessible health services, fear of COVID-19, lack of soap and water has increased unsupervised home births which risk the lives of mothers and babies.  Help us reverse this trend.
results_text: Activity website

title: Empower 1500 Orphan & Vulnerable Children in Kenya
description: This project will provide   food, Sanitary towels, inner wears, Hygiene items, hand washing Systems,face mask, build empowerment center, training, clean water, guidance and counselling  to 1500 Orphan and Vulnerable children  subjected  sexual abuse,child labour and psychological stress in Kenya. The emergence of COVID-19 has compelled impoverished girls to indulge in sex in exchange for food, sanitary towels resulting to child pregnancies and  child marriages, STIs and HIV/AIDs infections.
results_text: Activity website

title: Moringa for Health and Water Purification
description: Moringa for Health and Water Purification project will provide 500 Community Members from Tharaka Nithi County with 50 Moringa tree each to plant on their farms. Planting these high yield trees will go a long way to address malnutrition and contaminated water in Tharaka Nithi County.
results_text: Activity website

title: ENHANCE ACCESS TO CLEAN WATER & SANITATION
description: Water and sanitation are essential for life and health, but they are also essential for a dignified life, empowerment and prosperity. Water and sanitation are human rights, fundamental to every human life. In Kenya, poor sanitation and hygiene as well as unequal access to safe drinking water, in the informal settlements, slums and the rural villages, make thousands of children very sick and at risk of death. Many households spend thousands of shillings in and out of hospital every other day.
results_text: Activity website

title: Educate a child from Kibagare Slum at St Martins
description: St Martins School is an oasis where 777 primary and almost 250 high school girls receive daily food, clean water, education, computer access, and guidance.  We are a non-profit and we rely on charitable donations to fund our activities. Our goal is to provide education with sponsorships to all our students and as many children from the Kibagare slum as possible. In communities like ours, one in five high school-aged girls are in school and we wish to bridge this for the good of this community.
results_text: Activity website

title: Invest in Menstrual Health for girls and women
description: This project supports young girls to remain in school and graduate. It also delivers a Community Menstrual Health programme through our trained Ambassadors to both men and women through education, eradication of myths and taboos, provision of reusable sanitary pads, access to clean water, handwashing facilities, and safe reliable washrooms in schools.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean water for 442 households in Kenya
description: Clean water is essential for good health.  Right now 55% of households across Kericho county, Kenya have to use dirty water from rivers and ponds.  Access to clean water and good sanitation is a basic human right.  This project will support 2 key areas - protection schemes for 4 natural spring water sources serving 442 households with a population of 2,260 and protecting childrens' health in over 300 schools through provision of rain water harvesting, toilets and handwashing stations.
results_text: Activity website

title: Keep 300 schools in rural Kenya safe from COVID-19
description: Children do not have access to basic handwashing facilities in school like clean, running water and soap.  How can they be protected from COVID-19 transmission when schools don't have these basics?  This project supports 300 schools across Kericho county to create a clean, safe environment for children with rain water harvesting, handwashing stations, improved toilets, hygiene education and teacher training.  Over 104,000 boys and girls will stay healthy and stay in school.
results_text: Activity website

title: Empower 1500 Orphan &Vulnerable Children in Kenya
description: This project will provide   food, Sanitary towels, inner wears, Hygiene items, hand washing Systems,face mask, build empowerment center, training, clean water, guidance and counselling  to 1500 Orphan and Vulnerable children  subjected  sexual abuse,child labour and psychological stress in Kenya. The emergence of COVID-19 has compelled impoverished girls to indulge in sex in exchange for food, sanitary towels resulting to child pregnancies and  child marriages, STIs and HIV/AIDs infections.
results_text: Activity website

title: Protect Kenyan girls from Gender-Based Violence
description: Imagine being afraid to fetch water or being forced to marry instead of going to school. In Kenya we are building a community resource center to protect girls from Gender-Based Violence (GBV). It will house and educate 30 girls who have survived GBV and host our afterschool program designed to prevent GBV and keep 100s of girls safe and in school. We are now raising funds to complete construction of the resource center, where we will be able to serve the community for years to come.
results_text: Activity website

title: CLUB 10 INITIATIVE: Clean Water and Sanitation
description: Hifadhi Africa Organization is launching CLUB 10, a new monthly giving community that invites donations of just $10 monthly. This budget-friendly entry point recognizes that even those who might not have much to give can still play an important role in supporting the cause of clean water for all under SDG 6. While $10 monthly may not seem much, over a year's time, this grows to $120 and provide at least one person with reliable water access for an entire year.
results_text: Activity website

title: Sand Dams, Climate Change, and Hope
description: A sand dam is a reinforced concrete wall built on bedrock across a seasonal sandy river to collect water and sand during the rainy season and store it for use during the dry season. When it rains, the dam captures soil-laden water behind it - the sand in the water sinks to the bottom, whilst the silt remains suspended in the water. HAO has found sand dams to be the most cost-effective method of water harvesting, conservation and recharging in dry land and very remote environments.
results_text: Activity website

title: CLEAN WATER ACCESS AT THE CENTRE OF LOVE KIBERA
description: The Centre of Love's sustainable WASH project has made a great impact! Minimizing the spread of disease throughout the pandemic 500 households and 3000 community members access water at a reduced price and our water champions promote the values of clean water, sanitation and hygiene.  Our water storage tanks provide water when the Nairobi water supply is rationed. Improved water pipes, an upgrade to our purified water systems, and a closer line will assist in meeting additional water needs.
results_text: Activity website

title: Train 50 youth in rural Kenya in Agribusiness
description: The COVID 19 situation has worsened Kenya's endemic problem of youth unemployment. As a result, many young people have become disillusioned and hopeless, and have turned to crime and drug abuse. CORAT Africa will train 100 unemployed youth from rural Kenya who have unused family land for Agribusiness ventures. The youth will also be provided with rainwater harvesting tanks and farm inputs so that they can make a living selling agricultural products.
results_text: Activity website

title: Provide clean water to over 1800 Nyamongeans
description: This project drills a bore hole, installs a submersible water pump, a water tower, constructs a digital kiosk, and water bottling plant, to provide clean safe drinking water to 1200 students/pupils, 100 staff and about 500 villagers in the drought-stricken Nyamonge Community.
results_text: Activity website

title: Help us build a Fence to Protect our Water Well
description: This project will build a fence to protect our water well at Scotty's Rescue Centre. Our water well is crucial in making Scotty's a self-sustainable Rescue Centre for the women and children currently living on the streets of Nairobi. By selling the water, the local rural communities will also have access to this vital resource. The fence is a vital means of protecting the well, building our fence will push us further along our mission of completing Scotty's Rescue Centre.
results_text: Activity website

title: Help Baran, a four-year-old Chimpanzee!
description: Please help us support Baran, a four-year-old chimpanzee who arrived at Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary in July 2021. She was born prematurely in Eram Zoo and once her mother died, it became impossible for her to integrate with the other chimpanzees and so she was moved to a cage for her protection. She was brought to the Sanctuary, to live a better life and we cannot wait to help her settle in.
results_text: Activity website

title: Provide Clean Water for a School in Gilgil, Kenya
description: This project will provide the Morop Mixed Day Secondary School with a new 10,000 liter water tank that will supply clean and safe water to the children and the surrounding community.  This will increase the retention of students in school.  Having clean water reduces student absence due to infection from water borne diseases.  With clean water, the school can implement a tree planting program as well as kitchen gardens which can augment the lunch program.
results_text: Activity website

title: Breaking The Bias with International Women's Day
description: Our project helps women of all ages to challenge gender equality and break the bias in rural Kenya. Supporting girls to stay in school and graduate, offering an alternative to FGM, delivering a sexual and reproductive health programme with trained Ambassadors, providing access to sanitary pads, clean water, hand washing facilities, health centres equipped with trained staff & maternal health services, trainings on life skills and creating a sustainable income, ensuring all voices are heard.
results_text: Activity website

title: Beautification & Greening of schools in Kenya
description: The Mabati Technical Training Institute is planning to harvest and store rainwater during the upcoming rainy season in September to store over 1,500,000 litres of water. The dam measuring 1059 cubic metres if repaired with High-density polyethylene (HDPE), can last between 10 to 30 years & supply enough water to irrigate our kitchen garden to produce  vegetables to support our school feeding program and to  educate our youth  on the importance of environmental conservation  and tree planting.
results_text: Activity website

title: East Africa Food Crisis
description: The Horn of Africa is facing one of the worst droughts on record with some 14 million people in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Somaliland facing severe hunger and water shortages. ActionAid is working with local partners to provide food relief.
results_text: Activity website

title: East Africa Hunger Relief Fund
description: Across East Africa, millions of people are facing famine. Climate-crisis-induced drought, regional and local conflict, and long-reaching impacts of the war in Ukraine and COVID-19 are creating a dire situation in multiple countries, including Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan. Your donation to the East Africa Hunger Relief Fund will provide emergency relief, food, water, medicine, and other essential supplies to people in need.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean Water for the Watha
description: Access to clean water is a major issue for the Watha people. Although there is a constant threat of crocodile attacks as well as the possibility of contracting cholera and typhoid, the only option for many Watha is to collect water from nearby contaminated rivers. The Watha Project, working with village elders and volunteers, will construct a fifth well to provide clean and safe water to hundreds of Watha and provide water and health education to all, drastically improving their quality of life.
results_text: Activity website

title: Sustainable and key support for Kibagare Community
description: St Martins School and the Kibagare Community, Nilinde Nijijenge aims to support a sustainable community and in doing so enable this Community to maintain the support that they give.  Working and focussing on those most in need and those who can be enabled.  By creating self-sufficiency across households, we are improving the community in itself.  Kenya is enduring its worst drought in 40 years.  Food and water shortages, coupled with skyrocketing prices are hard-hitting in slum communities
results_text: Activity website

title: Kibagare Pad Project - Giving women Dignity
description: Many women and girls in our community struggle with coping with their monthly periods. Many have no access to sanitary pads or clean water, and are faced with taboos and customs that discourage and or look down on issues relating to the menstrual cycle every month. Kibagare Pad Project aims to bring Compostible Sanitary Pads to the community and help educate, support and guide women, not only with their monthly cycle, but also with female health, education and provide Dignity Packs.
results_text: Activity website

title: Clean Water & Food Forest for 300+ Kenyan children
description: This project will provide plentiful water, hygiene facilities and plant a food forest at Elong'o primary school pupils and staff can easily grow their own food.  With access to clean water, children will no longer have to carry jerrycans of water to school. Illness and disease will be reduced with improved hygiene facilities.  The forest will invigorate the barren landscape around the school, provide the children with a more varied diet, and provide an income source to the school.
results_text: Activity website

title: SOLVE WATER PROBLEM FOR CHILDREN WITH DYSLEXIA
description: This project provides clean water for 250 children with dyslexia and other neurobiological disorders at Rare Gem Talent School. Sinking a borehole will provide running water to ensure a hygienic environment and prevent the children from contracting cholera which has already been reported in the neighborhood.  The water will serve the school and the community around it.
results_text: Activity website

title: Help floods victims in Nyalenda KENYA.
description: Nyalenda community sits in Kisumu  county which is one of the 47 counties within Kenya. Nyalenda  has a population of around 100,000 people who lives in the slums and who lives below a dollar a day. Due to heavy rains this year most houses have been marooned in flood waters. The area has been experiencing  perennial  flooding and people have been displaced each and every year. The women and children and elderly living in the slums have been displaced hence needs urgent interventions.
results_text: Activity website

title: Food Security for 500 families in WestPokot Kenya
description: West Pokot is an Arid Land of Kenya, where the drought has devastating effects on the livelihoods of the rural communities. CEFA supports resilience-building through training on modern beekeeping and beehives distribution for 50 beekeepers, construction of 1 honey processing unit and beehives carpentry, training on nutrition sensitive agriculture and distribution of drought-resistant seeds for 100 farmers, construction of 5 water points in 5 villages for 250 households and their livestock.
results_text: Activity website

title: Protect our ocean & safeguard livelihoods in Kenya
description: Life on the Kenyan coast is precarious. Overfishing has severely depleted local waters, and the local community, who rely on this essential food source, are working hard to improve and increase local marine biodiversity, whilst ensuring they can still source food to eat and earn a living.
results_text: Activity website

title: Borehill Drilling
description: Clean Water in Nakuru, Kenya, is a vital resource that brings not only health but also hope and numerous opportunities. We are striving to drill a 250-meter borehole, which requires $12000. We need $4000 to fulfill this project. Once completed, water availability will pave the way for transformative initiatives such as our ecosystem farm, livestock ventures, trade school, and the upliftment of the local community. With your support, we can provide clean water.
results_text: Activity website

title: Empower children in poverty with healthcare access
description: Poverty has many faces. Sometimes they're obvious: sunken cheek bones, bodies maligned from malnourishment and harsh living conditions. But often, poverty shows itself in what we don't see: the energy to dance or run across a sports field, plates of food at mealtimes, or clean water in cups. These examples point to the same truth: a lack of healthcare access is both a cause and an effect of poverty, keeping those affected trapped within its vicious cycle. We're on a mission to break it.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Sumba Water Supply
description:
In Kaksingri valley in the nearby areas to Sumba West in Suba District Kenya there are today five boreholes for water. People who fetch water from these boreholes have increased as well as the consumption of water. There has occationally been some small fi
ghting incidents for water close to the waterstations mainly because of long queues. One of the boreholes is nearby the Rukongo Youth Polytechnic (RYP) since the mid 1980-ties. Water at this borehole is pumped with solarenergypowered waterpumps and is led 
to a tank where villagers are pumping water manually.  Sumba village at about 15 kilometers away lacks its own well for water and the school children at Sumba School are carrying water from home to school water which sometimes is of poor quality. This affe
cts the health of the children and their possibility to concentrate  and eventually on their school results. The cattle is walking up to 15 kilometers every day during dryseason to drink water. The area is very hilly has significant elevation differences w
hich is consuming energy and time to fetch water. Sumba area also lacks water places for cattle. For this purpose the villagers are today referred to the nearby Lake Victoria that lies at distance of about seven kilometers from the village. The long walk f
or water makes the livestock less productive.   By drilling deep for water and building infrastructure for a couple of new waterstations as well as a drinkingplace for cattle at about 1-15 kilometers from the closest borehole and uphills on the slope in th
e Sumba village these problems may be solved for a long time.    The borehole will according to the plan be drilled close to the Sumba Primary School. Water will be pumped with solarenergy from the borehole to two diffrerent watertanks with handpumps one o
n the school compound and the other one just next to the borehole where the villagers can fetch water. The pupils may use water during daytime and also bring some along with them when they return home after the school day is over.    Water is pumped with a
 handpump from one of the tanks and is led through a channel to a drinking place for cattle. Overflow water may also form from the pumpingplaces. Since water is pumped authomatically from the borehole as long as sun is shining (daylight) there might at tim
es be an overflow. All overflow water will be led to a drinkingplace for cattle.
participating_orgs: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland / FI-3 / 1 | Svenska Lutherska Evangeliforeningen i Finland rf / 22000 / 3

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Local Cooperation Fund (LCF) in Kenya
description:
Hurinet made remarkable progress in its previous project implementation activities ranging from peace building and human rights promotion training workshops which were able to avert electoral violence during parliamentary and presidential elections through
 dialogues involving political parties CSOs students and faith based institutions. Through exchange programme the member organizations were able to get exposure to new practices approaches and methodologies applied in other countries in peace building and 
human rights promotion. The strategic meetings strengthened networks of members through collective agenda setting regarding the discourse on peace human rights and contribution to national reconciliation and transitional justice processes that will soon cu
lminate into national laws and policies.There is increased lack of respect for rule of law witnessed by regular interference by the executive in decision making processes at the expense of other arms of government. Land disputes and utilization of natural 
resources and revenues still persists despite repeated calls for transparency and accountability. Ethnic conflict still continues to be witnessed in Karamoja region due to water and pasture as well as small arms proliferation despite the disarmament exerci
se being undertaken. The above situation creates a future of uncertainty and if not handled well and mitigated the effects will degenerate to the old time where there was massive abuse of human rights and use of violence to resolve conflicts in Uganda. Les
sons learnt from the previuos project reveal the need to build the capacity of CSOs in early warning and conflict trasformation through trainings and development of innovative tools mechanism and structures. However amidst the achievemnets the situation in
 the country seem to be getting back to the post colonial days with increased post election tensions and violence that calls for dialogue among different stakeholder. The project plans to implement a number of activities through three strategic objectives,
 1) to enhance capacity of CSOs and communities to effectively utilize the early warning mechanism for crisis prevention and peaceful conflict resolution,  2) to promote dialogue with government and other relevant stakeholders to support appropriate soluti
ons to emarging threats, 3) to enhance effective collaboration and networking among the civil society organizations and the grassroot communities for sustainable peace.
participating_orgs: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland / FI-3 / 1 | Embassy of Finland / 11000 / 3

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Kenya: Refocusing small arms interventions on impact: Connecting global policy to community driven approaches to security
description:
At a formal level Kenya qualifies as a champion of SALW control. However there is ample evidence that international and national SALW interventions and goals in Kenya have not  addressed the problem sufficiently locally especially in pastoralist areas wher
e communities who are nomadic have to seek out and share limited pasture and water resources bringing them into conflict with each other. The intention is to help communities achieve their rights to security currently under threat from the proliferation an
d misuse of small arms and light weapons (SALW) by ensuring that the communities themselves are at the heart of the prioritisation planning implementation and monitoring and evaluation of the programme.  As well as being of immediate benefit to the target 
communities by developing credible evidence from these practical efforts the programme also intends to inform national and international processes. Across two locations in Kenya this project aims to address some of the factors contributing to insecurity wi
th a view to make a positive contribution to meeting the national development agenda under the following areas: 1.Enhancement of security along the borders to address proliferation of small arms across the borders, 2.Institutionalising national and inter-c
ommunity dialogue in order to build harmony among ethnic racial and other interest groups, 3.Deepening policy legal and institutional reform for improved enforcement of law and order. During the two yearlong project several seminars forums and workshops wi
ll be organized on security and monitoring the use of SALW for both local people and authorities. Theinteraction between local population and local authorities will be strengthened. The aim is also to develop locally ways to reduce the proliferation and mi
suse of SALW. During the program interaction between the local beneficiaries and international experts on SALW will be organized. The program will be implemented by an NGO spezialized on arms control with close cooperation with local Kenyan partners. http:
//www.saferworld.org.uk/where/kenya
participating_orgs: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland / FI-3 / 1 | Other INGO / 21000 / 3

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Local Cooperation Fund (LCF) in Kenya
description:
The peace building and conflict resolution project targets marginalized pastoralist community groups of Kenya-Ethiopia border. Pastoralist Community Development Organization has four major thematic areas that mainly target the marginalized groups, the them
atic areas are capacity building democracy good governance HIV/AIDS Environment and gender as cross cutting themes in the programs.  The region has been living under time bombs due to historical injustices and insecurity. The problems in the northern Kenya
 are anchored in the poor participation of the communities in the development agendas conflict and tension over resources insecurity among ethnic tribes and boarder countries influx of cheap and sophisticated weapons from the porous borders of Ethiopia Som
alia and Sudan. This includes continous aimless killings invasions poor economic infrastructure unequal or poor distribution of resources lack of adequate water pasture and grazing boundaries. The peace-building and reconciliation project targets the ethni
c groups of seven districts in Marsabit county and the Kenya- Ethiopia boarder communities. The project will empower and prepare communities and groups towards lasting sustainable peace and coexistence of communities based on their face-to-face discussed a
nd debated facts truths concerns and issues towards realization of peaceful co-existence.

description:
Integrated Water Resource Management including Sanitation & Hygiene | Sustainable  Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services through Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) is the ultimate goal of Watershed. title: Frame Agreement with NGO (Foundation for Human Rights/KIOS)
description:
The evaluation of legislation of ESC rights, Public interest litigation, advocacy , the organization's support . Hakijamii, in its project, focuses on the right to health, water and sanitation, and implementations of these rights. The Constitution defines 
the part of health care as a fundamental right for all citizens, but especially among the poor the unavailability of services is a major problem. The development process of the nationwide network of water distribution network, in turn, has suffered from in
efficiency, corruption and mismanagement. One of the downturn was, when  along with the Water Act in the 2002, the water privatizations occurred. From the lack of clean water and sanitation suffer both rural and urban slums, and in particular the marginali
zed groups. Kenya's estimated population of 42 million, about 30% now live in cities, and the urbanization is rapid. Slums have been incorporated into urban planning and budgeting, and residents have very little chance of the health, education and other ba
sic services. It is estimated that only 20 per cent of slum residents have the opportunity to have permanently clean water and slum residents also pay out of the water several times more compared to other residents. The project aims to promote economic and
 social rights implementation. The aim is both to improve the State's procedures for new policies and legislation, as well as through the adoption of improving the economic and social rights, the implementation of fundamental rights through the bringing of
 the action. The project beneficiaries are the most vulnerable groups whose needs are taken into account in the content promoted laws, women, the elderly, the disabled, children, young people and minorities, and other vulnerable groups. Hakijamii was found
ed in 2004 to fill the gap in Kenya to deal between the organizations, which focuses on the human rights field, and on the other hand the organizations that handle the economic and social problems in a non-legal perspective.

title: Promoting Eco-sanitation and Water Services in People?s Settlements in Kibera and Mukuru ? Nairobi Kenya ? Phase II
description:
With a population approaching 3 million Nairobi is rapidly urbanizing and the peoples? settlements increasingly characterized by exclusion overcrowding and insalubrious conditions. Kibera and Mukuru as all of Nairobi?s informal and unplanned settlements ha
ve limited access to sanitation facilities and water primarily due to lack of vehicular access and difficulty in establishing formalized water pipes or sewers. Most residents do not have access to adequate sanitation thus relying on filled-up latrines or o
pen spaces and further increasing the thriving occurrence of water borne diseases.The  overall objective of the proposed project is to increase the use of eco-friendly sanitation technologies and their by-products  for improved health and livelihoods in th
e informal settlements of Kibera and Mukuru by means of  improved management of human waste  increased access to sanitation services and safe water and improved community health.  The project continues to build on the ecological sanitation facilities const
ructed in Phase I (bio-center and UDDTs) thus supporting existing structures but adding a new concept of closing the sanitation circle by focusing on end-use and marketing of the final products.The objective will be achieved through:a) Research development
 and marketing of by-products i.e. bio-gas from the bio-center and urine and compost from the composting latrinesb) Construction of one bio-center with water kioskc) Developing the capacity of community-based resource persons and artisans in the design pla
nning and sustenance of ecological sanitation servicesd) Implementing a sanitation marketing process which embraces interactive hygiene promotion tools and methodse) Business development services share-holding in water and sanitation and participation in c
ommunity-managed water and sanitation financing facilityThe project will directly benefit 1500 users from the new and the already existing bio-centre as well as the  pupils and teachers using composting latrines primarily through access to improved sanitat
ion facilities, increase in artisan skills for 100 people increased hygiene promotion through 60 trained ToTs, and income generation from the sale of by-products and wages paid to the artisans. Equal access will be available to women men children and the d
isabled with efforts made to enhance gender equality and reduce inequalities among beneficiaries.
participating_orgs: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland / FI-3 / 1 | Finnish NGO, Wimma liikuttaa sinuakin ry / 22000 / 3

title: Pastoralist Community Development Organization - Peace building and conflict resolution in Marsabit County
description:
The peace building and conflict resolution project targets marginalized pastoralist community groups of Kenya-Ethiopia border. Pastoralist Community Development Organization has four major thematic areas that mainly target the marginalized groups, the them
atic areas are capacity building democracy good governance HIV/AIDS Environment and gender as cross cutting themes in the programs.  The region has been living under time bombs due to historical injustices and insecurity. The problems in the northern Kenya
 are anchored in the poor participation of the communities in the development agendas conflict and tension over resources insecurity among ethnic tribes and boarder countries influx of cheap and sophisticated weapons from the porous borders of Ethiopia Som
alia and Sudan. This includes continous aimless killings invasions poor economic infrastructure unequal or poor distribution of resources lack of adequate water pasture and grazing boundaries. The peace-building and reconciliation project targets the ethni
c groups of seven districts in Marsabit county and the Kenya- Ethiopia boarder communities. The project will empower and prepare communities and groups towards lasting sustainable peace and coexistence of communities based on their face-to-face discussed a
nd debated facts truths concerns and issues towards realization of peaceful co-existence.

title: Evaluation of Kenya Country Programme
description:
Kenya is one of Finland's long-term partner countries. There is a long-standing development partnership ? over thirty years ? between Kenya and Finland. The objectives of current country strategy of Finland in Kenya (2013-2016) are: The objectives for Finl
and?s cooperation with Kenya are: 1) Kenya?s development towards a democratic and accountable society that promotes human rights, 2) poverty reduction through inclusive green growth in the agricultural sector, and 3) improved management and use of forest a
nd water resources.The last evaluation of Finland?s development cooperation in Kenya was conducted over ten years ago in 2002. In 2009 there was an evaluation on Finnish Aid in Western Kenya to assess the impact of Finnish supported projects/programmes in 
Western Kenya and to provide recommendations for planning the new cooperation in the area.The evaluation will consist of two parts: 1) Desk review on the Finnish development cooperation in Kenya in 2003-2013 focusing on impact sustainability effectiveness 
and efficiency, and 2) Comperehensive evaluation on results of the development cooperation in 2009-2013. The purpose of the evaluation is to provide an assessment on the overall results obtained and lessons learned from the past cooperation in Kenya. The e
valuation will be forward looking and will bring forward issues lessons learned and recommendations to support planners and decision-makers in different departments of the Ministry.The tender process will be started in March so that the evaluation could be
 started in May 2014. The evaluation results are expected to be had in autumn 2014. The budget of the evaluation is 200 000 Euros.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: Nyagowa Water Supply
description:
Kenya has approximately 40 million people and nearly half of the population lack clean drinking water. Nyagowa is situated in an area where water sometimes is found only in small water streams and where cattle and people have to share the same water source
. Drinking water is fetched from streams or from shallow wells water which is not drinkable untreated. In many cases water is collected from roofs and roofs may sometimes be carriers of various diceases spread by birds and small vector animals. Some roofin
g materials are also hazardous for peoples health. Up to 50 % of the deceases are waterborne deceases.The plan of the project is therefore to provide the health facility schools and the local community with clean drinking water which need not to be boiled 
before consumption. If the water flow is high enough the excess water will be led to water basins for the cattle.The plan of the project is to drill a hole to groundwater level in order to pump up clean drinkable water. The pumping system will be driven by
 solar energy (with an option to use landline electricity at times) which is an environment friendly sustainable and affordable way for the people to get clean water. Water will be distributed to strategically well placed water stations through a piping sy
stems and excess water will be distributed to drinking basins for the cattle. Concerning the sanitary conditions there are outdoor latrines built on a two-three meters deep wells in most of the homes. Hygiene is cared for either in streams or in private pl
aces specifically arranged for this nearby the homes. This project will therefore mostly concentrate on how to protect clean water from being contaminated and to encourage people to construct protected latrines where needed. No water flush toilets are in t
he area and the project will not build any either.The plan of the project is also to replace the water catching roofmaterial of the Health Clinic with ironsheets since water is collected from the roof to a tank. Water from the rainwater tank is today used 
for cleaning floors and for other use in the clinic but since the roof material is containing asbestos it should long ago have been replaced. If the roofmaterial is changed the rainwater tank may after a small repair serve as a water reserve for the clinic
 and be used in case of temporary absence of water from the borewell eg during maintenance of the water supply system.
participating_orgs: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland / FI-3 / 1 | Svenska Lutherska Evangeliforeningen i Finland rf / 22000 / 3

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: WASH project in Turkana
description:
Turkana is in many ways the most underdeveloped area in Kenya. The proposed project aims to improve the area?s wellbeing by providing assistance in water supply and sanitation sectors in the neediest villages in northern Turkana County which have been sele
cted by the Turkana community themselves.During the project efforts are made to repair and rehabilitate dysfunctional water wells in the project area. In addition ca. 10 new wells with water pans and 10-20 hygienic latrines will be built and also the commu
nities are educated in the proper ways to operate and manage the mentioned facilitie.The Turkanas haven?t needed to pay fees regarding the use of drinkable water in the past. We have learned during our preparatory mission that most of the wells built in th
e Turkana County have not been properly handed over to the consumers/villages which has led to poor understanding on the ownership and responsibility issues. During the project WaterFinns develops together with the Turkana communities a maintenance and man
agement model which will be implemented in the use of the water points and the improved hygienic environment.The perennial boreholes will contribute to people living in stationary villages near schools increase the attendance in schools and decrease the nu
mber of people affected by using unsafe drinking water. This will provide a steady and healthy environment for the children and youth to grow up in.The Project aims to achieve its purpose through three interlinked results (outputs):1: Lessons learned from 
success and failure of long-term sustainability of rural WASH services reported and benchmarks of best practices promoted.2: Strengthened capacities of selected CBOs village spokesmen and wards in their management and efforts of further improving the WASH 
services.3: Improved WASH facilities in selected communities in order to fulfill their needs and HR requirements on a sustainable basis.A key element of the proposed project is to create opportunities for the future water sector professionals to have an in
teresting and unique possibility to participate in voluntary work which focuses on long-term learning of the sustainable schemes.The proposed project partner (GWAKO) has amble experience to carry out rural water and sanitation projects and they also have e
xperience in working in the northern Turkana County.  The proposed project would last two-and-a-half years (2015-2017) and its proposed budget is 257 200 ?.

title: Scaling up health emergency response interventions to flooding and cholera in 8 most affected counties in Kenya
description: The main objective of this project is to scale up health emergency response interventions to flooding and cholera in the eight most affected counties in Kenya. WHO focuses on preventing and managing vector and water-borne diseases such as Malaria, Rift Valley fever, Dengue fever, Cholera, and vaccine-preventable diseases like Measles in these flood-affected counties. WHO strengthens early warning and disease surveillance through rapid response teams and community health promoters to conduct outbreak investigations and initiate response interventions. The response supports national and county coordination for a multisectoral approach, including the distribution of WHO emergency health kits and essential medical supplies. WHO targets 58,237 people, including 11,647 women, 5,832 men, and 40,767 children.

title: Kenya Acute JR 2022
description:
4 successive failed rain seasons, coupled with other shocks such as the crisis in Ukraine, have resulted in an extreme reduction in families’ ability to access food and water in the (semi) arid counties in northern Kenya due to decreased crop production and livestock conditions, increasing food commodity prices and trekking distances to water points. 4.1 million people are food insecure, including 1.1 million in IPC4. 942,000 children under 5 are acutely malnourished: 229,000 with Severe Acute Malnutrition and 713,000 with Moderate Acute Malnutrition. Wajir county is among the most affected with 468,758 people facing food insecurity – 60% of its population. Needs in Wajir are high with relatively low humanitarian support currently provided. | The response will target 500HHs with 3 tranches of MPC though mobile money platforms. MPC will be tied with behaviour change communication on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) in line with SC’s evidence-based cash+ approach. Following IMAM guidelines, WARDA will conduct screening of children under five and Pregnant and Lactating Women and refer them to SC who will support 12 health facilities and 30 outreach sites with nutrition commodities and essential drugs for nutrition treatment. PLWs will be counselled on IYCF and linked to existing mother to mother support groups. 
WARDA will support the county government with fuel and daily subsistence allowance to conduct water trucking. Warda will enhance hygiene conditions of the target community through procurement and distribution of hygiene kits and menstrual hygiene kits, and by providing hygiene promotion sessions. SC and WARDA will disseminate messages on protection, GBV and safeguarding during nutrition screening, hygiene promotion and MPC distribution. | SC targets 4000 HHs most in risk of food insecurity due to lack of access to food and HHs most at risk of malnutrition. These include HHs in IPC4 coupled with loss of 95% of their assets (livestock), women- and child-headed HHs, HHs with People with Disabilities, HHs with chronically ill or elderly caretakers and HHs with SGBV survivors. To ensure the most vulnerable community members are reached, the project will work with existing community-based relief committees to identify target criteria to ensure community-based targeting.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: F.a: Enhancing Women’s participation in County Governance in Kenya
description:
Social economic rights in Kenya are enshrined in the 2010 Constitution. These are not realised. The progressive realisation of these rights has been very slow. This has been even slower for rights that impact women the most for example health rights, acces
s to water, right to education etc. The aim of this project is to empower women at grassroots level to claim their rights, participate in budgeting and governance of county funding and access constitutional allocated funds for women. This will be done thro
ugh a series of activities dependent on the region of the country. Some counties have women who are already in a small way engaging in this process. While in other counties, more engagement will be required to build their capacity and confidence to activel
y demand for services and access their rights. www.informaction.tv

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: F.a: Mogotio Area Development Project
description:
The programme works for the improvement of rural communities’ socio-economic situation and quality of life, as well for the strengthening of community capacities and enhancing children’s rights in Mogotio, Western Kenya. The programme was evaluated in 
2016, and based on evaluation findings the new programme period will focus on WASH (water, sanitation and health) activities, including livelihood support, such as providing access to clean water for households, health centres and schools, in cooperation w
ith local water authorities, and child protection as well as participation. The evaluation findings were positive. More people have access to clean water, and water-born disease cases have decreased.  Families can provide better for their children, and in 
around 40 % of families, at least one parent has sustainable income. HIV/AIDS prevalence has decreased in the area. There remain some challenges especially related to access to clean water and livelihoods in the dry season. The water network should be exte
nded, existing water faucets reconditioned and the water committees offered capacity for sustainable management of water faucets. Also, project teams consisting of members of the community and the structures relevant to sustainability still need support. T
he status of protection and participation of children still requires support. Gender inequality, child marriage and violence against girls are some of the remaining issues in the community. Children's participation in collective decision-making is encourag
ed through Children's Parliament and the situation of women and girls are supported through focus on harmful traditions such as female genital mutilation and early marriages, as well as acts of violence against girls. Community advocacy groups are facilita
ted to engage in county planning in budgeting for sanitation and hygiene programmes and to mobilize resources. The water committees are facilitated to handle the use, maintenance and monitoring of water resources. The program beneficiaries are the 16 840 p
ersons living in the programme area. The main partner is World Vision Kenya that runs the implementation and accounts for the use of funding.
participating_orgs: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland / FI-3 / 1 | Suomen World Vision / 22000-175 / 3
