reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: F.a: FAMILY WELFARE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
description:
The Country Programme in Kenya has 5 components: Nairobi Street Children, Kakamega Children with Disabilities, Maasai Girls, Psycho-Social Support and Care (PSS), and Environment. The Programme is contributing towards the fulfilment of beneficiary rights t
o health, education and adequate standards of living and empowerment of the partner, Full Gospel Churches of Kenya (FGCK). The main beneficiary groups are children, youth, women, parents, teachers and poor farmers. The programme is supporting around 7300 d
irect beneficiaries and around 70 700 indirect beneficiaries. The Programme is working in different areas including the slums of Nairobi (Kawangware, Riruta, Waithaka), suburbs of Kakamega town and adjacent areas, and villages in Nyanza, Narok, Tangulbei, 
Loglogo, Chamari, Kasikini, Duke, Diririsa, Kadzandani, and Bilisa and Odole (among others). All these areas are remote and marginalized. The problems affecting these communities include poor access to education (lack of schools, low school enrolments, low
 school retention, poor transition rates, high illiteracy rates for parents and youth), poor access to health (child and spousal abuses, child-headed households due to parental deaths, drug abuse, sexual violence on girls, limited medical services for chil
dren with disabilities, high maternal death rates) and poor access to adequate standards of living (high unemployment rates, high illiteracy levels, poverty and marginalization). The communities also experience food and water shortages caused by perennial 
droughts. The pastoral communities experience deadly community conflicts caused by political incitement, historical issues, and conflict over resources. #The Programme is currently providing educational support to community schools (providing facilities, m
aterials, trainings) and children, promoting health and psycho-social resources (guidance, counselling, child protection) for children, youth and families and promoting household livelihoods through entrepreneurship (trainings in income generating activiti
es, savings and loaning services, extension services to farmers), building the capacity of Full Gospel Churches of Kenya leadership (management trainings, development of policies and manuals, setting up of partner in Income Generating Activities) and promo
tion of advocacy for the partner (sensitizing partner on advocacy, assisting partner to set up an advocacy strategy).

title: Kenya Drought 2014
description: Poor rainfall between March and May - supposed to be the wettest months of the year - has affected the production of food and livestock for many households throughout the northern and coastal regions of Kenya. The situation has also worsened by increasing food prices driven by the increase in fuel costs and general inflation which continue to erode the purchasing power of individuals and families. The IFRC has launched an appeal for CHF 8 512 016 to support the Kenya Red Cross Society to assist 649 175 beneficiaries for nine months (to be completed June 2015). The KRCS will scale up interventions to affected communities focusing on improving access to safe water (human consumption and livestock) essential health and nutrition services support to school feeding programmes and support to agricultural livelihood activities. Details of the appeal are available at: http://adore.ifrc.org/Download.aspx?FileId=63222

title: Water, Sanitation, And Hygiene Finance (WASH-FIN)
description: USAIDs WASH-FIN project will work in collaboration with national governments, development partners, financial institutions and local stakeholders in at least eight countries to close financing gaps and improve governance structures such that water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) service providers can access reliable sources of capital for sustainable and resilient water and sanitation infrastructure.  WASH-FINs approach to closing financing gaps is based on the premise that citizens should be treated as valued customers by service providers operating on sustainable business models that strengthen creditworthiness within clear regulatory and governance structures. Only then can increased public investment and market finance be effectively leveraged to expand or improve service delivery. | L'objectif de cette commande de tâches est de : Améliorer la fourniture de produits de santé de qualité garantie grâce à l'approvisionnement et à la logistique des produits à l'échelle mondiale. Fournir une assistance technique axée sur le renforcement des systèmes afin d’améliorer la chaîne d’approvisionnement du pays et d’accroître la sécurité des produits de base. Améliorer la coordination entre les acteurs mondiaux de la santé maternelle et infantile (SMI) et de la chaîne d'approvisionnement pour renforcer la réponse collective aux programmes liés à la santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile. | Le projet WASH-FIN de l'USAID travaillera en collaboration avec les gouvernements nationaux, les partenaires de développement, les institutions financières et les parties prenantes locales dans au moins huit pays pour combler les déficits de financement et améliorer les structures de gouvernance de telle sorte que les prestataires de services d'eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène (WASH) puissent accéder à des sources de capitaux fiables pour des infrastructures d'eau et d'assainissement durables et résilientes.  L’approche de WASH-FIN pour combler les déficits de financement repose sur le principe selon lequel les citoyens doivent être traités comme des clients appréciés par les prestataires de services opérant selon des modèles commerciaux durables qui renforcent la solvabilité au sein de structures réglementaires et de gouvernance claires. Ce n'est qu'alors que l'augmentation des investissements publics et du financement du marché pourra être efficacement exploitée pour étendre ou améliorer la prestation de services. | O projecto WASH-FIN da USAID trabalhará em colaboração com governos nacionais, parceiros de desenvolvimento, instituições financeiras e intervenientes locais em pelo menos oito países para colmatar lacunas de financiamento e melhorar as estruturas de governação, de modo a que os prestadores de serviços de água, saneamento e higiene (WASH) possam aceder a fontes fiáveis ​​de capital para infra-estruturas de água e saneamento sustentáveis ​​e resilientes.  A abordagem da WASH-FIN para colmatar as lacunas de financiamento baseia-se na premissa de que os cidadãos devem ser tratados como clientes valiosos pelos prestadores de serviços que operam em modelos de negócios sustentáveis ​​que fortalecem a solvabilidade no âmbito de estruturas regulamentares e de governação claras. Só então o aumento do investimento público e do financiamento do mercado poderá ser eficazmente aproveitado para expandir ou melhorar a prestação de serviços.

reporting_org_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
title: F.a: Strengthening biocultural rights by bringing community together (Tharaka, Eastern Kenya)
description:
Tharaka's unique biodiversity and bio-cultural heritage are severely threatened. The existing laws do not explicitly recognise sacred natural sites and territories, nor their customary governance systems. It is now important to document these and to lobby 
the county government to pass these into a law to be able to hold people accountable for the protection of their biocultural life-heritages and livelihoods against land grabs and other extractives. The customary laws will help maintain original order which
 will revitalize the roles of both women and men. In the proposed project SALT will run monthly community dialogues and learning exchanges amongst the Tharaka Indigenous community in Eastern Kenya. The purpose of these community dialogues, over the 18 mont
hs of the project, is to support indigenous communities to assert their biocultural rights and thus work towards securing respect and their legal recognition. Whilst the focus of the project is in Tharaka, the project will also link with Maasai in Narok (L
oita Forest) and the Bagungu community in Buliisa district of Uganda through the learning exchanges. Main activities of the project are: Community dialogues and learning exchanges, Developing materials for claiming the rights of communities and recognition
 of their sacred natural sites and ancestral lands and customary governance, documenting clan constitutions and customary laws, Lobbying for relevant national and international legislation and policies and work on integrating them into county level legisla
tion and policies, Collaboration with allied partners nationally and regionally, Pilot use of creative arts (poems, dances, storytelling, drama and festivals, nature experiential learning processes) for intergenerational learning to regenerate and reclaim 
rights of nature of the River Kithino for pupils of Kithino Learning Centre. Expected results are, among others: Increased protection and regeneration of sacred natural sites through demarcation and restoration of watershed areas and healthy ecosystem, Str
engthened solidarity and alignment between communities and custodians of sacred natural sites through exchange visits, Improved community participation and contribution towards documentation of their customary laws and governance systems and community cons
titutions. The project would be reaching more than 1,000 direct beneficiaries and over 10,000 indirect beneficiaries.

title: Turkana drought response
description: Oxfam is targeting the most vulnerable people in Turkana, where it has been working since the 1960's and has an established presence and long term partnerships to build on. Specifically, Oxfam will target women and children that don't have access to water and food or have to walk large distances to reach water sources, as well as vulnerable population groups like lactating women, elderly and children that are at risk of dropping out of the school system.  To identify beneficiaries, communities and locations to target Oxfam will partner closely with the Turkana county (local government), with the Water User Associations (WUAs) and the Water Users Committees (WUCs), , and with the Hunger Safety Net Programme 2, to utilise the experience of these authorities when it comes to needs and targeting. Oxfam will also work in schools, health centres and in the communities to identify the most vulnerable House Holds (HHs). Beneficiary selection will be undertaken in a participatory manner ensuring participation of the most vulnerable groups such as women headed households, households with pregnant and lactating women, elders and with children below 5 years. There will be selected community members acting as beneficiary reference groups who can share the feelings and feedback of the community towards the project to ensure accountability. This process of community -based targeting has the benefit of bringing local knowledge and priorities into the programme and developing a sense of ownership that will help mitigate potential sources of conflict

title: Developing performance-based design for foundation systems of WIND turbines in AFRICA (WindAfrica)
description: Africa is facing the challenge of generating more power to meet existing and future demand. Currently, about one-half Africa's total population is lacking access to electricity. However, the continent is well endowed with renewable energy resources; it is estimated that about 35% of the world resources for wind energy are located in the continent. There are many challenges which hinder the development of infrastructure for wind energy in Africa. Designing suitable foundations to sustain the loads typically applied by wind turbines represents a particular challenge. Most potential locations for wind turbines in Africa are in tropical zones where fluctuation in ground water level is severe. The cycling of water levels means that many deposits of interest are unsaturated for at least part of the year. Unsaturated soils exhibit complex mechanical behaviour, coupled to changes in water content. This research aims to provide design for the foundations of wind turbines in unsaturated soils. | The Global Challenges Research Fund (GCRF) supports cutting-edge research to address challenges faced by developing countries. reporting_org_name: DEPARTMENT FOR BUSINESS, ENERGY & INDUSTRIAL STRATEGY
title: Geothermally Sourced Combined Power and Freshwater Generation for Eastern Africa (Combi-Gen)
description: Lack of safe and clean water is a long-standing challenges in much of Africa, and especially in Ethiopia and Kenya. Around 50 million people in Ethiopia lack access to safe water, and the country is currently suffering from its worst drought for 50 years, leaving some 18 million people in need of urgent aid. Similarly, only 41% out of the Kenyan population of ~ 47 million have access to safe water.   Despite substantial undeveloped renewable resources, both Ethiopia and Kenya are energy poor. Ethiopia has around 2 GW of electricity generation capacity, meeting only 10% of national electricity demand, and reaching only 12% of the population. Kenya, with an installed electricity capacity around only 2.2 GW, has better grid connectivity, reaching about 55% of its households, but is still plagued by frequent, lengthy outages. In both countries, geothermal energy is vastly under-utilised and represents an exciting opportunity of addressing energy challenges, alleviating poverty, and promoting economic development.   The Combi-Gen project aims to develop a novel geothermally sourced-combined power and freshwater generation technology, which promises to initiate a genuinely innovative shift in the engineering response to the twin challenges of energy shortage and water-scarcity in Ethiopia and Kenya. The research will provide a novel technology that can significantly improve the utilisation of the precious geothermal resources in Ethiopia and Kenya, and can produce both power and freshwater simultaneous to address the long-standing twin challenge of water and energy shortage in both countries and others of this kind. Once the developed Combi-Gen system is widely installed, it will contribute to sustainable development through reliable renewable energy and freshwater generation, and a reduction in poverty through promoting economic development and employment growth.   Combi-Gen tackles a number of key priorities for development identified by the GRCF that relate to challenges of health, clean energy, safe water, sustainable agriculture, and foundations for inclusive growth. The core of the project is to tackle challenges associated with 'Sustainable infrastructure development'. The geothermal focus is strategically aligned with the government energy policy priorities on developing renewable and sustainable energy to meet power demand in both countries. | The Global Challenges Research Fund (GCRF) supports cutting-edge research to address challenges faced by developing countries. title: Shape sensing textile for orthotics - SmartSensOtics
description: Orthotic products are of great importance to a number of people around the world. The process of fabricating orthoses is well established, but depends on a time and resource consuming plaster cast method developed over 100 years ago. This is associated to a number of reasons e.g. the fact that an Orthotist has to shape the patient's body to define the shape of an orthosis. In particular in the case of children or patients with joint contractures and anatomical deformities, such as those affected with neurological and neuromuscular medical conditions, such as Cerebral Palsy. This issue prevents the efficient application of MRI, CT or optical imaging techniques, because these require extensive post-processing to discriminate between the patient's body and the Orthotist's hands. Additionally, such imaging equipment is expensive and requires a highly technicians. Hence, providing orthoses is only possible if, hospitals, expensive medical scanners, consumables, and workshops are accessible. This is not the case in developing countries, consequently orthoses in LMICs are often fabricated form scrap such as old water canisters.  Recently, the development of flexible, soft electronics, as well as the spread of wearable electronic devices has made significant progress. Here we want to develop a smart, portable and stretchable textile sleeve with integrated sensors connected to a smartphone to realize an entirely new, versatile, and wearable body shape imaging technique. The digital limb models by our system can then be used for the computer aided fabrication of customized orthotics, without the need for significant infrastructure. Our smart textile will contain an active array of stretchable strain sensors to measure the deformation of the textile itself. The knowledge of the strain distribution inside the tight fitting stretchable textile when worn over a limb or body part will be used to determine the exact three-dimensional shape of the limb. Any external influence such as the force applied by the Orthotist will also be quantified, but will not interfere with the shape measurement. The development and fabrication of biocompatible, polymer based strain gauges able to measure strain of >200% will be done in the semiconductor manufacturing cleanroom at the University of Sussex. This cleanroom is optimized for the fabrication of flexible electronic thin-film devices on plastic substrates. The sensors will then be unobtrusively integrated into an elastane fabric using embroidery, and interconnected using conductive yarns. We will evaluate the required sensor density to achieve a measurement resolution sufficient for the fabrication of orthotic products. In a next step, the acquired sensor data will be proceed on a smartphone to automatically generate a three-dimensional model of the imaged body part. Hence no professionals, additional infrastructure or consumables are needed to support the Orthotist in treating the patients. The generated digital model can then be electronically sent to a manufacturer or used to produce the orthosis in a mobile 3D printer, whereas printing of a mould for the conventional fabrication of orthoses, and direct printing of an orthosis will be evaluated. John Florence Ltd. will be responsible for the fabrication of the Orthotic products and the evaluation of their quality.  To assess the technology as a whole, and to define workflows for the fabrication of orthotic products in rural areas in developing countries, the Kenya Medical Training College and the Ability Therapy Place will support us evaluate the developed wearable in Kenya. The shape and force sensing technology developed here will not only revolutionise the fabrication of orthoses, but also influence the development of other medical products such as prostheses, monitoring of diseases related to the shape, size or deformation of the skeletal system or soft tissue, and even the realization of artificial sensor skins for interactive soft robots | The Global Challenges Research Fund (GCRF) supports cutting-edge research to address challenges faced by developing countries. title: GCRF Groundwater for Resilience in Africa Network (GRAN)
description: The key strategy and framework around GRAN implementation is to strengthen the research-operation-policy axis related to groundwater and its integration into broader water resources management and development policies. This will be achieved through these key activities:  1. An initial stakeholder mapping and consultation exercise, scoping out the seven potential network themes and further engaging and committing key network partners to a joint vision of sustainable groundwater development and management in Africa through enhanced collaboration, capacity development and solution implementation 2. Synthesis, translation and dissemination of research outputs (in collaboration with researchers and programme knowledge brokers) to create relevant, accessible (online) and useable material to a range of non-academic stakeholders. This step will focus on research outputs, which have already demonstrated solutions (technical, legal, policy, institutional/engagement based) with significant outscaling potential. Research results will also feed into important capacity development networks in Africa (e.g. AGW-Net) to stimulate a domino effect of dissemination of knowledge. 3. Two continental-scale workshops, organised to coincide with existing events led by AMCOW and SADC-GMI, which will bring together academic and non-academic beneficiaries to exchange experiences around each network theme; themes may then go on to form the basis of several sub-networks 4. Support to smaller (national-scale) events and online interactions (such as the RWSN webinar series) responding to expressed demand for research-into-use collaboration around groundwater 5. Ongoing engagement with network partners through identified sub-network leads or champions to anchor sub-networks beyond the GRAN, with support from GRIPP.  The proposed network, GRAN, will build on and expand existing groundwater-related structures through two major international events, complemented by smaller events, virtual meeting activities and curation and dissemination of material through online platforms such as GRIPP and the Africa Groundwater Atlas. The larger events, one of which will be held within the first six months of the network, will evolve around already planned events, one with focus on policy development and one with focus on Research-into-Use, while both will target policy makers, researchers and practitioners. The first will be led by AMCOW (in Western Africa), and the second by SADC-GMI (in Southern Africa). The key objective of the meetings is to exchange knowledge on groundwater management and development potentials and risks and how to address these by incorporating lessons from recent significant research and piloting/implementation of technical, institutional or policy solutions, with implications for capacity development. The meetings will make updated inventory of key institutions in the regions engaged in groundwater research, management and policy development. The events will be thematically structured around key challenges that may ultimately underpin a series of sub-networks. | The Global Challenges Research Fund (GCRF) supports cutting-edge research to address challenges faced by developing countries. title: UNEP-wide project on Improving Air Quality
description:
UNEP’s new Medium-Term Strategy (MTS) 2022 - 2025 sets an ambitious air quality target: “By 2025, 30 per cent of the 
world’s population live in areas where WHO Air Quality Interim Target 3 for outdoor PM2.5 (fine particulate matter) is 
attained”. Currently, only 19% of the global population lives in areas where concentrations of PM2.5 pollution is below 
15 micrograms per cubic meter, and thus locations where an additional 11% of the world population reside must 
improve the air quality significantly in coming years, if the MTS target is to be met.
The “UNEP-wide project on Improving Air Quality” is the primary UNEP response to the global air pollution crisis. It will 
mobilize UNEP’s and its key partners’ collective capacity to reduce air pollution from major sources in high impact 
sectors, and to strengthen air quality monitoring and management capacities of key stakeholders.
The “Improving Air Quality” project contributes mainly to Outcome 3C of the Chemicals and Pollution Action 
Subprogramme, “Releases of pollutants to air, water, soil and the ocean are reduced”, and delivers on Direct Outcome 
3.4 “Air pollution action, sustainable mobility and clean energy are supported”. It builds on UNEP’s and CCAC’s 
accomplishments, including lessons learned, gaps and challenges experienced during the implementation of project 
533.1 “Providing support to countries and cities in improving air quality in order to improve environmental quality and 
the health and well-being of all”. This new project will advance air quality action with more impact, visibility, and 
resources, by integrating UNEP’s multi-region and multi-level efforts to improve air quality, by leveraging more partners, 
financial resources and buy-in among industry, finance and the UN system, and by providing a platform to mobilize 
efforts across the house, particularly under projects aimed at transforming key sectors such as transport, waste, 
energy and other high-impact sectors so that air quality benefits can be fully harnessed.
The direct outcome of the project is that governments have measures, policies, or frameworks in place to reduce 
emissions of air pollutants from sources related to human activities for improved air quality and human health at 
national and subnational level through the support of UNEP. In order to achieve this outcome, the project will 
implement the following outputs:
Output 1: Partnerships and finance mobilized with industry and private sector to shift investments across high impact 
sectors
Output 2: Advisory and support services provided to countries and cities to detect and reduce the most harmful 
pollutants in high emitting impact sectors – widening, deepening, and connecting
Output 3: Increased evidence base for informed decision making through continued air quality monitoring, targeted 
assessments on health and economic impacts, sector specific interventions and economics of air pollution
Output 4: Global and regional movements strengthened to safeguard clean air for all with a focus on air quality and 
health nexus

title: F.a: Business from Waste for Women in Nairobi
description:
1.	Project: 12150 Business from Waste for Women in Nairobi  2.	Project area and Country: Nairobi, Kenya 3.	Project justification:  In Nairobi, 50% of waste is being dumped in the environment and the other 50% collected for disposal at Nairobi?s only official dumpsite, Dandora. While 93% of Nairobi?s waste is potentially reusable, less than 5% is recycled and/or composted, which is not sustainable. The poor management and improper disposal of solid waste pollute the air, water, and soil causing significant health and environmental problems. In Nairobi, this especially concerns marginal societal groups, many of whom engage in waste picking for an irregular income. A large percentage of waste pickers are women. The potential economic value of recyclables, coupled with heightened environmental awareness, is gradually creating interest in waste management as a form of social enterprise. In Nairobi, local recycling facilities have until recently been lacking. A Nairobi-based waste management and recycling company, Taka Taka Solutions LTD, has recently opened Kenya?s first recycling plant for single-use plastic containers and the recycling plant for flexible plastic packaging, creating an opportunity for sustainable employment for women.  4.	The main objective and the expected results: The main objective of the project is to improve women?s economic status by creating income opportunities in the waste value chain, more specifically in the solid waste collection, recycling, and reuse in the informal settlements of Nairobi. The project will achieve this through capacity building of waste pickers on the waste management value chain to supply previously unrecyclable plastics through Taka Taka Solutions? network of buy-back centers. This will result in the creation of new jobs for women through the selling of previously unrecyclable plastic waste streams, increased income, and improved knowledge of material streams through capacity building, improvement of labour conditions through a social benefit scheme such as protective equipment to ensure the safety of waste pickers. 5.	Right-holders/beneficiaries: 590 women Duty bearers: National government representatives, County government/Nairobi Metropolitan Services (NMS), National Environmental Management Authority (NEMA), Local manufacturing companies. 6.	Implementing partner: Taka Taka Solutions Company Ltd. 7.	Budget 2022: EUR 100,000 | 1.	Hanke: 12150 Jätteestä liiketoimintaa Nairobin naisille
2.	Hankealue ja -maa: Nairobi, Kenia
3.	Hankkeen perustelut: 
Nairobissa 50% jätteestä kaadetaan ympäristöön ja 50% kerätään Nairobin ainoalle viralliselle kaatopaikalle nimeltään Dandora. 93% Nairobin jätteestä on potentiaalisesti uusiokäyttöistä, mutta vain vajaa 5% kierrätetään ja/tai kompostoidaan, mikä ei ole kestävää. Huono jätehuolto saastuttaa ilmaa, vettä ja maaperää ja aiheuttaa siten merkittäviä terveys- ja ympäristöongelmia. Nairobissa tästä kärsivät etenkin syrjäytyneet ryhmät, jotka usein myös saavat jätteiden keruusta epäsäännöllistä tuloa. Suuri osuus jätteen kerääjistä on naisia. Kierrätettävien materiaalien taloudellinen potentiaali sekä lisääntynyt ympäristötietoisuus on vähitellen lisännyt kiinnostusta jätehuoltoon sosiaalisena yritystoimintana. Viime aikoihin asti paikalliset kierrätyslaitokset ovat puuttuneet Nairobista, mutta nairobilainen jätehuolto- ja kierrätysyritys Taka Taka Solutions LTD on hiljattain avannut Kenian ensimmäisen kierrätystehtaan muoville, luoden samalla mahdollisuuden kestävään toimeentuloon naisille. 
4.	Hankkeen päätavoite ja odotetut tulokset:
Hankkeen päätavoite on parantaa naisten taloudellista asemaa luomalla mahdollisuuksia tulojen kasvattamiselle jätehuollossa eli jätteiden keräämisessä, kierrättämisessä ja uudelleenkäytössä Nairobissa. Tämä saavutetaan kouluttamalla jätteen kerääjiä jätehuollossa, jotta ennen kierrättämätön muovi saadaan kerättyä Taka Taka Solutions -yhtiön muovinkeräyskeskuksiin. Tuloksena naiset saavat uusia työpaikkoja, heidän tulonsa kasvavat, ja tietoisuus materiaalien kierrättämisestä lisääntyy. Lisäksi työolot parantuvat, kun naiset pääsevät sosiaalietuuksien ohjelmaan, johon kuuluu muun muassa suojavarusteet työturvallisuuden parantamiseksi.

title: F.a: Strengthening the role and capacity of the hunter-gatherer indigenous people in safeguarding their natural resources
description:
The traditional territory of the Yiaku indigenous people of Kenya, the Mukogodo Forest in Laikipia County, is subject to many different economic interests. However, only very little of the proceed from there has been channelled to the Yiaku. Instead, the basis of their entire existence, identity and livelihood is at risk under the pressure of these external pressures. In order to strengthen the legal, cultural and livelihood basis of the Yiaku, Siemenpuu supported the drafting of the first biocultural community protocol (BCP) of the Yiaku in 2020-21 as part of Yiaku Laikipia Trust?s (YLT) joint project together with two other organizations of the hunter-gatherer people of Kenya (the Ogiek and the Sengwer). This BCP has been further worked on. In this project, together with the community groups of the Lmartin people (who are closely related to the Samburu), YLT will specify and document the principles regarding access to and benefits of genetic resources for the Yiaku and the Lmartin people based on the Nagoya Protocol of the UN Convention on Biodiversity. Regarding the Yiaku, BCP-based resource utilization Mutually Afraid Terms (MAT) and 'Free and Informed Prior Consent' (FPIC) principles regarding Mukogodo forest and the use of its resources are drawn up. Regarding the Lmartin people and their area (Ntimu-Nariko forest in Samburu County), the groundwork for them will be done by drawing up the community's own BCP. The project also grows saplings of local tree species and aims to restore degraded forest areas by planting, and identify forest related female-led business models. The beneficiaries of the project belong to the Yiaku and Lmartin hunter-gatherer communities. They are estimated to be around 10,800 in total. Other beneficiaries are the wider community of Laikipia and Samburu Counties (including Maasais, Rendilles and Pokots), who benefit from the protection and restoration of forests and from improved cattle pastures and water management. | Kenian yiaku-alkuperäiskansan perinteiseen alueeseen, Laikipian piirikunnan Mukogodo-metsään, kohdistuu monia erilaisia taloudellisen toiminnan intressejä. Sieltä saatavista tuotoista on vain hyvin vähän kanavoitunut yiakuille. Sen sijaan heidän koko olemassaolonsa, identiteettinsä ja toimeentulonsa perusteet ovat vaarassa näiden ulkoisten paineiden puristuksessa.
Yiakujen oikeudellisen, kulttuurisen ja toimeentulon perustan vahvistamiseksi Siemenpuu tuki 2020-21 yiakujen ensimmäisen biokulttuurisen yhteisöpöytäkirjan (BCP) laadintaa osana Yiaku Laikipia Trustin (YLT) yhteishanketta kahden muun metsästäjä-keräilijäkansan (ogiekit ja sengwerit) järjestöjen kanssa. Yhteisöpöytäkirjaa on hankkeen pohjalta työstetty edelleen. 
Tässä hankkeessa YLT tekee yhteistyötä samburuihin läheisesti liittyvien lmartin-kansan yhteisöryhmien kanssa. Hankkeessa on kyseessä YK:n biodiversiteettisopimuksen Nagoyan pöytäkirjaan pohjautuvien geneettisten resurssien saattavuutta ja hyödyntämistä koskevien periaatteiden täsmentäminen ja dokumentointi yiakujen ja lmartinien osalta. Yiakujen osalta laaditaan BCP:hen pohjautuvat resurssien hyödyntämisen ehdot (Mutually Afreed Terms) ja ’vapaan ja tietoon perustuvan ennakkosuostumuksen’ (FPIC) periaatteet Mukogodo-metsää ja sen resurssien käyttöä koskien. Lmartineiden ja heidän alueensa (Ntimu-Narikon metsä Samburun piirikunnassa) osalta tehdään heitä koskeva pohjatyö laatimalla yhteisön oma BCP.  
Hankkeessa myös kasvatetaan paikallisten puulajien taimia ja pyritään istuttamalla ennallistamaan elonkirjoltaan köyhtyneitä metsäalueita sekä kartoitetaan metsiin pohjautuvia naisjohtoisia yritystoiminnan malleja.
Hankkeen hyödynsaajat kuuluvat yiaku- ja lmartin -metsästäjä-keräilijäyhteisöihin. Heitä arvioidaan olevan yhteensä noin 10 800. Muita hyödynsaajia ovat Laikipian ja Samburun piirikuntien laajempi yhteisö (ml. maasait, rendilet ja pokotit), jotka hyötyvät metsien suojelusta ja ennallistamisesta sekä paikallisesti parantuneista karjan laidunmaista ja vesitaloudesta.

title: Improving nutrition for women and children in Western Kenya
description:
This project will improve the nutrition and health of 73,729 vulnerable men, women & children (18,163 direct beneficiaries) in Western Kenya. 

Farms will be transformed so families have sufficient, nutritious food to eat all year round. Families will learn how to stay well and be able to access vital health services and safe water. Small businesses will be developed and savings & credit schemes established to ensure economic resilience. Women will be empowered to make decisions that will positively impact the well-being of their families.

title: Efficient operations at dairy processing plant (2)
description:
Partnership Mukurwe-ini and Agriterra is all about starting up processing plant. Mukurwe-ini has installed its new yoghurt processing line. Testing with water is done and soon first yoghurt will be processed. 

Activities in the action plan have the following overall goals (as elaborated by Mukurwe-ini):1. Receiving and processing 50,000L/day at the end of 2016, 40,000L/day from its members and 10,000L/day from other stakeholders. MWDL also aim to be processing 40,000L/day by mid-2016; 35,000L/day from its members by the said period.2. Increase the product portfolio by investing on a separator and a butter churner. Also, look into other opportunities by undertaking a feasibility study on water bottling. 3. Complete the already constructed satellite cooling centre and invest on one more4. Prioritize the Production and marketing of yoghurt.







Though milk has not been able to improve significantly in Mukurwe-ini, they have been able to lower the levels of fluctuations’ between the peak and off peak periods. This year, during the months of Jan to end of March, Mukurwe-ini received a low of 24000L/day and so far they have been able to record a high of 30000L/day including close to 3000L from a small cooperative within Nyeri County. For all these milk they are receiving, they are able to process upto 83% of it. Majority of the processed milk being in bulk (60%) and the rest in pouches (40%). Though pouches gives good margins, the company has been curtailed by the low capacity packaging machine that can package upto 5000 pieces per hour excluding cleaning time. The company has however ordered a new packaging line meant to increase the packing capacity and improve margins for the company. Before this was arrived at, we did some calculations together with Fred and proved that from the differentials and assuming that the same marketing conditions prevail, Mukurwe-ini will be able to repay the machine in less than four months.  Agriterra has continued to support Mukurwe-ini in its extension and though there has been a low milk increase (3%) for the past three years, the fact that they have reduced the margin of seasonal fluctuations is a big stride in the right direction. They now have two full time extension staff and brought in recently two SPEs on board to support the team. Extension, processing and marketing therefore remains the three main areas of focus. In Feb 2015, the company was already making good profits, they made 8 million after loan interests and this allowed them to pay the farmer a record high milk price of KES 34 per litre. At the factory, construction issues identified by the mission team in January have already been addressed; now the homogenizer working and a new ice bank ordered for the existing one to be fully repaired and be on standby. The company got a grant of KES 26M from the County government of Nyeri and they have followed the January mission’s advice that they should invest it on a yoghurt processing line. This line has been ordered at a cost of around KES 35M.

The action plan will focus on increased milk volumes, starting up processing of yoghurt and critically assessing opportunities to further diversify product portfolio. Much focus will also be on marketing and on organisational strengthening on financial management and governance.

2016 Goals:1. Receiving and processing 50,000L/day at the end of 2016, 40,000L/day from its members and 10,000L/day from other stakeholders. MWDL also aim to be processing 40,000L/day by mid-2016; 35,000L/day from its members by the said period.2. Increase the product portfolio by investing on a separator and a butter churner. Also, look into other opportunities for diversification. 3. Complete the already constructed satellite cooling centre and invest on one more4. Prioritize the Production and marketing of yoghurt.

title: Irrigation system for demo plot roughage feed production
description:
Kieni targets to improve quantity and quality of roughage feed to milking cows. To increase milk yield on a daily basis, cows need to be fed well, also in periods of drought. Kieni takes up buying and producing roughage and supplies this to the primary cooperatives, which in turn will sell these feeds to their members.

One specific component of this plan is the establishment of a demonstration hay production sites (a plot near Kieni’s collection centre (see photo above) to gain experience in modern quality hay production and to disseminate this knowledge to its members. An important aspect is irrigation of the grasslands for hay, as this region can be affected by droughts.

Therefore, Kieni started the construction of a gravity water supply system (pipeline of 6 kilometres) to be able to irrigate the 10 acre plot around its premises (see also photo above). 

The pipeline is already finalised by own financial means of Kieni Dairy. The objective of this project is to invest in the demonstration plot in order to show best practices and train members on hay production and quality feed for cows.

The objective of this project is to invest in the demonstration plot (in particular irrigation system) in order to show best practices and train members on hay production and quality feed for cows.

title: Action plan - Developing business plan on milk processing
description:
In November 2010 a representative of Agriterra with support from a dairy expert from the Dutch dairy cooperative FrieslandCampina and hosted by Co-operative Alliance of Kenya visited Kiambaa Dairy for the first time and concluded that 
- Professional management and good leadership offer good prospects for company growth and dairy development.
- The company has a strong drive to strengthen position of producers in the value chain. 
- There seems to be a clear match between the request for advice by dairy and other experts stemming from the Dutch agribusiness and services Agriterra can offer, including those via AgriPool. 

In January 2011 a three days company assessment took place in order to achieve an in-depth understanding of the practice and performance of Kiambaa Dairy and also to jointly prepare a lean action plan as a roadmap leading to the development of a sound and investmentready business plan for Kiambaa Dairy by the end of 2011.

Kiambaa Dairy, SNV and Agriterra agreed to deliver the following targets by the end of 2011:
- Increase in active membership from .... (2010) to 2300 (2011)
- Average intake per day in kgs from ..... (2010) to 17000 (2011)
- No. of farmers accessing training through farmer field schools .... 
- 1 investmentready business plan for milk processing
- 1 investmentready business plan for water bottling and marketing
- Stock management 15 feedstores computarized 
- Extension service program in place through recruitment of extension officer in combination with a series of farmer field schools and field days.


ACTION PLAN 2012

300 farmers trained
Increase milk intake to 16,000 l/dayfor society
Sample Farmers increase milk production by 10%
Increased sales of Semen to Farmers by 5-10%
Increased area planted with fodder crops and use of silage by sample farmers (> 10%)
Well trained management  staff and Board> 500,000 net profit from milk business
Operational costs at 20% and milk payment at 80%
Marketing plan/strategy
Contract with Dairy land


The following activities will be executed:

Farmer trainings(general)
-	Maintain a Famerstraining register and update it regularly
-	Training of Farmers on fodder management, calf rearing and AI
-	establish 3 demonstration farms per route and manage expectations between the parties involved (Cooperative, Extension Officer and Farmers)
-	Undertake training needs assessment of the Extension Officer and Lead Farmers and carry out the  necessary training
-	Engage a Local Capacity Builder to backstop the Extension Officer 
-	Create a sample of 50Farmers and ensure follow –up to assist track impact. Design and use monitoring form.
-	Stimulate service provider enterprises through training of Service providerse.g. youth groups
-	Explore possibilities for use of Students undertaking research for their study preferable Agri-Business or Agriculture from the Membership of Agriterra.

Artificial Insemination/ Animal Feed
-	Farmer education on AI including breed type, cost etc
-	Periodic milk quality testing as well as animal feeds
-	Establishing links between AI Cooperative and AI service providers e.g. CAIS, Coopers, LGS among others
-	Undertake branding of the AI  services vehicle

Performance management
-	Follow up training of staff and Board
-	Undertake a training needs assessment to inform future trainings
-	Evaluate the 2011 salary review  in relation to staff turnover develop performance contracts
-	Develop an appraisal system
-	Develop a service charter

Implementation of supply chain recommendations
-	Introduce a log for tracking milk supply
-	Improve member loyalty through information sharing and incentives
-	Complete Google  maps, develop analytical tools and put in use

Value addition – Implementation of market and business case strategies
-	Improve chilling capacity
-	Stakeholder Forum once  a quarter
-	Develop a sales and pricing strategy as part of marketing plan
-	Training of sales team

Cooperation between Ndumberi and Kiambaa
-	Hold a brain storming workshop with the two management committees
-	Develop a roadmap for the Cooperation/venture

At present (January 2011) picks up 14,000 L of milk a day. Of that amount, approximately 30% goes to the processors Sameer, Brookside and Eldoville. Usually they make payment after 45 days, something that is, in fact, disadvantageous for the cooperative’s cash flow. 25% of the intake goes to medium-priced hotels in Nairobi and 45% is sold through hawkers, including their own milk shops as outlet stores. Furthermore it is estimated that coop members are supplying hawkers directly, without the offices of the cooperative, with as much as 40%!

The board and the manager are considering to make a next step upwards in the value chain in a series of phases. Members are currently building up share capital in order to increase the cooperative’s assets, making it able to get a loan to make the necessary investments. Since April 2010, it has been picking up 350,000 KSh per month for this purpose. In addition, the cooperative aims to start selling bottled water and makes use of a plot beside the office for paid parking and a car wash in order to generate more cash flow to realise expansion of the company in the near future. 

The cooperative is considering pasteurising the milk for sales in the region via techniques including a dispenser, estimated to cost 500,000 KSh. The cooperative sees this as a niche market, related to present sales of fresh milk in the region via milk shops. For the time being, the existing location and facilities are sufficiently equipped to receive milk. Nevertheless, to realise its ambitions, the cooperative believes a new location is necessary to realising sufficient quality, not only for the intake but also for the processing part. The cooperative is clearly looking for expertise to work out feasibility, market analysis and business planning and then realise it goals. Until now, the cooperative has always realised its plans on its own and has not received support from other development organisations.

The underlying action plan describes the activities foreseen in 2011 and targets mostly aspects related to increased productivity, improved supply chain management, scoping new markets and improving membership patronage. Activities related to daily operations such as intake, cooling and trading of milk have been left out of the action plan.

ACTION PLAN 2012
Looking at the developments and challenges in 2011, for 2012 the main recommendations are:
• To have a quality focus at Kiambaa by further improving the quality throughout
their supply chain and at the same time promote their quality of milk to (new) customers. This includes also the improvement of hygiene standards at farm level (during milking, cleaning etc)
• Focus on the markets Kiambaa is already in and improve their profit to substitute from low end to higher end. From there, gradually build new (niche) markets. Processing capacity should grow together with the market position.
• Gradually build a processing plant, first by increasing current capacity and install dairy equipment only when a profitable market position has been build or when milk supply volume has grown substantially.
• Find a partner (Ndumberi) to jointly invest or even merge to obtain loading for future processing equipment.
• Keep training staff and farmers. Further develop capacity of employees to strengthen sales and marketing staff and keep training the farmers to support further milk supply growth.

The next steps for Kiambaa in 2012 are to invest in chilling capacity (see business case 1), promote & invest in quality and continue the training programs. Furthermore, the intended merger with Ndumeri needs to be worked out and hopefully realized in 2012 to support future profit growth. Finally the development of a practical and innovative logistics analytical tool will be one of the activities in 2012.

For 2013: elaborate business plan for processing plant

title: Developing business model for dairy microfranchising _ Orientation stage
description:
As a follow up of the partnership election that RFC won in cooperation with Agriterra, with their idea for setting up an innovative business idea in Kenya, this project gives an orientation of how to go about, in case we elaborate upon this concept that won the prize in the Partnership election. 

Approximately a third of the Kenyan population suffers from malnutrition. Dairy has the unique combination of local availability, low prices and high nutrition density, making it very suited for combatting malnutrition. Kenya produces about 5 billion kg of milk each year. About a fifth of this however is lost due to spillage in the journey from cow to end consumer. This amount equals two glasses of milk per Kenyan per week.
 
There is a plethora of small dairy cooperations which do not process milk themselves and which have insufficient market power to negotiate a good price with large dominant dairy processors (of which there are only a dozen or so). The market price for milk in Kenya is about 35% under world market price level, most likely due to this market structure. Because of this very structure, much milk is spilled, also due to haphazard contracting.  
Solution
In order to combat milk spillage in Kenya a micro franchise model will be developed and executed. FrieslandCampina possesses knowledge in all parts of the dairy chain; ‘from grass to glass’. With this international knowledge and the expertise of Agriterra on cooperative development, a good micro franchise model will be built where local distributors can join. This stimulates local entrepreneurship and creates employment. 
In the micro-franchise model  all important parts of the dairy chain: training of local farmers, quality assurance, CSR, support of local cooperations and the development of distribution channels. 

With this solution, farmers will be offered a guaranteed turnover whilst at the same time making goodness of dairy affordable for a lot of Kenyans. 

Feasibility and long term goals
Our goal for 2020 is to:
•	Have 16 million kilograms of milk processed to end product by local cooperations, which equals a market share of 3% of all milk processed in Kenya.
•	Pay a loyalty benefit of 2.5 cents per kg of milk to the participating cooperations.
•	Create jobs and employability for 5.000 Kenyans in the form of distributors and sales representatives, earning a year income which is higher than the national mean income. 
•	Offer a branded dairy product for a price per kg which is on par with or slightly below the current non-branded market price of approximately € 0,80/kg
•	Generate an EBIT for FrieslandCampina of € 1.2 mln on a yearly basis.

Local dairy farmers and sales(wo)men do not bear any financial risk in this franchise model and for distributors an earn-back period of approximately one year was calculated. The threshold for participation for locals is therefore quite low. FrieslandCampina bears the major part of the financial risk with a projected earn-back period of 5 years. 

We will use the years between now and 2020 to steadily grow to the volumes and turnovers mentioned. In the meantime, both Agriterra and FrieslandCampina will report progress on a yearly basis to their stakeholders via the annual report. The underlying project only covers the orientation stage, ending on 1st April.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Abwasser Lake Victoria
description: Der Viktoriasee, die bedeutendste Süßwasserreserve in Ostafrika, ist im Zuge des steigenden Bevölkerungswachstums und der voranschreitenden Verstädterung zunehmend bedroht von Verschmutzung durch die Einleitung ungeklärter Abwässer in die Flüsse im Wassereinzugsgebiet. In vielen Städten im Wassereinzugsgebiet mangelt es an adäquater Trinkwasserver- und Abwasserentsorgung.Das Vorhaben soll zum einen durch die Verbesserung des Abwassermanagements einen Beitrag zum Schutz des Viktoriasees leisten und zum anderen den Zugang der Bevölkerung in ausgewählten Städten zu Sanitäreinrichtungen und Trinkwasserversorgung verbessern. Die geplanten Investitionsmaßnahmen des Vorhabens bestehen überwiegend aus Bauleistungen zur Rehabilitierung und Erweiterung bereits bestehender Wasserversorgungs- und /oder Abwasserentsorgungssystemen in den Städten Kericho, Kisii und Litein. Voraussichtlich rd. 94.000 Menschen werden Zugang zur leitungsgebundenen Wasserversorgung erhalten und ca. 30.000 Zugang zur leitungsgebundenen Abwasserentsorgung. Während die direkte Zielgruppe die urbane und peri-urbane Bevölkerung in den Städten Kisii, Kericho und Litein umfasst, profitieren indirekt auch die gesamte Bevölkerung des Einzugsgebiets des Viktoriasees von der verbesserten Abwassersammlung und -reinigung im Projektgebiet. Das FZ-Modul schließt direkt an das inzwischen abgeschlossene Vorhaben Entwicklung des Wasser- und Sanitätssektors - Lake Victoria South an, in dessen Rahmen u. a. auch in Kisii, und Kericho bereits Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung der Wasserversorgung sowie der Ausbau der Kläranalage am Standort Kisii umgesetzt wurden. Das Modul ist Teil der trilateralen Kooperation mit Israel. Von der israelischen Regierung wurden Trainings für Institutionen im Wassersektor in der Region durchgeführt. | Lake Victoria, the most important freshwater reserve in East Africa, is increasingly threatened by pollution from the discharge of untreated sewage into the waterbodies of the catchment area as a result of rising population growth and advancing urbanisation. Many towns in the catchment area lack adequate water supply and wastewater disposal.The project aims to contribute to the protection of Lake Victoria by improving wastewater management and by improving the populations access to sanitation facilities and water supply in selected towns. The planned investment measures of the project mainly consist of construction works for the rehabilitation and expansion of already existing water supply and/or sewage disposal systems in the towns of Kericho, Kisii and Litein. It is expected that about 94,000 people will have access to water supply and about 30,000 to sanitation. While the direct target group comprises the urban and peri-urban population in the towns of Kisii, Kericho and Litein, the entire population of the Lake Victoria catchment area will also benefit indirectly from improved wastewater collection and treatment in the project area. The FC module is a direct follow-up to the now completed project Development of the Water and Sanitation Sector - Lake Victoria South, under which measures to improve the water supply and expand the sewage treatment plant at the Kisii site have already been implemented in Kisii and Kericho, among other places. The module is part of the trilateral cooperation with Israel. The Israeli government has conducted training for institutions in the water sector in the region. | Beitrag zum Schutz des Viktoriasees durch Reduzierung von Abwässern

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Entwicklung des Wasser- und Sanitärsektors - Water Services Trust Fund, Phase III
description: Ziel der FZ-Maßnahme ist die Sicherstellung einer ausreichenden, hygienisch einwandfreien, sozial verträglichen und nachhaltigen Wasser- und Basissanitärversorgung für städtische Arme in Kenia.  Programmträger der FZ-Maßnahme ist der Water Services Trust Fund (WSTF), eine nationale Finanzierungsinstitution zur Mobilisierung und Umsetzung von sektorspezifischen, armutsorientierten Investitionen. Die Durchführung der Maßnahmen in städtischen Armutsgebieten erfolgt dabei ausschließlich durch lizenzierte Wasserversorgungsunternehmen, die sich im Rahmen regelmäßig abgehaltener Ausschreibungswettbewerbe für die Finanzierung durch den WSTF qualifizieren müssen.  Zielgruppe der Maßnahme ist die noch unzureichend mit Trinkwasser und Sanitäreinrichtungen versorgte Bevölkerung in städtischen Armutsvierteln in ganz Kenia. Das Vorhaben wird in enger Zusammenarbeit zwischen GIZ und KfW in einem integrierten, kohärenten Ansatz mit einer Gesamtlaufzeit von rund drei Jahren durchgeführt. Die FZ-Mittel werden dabei flexibel und bedarfsabhängig für die Verbesserung der Wasser- und Sanitärversorgung in städtischen Armutsgebieten eingesetzt. Hauptmaßnahmen sind (1) der Ausbau der städtischen Wasserversorgung über angepasste technische Lösungen, z.B. Wasserkioske, sowie (2) der Bau von öffentlichen und privaten Sanitäreinheiten zur Basissanitärversorgung armer Bevölkerungsgruppen. Innovative Betriebskonzepte, bedarfsorientierte Aufklärungs- und Sensibilisierungsmaßnahmen sowie abgestimmte Maßnahmen zur Stärkung des Trägers ergänzen das Vorhaben. Die Gesamtkosten der FZ-Maßnahme betragen insgesamt rund EUR 10,2 Mio. Der FZ-Zuschuss für das Programm beläuft sich auf EUR 8,5 Mio. und wird ergänzt um einen Eigenbeitrag des Partners in Höhe von 1,7 Mio. EUR (20% des FZ-Zuschusses). Seit Ende 2011 erfolgt eine Ko-Finanzierung mit der Bill und Melinda Gates Stiftung (BMGF) in Höhe von USD 7.130.699 mit Fokus auf den Ausbau der Basissanitärversorgung. | Development of the water and sanitation sector - Water Services Trust Fund, Phase III | EZ-Programmziel (Impact): Sauberes Wasser und grundlegende sanitäre Einrichtungen werden von der Bevölkerung in den unterstützten (rand-)städtischen Gebieten nachhaltig und gleichberechtigt genutzt, wobei Wasserressourcen geschützt werden.FZ-Modulziel (Output):Sicherstellung einer ausreichenden, hygienisch einwandfreien, sozial verträglichen und nachhaltigen Wasserversorgung und Basissanitärversorgung (WV/SV) für städtische Arme in Kenia.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Wasser- und Sanitaerversorgung in (rand)städtischen Wachstumsregionen
description: Kenia ist der Entwicklungsmotor Ostafrikas. Es ist von schneller Urbanisierung und hohem Bevölkerungswachstum gekennzeichnet. Davon sind überproportional die (rand-)städtischen Wachstumsregionen (Satellitenstädte) um die Hauptstadt Nairobi betroffen - sie wachsen mehr als eineinhalb Mal so schnell wie der Landesdurchschnitt. Infolgedessen stehen sie vor der großen Herausforderung, öffentliche Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen sowohl umgehend bereitzustellenals auch den Bedarf langfristig zu decken.Von der fehlenden öffentlichen Infrastruktur ist insbesondere die Wasser - und Sanitärversorgung beziehungsweise Abwasserentsorgung betroffen. Chronische Wasserrationierungen und Gesundheitsrisiken für oftmals einkommensschwache Verbraucher sind die Folge. Zudem wird sowohl die Umwelt als auch die Entwicklung der Industrie durch die fehlende Wasser - und Abwasserinfrastruktur negativ beeinträchtigt. Vor diesem Hintergrund zielt das Vorhaben auf die Sicherstellung eines ausreichenden, sozial und wirtschaftlich tragfähigen Zugangs der Zielbevölkerung in den Satellitenstädten zu sauberem Wasser, in Einbindung weiterer Investitionen ineine angemessene Abwasserentsorgung.Die Gestaltung des FZ-Vorhabens basiert auf einem in Kenia bislang einzigartigen, partizipativen Bottom-up-Ansatz. Dabei schlugen Wasserversorgungsunternehmen aus den Zielgebieten Investitionen mit Fokus auf arme Bevölkerungsschichten vor. Eine Besonderheit ist dabei, dass die Investitionsvorschläge im Sinne eines ganzheitlichen, arbeitsteiligen Vorgehens andere Interventionen im Programmgebiet ergänzen. Hierbei sind insbesondere Investitionen in die Sanitärversorgung zu betonen, welche von dem EZ-unterstützten Water Sector Trust Fund (WSTF), der kenianischen Regierung und anderen Gebern finanziert werden.Aufgrund des enormen Investitionsbedarfs wurde das FZ-Vorhaben für mehrere Phasen geplant. Die hier dargestellte Phase I bezieht sich auf die 2013 zugesagten FZ-Mittel in Höhe von 28 Mio. EUR. Sie umfasst den Ausbau der (rand-)städtischen Wasserversorgung in den Gebieten Ruiru-Juja und Ongata Rongai/Oloolaiser sowie Consultingleistungen für u.a. Bauplanung und Bauüberwachung. Es ist geplant, die Programmträger mit einer Aus- und Fortbildungsmaßnahmeund einer Unterstützung durch die Technische Zusammenarbeit zu stärken. Die Laufzeit der Phase I wird auf rund dreieinhalb Jahre geschätzt. Da sich die die deutsche Entwicklungszusammenarbeit aus dem Wassersektor zurückzieht, ist derzeit keine weitere Phase geplant.Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss der FZ-Maßnahme (Phase I) soll die Wasserversorgung für rund 340.000 Menschen verbessert sein (davon rund 260.000, die bislang keinerlei Zugang haben). Gleichzeitig sollen die kenianischen Institutionen in die Lage versetzt werden, eigenständig die weitere Ausdehnung und Verbesserung der Wasser - und Sanitärversorgung vorzunehmen.Die Gesamtkosten der FZ-Maßnahme (Phase I) betragen rund 30,8 Mio. EUR. Diese sollen über ein FZ-Darlehen in Höhe von 28 Mio. EUR und einen Eigenbeitrag der kenianischen Regierung in Höhe von rund 2,8 Mio. EUR finanziert werden. Hinzu kommen - bei entsprechender Nachfrage des Empfängers - weitere 1,3 Mio. EUR Zuschuss für die A+F Maßnahme (BMZ-Nr. 1930.0508.9), welche bereits im Rahmen des benachbarten FZ-Vorhabens Erweiterung und Modernisierung der Wasserversorgung in Nairobi zugesagt wurden. | Support to water and sanitation services in peri-urban areas | EZ-Programmziel (Impact): Sauberes Wasser und grundlegende sanitäre Einrichtungen werden von der Bevölkerung in den unterstützten (rand-)städtischen Gebieten nachhaltig und gleichberechtigt genutzt, wobei Wasserressourcen geschützt werden.FZ-Modulziel (Output):Sicherstellung eines ausreichenden, sozial und wirtschaftlich tragfähigen und nachhaltigen Zugangs der Zielbevölkerung zu sauberem Wasser.

reporting_org_name: Imperial College of Science, Technology and Medicine
title: NIHR Global Health Research Group on Digital Diagnostics for African  Health Systems
description: The Project aims to investigate whether a new type of diagnostic test, called a digital diagnostic, will be better than currently available diagnostic tests in African health care settings. We aim to evaluate whether digital diagnostics technology will work properly, whether it will provide accurate diagnoses, and whether we can optimise it to give the maximum chance that it is adopted intopractice in African healthcare systems. To do this, we need to fully understand the context in which it will be used, and understand the perspectives of all of those who might be impacted, from the patients and healthcare workers right up to ministries of health and international policy makers. We do this through different types of interviews and focus groups. We optimise the design of digital diagnostics in partnership with the intended users – so called “co-design”. We assess the potential impact on health systems to understand how other aspects of diagnosis and care might be affected. We compare accuracy of diagnoses using our digital diagnostics technology against those of the best possible "gold standard" diagnostic tests, and also against any tests in common use in Africa.We want to look at different scenarios where there are important gaps in the availability, accuracy, or data collection from currentdiagnostic tests. These scenarios are:   1. detection of malaria parasites;   2. cause of fever in young children;   3. detecting bacterial contamination of water and food. The countries where the research is underatken are:   - The Gambia  - Ghana   - Burkina Faso  - Kenya   - Sudan   - Zambia The research plan is structured in 6 cross-cutting Work Packages and 10 Sub-Projects as follows: WP1 | Technology Development Lead: Prof. Pantelis Georgiou (Imperial College London)WP2 | Community Engagement and InvolvementLead: Prof. Salome Bukachi (University of Nairobi)WP3 | Diagnostic Evaluation Leads: Dr Jane Achan (Malaria Consortium), Dr Samuel Duodu (University of Ghana)WP4 | Health Systems Lead: Dr Julie Balen (University of Sheffield)WP5 | User Interface Co-designLead: Dr Talya Porat (Imperial College London)WP6 | Data Integration and ApplicationLeads: Prof. Céire Costelloe (Institute of Cancer Research), Mr Darlington Akogo (minoHealth AISP1 |  Evaluation of the detection of asymptomatic carriage of malaria parasites in cross-sectional community screening surveys using a point of care digital diagnostic PhD Student: Dimbintsoa Robinson, MRC Unit The Gambia (LSYTM) – Supervisors: Prof. D'Alessandro, Prof Tinto                 SP2 |  Evaluation of the detection of malaria parasite species and anti-malarial resistance in uncomplicated malaria patients using a point of care digital diagnostic  PhD Student: Martin Chamai, University of Ghana, WACCBIP – Supervisors: Dr Amoah, Prof. AwandareSP3 |  Evaluation of the detection of malaria in pregnancy and anti-malarial drug resistance using a point of care digital diagnostic PhD Student: Jean-Bertin Kabuya, Tropical Diseases Research Centre – Supervisor: Prof. Christine ManyandoSP4 |  Evaluation of detection of P. falciparum and P. Vivax malaria and G6PD deficiency using a point of care digital diagnostic PhD Student: Waleed Mohammed Alhaj Jebreel, University of Khartoum, IEND – Supervisors: Prof. Osman, Prof. MahdiSP5 |  Evaluating a digital diagnostic to distinguish between causes of childhood febrile illness PhD Student: Flavian Akite, University of Ghana, WACCBIP – Supervisors: Dr Duodu, Dr Usuf, Dr CunningtonSP6 |  Developing and evaluating a digital diagnostic for environmental pathogen detection PhD Student: Erick Odoyo, Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST) – Supervisors: Dr Sifuna, Dr Rodriguez ManzanoSP7 |  Evaluating digital diagnostic implementation through national and international health policy &   health systems analysis PhD Student: Shola Kelly Molemodile Dele-Olowu, University of Ghana – Supervisors: Dr Balen, Prof. Yeung, Prof. YawsonSP8 |  Evaluating digital diagnostic implementation through local health systems and service analysis PhD Student: Mamadu Baldeh, MRC Unit The Gambia (LSYTM) – Supervisors: Dr Balen, Prof de Witte, Prof YeungSP9 |  Co-design and development of user interfaces for digital diagnostics PhD Student: Angelina Ankah Amengu, University of Ghana – Supervisors: Dr Porat, Dr AbdulaiSP10 |  Integration and application of data from digital diagnostics for disease surveillance and control PhD Student: Francis Dzabeng, University of Ghana – Supervisors: Dr Abdulai, Mr Akogo, Dr Okell, Dr CostelloeThe involvement of community members, as potential end-users of the diagnostics, is central to the codesign process. Wider community engagement will be undertaken for the diagnostic accuracy studiesto ensure that the research is appropriate and approved by the local communities.

title: Strengthening the resilience of smallholder families to drought disasters in rural Kenya
description: Insufficient rainfall has led to one of the worst droughts ever in northern and eastern Kenya. The project will support farming households in sustainably using and regenerating their livelihoods, consisting of crops, livestock, water and pasture. Training and concrete measures on marketing, animal husbandry, hydroponics, conservation of natural resources, seed preservation are offered. The target group consists of two thousand households, most of them women. | Zu geringe Regenfälle haben im Norden und Osten Kenias zu einer der bisher schlimmsten Dürren geführt, Das Projekt wird bäuerliche Haushalte dabei unterstützen, ihre Lebensgrundlage, bestehend aus Feldfrüchten, Vieh, Wasser und Weideland, nachhaltig zu nutzen und zu regenerieren. Dazu werden Fortbildungen und konkrete Maßnahmen zu Vermarktung, Tierhaltung, Wasserbau, Konservierung natürlicher Ressourcen, Bewahrung von Saatgut angeboten. Zielgruppe sind zweitausend Haushalte, zu einem großen Teil Frauen.

title: Clean Energy + Improved WASH for Schools in Upper Eastern
description: Within the project water infrastructure will be built at 6 target schools (through ferrocement tanks and boreholes), sanitary infrastructure including hand washing facilities will be built and existing ones will be improved. Per school one biogas plant will built, which will be fed by the students excrement and convert it into biogas. The residual mass of biogas production is used as fertilizer in the school gardens and reforestation is actively carried out in the schools. There are training courses in good hygiene practices for students and teachers, as well as training in forestry and soil- and environmentally-friendly agricultural practices | Im Projekt werden an 6 Zielschulen Wasserinfrastruktur gebaut (durch Ferrozementtanks und Bohrlöcher), Sanitärinfrastruktur inklusive Handwaschvorrichtung neu gebaut und bestehende verbessert, sowie jeweils eine Biogasanlage gebaut, die durch das Wasser und die Toiletten gespeist wird und die Ausscheidungen der Schüler:innen in Biogas umwandelt. Die Restmasse der Biogasproduktion wird als Dünger in den Schulgärten verwendet und es wird aktiv Wiederaufforstung an den Schulen betrieben. Es gibt Schulungen in guten Hygienepraktiken für Schüler:Innen und Lehrkräfte, sowie Schulungen in Forstwirtschaft und boden- und umweltschonenden landwirtschaftlichen Methoden.

title: Resilience Strengethening Turkana West
description: Turkana West is characterized by water scarcity, land degradation, and declining agricultural productivity. The project aims to strengthen the resilience of eight communities in Turkana West through income diversification, food security, and the protection and restoration of natural resources, with a particular focus on soil quality. Key measures include improving access to safe water, promoting vegetable cultivation, and introducing energy-efficient stoves that also serve as chicken incubators. In addition, cultivation of vetiver is supported to enhance soil fertility and ensure fodder availability for livestock. | Turkana West ist geprägt von Wasserknappheit, Bodendegradation und sinkender landwirtschaftlicher Produktivität. Das Projekt stärkt die Resilienz von acht Gemeinden in Turkana West durch Einkommensdiversifizierung, Ernährungssicherung sowie Schutz und Wiederherstellung natürlicher Ressourcen, insbesondere der Bodenqualität. Zentrale Maßnahmen sind der verbesserte Zugang zu sicherem Wasser, die Förderung des Gemüseanbaus sowie die Einführung energiesparender Öfen, die zugleich als Hühnerbrüter dienen. Ergänzend wird der Anbau von Vetiver unterstützt, um Bodenfruchtbarkeit und Viehfutterversorgung zu sichern.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Bewässerungsfeldbau im semiariden Bereich für Kleinbauern zur Ernährungssicherung 2
description: Die im Land weit verbreitete Technologie der Wasserspeicherung, der Sanddamm-Technologie (https://wasser-fuer-kenia.de/sanddaemme/), wurde von unserer Partnerorganisation bisher überwiegend nur zur Trinkwasserbeschaffung verwendet und diente bisher selten der dauerhaften Existenzsicherung durch Bewässerungsfeldbau. Dies wurde durch das von Bengo geförderte Projekt P5468 beispielhaft geändert: Dazu wurde an einen vorhandenen Sanddamm eine von der lokalen Bevölkerung zu bauende Wasserleitung mit Solarpumpe, Speichertank, Wasserkiosk, Viehtränke und v.a. Bewässerungsfeldbau mit Tröpfchenbewässerung angebunden. Ziel war die Vermeidung der Ernährungsunsicherheit, die dauerhafte Existenzsicherung von 80 Kleinbauernfamilien und damit die Reduzierung des Migrationsdruckes. Das gelungene Beispiel und die dabei gemachten Erfahrungen können nun auf andere für Sanddämme geeignete Flusstäler bei ähnlichen physisch-geographischen Verhältnissen übertragen werden. | The sand dam technology (https://wasser-fuer-kenia.de/sanddaemme/), which is widely used in the country for water storage, has so far only been used by our partner organisation to procure drinking water and has rarely been used to secure long-term livelihoods through irrigation farming. This was changed in an exemplary manner by the P5468 project sponsored by Bengo: To this end, a water pipeline to be built by the local population was connected to an existing sand dam with a solar pump, storage tank, water kiosk, cattle drinking trough and, above all, irrigation field construction with drip irrigation. The aim was to prevent food insecurity, secure the long-term livelihood of 80 smallholder families and thus reduce migration pressure. The successful example and the experience gained can now be transferred to other river valleys suitable for sand dams with similar physical and geographical conditions.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Drinking water supply at Chulaimbo Hospital Kisumu
description: An existing borehole is to be converted into a solar-powered well, enabling us to establish a drinking water supply, improve the sustainable provision of clean drinking water to the population and ensure hygiene in the hospital. The borehole belongs to the hospital as trustee of the county government. Currently, there is no drinking water supply because the pump is not working. The borehole is to be equipped with a solar-powered pump to ensure the supply. The objectives are therefore to provide running drinking water, improve hygiene, expand the hospitals own agricultural food production, and establish a water distribution point for the population. Once the project is complete, medical staff and patients will be supplied with clean drinking water. The project will be implemented by local construction companies with the support of students from a vocational school in Kisumu. | Eine vorhandenes Bohrloch soll zum solarbetriebenen Brunnen ausgebaut werden, damit wollen wir eine Trinkwasserversorgung aufbauen, die Versorgung der Bevölkerung mit sauberem Trinkwasser nachhaltig verbessern und die Hygiene im Krankenhaus gewährleisten. Das Bohrloch gehört dem Krankenhaus als Treuhänderin des County Governments. Aktuell gibt es keine Trinkwasserversorgung, da die Pumpe nicht funktionstüchtig ist. Das Bohrloch soll mit einer solarbetriebenen Pumpe ausgestattet werden, um die Versorgung zu gewährleisten. Ziele sind somit die Versorgung mit fließendem Trinkwasser, die Verbesserung der Hygiene, der Ausbau der eigenen landwirtschaftlichen Erzeugung von Lebensmitteln, sowie die Wasserausgabestelle für die Bevölkerung. Nach Fertigstellung des Projekts sind das medizinische Personal und die Patienten mit sauberem Trinkwasser versorgt. Das Projekt wird von Bauunternehmen vor Ort mit Unterstützung von Schüler und Schülerinnen einer Berufsschule in Kisumu umgesetzt werden.

reporting_org_name: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
title: Solar-powered water supply for a school in Kenya
description: The municipal partnership between the town of Gersthofen and Baringo County in Kenya has been in place for many years. Sabor Secondary School in Kenya currently has no reliable drinking water supply. The existing water tank on the school grounds is filled with rainwater, but this is not sufficient to meet water needs during periods of drought. The lack of water supply significantly affects the hygienic conditions, health and overall quality of life of the pupils and teachers. The main objective of the project is to ensure a sustainable drinking water supply for the school. To this end, a well is to be drilled and a solar-powered water pump installed. This will ensure a continuous and environmentally friendly water supply. Drilling of a well near the school to obtain clean drinking water. Installation of a solar-powered water pump for sustainable and independent water supply. The solar-powered pump fills the water storage system (tank). Construction of a water storage system for temporary storage and distribution of water. The tank is installed on a sturdy steel frame to ensure sufficient height for the water to be distributed to the connected extraction point using natural gravity. Training the school community in the sustainable use and maintenance of the water system. Capacity building on site: two experts from Germany fly to Baringo to familiarise the teaching staff with the maintenance of the pump and the solar system. | Die kommunale Partnerschaft zwischen der Stadt Gersthofen und dem County Baringo in Kenia besteht bereits seit vielen Jahren. Die Sabor Secondary School in Kenia verfügt derzeit über keine zuverlässige Trinkwasserversorgung. Der bestehende Wassertank auf dem Schulgelände wird durch Regenwasser gefüllt, reicht jedoch nicht aus, um den Wasserbedarf während Dürreperioden zu decken. Die mangelnde Wasserversorgung beeinträchtigt die hygienischen Bedingungen, die Gesundheit sowie die allgemeine Lebensqualität der Schülerinnen, Schüler und Lehrkräfte erheblich. Das Hauptziel des Projekts ist die nachhaltige Sicherstellung der Trinkwasserversorgung für die Schule. Hierfür soll ein Brunnen gebohrt und eine solarbetriebene Wasserpumpe installiert werden. Dies gewährleistet eine kontinuierliche und umweltfreundliche Wasserversorgung. Bohrung eines Brunnens in der Nähe der Schule zur Gewinnung von sauberem Trinkwasser. Installation einer solarbetriebenen Wasserpumpe zur nachhaltigen und unabhängigen Wasserförderung. Die solarbetriebene Pumpe befüllt das Wasserspeichersystem (Tank). Errichtung eines Wasserspeichersystems zur Zwischenlagerung und Verteilung des Wassers. Der Tank ist auf einem stabilen Stahlgerüst installiert, sodass eine ausreichende Höhe gewährleistet ist, um das Wasser mit natürlichem Gefälle an die angeschlossene Entnahmestelle zu verteilen. Schulung der Schulgemeinschaft zur nachhaltigen Nutzung und Pflege der Wasseranlage. Capacity Building vor Ort: zwei Fachleute aus Deutschland fliegen nach Baringo, um das Lehrpersonal mit dem Unterhalt der Pumpe und der Solaranlage vertraut zu machen.
