title: Kipini Swahili Eco-lodge
description: The Kipini Conservancy is located in the northeast of Kenya, and consists of an area of 220 km2. The conservancy links the coastline to the hinterland and is part of a connected migration corridor for elephants and other species.The size, geographical location and biodiversity of conservancy are unique and recognised as ecologically and biologically outstanding by the WWF.The project partners have developed a concept in which conservancy, tourism, and community involvement are integrated and interconnected. This concept is already successfully introduced with a PSOM grant in Ethiopia.The joint venture will develop and exploit lodges and tourist activities, and thereby generate income for conservancy and local communities. A separate entity, The Kipini Wildlife and Botanical Conservancy (KWBC), will be responsible for maintaining and developing the conservancy. The consortium will contribute a minimum of 25% of his profit to the KWBC. The local communities will be an essential part of the tourist activities. Touristic potential in the communities (Orma tribe, Kipini women's group, Fishery Association Kipini) will be developed, together with the consortium, what will lead to steady income for the locals. They will also add to the maintenance of the conservancy by the sustainable use of it. A joint venture will be established between Princeps Management Consultants and Nairobi Ranching Company.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)The whole business concept is set up around environmental sustainability, ecological conservancy, ecotourism, inclusion of the local community and capacity building of the local community.The joint venture will follow the internationally recognised ETI Base Code regarding the basic working conditions. In addition they will provide free lunches, payment of medical care insurance, education and professional training, access to HIV/AIDS prevention, family planning programmes, housing and transport to and from the lodge. Furthermore, the ecolodge will be certified by the Eco Tourism Society of Kenya, which guarantees a sustainable approach with regard to energy (solar/wind), waste disposal and the design and construction of the lodge. An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) will be executed at the beginning of the project.Impact•	Employment and working conditions36 full-time jobs will be created. In addition employment will be created in the local communities. They estimate that 150 indirect jobs will be created in the local communities at the end op the project. The joint venture will follow the internationally recognised ETI Base Code. Following working conditions will be provided by the joint venture:- Good salaries.- Company lunches.- Medical care insurance/reimbursement of medical costs of employees.- The opportunity of education and professional training.- Access to a HIV/AIDS prevention and family planning programme.- Transport to and from the lodge.- Housing.•	Innovation/Transfer of knowledgeThis project introduces a new business concept to Kenya, in which conservancy, tourism, and community involvement are integrated and interconnected. All stakeholders, including guests, will be taught about the concept, on their own level:- Employees will receive training in the principles of the concept.- The inhabitants of the involved communities will be trained in the development of sustainable economic activities and the sustainable use of the conservancy.- Guests of the lodge (the tourists) will be offered the opportunity to learn about the concept, the unique characteristics of Kipini and the local community culture and traditions.•	Chain effectsParties that benefit directly from the project on long term are:- Employees, by having the opportunity for a secured long term job.- Local communities around the conservancy, by having opportunities to generate income from tourist activities.- KWBC, by receiving a steady flow of income for the maintenance and development of the conservancy.- Tour operators, by being able to offer new activities/locations.- Tourist accommodations in the region, by spin off effect and enhancement of the attractiveness of the area.•	EnvironmentThe central aim of the project is the preservation of the natural environment of the Kipini conservancy. The lodge will be designed by a professional eco-architect to fit as harmoniously as possible into its natural environment. In the design, as many natural materials as possible will be used. State-of-the-art sustainable solutions will be used regarding energy (solar energy, wind energy), water (use of rain-water for flushing toilets, waste water treatment by means of helophyte filters), and waste disposal (a waste treatment and separation system will be considered).•	Position of womenAt least 50% of the workforce will be female. They will be trained and educated. Furthermore, the Community Cultural Tourist Clusters (CCTC) will be managed by local women's groups. Since women will be managing the clusters, mainly women will be trained, in the field of management and creating sustainable income generating economic activities.

title: Jambo Fish: aquaculture learning and fingerling production
description: Applicant Fleuren & Nooijen B.V. is specialised in the hatching and breeding of African catfish. Local partner Jambo Fish Ltd. is a small aquaculture firm that started up in 2010. It is partially owned by the applicant. After researching the growth conditions of catfish in Kenya for a few years, the partners planned to start a commercial pilot project. The partners intend to build a new hatchery for catfish fingerlings. Jambo Fish has difficulties selling its limited production of table sized catfish. However, the company cannot meet demand of catfish fingerlings. Based on this experience they plan to increase the size of the market for fingerlings by training extension workers and farmers on modern aquaculture. These fingerlings will be raised in ponds by farmers. The partners hold the opinion that selling fingerlings to small scale farmers is a better way to penetrate the Kenyan market than by growing fingerlings to table sized fish themselves. By doing it this way, they will reach the largely informal markets that the partners cannot reach themselves. The government of Kenya is stimulating the development of aquaculture financially as well as through the construction of thousands of fish ponds.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)The largest CSR risk is the origin of the fish feed. Since all this will be sourced from Nutreco, this is sufficiently covered.The partners pledge to devote time and effort to implementing and defining CSR guidelines, not only because of the social impact, but also because they consider this necessary for committed and dedicated employees. A written CSR statement on the local joint venture's policy and its implementation will be part of the first project result.Impact•	Employment and working conditionsSalaries will be at least 20% above minimum wages. The employees will be extensively trained on aquaculture. Extension workers will be trained in didactical skills to train farmers and visitors. They will also be trained to detect child labour indications, health and safety procedures. The extension workers will also be trained in business skills to help the farmers in making tailor-made business plans for profitable catfish production.•	Innovation / Transfer of knowledgeCurrently, there is no other large scale hatchery of catfish fingerlings in Kenya. Catfish aquaculture as such is undeveloped.•	Chain effectsNo local suppliers are involved in this project.One of the goals of this project is that aquaculture is no longer seen as a subsistence activity by farmers, but as a commercial activity with the aim of making significant economic gains. Next to being a supplier of fingerlings, feed and aquaculture accessories, the new joint venture will also act as a training centre where farmers, students, government and NGO extension workers, researchers, and local entrepreneurs will be trained.•	Impact on the sectorNGOs working with small-scale farmers in areas such as nutrition and fish rearing will be able to follow or organise trainings.•	EnvironmentPressure on natural fish stocks in Kenya is high and this has resulted in overfishing. It would be a benefit if the successful introduction of catfish aquaculture leads to less overfishing.•	Position of womenThe managing director of the joint venture will be female. Also, half of the total staff employed will be women. The project will actively promote women participation in fish farming.•	Impact on food safetyFish is a critical source of dietary protein and micronutrients. Aquaculture makes a direct contribution to improving food security through the provision of high quality food, self-employment and income. The availability of affordable fish makes a huge contribution towards improving household food security, especially in terms of improved access to animal proteins.•	Impact on waterThe joint venture will use a closed circuit approach in the hatchery and a closed line approach in the grow-out ponds. This approach allows for more efficient use of water resources than traditional 'flush through' ponds. | The partners intend to set up a catfish hatchery that will sell 1,900,000 catfish fingerlings annually, that will provide catfish aquaculture training, and acts as a service centre for hatchery feed, grow out feed and aquaculture tools.

title: Koppert Cress a new way of growing and marketing
description: Update on the projectSupplying for the high-end market in the Netherlands turned out to be a challenge. Although the partners looked for other buyers in a different market segment the scale of the project remained modest. With a net positive result and a growing market potential this project has the potential to scale-up when the market not only embraces the idea, but actually starts buying.DescriptionThe project partners, Koppert Cress B.V. from Monster, the Netherlands and The African Herb Company Ltd., based in Nanyuki, Kenya, plan to set up a joint venture that will supply fresh herbal teas to the high end restaurant market in Europe. Koppert Cress is a horticultural company supplying the world's most renowned restaurants with cresses and micro sized vegetables. The African Herb Company, started up in 2010, currently produces fresh mint and rosemary for the European market. The export of fresh herbal tea (technically not tea but an infusion) is a new product for Kenya. Each serving of a combination of herbs will provide information on the workers that plucked and assembled the herbs, and provide information on the life and living conditions of individual employees through a mobile phone application. Therefore, a number of professional videos will be made at the project site in Nanyuki. These serve to make the customer aware of the origin of the product. This will also be part of the 'pull marketing' strategy that the applicant always uses when introducing new products. The joint venture will also produce a number of 'micro vegetables'. These are trademarked products of Koppert Cress such as Pepquino, Cressabi and an edible type of orchid. Currently, the applicant is unable to produce these vegetables year round. Producing in Kenya will change that. The project partners will gain Fair Trade Certification. There will be a tree planting programme at the estate to compensate for CO2 emissions. ISO 26000 standards will be incorporated in order to link up with the business operations of Koppert Cress.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)CSR is considered very important for this project by the partners. The subject will be used extensively in the related marketing campaign.The marketing of the product will involve the makers of the product i.e. the workers on the farm. The product will be certified socially as well as organically. Also care for the environment is an important issue for the partners.The wife of one of the owners of the local company is a wildlife conservationist. She is very much involved in getting the unused part of their land back into the forested area that it once was. In recent times trees were chopped down for the production of charcoal and the land was degraded due to intensive goat grazing. She has set up a conservation management plan for their estate. The tree planting programme in order to compensate for CO2 emissions during transport will be a stimulus for this plan.The project creates almost a 100 full-time jobs in a region with limited job opportunities. By doing this the partners are reducing the region's dependence on food aid.Impact•	Employment and working conditionsWorkers will receive extensive on the job training on biological control and safe handling. More advanced trainings will be about insect monitoring, diseases, propagation, hygiene, use of biological pest control. The small-sized bundles of herbs is a new product that must be handled with care. The local partner compares it with the early stages of fresh flower growing in Kenya, when it took a lot of effort to convince employees on the necessity of careful treatment of flowers. The joint venture will also provide training on a number of social issues such as women's sexual health, family planning and healthy nutrition. The partners consider these trainings as essential for maintaining a good relationship with the workers and the larger community. They also believe it will help to break the continued reliance on food aid. The joint venture will pay living wages.•	Innovation / Transfer of knowledgeSome of the herbs, such as mint, are currently available from Kenya, e.g. from the local partner. New is the combination of products and the way that they are packaged as a labelled product instead of being sold off as a commodity product. Fair Trade and food quality certification are also new for these products in Kenya. Most producers of fresh mint do not have access to the supermarket channels in Europe because of a lack of quality certifications.•	Chain effectsImpact on local suppliersBecause of the demanded high standards on MRLs and traceability of the partners do not see an opportunity in the short term to work with outgrowers. The applicant does not want their product to be produced by anyone other than exclusively contracted parties.Impact on local customers or consumersThe project has no impact on this group, as all of the production will be exported.•	EnvironmentAn Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) will be part of the project. The owners of the local partner are strongly conservation minded. The new irrigation dam will improve the availability of water and therefore the survival chances of wildlife in the region.•	Position of women90% of the new employees will be female.•	Impact on food safetyThe projected area is currently not in use for food production.•	Impact on waterThe projected irrigation dam serves to retain rain water that otherwise passes by the locality. An Environmental Impact Analysis will be part of the first project result. The project partners plan to make this water available to the local community by building a pipeline to a location outside the fence. | The goal of the project is to produce and market 90,000 kg annually of Fresh Herbal Tea and to produce year round 5,000 kg of micro vegetables.

title: Rift Seed Valley hybrid seed production 2.0 in Kenya
description: The applicant, C.G. Zuurbier and Co International B.V. was established in 2001 and is active in the handling and sales of cut flowers from Kenya. The local partner, Bilashaka Flowers Ltd was established in 2001 and is based in Naivasha. Bilashaka Flowers Ltd produces around 60 million stems of cut roses a year. The company has 600 employees of whom 50% is female. With the growing competition the market of cut roses has become increasingly difficult. This situation made the local partner look for ways to diversify. They carried out trials with new techniques and other flower crops in the past to explore new opportunities. A promising opportunity was offered by Syngenta in 2011. This buyer was actively looking for reliable and capable farms in East Africa for the production of hybrid determinate tomato seed. The modern production process and facilities, the experienced management, the available knowledge and sustainable farming experiences were the reasons why the partners were approached for a trial.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)The partners already have a broad set of CSR certificates which will also be applied to the new project. A Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) will regulate aspects like maternity leave, minimum wage and social security. The local partner is already compliant with Kenya Flower Council-silver (KFC-silver), Fair Flowers Fair Plants (FFP), GlobalGAP and Fairtrade. This forms a social code of practice and will be a starting point for the composition of the CSR. Another target will be to work with GSPP standards (Good Seed and Plant Practices).Other issues that will be addressed and included in the policy: tribalism in order to prevent tribal issues, annual refreshment training for all staff members on technical aspects and social aspects (family planning, HIV prevention, first aid etc), access to the existing library for all employees.Measures to prevent corruption, bureaucracy and red tape will also be taken. A CSR policy for the joint venture is planned to be published in the first project result.Partner Syngenta already has a CSR policy in place with high standards to which all producers have to comply, dealing with issues like working hours, child labour, freedom of association and discrimination. In the contract to be signed between the partners and Syngenta these issues will be included.Impact•	Employment and working conditionsAll the employees will receive permanent contracts, starting with 1 month probation time. The salaries paid will be at least 30% more than the minimum wage agreed in the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). The local partner is already paying this amount. Next to their wages, all employees will receive one free meal per day, free health insurance, access to a cooperative saving system (micro finance), access to primary and secondary schools and health clinic in the neighbourhood. Changing rooms with lockers, sanitary rooms and other facilities will be put in place for all new employees. Employees will put on the available protective clothing (PPE) in the sterilisation units, attached to the greenhouse. Labour issues can be reported to the workers representatives of the union, the supervisor and the HR manager. These issues will be discussed with relevant management and solutions will be found.•	Innovation / Transfer of knowledgeThe farm is the first out grower of hybrid tomato seeds in Kenya.The required production process is new for the country.Statement from the Embassy: Production of hybrid determinate tomato seeds is new to Kenya. These seeds are not produced locally, but normally imported from other countries outside Africa. The proposed project is to produce these seeds of high quality year-round using high-tech facilities and production processes that are not yet seen in Kenya. In East Africa, there are three hybrid vegetable seed production companies owned by seed breeders, who produce other seeds than determinate tomato seeds.•	Chain effectsImpact on local suppliersThe most important local suppliers are distributors of pumice substrate, fertiliser, chemical and biological crop protection supplies.Impact on local customers or consumersThe customer is Syngenta Seeds B.V. who buys the produced seeds. Syngenta processes the seeds and checks the quality in the Netherlands and resells them world-wide.Part of the seed will undoubtedly find its way back to Kenya as African countries form the fastest growing market for the bush tomato.•	Impact on the sectorKenya has a major potential to produce high quality hybrid vegetable seed. Besides Syngenta, also other seed breeding companies are looking for outgrowers in Kenya. This project can deliver valuable experiences how to take advantage of this opportunity. Seed breeding companies have the strategy to contract several seed producers on different locations for reasons of risk spreading. This means that replicating the business concept will be possible for other horticultural producers. By initiating a knowledge network within the project, the experiences from the project will be shared with the sector and Kenyan institutes. Important aspects will be sharing experiences on all aspects related to high-tech farming, phytosanitary control, and quality management. The partners will start working on the knowledge network from the start of the project.•	EnvironmentThe partners will minimise the environmental impact of their activities. As one of the very few farms, the local partner is already collecting all rainwater from the greenhouse roofs in big basins. This water harvesting results in minimising the interaction with the groundwater and all water is used efficiently. Water demand has decreased with significant quantities using hydroponics cultivation. The excess drainage water is collected filtered and re-used, so a 100% closed water cycle is achieved. The impact on the environment is therefore very limited. The company is updating environmental impact assessments through the annually required audit. A set of objectives, which are reviewed regularly are evaluated to ensure that environmental goals are continually met.•	Position of women65% of the employees will be female. While hiring, special attention will be given to women in management positions, the partners intend to have twelve women (7%) in medium to high positions.•	Impact on food safetyThe project has positive impact on the world wide issue of food security. The production of these hybrid tomato seeds means high productive vegetables can be grown in subtropical semi-arid areas in the world, for instance in East Africa, but also in areas like Latin America, Tunisia and Turkey. In Africa, not only professional growers, but also smallholders are gaining access to improved technology and hybrid seeds. Particularly the determinate tomato seeds are suitable for these types of farming.The largest market increase will take place in Africa and the Middle East, for these regions the demand for bush tomato seeds in Africa and the Middle East is expected to grow substantially in 2018.•	Impact on waterThe project shows an example on how water consumption can be reduced in an economic way within the Naivasha basin.

title: Baseline study Lake Turkana, Kenya
description: This study will give local governments of Marsabit and Turkana the tools and insight needed to manage the lake sustainably and create a pathway for sustainable development of the fisheries sector an contributing to employment and improved food security. Updated knowledge regarding the lake's Maximum Sustainable Yield and stock level status will allow local governments to determine how much fish can be caught annually sustainably. Understanding the water level's effect will enable local authorities to use this information for years. It will also assist development partners in developing sustainable intervention in support of the County Governments.

title: Affordable Recirculation Aquaculture Systems (A-RAS) to small-scale fish farmers in Nyeri, Kenya
description: This feasibility study tests and enhances the practicality of two new technological designs of affordable Recirculation Aquaculture Systems (A-RAS constructions) among small scale farmers in Kenya. Clean sufficient water is a scarce asset in Sub-Saharan Africa in general, including in Kenya. With Recirculation Aquaculture Systems (RAS), water use is expected to be reduced with 80-90%, while even with this reduced water use, fish production can go up (up to) 40x compared to the current practice. The effectiveness of the components that are locally available, locally designed and with manufacturing capabilities, smart and innovative combinations of affordable sensors and algorithm technology, and use of solar energy (SDG13) will be assessed.The reduction of fish farmer water use and the increase in fish production will be analysed. The long term ambition is to prepare for making the A-RAS constructions (System 1 and System 2) accessible to thousands of fish farmers, so that a large-scale use after project time can deal with a series of challenges including urgent problems of water recirculation (SDG6) and undernourishment of millions of people (SDG2) caused by limited clean water accessibility across African countries.

title: Smart Cities Kenya
description: The consortium Smart City Kenya will test the Upande Non-Revenue Water (NRW) system. This innovative combination of hardware and software aims to reduce water losses of utility systems through real-time, automatic water flow/pressure measurement. At the same time, consumers will be able to view their water consumption data via their smartphones. The consortium consists of Upande BV, TagMeter Systems BV, Kisumu Water and Sanitation Company Lt., KIWASCO and Runda Water.

title: Twiga Foods Ltd.
description: Established in 2014, Twiga Foods (Twiga or the Company) is a distributor of fresh fruits & vegetables and fast-moving consumer goods in Kenya. Through its unified digital platform and robust logistics network, the company efficiently connects farmers and retail vendors to increase the availability, affordability and accessibility of food. The company is an existing IFC Disruptive Technologies and Venture Capital group portfolio client (#41195). IFC is also currently offering advisory services to Twiga on food safety, agronomy, soil & water, and agri-finance through the Africa Food Safety Program (AS project #601759).   IFC is proposing to invest, through unfunded Risk Sharing Facilities (RSFs) with tier 1 commercial banks in Kenya, up to KES1.6 billion (US$15 million equivalent) for an aggregate portfolio of loans up to KES3.2 billion (US$30 million equivalent) to support the development of up to 300 irrigated medium-scale (>15ha) contract farmers (the Program). Complementing seasonal supply from Twigas existing ~19,500 smallholder supply base, the irrigated medium farms are expected to add stable year-round volume which would contribute to better food availability, affordability and quality in the markets Twiga serve. The RSFs will be scaled up in phases and the first phase will be implemented with KCB Bank Kenya Limited (KCB Kenya).  The Program will also be potentially supported with blended finance through the Global SME Finance  Facility (GSMEF) and the Women Entrepreneurs Finance Initiative (We-Fi) to de-risk the project and incentivize the Company to achieve significant growth in lending to medium scale farmers which are Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) including women SMEs (WSMEs).

title: Grit REIG Project
description:
The proposed investment is a US$25.0 million A Loan (the IFC Loan) to a Kenyan subsidiary of Grit Real Estate Income Group Limited (the Group, the Guarantor, GREIG), a Mauritius-based listed (London Stock Exchange (LSE), Premium Segment, and Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM)) real estate investment company with REIT type characteristics building a diversified portfolio of income generating properties across Africa. GREIG will use the IFC Loan to finance a sale-lease back transaction, which comprises:   i) the acquisition of an industrial facility (the Existing Facility) with vacant land in Nairobi, Kenya from its current owner with the immediate lease back of the existing premises to Orbit Products Africa Limited (OPAL); and ii) the refurbishment of the Existing Facility as well as construction of new premises on the vacant land (the Additional Facility), which will be similarly occupied by OPAL on a long term lease upon successful completion (the Project). OPAL is an established regional manufacturer of popular personal care and home care products for multi-national clients in East Africa. | The most significant expected project-level outcomes are i) environmental effects, through reduction in energy and water uses; and ii) economywide effects through value addition and job creation. 
Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will facilitate the integration of the Kenyan real-estate market into regional and global financial markets through demonstration effects for REIT and REIT-type vehicles.

title: Star Bright Holdings Limited
description: The proposed investment is a senior loan of up to 11 million to Star Bright Holdings Limited (Star Bright or the Group) for its capital expenditure at its Kenya and Ethiopia farms and across group operations including but not limited to environmental and sustainability initiatives such as setting up water recycling at the packhouses and installation of energy efficient lighting (together the Project).  Star Bright, domiciled in Mauritius, specializes in summer flowers production in East and Southern Africa under the Marginpar brand. The Group operates 10 flower farms in Kenya and Ethiopia, with a production output of ~220 million stems a year that are exported to the Europe and Asian markets. In addition, the Group sources flowers from three partner farms in Tanzania and four partner farms in Zimbabwe. | The primary anticipated outcome is the broad economic impact, including increased domestic value addition, job creation, and foreign exchange generation. In addition, IFC expects its financing to enhance market competitiveness through demonstration effects and opportunities for replication.

description: Summary Of Project Information (SPI)       Project Name    Kenya - Magana Flowers      RegionSub-Saharan Africa   Sector   Project No010149   Projected Board DateApril 15, 2000   Company NameMagana Flowers (K) Limited    Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholders    	The project is sponsored by Magana Holdings Ltd. (MHL) which owns 70% of the shareholding. MHL is a family-owned holding company incorporated in Kenya in 1973. It is involved in coffee farming, real estate development and investment. It is headed by Dr. Magana Njoroge Mungai who is a well-established businessman in Kenya. The other shareholders are Kenya Equity Capital Ltd. (KECL) which currently holds 30% of the equity. KECL is an investment fund that was established by Equator Bank and the European Investment Bank (EIB) to promote economic development in Kenya.    Project Cost Including proposed IFC investment    	The total project cost is estimated at US$3.0 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of US$1.2 million    Location of project and Description of site    	Magana Flowers farm is situated on the outskirts of Nairobi, around 18 km from the city centre off the main Nairobi-Nakuru highway, and 30 km from the main International Airport. The company is carrying on rose growing operations on an area of about 7 ha on a gently sloping hill that is well drained and terraced.     Description of Company and Purpose of Project    	Magana Flowers is engaged in rose cultivation for export to the European market. The operation was established in 1994 on a 2 ha farm. It has since undergone two phases of expansion to its current size of 7 ha exporting about 14 million stems from 6 million in 1995. The company proposes to undertake an expansion of an additional 4.5 ha comprising of 4 ha of roses and 0.5 ha of lilies, which have had successful trials and a positive market response.     IFC provides a foreign currency loan, which is not readily available in Kenya. IFC will also play an important role in ensuring the company complies with the World Bank environmental protection guidelines through its regular supervision. The project creates employment for about 80 workers, the bulk of which will be women and will earn the country about US$2.6 million of foreign exchange. This is in line with the World Banks strategy of alleviating poverty and establishing sustainable local resource-based industries. The project will introduce high agronomical standards on the farm, which will ensure high quality export products and thus help Kenya to sustain its position as a quality horticultural producer. Description of Company and Purpose of Project:  Ceres Estates Ltd. (Ceres) is a limited liability company involved in the growing and processing of coffee and tea mainly for the export market.  It consists of a 250 acre tea plantation, a 350 acre coffee plantation, a coffee factory, and a tea factory. The estates were purchased by the current owners from a cooperative group in 1993.  At that time, the plantations were in very poor condition and a 3-year rehabilitation program was started.  While a considerable amount of work has been done to improve plantation yields and quality, additional work is required to make the estates commercially viable. The project is expected to enhance the countrys foreign exchange earning potential, employ an additional 173 people, and provide a sustainable market for small scale tea out-growers who depend on the project for their livelihood.  The project also illustrates the application of modern farming methods in rural coffee/tea estate management to local farmers.    In addition to the provision of scarce medium term financing and to the mobilization of local bank financing, IFC is also assisting the sponsors in defining the projects concept and financial structure and in preparing a satisfactory environmental protection plan. The project will be managed and operated by Portia Management Services Ltd. (PMSL), a UK management and consulting company specializing in port grain handling operations. It is also a drop off point for grains from international donor aid agencies to other countries like Somalia, Rwanda, and Burundi.  GBHL will build and operate the first modern bulk handling and storage facility in Mombasa for imported grains and fertilizers. description: Summary Of Project Information (SPI)       Project Name:    Kenya: Kipevu II      Region:Sub-Saharan Africa   Sector:Power   Project No:008917   Projected Board Date:August 5, 1999   Company Name:Tsavo Power Company Limited (TPC)   Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholders    	The project will be sponsored by 4 main shareholders: Wartsila NSD Power Development Inc. (Wartsila), the principal developer, with 23%; Cinergy Global Power Ltd. and Industrial Promotion Services(Kenya) Ltd., who through a joint-venture will be the lead shareholder with 47%; and the Commonwealth Development Corporation with 30%. IFC is expected to take up to a 10% equity interest reducing Wartsila''s share to 13%. IFC has extensive working experience with all of the sponsors.     Project Cost Including proposed IFC investment    	The total project cost is US$84 million. IFC''s proposed investment is a US$17 million "A" Loan, a US$26.7 million "B" Loan/DEG, a US$2 million "C" Loan and up to US$2 million in equity investment.    Location of project and Description of site    	The project will be located on the outskirts of Mombasa, which is Kenyas second largest city (after Nairobi). The site is adjacent to a similar state-owned project known as Kipevu I, and near Mombasa Port.     Description of Company and Purpose of Project    	Over the past few years Kenya has been experiencing epidemic brown-outs and load shedding, a situation which is stifling economic growth. The system operates with practically no reserve margin and, with 80% of its capacity coming from hydropower, is particularly vulnerable to hydrological variations. Unable to fund new generation capacity, the Government of Kenya invited the private sector into power generation in 1996, choosing also to diversify into thermal resources.    	Kipevu II, which will be Kenya''s third IPP, is a 74 MW diesel power station burning residual fuel oil No. 6 to be developed under a build-own-operate (BOO) scheme. The project was awarded to Wartsila following an international competitive bidding process. Although bid as a mid-peak plant to provide power locally and to act as a back up to the hydroelectric system, the prevailing electricity shortage in Kenya will require the plant to be base-loaded for at least the first few years of operation. The capacity and output of the plant will be sold to Kenya Power & Lighting Company Ltd. (KPLC), the national transmission and distribution utility, under a 20 year Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) signed with Tsavo Power Company Limited (TPC), a special purpose project company formed by the Sponsors. Affiliates of Wartsila will act as the Engineering/Procurement/Construction contractor and the Operations & Maintenance contractor for the project.     Environmental Category and Issues    	This is an environmental review category B project.  Issues include air emissions and ambient air quality impacts, noise, water supply and liquid effluents, fuel transmission and spill control, liquid and solid waste disposal, fire protection and emergency response, general workplace safety, and cumulative impacts from the project and the adjacent Kipevu I project. The plant will be equipped with a 45 m height stack, an acoustically insulated power house, and fuel oil storage tanks with complete containment to prevent spills.  A comprehensive Environmental Action Plan was prepared. KPLC is independently building a transmission line that is not directly linked to this project. IFC is assisting KPLC to ensure that resettlement associated with this transmission line will be carried out in accordance with IFCs requirements.    The  is  from the InfoShop. It is being built along the Murera river next to a river-forest and a prominent rock formation.  The site is generally flat with a gentle slope to the river.     Description of Company and Purpose of Project    	The project company, Meru Park Adventure Ltd, was incorporated in 1997 for the purpose of implementing the project. description: Summary Of Project Information (SPI)       Project Name    Kenya - Mabati Rolling Mills Limited,      RegionSub-Saharan Africa    Sector   Project No009619   Projected Board DateSeptember 27, 1999   Company NameMabati Rolling Mills Ltd.   Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholders    	The Continuous Galvanising Line plant and equipment will be supplied by Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd of Japan, which will provide supervising services for erection and also provide technical assistance for operations. Technology transfer and technical assistance for Aluminium-Zinc Coating (Al-Zn) will be provided by BIEC International, a corporation incorporated in the United States of America. Project Cost Including proposed IFC investment    Estimated Project Cost:	US$30.4 million. Proposed IFC Investment: a Senior Loan (A loan) of US$7.0 million and a Subordinated Loan (C loan) of US$4 5 million.    Location of project and Description of site    	The project will be located adjacent to the company''s Cold Rolling Mill (CRM) at Mariakani near Mombasa, Kenya. Mariakani is a small rural town situated about 40 km from Mombasa along the Mombasa-Nairobi road. It is within close proximity of the main Kenya railroad that runs to Uganda and is also close to the main Port of Mombasa.    Description of Company and Purpose of Project    	Mabati Rolling Mills, the Company, currently has two operations i.e., a Cold Rolling Mill (CRM), which obtained ISO 9002 certification in 1998, and a small chemicals plant. The CRM produces a wide range of cold rolled steel to suit variety of individual applications. The chemical plant produces caustic soda, hydrochloric acid and sodium hypochlorite for Group companies and also for sale in the external market. The Company is one of the flagship companies of the Comcraft Group in Kenya. The Comcraft Group is a multinational group with wide interests in East Africa and in other African countries, as well as well-established operations in Asia and Europe. One of the Group''s companies in Kenya, Galsheet Kenya Ltd (Galsheet) operates two galvanizing lines (one each at Mombasa and Nairobi) and a color coating line.     	The purpose of the project is to replace the two existing galvanizing lines of Galsheet with a single state-of-the-art unit at Mariakani near Mombasa. The technology chosen is a non-oxidizing furnace-type hot dip galvanizing and Al-Zn coating with an on-line annealing. The new plant will have the capacity to manufacture 80,000 tons per annum of highest quality galvanized and Al-Zn coated coils for the local market as well as for exports in the region. Hot rolled steel coils (mostly imported from Japan, Europe and South Africa) are processed by the Company''s in-house Cold Rolling Mill into cold rolled coils, which in turn will be used for the manufacturing of galvanized and Al-Zn coated coils. These coils will be partly used for producing color coated coils. The galvanized/Al-Zn/color coated coils will, after undergoing further processing into plain, corrugated and other profiles, be used mainly for industrial and residential roofing.    The project will: introduce new technology (Al-Zn coating) and products to the East African and neighboring market; provide benefits to consumers (e.g. for housing in lower income rural areas) of higher quality and longer lasting goods at comparable prices; provide further development of Mariakani and the adjoining areas as the industrial activity gets a boost with the new plant converting the existing operations into a mini-industrial complex; create indirect employment in the Mariakani and adjoining areas, as a result of the increased industrial activity; generate increased foreign exchange earnings by export diversification as sales to regional markets are realized; and provide an opportunity for local participation in the investment as the Company ultimately is listed. This audit included identifications of necessary Corrective Action together with a timetable for implementation. Key corrective action measures and mitigation include improvement of safety and housekeeping measures, air emissions monitoring, emergency and safety planning, and waste management. Mabati are targeting ISO 14001 certification and their operations are currently ISO 9000 certified.    The  is from the InfoShop. title: Magadi Expansion Project
description: MSC is a Kenyan soda ash producer with 300,000 tpa of nominal capacity, and 2001 sales of $31 million.  Magadi is one of Kenya''s oldest companies, operating for about 85 years utilizing Lake Magadi''s trona to produce sodium carbonate (soda ash).  The venture, an expansion of an existing IFC-financed project, consists of the construction of a new plant and associated off-plot projects that would produce up to 365,000 tons annually of higher purity soda ash for export, primarily to the glass packaging sector in Magadi''s existing markets.  The new plant will be constructed over a  27-month period.  The existing plant would continue to operate at full capacity throughout project implementation, and, thereafter, produce about 75,000 tons annually of lower quality soda ash for about 5 to 10 years after the new plant initiates commercial operations.  To stay in business in the medium-to-longer term, Magadi needs to implement this project.  Its existing lower-grade soda ash product will face shrinking  markets as demand shifts to higher purity soda ash.  Without this project, Kenya will lose one of its most important exports and leave unutilized a valuable renewable natural resource - the trona reserves in Lake Magadi.   Moreover, the closure of the company''s operation in a remote part of Kenya would leave the surrounding community without basic life-sustaining services and development.    The project has a strong development impact.  First of all, Magadi provides direct permanent employment to about 400 people and temporary employment to another 100.  At its peak, the construction of the project would require about 350 additional employees.  Secondly, the company is an integral part of the local Maasai community, helping it to cope with depressed economic conditions and develop socially and economically.  Magadi provides health, water, education, and transportation services to the township and promotes entrepreneurship among the community members.  The company maintains a hospital, three primary schools and one secondary school, housing for employees, teachers and medical personnel and an 86 km road to Magadi.  It has contracted out cleaning services to the local community. It has reserved 40% of the stalls in the public market for locals. It is exploring business opportunities in tourism and ways of diversifying  income sources, away from livestock raising into bee-keeping and maize mills - especially for local women.  Thirdly, Magadi is an important foreign exchange earner for Kenya.   Finally, the project will upgrade the environmental standards of the existing operation, particularly with respect to the reduction of dust levels at the Mombasa terminal.    The proposed investment follows from an IFC review of the technical, commercial and financial aspects of a project undertaken in 2000 at the request of the company.  On the technical side, IFC has played an important role in reviewing the development of the production process for improved purity ash, its capital costs, project management structure and arrangements, operating costs, marketing arrangements, and environmental and supply chain aspects.   Moreover, IFC has helped ensure that the proposed improvement of environmental standards of the existing operation, particularly with respect to the reduction of dust levels at the Mombasa terminal, was incorporated in the Environmental Action Plan for the project.  Finally, IFC has played a significant role in developing a bankable financial plan and in helping Magadi, a middle-tier company, raise both term loans and quasi-equity from international financial institutions.

title: KenyaUganda Rail
description: On October 14, 2005, the Government of Kenya (GOK) and the Government of Uganda (GOU) jointly tendered, via an international, competitive bid process, two substantially identical 25 year concessions for the rehabilitation, operation and maintenance of the railways currently run by Kenya Railways Corporation (KRC) and the Uganda Railways Corporation (URC).      The tenders were awarded to two special purpose concession companies (each a Concessionaire) to be set up by the Rift Valley Railways Consortium (RVRC), which would be a holding company with 100% ownership of the two concessionaires.  The tender process was coordinated on behalf of the Governments of Kenya and Uganda by their respective financial advisers, the Corporate Advisory Services (CAS) of IFC (for GOK) and CANARAIL (for GOU).  The transaction is the first concession-based privatization in Kenya.  The objective of the Concessions is to improve the management, operation and financial performance of the two railway networks in a coordinated manner by granting exclusive rights to the Concessionaire for the provision of freight services in both Kenya and Uganda for the duration of the concession.  In Kenya, the Concessionaire will also be obliged to operate the passenger services as designated in the concession agreement for a minimum period of five years. There is no existing passenger service in Uganda.  Though legally separate, the two concessions will be operated seamlessly as one railway system.  This is particularly important for Uganda, which as a landlocked country, depends upon the Kenyan port of Mombasa for sea access. Currently, the system comprises a total track length of 2350 km (1920 km in Kenya and 431 km in Uganda), with 219 locomotives (175 in Kenya and 44 in Uganda) and approximately 7500 wagons and three water ferries (approx. 6000 wagons and one ferry in Kenya and 1433 wagons and two ferries in Uganda).  However, only 41% of KRCs wagons and 20% of KRCs locomotives are presently operational (the corresponding figures for URC are 89% and 73% respectively).    The project is an IFC corporate loan to RVRC to support its first five year investment program for the rehabilitation, operation and maintenance of the railways currently run by KRC and URC.  RVRC is led by Sheltam Rail Company (Pty) Limited, a South African rail and marine services firm.  The investment program will include rehabilitation of track to allow safe passage of trains at an average of 30 km/hour; upgrading and modernization of the locomotive fleet; wheel and brake replacement and other rehabilitation of the wagon fleet; rehabilitation of passenger coaches; purchase of new locomotives and wagons; renovations of buildings, workshops, depots and machinery; and installation of new information technology (IT) systems.  In addition to IFC, RVR is also seeking a parallel loan from KfW, the German bilateral development finance institution. | Over the past two decades, the two railways have deteriorated operationally and financially, with current traffic volumes at about half of historical peaks, with negative cash flows and severe under-spending on maintenance and pension obligations.  It is expected that the concessioning of the railways to a private sector railway operator will have a significant development impact on the countries and the region in the form of:     -  more efficient and competitive operation of the rail network;    -  a transfer of heavy bulk traffic from road to rail thereby reducing road deterioration;    -  increased reliability of transport services through stronger inter-modal competition;    -  improvement in infrastructure through track and rolling stock improvements and regular maintenance;    -  reduction in the two countries fiscal burden with the transfer of financial and operation responsibility to the private sector, as well as via increased government revenues through annual concession fees, and    -  more broadly, enhanced regional transportation, trade and economic development via increased efficiencies and lower transportation costs.

title: WWF Voices for Diversity- safeguarding ecosystems for nature and people
description:
The World Wildlife Fund (WWF) program "Voices for Diversity - Safeguarding ecosystems for nature and people 2019-2022" is a three-year programme with a budget of SEK 75,000,000. The overall goal is to strengthen and anchor the integration of biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of natural resources with focus on a participatory approach, and to prevent illegal trafficking of endangered species in different but interconnected policy processes.Thematically it includes three - closely related - areas:• Participation and rights-based management of natural ecosystems (land and water),• Knowledge and policy development around nature-based solutions• Reduction of illegal trade in endangered speciesThe program will contribute to three main results in these areas:(1) That biodiversity conservation and participatory management for sustainable use of natural resources and poverty reduction are integrated into relevant global policy frameworks.(2) That global policy frameworks for biodiversity management and sustainable development are translated into effective implementation at regional and national level.(3) A strengthened interface between policy and implementation at national and local level, which enables more effective policy development and implementation.WWF will work with two main target groups: (1) authorities and governments in low-income countries; and (2) civil society organizations. Related target groups also include multilateral organizations at regional and global level, including UN agencies (e.g. UNFCCC, UNCBD) and regional organizations (e.g. EAC, SADC, AU, ASEAN).The program is global with implementation in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar, Myanmar and Vietnam. Criteria for land selection have been developed in dialogue with Sida and include, among other things, a focus on low-income countries, the possibility of overlap between the three thematic areas (participatory management, illegal trade in endangered species, and nature-based solutions), the possibility to cover both land-based and marine ecosystems, and opportunities for synergies with other ongoing Sida-supported WWF programs. In order to maximize synergies with other Sida-funded WWF programs, regional focus is on East Africa and Southeast Asia. WWF Sweden will forward 89% of the total budget, having a coordinating role, while WWF country offices will be the ones who primarily carry out the planned activities.The total budget is SEK 75,000,000 for a three-year period 2020-2022:- WWF's country offices will account for 51% of the budget. The support goes to six country offices, which means about SEK 2 million / country office / year. This includes, among other things, salary costs, travel expenses, meetings and workshops, as well as forwarding of funds.- Global coordination and support for policy work constitute 27% of the budget. This includes salary costs, support for the participation of local and indigenous representatives and experts from WWF in preparation as well as negotiation meetings, capacity building activities, relevant studies and workshops. Wage costs include 5 new services; 3 positions for global policy coordination, 1 position as policy coordinator for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Animals and Plants, and 1 position as coordinator for learning about the rights perspective and participatory management of natural resources.The program will start with a nine-month in-depth planning phase with the aim of enabling a more entrenched program document (including in-depth change theory, a performance framework, a follow-up system, and linked work plans). This period will also include impact work at global, regional and national levels to raise the voices of local and indigenous peoples, not least as a response to the new 10-year strategic framework that will be decided at the Biodiversity Convention's 15th party meeting in October 2020. | Världsnaturfondens (WWF) program "Voices for Diversity - Safeguarding ecosystems for nature and people 2019-2022" är en tre-årig insats med en budget på 75 000 000 SEK. Det övergripande målet är att stärka och förankra integreringen av bevarandet av biologisk mångfald och hållbart nyttjande av naturresurser, samt förhindra illegal handel av utrotningshotade arter i olika men sammankopplade policyprocesser. 
Tematiskt omfattas tre – nära relaterade – områden: 
•Deltagande och rättighetsbaserad förvaltning av naturekosystem (land och vatten), 
•Kunskaps- och policyutveckling kring naturbaserade lösningar 
•Minskande av illegal handel med utrotningshotade arter

Programmet skall bidra till tre huvudsakliga resultat inom dessa områden:
(1) Att bevarande av biologisk mångfald och deltagande förvaltning för hållbar användning av naturresurser och fattigdomsbekämpning är integrerade i relevanta globala policyramverk.
(2) Att globala policyramverk för förvaltning av biologisk mångfald och en hållbar utveckling översätts till effektivt genomförande på regional och nationell nivå.
(3) Ett förstärkt gränssnitt mellan policy och genomförande på nationell och lokal nivå, som möjliggör en effektivare policyutveckling och implementering. 

WWF kommer arbeta med två huvudsakliga målgrupper: (1) myndigheter och regeringar i låginkomstländer; samt (2) civilsamhällesorganisationer. Relaterade målgrupper innefattar även multilaterala organisationer på regional och global nivå, inklusive FN-organ (t.ex. UNFCCC, UNCBD) och regionala organisationer (t.ex. EAC, SADC, AU, ASEAN).

Programmet är globalt med implementering i Kenya, Tanzania, Mocambique, Madagaskar, Myanmar och Vietnam. Kriterier för landval har utvecklats i dialog med Sida och inkluderar bland annat fokus på låginkomstländer, möjlighet till överlappning mellan de tre tematiska områdena (deltagande förvaltning, illegal handel med utrotningshotade arter, samt naturbaserade lösningar), möjlighet att täcka in både landbaserade och marina ekosystem, samt möjligheter till synergier med såväl andra pågående Sida-stödda WWF-program. För att maximera synergieffekterna med andra Sida finansierade WWF program ligger regionalt fokus på östra Afrika och Sydostasien. WWF Sverige kommer vidareförmedla 89% av den totala budgeten, och har därmed en samordnande roll, medan WWF landkontor kommer att vara de som i första hand genomför de planerade aktiviteterna.

Den totala budgeten är 75 000 000 SEK för en treårsperiod 2020-2022:
- WWFs landkontor kommer stå för 51% av budgeten. Stödet går till sex landkontor vilket innebär ca 2 MSEK/landkontor/år. Detta inkluderar bland annat lönekostnader, resekostnader, möten och workshops, samt vidareförmedling i varierande grad.
- Global samordning och stöd till policyarbete utgör 27% av budgeten. Detta inkluderar lönekostnader, stöd till deltagande av lokal- och urfolksrepresentanter och experter från WWF i förberedande samt förhandlingsmöten, kapacitetsbyggande aktiviteter, relevanta studier och workshops. Lönekostnaderna inkluderar 5 nya tjänster; 3 tjänster för global policysamordning, 1 tjänst som policysamordnare för Konventionen om internationell handel med utrotningshotade djur och växter samt 1 tjänst som samordnare för lärande om rättighetsperspektivet och deltagande förvaltning av naturresurser.
- Externa parter: 11% av budgeten vidareförmedlas till organisationer som arbetar med ursprungs- och lokalbefolkningar. Under inledningsfasen kommer WWF utreda vilka organisationer som är aktuella för att ingå i programmet. 
- WWF Sverige behåller 11% av den totala budgeten vilket inkluderar lönekostnader, resekostnader, programutvärderingskostnader, workshops för inledningsfas och slutworkshop, uppföljning, utvärdering, revision och OH kostnad.

Programmet kommer inledas med en nio-månaders fördjupad planeringsfas i syfte att möjliggöra ett mer förankrat programdokument (inklusive fördjupad förändringsteori, ett resultatramverk, ett uppföljningssystem, samt sammankopplade arbetsplaner). Denna period kommer även inkludera påverkansarbete på global, regional och nationell nivå, för att lyfta lokal- och urfolksröster, inte minst som inspel till det nya 10-åriga strategiska ramverk som kommer beslutas vid biomångfaldskonventionens 15e partsmöte i oktober 2020. 

Sida är WWF Sveriges enskilt största bidragsgivare. Sida har sex pågående stöd till WWF varav CIVSAM står för det största stödet (400 MSEK 2018-2022), Sida Partnership Forum (SPF) har ett informationsbidrag till WWF Sverige (22 MSEK), Regionalt Balkan har just beslutat om en andra fas stöd genom WWF Sverige till WWF Adria (33 MSEK). Vidare finns två stöd som går direkt till landkontoren via det bilaterala stödet i Bolivia (24 MSEK) och Mocambique (41 MSEK). | Den övergripande förändringen som Voices for Diversity (VfD) programmet siktar
på att åstadkomma är: "att skydda ekosystem för natur och människor genom att
deltagande förvaltning införs som erkänd metod i globala policyprocesser, för
bevarandet av biologisk mångfald och hållbart nyttjande av naturresurser".
Tre huvudmål på tre olika nivåer (global/regional, nationell/nationell, lokal) ska
bidra till att uppnå den övergripande förändringen. Dessa är:
Huvudmål 1: Bevarande av biologisk mångfald och deltagande förvaltning för
hållbar användning av naturresurser, med en tydlig koppling till
fattigdomsbekämpning, är integrerade i relevanta globala policyramverk. Detta
inkluderar arbete inom post 2020 CBD, SDG targets, NDCUNFCCC). Exempel
på aktiviter är:
 Organisationer som representerar urfolk och lokala samhällen får stöd för att
öka sitt påverkansarbete i policyprocesser som prioriteras av dem.
 Arbete i förhållande till CITES (Convention on International Trade in
Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) ökad dialog med regeringar för
att stärka deras engagemang och få tillstånd robusta beslut inför CoP 2022.
Huvudmål 2: Globala policyramverk för förvaltning av biologisk mångfald och en
hållbar utveckling översätts till effektivt genomförande på regional och nationell
nivå. Exempel på aktiviteter är:
 Policyfrågor utvecklas för nationell och regional nivå med utgångspunkt från
globala ramverk
 Alliansbyggande kring dessa frågor och engagemang i nationella/regionala
policydialoger, t.ex. främjande av nationell lagstifning som främjar hållbart
småskaligt fiske och deltagande förvaltning.
Huvudmål 3: Förstärkt gränssnitt mellan "policypraktik" på nationell och lokal
nivå, som möjliggör en effektivare policyutveckling och genomförande. Exempel
på aktiviter är:
 Stöd till global lansering och utrullning av "zero poaching toolkit" inklusive
åtgärder för att bekämpa brott relaterat till vilda djur och växter och stärka
styrning och respekt för mänskliga rättigheter.
Insatsen kommer att adressera hur naturresurser kan brukas på ett mer hållbart
sätt, och hur ursprungs och lokalbefolkning kan delta i besultsfattande
processer relaterat till förvaltning av ekosystem och biodiversitet i Kenya,
Madagaskar, Mocambique, Myanmar, Tanzania och Vietnam. Genom att sprida
kunskap om den biologiska mångfaldens ekonomiska och sociala värden liksom
tyngden av att hindra illegal handel av utrotningshotade arter och naturbaserade
lösningarnas roll i att återställa och bevara ekosystem samt att nyttja på ett
hållbart sätt ekosystemtjänster, är ambitionen att kunna återställa och förvalta
den biologiska mångfalden, och lyfta urfolk och lokala samhällen ur fattigdom.
Globala, regionala och nationella plattformar/nätverk kommer att användas för
att hantera gap i policyramverk, konventioner, internationella avtal, osv.,
kopplade till förvaltning av naturresurser och den biologiska mångfalden (mark,
vattendrag, fauna och flora). Dessa involverar nyckelaktörer från civilsamhället,
myndigheter, och privata sektorn. Förutom att stärka WWFs egna policyarbete,
strävar programmet efter att möjliggöra ett ökat mångfaldigt deltagande i viktiga
policyprocesser. Detta kommer att möjliggöra för WWF ett utvidgande av sitt
arbete med partners, som har ett tydligt fokus på att inkludera marginaliserade
grupper i policyprocesser gällande förvaltande av naturresurser.
För att uppnå de huvudmål som nämnts ovan spårar VfD framsteg inom 5
påverkansvägar vilka mäter både interna och externa förändringar som
programmet bidrar till. Dessa är:
1. Förstärkt egenmakt av rättshavare och organisationer i det civila
samhället: inriktat på kapacitetsuppbyggnad av organisationer i det civila
samhället, urfolk och lokala samhällsgrupper för att delta i nationella, regionala
och globala politiska och beslutsprocesser, begära sina rättigheter och ställa
beslutsfattare till svars.
Inramning/skapande av debatt i en fråga
 Urfolk och samhällsorganisationer, civilsamhället samt andra aktörer blir
medvetna om de frågor som står på spel, organiserar sig själva och enas om en
ambitionsnivå när det gäller jämställdhet och kvinnors rättigheter, urfolks och
lokala samhällsgruppers rättigheter och andra rättighetsfrågor i debatten.
 Villkoren för den offentliga debatten påverkas: nya perspektiv och alternativ
tillvägagångssätt införs i den politiska debatten.
2. Kapabla WWFkontor: inriktad på att stärka kapaciteten hos WWFkontor att
bedriva högkvalitativ påverkansarbete och förespråkande på nationell, regional
och global nivå och omvandla till en inkluderande och rättighetsbaserade
naturskydd i policy och praxis.
Policypåverkan och beslutsfattande processer informeras av lokala prioriteringar
 Identifierade policyprioriteringar (från påverkansväg 1) återspeglas i
påverkansarbete från WWF och andra organisationer representativa av urfolk,
lokala samhällsgrupper och civilsamhället.
 WWF, urfolk och andra organisationer i det civila samhället som deltar i
programmet bjuds in till att delta i politiska och beslutsfattande processer som är
relevanta och där sakfrågor kan drivas.
 Policyprioriteringar tas upp och inkluderas av beslutsfattare i relevant policy
processer.
3. Lyhörda och ansvarstagande beslutsfattare: hänvisar till förbättrad
medvetenhet hos beslutsfattare för att bekämpa IWT och främja ett
rättighetsbaserat tillvägagångssätt och NbS i utformningen och genomförandet
av naturskydds och biologisk mångfaldspolitiken.
Policypåverkan
 Påvisbara ändringar (initiala eller slutgiltiga) eller förebyggande av
policyändringar, inklusive antagande/revidering av ny reglering/lagar och
förordningar.
 Graden av införda ståndpunkter från WWF, civilsamhället och urfolks och
samhällsorganisationer som tas upp i nya politiska handlingar och uttalanden
från tjänstemän på nationell och internationell nivå.
4. Inkluderande och utökat utrymme i policy processer: syftar till att skapa
utrymme för dialog, interaktion, inflytande och deltagande i policy processer
mellan urfolks, lokala samhällen, organisationer från civilsamhället,
beslutsfattare och WWF på nationell, regional och global nivå.
Ändrad praxis
 Konkreta förändringar i WWF:s, urfolks och andra organisationer i det civila
samhällets praxis när det gäller policypåverkan för ett mer inkluderande och
rättighetsbaserat naturskydd.
 Förändringar i beslutsfattande institutioners praxis när det gäller
tillvägagångssätt och sätt att arbeta med rättighetsbaserat och inkluderande
naturskydd.
5. Bidrag till regionala och globala policy processer
 Ökat engagemang och bidrag från WWF och dess partners till regionala och
globala policy och beslutsprocesser.
Den genomförande strukturen för programmet är som följande:
WWF Sverige leder programmet som genomförs på nationell nivå av WWF:s
landkontor i 6 länder (Kenya, Tanzania, Madagaskar, Mozambique, Myanmar,
Vietnamn) och på global nivå från WWF nätverkets globala funktioner, såkallade
"Global Practices" (Global Policy and Advocacy Team, Governance Practice,
samt Wildlife Practice). Samarbetet med "Global Practices" fokuserar främst på
genomförandet av kapacitetsutveckling för WWF:s egna kontor samt till
policypåverkan på olika nivåer. Utanför det interna nätverket har VfD även
samarbeten för att stärka genomförande på regional nivå med Non Timber
Forest Exchange Programme (NTFPEP) i Sydostasien, Indigenous Information
Network (IIN) i Afrika, samt på global nivå med Tribal Link Foundation och
Women4Biodioversity

 Policyprioriteringar tas upp och inkluderas av beslutsfattare i relevant policy

 Påvisbara ändringar (initiala eller slutgiltiga) eller förebyggande av

 Graden av införda ståndpunkter från WWF, civilsamhället och urfolks och

från tjänstemän på nationell och internationell nivå.
4. Inkluderande och utökat utrymme i policy processer: syftar till att skapa
utrymme för dialog, interaktion, inflytande och deltagande i policy processer
mellan urfolks, lokala samhällen, organisationer från civilsamhället,
beslutsfattare och WWF på nationell, regional och global nivå.
Ändrad praxis
 Konkreta förändringar i WWF:s, urfolks och andra organisationer i det civila
samhällets praxis när det gäller policypåverkan för ett mer inkluderande och
rättighetsbaserat naturskydd.
 Förändringar i beslutsfattande institutioners praxis när det gäller
tillvägagångssätt och sätt att arbeta med rättighetsbaserat och inkluderande
naturskydd.
5. Bidrag till regionala och globala policy processer
 Ökat engagemang och bidrag från WWF och dess partners till regionala och
globala policy och beslutsprocesser.

WWF Sverige leder programmet som genomförs på nationell nivå av WWF:s
landkontor i 6 länder (Kenya, Tanzania, Madagaskar, Mozambique, Myanmar,
Vietnamn) och på global nivå från WWF nätverkets globala funktioner, såkallade
"Global Practices" (Global Policy and Advocacy Team, Governance Practice,

genomförandet av kapacitetsutveckling för WWF:s egna kontor samt till

Forest Exchange Programme (NTFPEP) i Sydostasien, Indigenous Information
Network (IIN) i Afrika, samt på global nivå med Tribal Link Foundation och

title: WWF Voices for Diversity- safeguarding ecosystems for nature and people - WWF Biodiversity and climate change adaptation ny strat 2025-2029
description:
The World Wildlife Fund (WWF) program "Voices for Diversity - Safeguarding ecosystems for nature and people 2019-2022" is a three-year programme with a budget of SEK 75,000,000. The overall goal is to strengthen and anchor the integration of biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of natural resources with focus on a participatory approach, and to prevent illegal trafficking of endangered species in different but interconnected policy processes.Thematically it includes three - closely related - areas:• Participation and rights-based management of natural ecosystems (land and water),• Knowledge and policy development around nature-based solutions• Reduction of illegal trade in endangered speciesThe program will contribute to three main results in these areas:(1) That biodiversity conservation and participatory management for sustainable use of natural resources and poverty reduction are integrated into relevant global policy frameworks.(2) That global policy frameworks for biodiversity management and sustainable development are translated into effective implementation at regional and national level.(3) A strengthened interface between policy and implementation at national and local level, which enables more effective policy development and implementation.WWF will work with two main target groups: (1) authorities and governments in low-income countries; and (2) civil society organizations. Related target groups also include multilateral organizations at regional and global level, including UN agencies (e.g. UNFCCC, UNCBD) and regional organizations (e.g. EAC, SADC, AU, ASEAN).The program is global with implementation in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar, Myanmar and Vietnam. Criteria for land selection have been developed in dialogue with Sida and include, among other things, a focus on low-income countries, the possibility of overlap between the three thematic areas (participatory management, illegal trade in endangered species, and nature-based solutions), the possibility to cover both land-based and marine ecosystems, and opportunities for synergies with other ongoing Sida-supported WWF programs. In order to maximize synergies with other Sida-funded WWF programs, regional focus is on East Africa and Southeast Asia. WWF Sweden will forward 89% of the total budget, having a coordinating role, while WWF country offices will be the ones who primarily carry out the planned activities.The total budget is SEK 75,000,000 for a three-year period 2020-2022:- WWF's country offices will account for 51% of the budget. The support goes to six country offices, which means about SEK 2 million / country office / year. This includes, among other things, salary costs, travel expenses, meetings and workshops, as well as forwarding of funds.- Global coordination and support for policy work constitute 27% of the budget. This includes salary costs, support for the participation of local and indigenous representatives and experts from WWF in preparation as well as negotiation meetings, capacity building activities, relevant studies and workshops. Wage costs include 5 new services; 3 positions for global policy coordination, 1 position as policy coordinator for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Animals and Plants, and 1 position as coordinator for learning about the rights perspective and participatory management of natural resources.The program will start with a nine-month in-depth planning phase with the aim of enabling a more entrenched program document (including in-depth change theory, a performance framework, a follow-up system, and linked work plans). This period will also include impact work at global, regional and national levels to raise the voices of local and indigenous peoples, not least as a response to the new 10-year strategic framework that will be decided at the Biodiversity Convention's 15th party meeting in October 2020. | Världsnaturfondens (WWF) program "Voices for Diversity - Safeguarding ecosystems for nature and people 2019-2022" är en tre-årig insats med en budget på 75 000 000 SEK. Det övergripande målet är att stärka och förankra integreringen av bevarandet av biologisk mångfald och hållbart nyttjande av naturresurser, samt förhindra illegal handel av utrotningshotade arter i olika men sammankopplade policyprocesser. 
Tematiskt omfattas tre – nära relaterade – områden: 
•Deltagande och rättighetsbaserad förvaltning av naturekosystem (land och vatten), 
•Kunskaps- och policyutveckling kring naturbaserade lösningar 
•Minskande av illegal handel med utrotningshotade arter

Programmet skall bidra till tre huvudsakliga resultat inom dessa områden:
(1) Att bevarande av biologisk mångfald och deltagande förvaltning för hållbar användning av naturresurser och fattigdomsbekämpning är integrerade i relevanta globala policyramverk.
(2) Att globala policyramverk för förvaltning av biologisk mångfald och en hållbar utveckling översätts till effektivt genomförande på regional och nationell nivå.
(3) Ett förstärkt gränssnitt mellan policy och genomförande på nationell och lokal nivå, som möjliggör en effektivare policyutveckling och implementering. 

WWF kommer arbeta med två huvudsakliga målgrupper: (1) myndigheter och regeringar i låginkomstländer; samt (2) civilsamhällesorganisationer. Relaterade målgrupper innefattar även multilaterala organisationer på regional och global nivå, inklusive FN-organ (t.ex. UNFCCC, UNCBD) och regionala organisationer (t.ex. EAC, SADC, AU, ASEAN).

Programmet är globalt med implementering i Kenya, Tanzania, Mocambique, Madagaskar, Myanmar och Vietnam. Kriterier för landval har utvecklats i dialog med Sida och inkluderar bland annat fokus på låginkomstländer, möjlighet till överlappning mellan de tre tematiska områdena (deltagande förvaltning, illegal handel med utrotningshotade arter, samt naturbaserade lösningar), möjlighet att täcka in både landbaserade och marina ekosystem, samt möjligheter till synergier med såväl andra pågående Sida-stödda WWF-program. För att maximera synergieffekterna med andra Sida finansierade WWF program ligger regionalt fokus på östra Afrika och Sydostasien. WWF Sverige kommer vidareförmedla 89% av den totala budgeten, och har därmed en samordnande roll, medan WWF landkontor kommer att vara de som i första hand genomför de planerade aktiviteterna.

Den totala budgeten är 75 000 000 SEK för en treårsperiod 2020-2022:
- WWFs landkontor kommer stå för 51% av budgeten. Stödet går till sex landkontor vilket innebär ca 2 MSEK/landkontor/år. Detta inkluderar bland annat lönekostnader, resekostnader, möten och workshops, samt vidareförmedling i varierande grad.
- Global samordning och stöd till policyarbete utgör 27% av budgeten. Detta inkluderar lönekostnader, stöd till deltagande av lokal- och urfolksrepresentanter och experter från WWF i förberedande samt förhandlingsmöten, kapacitetsbyggande aktiviteter, relevanta studier och workshops. Lönekostnaderna inkluderar 5 nya tjänster; 3 tjänster för global policysamordning, 1 tjänst som policysamordnare för Konventionen om internationell handel med utrotningshotade djur och växter samt 1 tjänst som samordnare för lärande om rättighetsperspektivet och deltagande förvaltning av naturresurser.
- Externa parter: 11% av budgeten vidareförmedlas till organisationer som arbetar med ursprungs- och lokalbefolkningar. Under inledningsfasen kommer WWF utreda vilka organisationer som är aktuella för att ingå i programmet. 
- WWF Sverige behåller 11% av den totala budgeten vilket inkluderar lönekostnader, resekostnader, programutvärderingskostnader, workshops för inledningsfas och slutworkshop, uppföljning, utvärdering, revision och OH kostnad.

Programmet kommer inledas med en nio-månaders fördjupad planeringsfas i syfte att möjliggöra ett mer förankrat programdokument (inklusive fördjupad förändringsteori, ett resultatramverk, ett uppföljningssystem, samt sammankopplade arbetsplaner). Denna period kommer även inkludera påverkansarbete på global, regional och nationell nivå, för att lyfta lokal- och urfolksröster, inte minst som inspel till det nya 10-åriga strategiska ramverk som kommer beslutas vid biomångfaldskonventionens 15e partsmöte i oktober 2020. 

Sida är WWF Sveriges enskilt största bidragsgivare. Sida har sex pågående stöd till WWF varav CIVSAM står för det största stödet (400 MSEK 2018-2022), Sida Partnership Forum (SPF) har ett informationsbidrag till WWF Sverige (22 MSEK), Regionalt Balkan har just beslutat om en andra fas stöd genom WWF Sverige till WWF Adria (33 MSEK). Vidare finns två stöd som går direkt till landkontoren via det bilaterala stödet i Bolivia (24 MSEK) och Mocambique (41 MSEK). | Den övergripande förändringen som Voices for Diversity (VfD) programmet siktar
