title: KEWASNET: improved governance in the Kenyan       water sector
description:
Kenya Water and Sanitation Network (KEWASNET) program Water Sector Governance Support programmet tar avstamp i den konstitutionella rätten till vatten och sanitet i Kenya och avser att stärka deltagande, styrning och ansvarstagande av myndigheter och regeringen på lokal och nationell nivå inom vattensektorn. Insatsen kombinerar en nedifrån och upp ansats med kapacitetsuppbyggnad på lokal nivå för att hålla länsregeringar och vattenbolagen ansvariga, med en nedifrån och upp ansats med fokus på advocacy, fortsatt sektorreform och kunskapsspridning på nationell nivå. I utvalda län kommer dessutom budgetanalyser göras för att kunna rapportera på ett genomlysande sätt vad pengarna inom sektorn används till. Civila samhället inom vattensektorn kommer stärkas. Insatsen kompletterar annat stöd inom vattensektorn till statliga myndigheter rörande tillhandahållande av service på lokal nivå genom WSTF (Water Services Trust Fund) genom sitt rättighets- och deltagande perspektiv på lokal nivå. KEWASNET som nätverk har verkat i flera år och är en erkänd NGO aktör inom vattensektorn, men som autonomt nätverk endast i lite mer än 1 år och institutionella svagheter har identifierats i en utvärdering och den externa finansieringen är begränsad. Programmet löper i 3 år och tyngdvikt under det första året ligger därför på att bygga upp sekretariatet för att KEWASNET ska kunna uppfylla sitt mandat, utöka sin närvaro nationellt och även kunna hantera och attrahera ytterligare medel. | The purpose of the project is to strenghten CSO participation in the  WASH sector in Kenya in order to secure better governance and         sustainable delivery of water and sanitation services to the poor and underserved. | Programme Goal
Communities in the country enjoying a better quality of life through expanded and effective access to WASH and WRM basic services. This stems from better governance brought about by a strong and sustainable network of WASH/WRM sector actors pushing for change.

Programme Objectives
1. To improve citizen participation in WASH service delivery and WRM sector decisions
2. To improve sector decision making and resource allocation
3. To improve sector knowledge in key WASH and WRM issues
4. To ensure a strong, responsive and effective WASH Sector
sector_names: Education and training in water supply and sanitation | Water Supply & Sanitation
participating_orgs: Sweden / SE-0 / 1 | Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency / SE-6 / 3
results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | The Water Governance Support Programme (WGSP I) supported the Kenyan civil society in the water sector through Kenya Water and Sanitation Civil Society Network (KEWASNET), a member based umbrella organization, aiming to promote the human right to water in Kenya. The implementation period between November 2014 to October 2019 with a budget of SEK 24 000 000. During the implementation key approaches applied included capacity development, networking and collaboration, human rights based approaches and performance based financing. Through these, major accomplishments were realized including:

- development and production of key tools, training guides and curriculum that were used in developing capacities of CSOs, government officials, Water Resources User Associations (WRUAs) and community members to effectively participate in WASH and WRM affairs.

- support to two water companies to develop their service charters hence improving their service delivery.

- various products such as Understanding the Water Act 2016  a guide for CSOs, the Citizen Version of the Water Act 2016, and a guide to public policy formulation among others were developed and used.

- support to the development of various plans, polices and legislation including the County Integrated Development Plans (CIDPs) and Water Policies for Kiambu, Kisumu and Uasin Gishu Counties.  At national level, the programme took an active role in the ongoing drafting and development of the National Water Policy, the Environmental Health and Sanitation Bill.

-  the launch of the 4th Annual CSO Performance Report and the development of the 5th Annual CSO Performance Report further crystallized the deep desire among the WASH CSOs for self-governance, disorganization and continued contribution to the WASH/WRM sector. The programme was further enriched by the conduct of study cycles and technical working groups where key issues informing policy discourse were realized.

In 2019, a review was undertaken of the programme by external consultants. Quote from the Executive Summary of the report "Forward looking Verification of Results from the KEWASNET Water Governance Support Programme 2014  2018", Finnish Consulting Group (FCG) October 2019: 
"The consultant concluded that the WGSP I empowered citizens to collectively engage on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Water Resource Management (WRM) governance issues. In addition, WGSP I contributed to building CSOs capacity to facilitate citizen engagement and the governments capacity to create an enabling environment for citizen engagement. KEWASNET strategically implemented citizen participation activities based on Human Rights Based Approach (HRBA) and has achieved verifiable results and realised some impacts. Improved citizen involvement and engagement saw KEWASNET being included at the national and county level water leadership networks and committees. Under WGSP I, KEWASNET facilitated the formation of county level WASH
networks that are hosted by the county governments. These networks include various county level stakeholders, CSOs and county governments. WGSP I contributed towards improved citizen participation in the WASH sector through training on citizen participation held in the counties. Policy influencing was a key component of WGSP I on both national and county levels. This was done by engaging KEWASNET member CSOs and key stakeholders in policy development processes. At the national level, KEWASNET facilitated public participation processes and funded some of the meetings towards finalisation of the Water Act 2016. KEWASNET supported the formulation of the National Water Policy 2012 by facilitating the public participation by CSOs (the Water Policy has not yet been finalised). KEWASNET also supported the development of Kenya Environmental Sanitation and Hygiene Policy in 2016 by facilitating and funding public participation meetings. Towards sector knowledge in key WASH and WRM issues, a number of learning forums and activities were facilitated by KEWASNET. During such forums, gaps in interpretation of the Water Act 2016 by the CSOs and citizens were identified. This led to the development of popular versions of the Water Act for CSOs and citizens in 2018. KEWASNET had made a number of publications in the WASH/IWRM sector including CSOs performance reports which is being used by MoWS to inform its annual report. KEWASNET as an umbrella body for CSOs in water governance has contributed to building a stronger, more responsive and effective WASH sector by creating democratic spaces for rights holders to hold duty bearers accountable. An enabling environment was also created where key issues in the WASH/WRM sector were identified. In addition, KEWASNET has influenced collaboration between WASH/WRM stakeholders including CSOs and government institutions at national and county level." | Not applicable | No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published

The primary objective of the project is to enhance access to clean water for the target beneficiaries, leading to improved quality of life and socio-economic development in the area. | The overall objective (s) of the Project is to address the water scarcity issues faced by the local community households and two schools in Kisima ward by implementing rainwater harvesting systems. The primary objective of the project is to enhance access to clean water for the target beneficiaries, leading to improved quality of life and socio-economic development in the area.

results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | The MyTank Project, implemented in Kisima Ward, Meru County, Kenya, has achieved significant results in its first year (March 2024May 2025), addressing water scarcity, food security, and community resilience.

The MyTank Project has successfully met its year 1 targets by installing 150 water tanks, distributing 1,200 avocado seedlings, and training beneficiaries, directly improving water access and reduced average walking time to water sources from 30 minutes to 5 minutes, alleviating the burden of water fetching, particularly for women. Households now have reliable access to clean water for domestic use, farming, and livestock. By the second quarter of Year 2, the foundation had achieved 63% (95/150) of the yearly full installation target. Active installations are concentrated in Kisima and Subuiga, while Kamiti carried over from Year 1. Key activities included a feedback workshop with Year 1 beneficiaries and comprehensive avocado training for Year 2 beneficiaries. Primary challenges remain the delay in beneficiary payments and slower-than-expected fund disbursement, which have pushed completion timeline to February 2026. Health, and agricultural potential for vulnerable households - While avocado trees are not yet mature, the project anticipates an annual fruit yield of 2050 kg per household starting in year 3, laying the foundation for future income generation and improved nutrition and households being better equipped to adapt to climate variability.

Unexpected challenges, such as community tensions and technical adjustments, provided valuable lessons for future phases, while high beneficiary engagement underscored the project's resilience. These results align with SDGs 1, 2, 5, 6, and 13, demonstrating a holistic approach to rural development. While not a positive outcome, this highlighted the need for broader community engagement and transparent communication. 

Future efforts will focus on upscaling to underserved areas, enhancing monitoring, and strengthening climate education to sustain and amplify impact locally. | Not applicable | No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published | Agreement amendment My Tank Empowering Communities with Rainwater Harvesting | Agreement amendment -My Tank Empowering Communities with Rainwater Harvesting to Enhance Water Access and Livelihoods in Meru County, Kenya | Decision on Contribution (16778) My Tank 24-03-19 | My Tank agreement signed w annexes A-D

title: Kenya urbant vatten GPOBA
description: Output-based Aid in Kenya water sector. Provision of water supply and sanitation to households in small urban centres. Administrated through GPOBA/WBG. | Resultatbaserade subventioner i vattensektorn i Kenya. Vattentillförsel till hushåll på landsbygd och i mindre samhällen. Administreras genom GPOBA/Världsbanken. | The project objective is to increase the number of people in low income areas with access to improved water supply and sanitation services in Kenyan towns and cities.  Also, the programme is testing applicability and developing Results-Based Approaches in financing, and trying out mobilisation of local commercial capital for investments in water and sanitation in Kenya.
sector_names: Basic drinking water supply and basic sanitation | Water Supply & Sanitation
participating_orgs: Sweden / SE-0 / 1 | Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency / SE-6 / 3
results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | Outcome 1: Increase in the number of people in urban areas with access to improved water sources under the project

The achievement of Outcome 1 has been rated as high. At project closing 84,408 people were provided with access to improved water sources in the form of new household water connections and new community water points. The achievement of the final target against the original target of 135,000 was 63 percent, against the revised target of 94,500 was 89 percent, and against the final target of 81,000
was 104 percent achieved. Rehabilitation and construction of upstream infrastructure under the project were needed to accommodate new connections, contributing to the improved and expanded services by the WSPs to low-income areas. However these were
not measured in the results framework of the project. Before the project, many WSPs were facing constrained production capacity that limited their ability to provide access to clean and safe water, especially in low-income areas that were hard hit in times of water shortages. Thus, the residents had to resort to alternative sources of supply that took as much as 1.5 hours per trip in some areas, were of poor quality (some areas reportedly had high fluoride levels), unreliable, and expensive as indicated in the baseline surveys. These sources were not necessarily improved under the MDG definition, and certainly did not conform to the SDG definition either. The
project supported the WSPs in overhauling their aging water pipeline network and augmenting their distribution system, which helped to provide new household water connections and community water points in low-income areas. Access to piped water supply is recognized as one of the improved sources of drinking water and hence led to the achievement of the development outcome of the project and the long-term outcomes implicit in the theory of change, especially through the use of commercial financing.

At project closing, the project provided 15,167 new piped household water connections and 40 improved community water points, including yard taps, reaching 74,550 and 9,858 beneficiaries with improved water supply respectively. As a result, beneficiaries were able to access cheaper and cleaner source of water, that cost on average US$0.85 per cubic meter compared to US$ 1.12 per cubic
meter from private vendors (not including the cost of transportation required to fetch the water). Reports for a few sub-projects indicated that the average cost of water from private vendors could be as high as $10 per cubic meter (Nol Turesh), and beneficiaries
were reported to be spending less per month on water from the WSPs. In addition to water connections, the project was instrumental in constructing and rehabilitating upstream infrastructure such as water storage tanks, sedimentation tanks, and transmission mains to improve and expand their service delivery to low-income areas. These new construction and rehabilitation works benefited WSPs by increasing revenue from the new connections and increased cost coverage, lower non-revenue water (NRW) due to reduced leaks in the rehabilitated distribution system, increased water production capacity which enabled them to make the new connection possible, etc.

Outcome 2: Increase in the number of people in urban areas with access to improved sanitation

The achievement of outcome 2 has been rated as high. The project exceeded its targets, providing 40,355 people with access to improved sanitation services against a target of 39,500. The project helped to increase the sewerage coverage of the WSPs by investing in household sewer connections as well as augment their treatment capacity to accommodate the new connections. Sewerage connection is an internationally standardized measure of improved sanitation services, which led to the achievement of the projects outcome of improved sanitation services and long-term outcome of reduced disease burden. The project invested in 5,108 new household sewer connections in Embu and 2,963 in Nyeri, exceeding the respective targets of 5,000 and 2,906 connections. Other
investments under the project included upstream infrastructure in the form of 32 km of trunk sewer lines, 950 manholes, and 6 sewer treatment ponds in Embu, which helped it to improve the sanitary conditions in the central business district, and some parts of the
residential and commercial areas. The new waste stabilization ponds provided an additional capacity to treat wastewater of 2,000 cubic meters per day, which was a significant upgrade over the previous 800 cubic meters per day. Similarly, in Nyeri 23 km of trunk sewer lines and a sewer pumping station in Nyeri were constructed, in addition to the household connections. These investments led to increased intake of wastewater of about 1,500 cubic meters to the sewerage treatment plant that has a designed capacity of
6,000 cubic meters but was treating only 3,000 cubic meters before the project. Thus, the project enabled the Nyeri Water and Sanitation Company to optimize the operational capacity of its wastewater treatment plant from 50 percent to 75 percent. Increased
revenue generation from the increased number of connections for the WSP was reported but also improved sanitation and hygiene conditions in the target areas due to reduced pollution of surface water as measured by self-reported responses by the beneficiary on
health outcomes. For example, based on baseline and end line surveys, Nyeri had a 15 percent diarrhea incidence after the project compared to 27 percent before the project. Similarly, Embu reported a 3 percent diarrheal incidence compared to 36 percent after
and before the project respectively.

Investing in improved water and sanitation infrastructure in previously unserved areas required financing, and the project helped to leverage public funds by introducing commercial finance. Obtaining commercial loans on market terms for investments in low-income areas was a key requirement for the WSPs to receive OBA grants that would buy down up to 60 percent of the sub-project cost. Subsidies were a primary reason why WSPs extended services to low income areas, because these subsidies kept the cost of
paying back the loan low enough for services to be affordable to residents of low-income areas. The subsidies also allowed the WSPs to offer household loans to consumers to recover the connection fees over a period of time, given that the high cost of connection to WSS services is often a deterrent for low-income consumers. The design of the project ensured that on the one hand, these output-based subsidies held WSPs accountable for installing reliable water and sewer connections and upstream infrastructure thereby
ensuring a revenue stream to the WSPs. On the other hand, they made the investments more attractive to commercial banks not only because they helped WSPs secure additional cash, but also held them accountable for completing the sub-projects. The project supported ten utilities in total. The support built the capacity of WSPs to access commercial finance for the provision of WSS services, including for two utilities not eventually financed. The end result exceeded the intermediate indicator target of eight. Capacity building for WSPs was crucial for improving their chances to obtain commercial loans, given their limited relationships with commercial banks. Specifically, these WSPs were provided with technical assistance to create technical plans and prepare financially viable and bankable proposals to commercial banks. It should be noted that two of the utilities  Bomet and Thika, that were supported under the project 
eventually dropped out on account of extraneous factors outside of the control of the project. The Thika Water and Sanitation Company, which had signed a loan agreement with Equity Bank, had its board of directors dissolved following a dispute with Kiambu
County over the merger of the eight WSPs in the county. The lender subsequently withdrew its loan agreement with the WSP. Bomet Water Company too was provided technical assistance funding to prepare a bankable proposal. At the time it applied for a loan from the bank, however, a grant from the County Government failed to materialize, and it dropped out from the project.

Other outcomes and impacts

Gender
Although the project was not gender tagged and gender-specific data was not gathered, it can be argued that the access to improved water supply and sanitation was a significant progress for women. Women are usually in charge of care giving responsibilities at home,
and hence tasked with the duty of taking care of sick household members due to waterborne diseases. While not verifiable through actual medical records, the customers reported a drop in incidence of disease such as diarrhea and typhoid in the Output
Verification Reports (OVR). Thus, reduced disease burden from improved WSS services is expected to improve the lives of women in the project areas. Anecdotal evidence from a few WSPs also suggests a reduction in the time spent fetching water by women, which freed up time for other activities.

Institutional Strengthening
The project brought governance benefits to WSPs by preparing them to meet the market test to access credit and through additional oversight brought by lenders during implementation. The project helped develop WSP creditworthiness through a toolkit and
hands-on support for the loan application process which helped strengthen financial management, project modeling, and business plan preparation. Together with separate technical assistance, the toolkit helped local lenders improve their knowledge of
operations and risks in the water sector, and develop appraisal guidelines and loan structures, among other things. In the long term, the skills developed in planning, management, and investment will enable strengthened capacity by the county
government and WSPs to deliver sustainable development programs for water and sanitation.

Mobilizing Private Sector Financing
The project served as a catalyst for increased private sector participation in delivering water supply and sanitation services to low-income urban areas through a blended finance model. The project provided hands-on experience to WSPs on reaching out to
and working with commercial banks, while helping the latter gain know-how in appraising water projects. By giving them exposure to the water sector, it increased the interest and appetite among banks to lend to the water sector. The commercial loans to a
few of these WSPs were also supported by partial credit guarantees from Unites States Agency for International Developments (USAID) Development Credit Authority for investments in Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) to help mitigate lender credit
risk. This resulted in participation of three banks by the end of the project - Sidian Bank, Co-Operative Bank, and Family Bank. Two other banks, the Kenya Commercial Bank and Ecobank, were involved in appraising WSP applications. Equity Bank that had
approved the loan for Thika Water Company withdrew its loan agreement. Thus, of the ten water utilities supported under the project, eight accessed commercial loans, mobilizing a total of US$ 14.67 million in local private capital.

Poverty Reduction and Shared Prosperity

This project was instrumental in improving the quality of life of low-income residents in urban areas by incentivizing WSPs to provide WSS services to these populations through output-based subsidies. Low-income areas were to be initially identified through WSTFs
poverty database (Majidata), which uses multi-dimensional criteria of poverty including settlement and housing patterns and status, socio-economic indicators, and water and sanitation access indicators. However, this methodology did not work efficiently as
planned, and the IVA had to work with WSPs to screen the households when establishing the baseline, using socio-economic criteria based on Majidata. title: Oxfam GB - Humanitarian Support 2018-2021
description:
In 2018-2021, Oxfam GB plans to reach over 280,000 people in Algeria, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Iraq and Chad. The contribution will consist of four components focusing on emergency life-saving activities; multi-year resilience building projects; the possibility to respond to sudden onset or deteriorating humanitarian emergencies during the year through the Rapid Response Mechanism; as well as support to method development of cash-based programming.In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Oxfam will provide support to an INGO forum with 100 NGO members with the aim of increasing the effectiveness of humanitarian interventions through improved coordination. In Iraq, Sida will support a project focusing on first line emergency response. The projects will target 9,600 people and include activities of food distribution as well as distribution of non-food items and hygiene materials.Five 3-year projects are proposed to be funded with a total of 28 MSEK for 2018, 19 MSEK for 2019 and 16 MSEK for 2019 with the following breakdown:In Algeria, 126 600 Sahrawi refugees will be supported in a project focusing on improving dietary diversity and strengthening of small-scale agriculture with the aim of increasing food security in the refugee camps. To reach the planned goals of the project, Oxfam will distribute fresh vegetables and flour, conduct trainings and awareness sessions on agricultural production and introduce drought-resistant crops.In the Central African Republic, Oxfam will target 17,500 people with food, protection and WASH activities, together with resilience building through recovery of productive assets and strengthening of communities’ conflict management capabilities. The proposed activities include distribution of agricultural kits, awareness-raising on food diversification, protection and gender themes as well as strengthening of community protection committees.The project in Chad will target 49,087 people in a project aiming to improve access to basic social services, protection, and the restoration of livelihoods. The project activities include borehole drilling, trainings of water management committees, latrine construction and hygiene promotion. The project will also highlight issues of protection and gender-based violence through awareness raising, establishment of protection committees, mapping of care services for victims of abuses and violations and awareness raising sessions on protection issues.In Iraq, Sida will support a project focusing on capacity building of local humanitarian leadership with the aim of strengthening the local humanitarian response capacity. The projects will target local humanitarian actors as well as a number of local NGOs. Moreover, it is further proposed that Sida contributes with 25 million within the Rapid Response Mechanism, RRM, to enable Oxfam GB to respond to sudden onset or deteriorating humanitarian emergencies throughout the year.Moreover, in addition to funding provided directly to Oxfam GB, Sida will also support the Cash Learning Partnership (CaLP) in a 3-year intervention with a total funding of 9 MSEK (4+3+2 MSEK). CaLP is a network based on learning, knowledge sharing, networking and coordination around the appropriate and timely use of cash transfer programming (CTP) in humanitarian response. CaLP does not deliver cash transfer programmes directly. The vision of CaLP is that humanitarian assistance creates the greatest value, choice and dignity for people in crisis. | Detta beslut avser stöd till Oxfam GB för humanitära projekt genom ett nytt avtal mellan Sida och Oxfam GB för perioden april 2018 – juni 2021.

Under 2018 kommer fler än 135 miljoner människor vara i behov av humanitärt bistånd världen över till en kostnad av 22,5 miljarder dollar enligt United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Sveriges humanitära bistånd är behovsbaserat och Sida genomför i enlighet med detta årligen en humanitär allokeringsprocess, vari samtliga humanitära kriser analyseras utifrån de humanitära behoven och där de mest relevanta av strategiska partnerorganisationer att svara upp mot identifierade behov utväljs.

Ett flertal av de identifierade globala behoven för 2018 återfinns i utdragna och bortglömda kriser och Sida bedömer att Oxfam GB är väl positionerad att svara upp mot dessa behov i kraft av att organisationen även arbetar med långsiktigt utvecklingssamarbete, har god kännedom om den lokala kontexten i samtliga föreslagna projekt samt genom att kapacitetsstärkande av lokala aktörer är centralt i Oxfam GB’s humanitära arbete. År 2018–2021 föreslås därför att Oxfam GB, utöver stöd för akut livräddande aktiviteter, även erhåller finansiering för mer långsiktiga aktiviteter i syfte att stärka samhällens motståndskraft mot kriser och katastrofer.

Oxfam GB har under tidigare samarbeten med Sida, senast genom stöd under avtalsperioden 2011–2013 samt 2014–2017, påvisat att organisationen är en effektiv humanitär aktör. Enbart under 2016 lyckades Oxfam GB nå 1,2 miljoner människor med stöd inom vatten, sanitet och hygien, 94 000 människor med tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning och förbättrade försörjningsmöjligheter samt bidra med stärkt skydd för 106 000 människor i konfliktdrabbade miljöer. Sida bedömer i linje med detta att Oxfam GB framförallt har ett mervärde vad gäller aktiviteter inom tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning, genom matdistribution och kontantbaserat stöd; försörjningsmöjligheter, bland annat genom stöd till återhämtning inom boskapsskötsel och jordbruk; vatten, sanitet och hygien, både genom akut livräddande aktiviteter och långsiktiga aktiviteter i syfte att stärka vattensystem; samt skydd, såväl genom integrering av skydd i exempelvis matdistribution som specifika skyddsaktiviteter i syfte att exempelvis öka medvetenheten om könsbaserat våld. Oxfam arbetar även aktivt med påverkansarbete kring internationell humanitär rätt och de humanitära principerna.

År 2018-2021 planerar Oxfam GB att nå över 280 000 personer i Algeriet, Centralafrikanska republiken, Demokratiska republiken Kongo, Irak och Tchad. Insatsen kommer bestå av fyra komponenter med fokus på akut livräddande aktiviteter; projekt i syfte att stärka samhällens motståndskraft mot kriser och katastrofer; möjlighet att snabbt svara upp mot hastigt uppkomna behov i nya kriser eller akuta försämringar av pågående kriser inom ramen för snabbinsatsmekanismen RRM; samt stärkt effektivitet i det humanitära systemet genom metodstöd som syftar till att öka kunskapen om kontantbaserat stöd.

Sida bedömer att Oxfam GB’s planerade projekt svarar mot aktuella humanitära behov i enlighet med Sidas geografiska analys och stöd till den föreslagna insatsen bedöms som relevant för att uppnå målen i Strategi för Sveriges humanitära bistånd genom Styrelsen för internationellt utvecklingssamarbete (Sida) 2017–2020. Sida föreslår därför att stödja Oxfam GB’s humanitära projekt till en kostnad av 104 MSEK i enlighet med följande:

Landprojekt

Två 1-åriga projekt föreslås finansieras med totalt 5 MSEK med följande fördelning:

Demokratiska republiken Kongo: 1 MSEK
I Demokratiska republiken Kongo planerar Oxfam GB att stödja ett INGO-forum med 100 icke-statliga medlemsorganisationer i syfte att öka effektiviteten av humanitärt bistånd genom stärkt samordning.

Irak: 4 MSEK
I Irak föreslås att Sida stödjer ett projekt som riktar sig till 9 600 personer med livräddande aktiviteter inom bland annat vatten, sanitet och hygien samt tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning genom exempelvis distribution av hygienartiklar, mat och andra basala förnödenheter.

Fem 3-åriga projekt föreslås finansieras med totalt 28 MSEK för 2018, 19 MSEK för 2019 samt 16 MSEK för 2020 med följande fördelning:

Algeriet: 15 MSEK (5+5+5 MSEK)
I Algeriet planerar Oxfam GB att stödja 126 600 västsahariska flyktingar i ett projekt som fokuserar på tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning och stärkt motståndskraft mot framtida kriser och katastrofer, genom bland annat distribution av färska grönsaker och introduktion av klimatanpassade grödor.

Centralafrikanska republiken: 18 MSEK (10+5+3 MSEK)
I Centralafrikanska republiken planerar Oxfam GB att nå 17 500 personer från de mest utsatta konfliktdrabbade grupperna i två projekt med aktiviteter inom tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning, skydd samt vatten, sanitet och hygien, genom exempelvis distribution av jordbruksredskap, utbildning i syfte att stärka kunskapen om diversifierad kosthållning samt skyddsaktiviteter, bland annat bestående av kapacitetsstärkning av skyddskommittéer.

Tchad: 18 MSEK (10+5+3 MSEK)
I Tchad planerar Oxfam GB att stödja 49 087 människor, inklusive internflyktingar och personer från värdsamhällen, med aktiviteter inom skydd samt vatten, sanitet och hygien. Projektverksamheten innefattar bland annat brunnsborrning, utbildning inom vatten, sanitet och hygien samt konstruktion av latriner. Projektet kommer även inkludera inrättande av skyddskommittéer samt aktiviteter som syftar till att öka medvetenheten om könsbaserat våld.

Irak: 12 MSEK (3+4+5 MSEK)
I Irak förslås stöd till ett kapacitetsstärkande projekt av lokala humanitära organisationer samt ett antal lokala civilsamhällsorganisationer i syfte att förbättra den lokala responskapaciteten och därmed stärka lokalsamhällets motståndskraft mot framtida kriser och katastrofer.

Rapid Response Mechanism

Vidare föreslås att Sida bidrar med 25 MSEK inom ramen för snabbinsatsmekanismen RRM för att möjliggöra för Oxfam GB att snabbt svara upp mot hastigt uppkomna behov i nya kriser eller akuta försämringar av pågående kriser.

Metodstöd

Ett metodprojekt till Cash Learning Partnership (CaLP) föreslås finansieras med totalt 4 MSEK för 2018, 3 MSEK för 2019 samt 2 MSEK för 2019:

CaLP är ett nätverk som arbetar med lärande, kunskapsdelning, nätverkande och koordination gällande kontantbaserat stöd. Mot bakgrund av att Sida i samband med World Humanitarian Summit och Grand Bargain åtagit sig att stärka arbetet med kontantbaserat stöd, rekommenderas i denna beredning att inkludera stöd till CaLP. Detta stöd ingår i beredningen av Oxfam GB eftersom CaLP inte är en egen juridisk person utan återfinns inom Humanitarian Department of Oxfam House.

Sida föreslår även att finansiera Oxfam GB’s programhanteringskostnader till en total kostnad av 2 MSEK för 2018. Programhanteringskostnaderna täcker en programkoordinator (100%), en finansiell funktion (75%), en programansvarig (100%), tekniskt rådgivande stöd (inom exempelvis tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning och skydd) samt fältuppföljning och externa revisionskostnader. Sida bedömer att programhanteringskostnaderna är nödvändiga för att säkra kvaliteten på hanteringen av Sida-medlen eftersom delar av de administrativa kostnaderna på 7% vidarebefordras till andra delar av Oxfams federation och därmed inte kommer Oxfam GB till del.

För detaljerad överblick och fördelning av Sidas stöd hänvisas till avtalets bilaga VII (Budget summary).

Även om Sida bedömer att Oxfam GB har god kapacitet att implementera humanitära projekt har Sida under tidigare samarbeten noterat vissa svagheter vad gäller intern styrning och kontroll, framförallt vad gäller revision, vidareförmedling samt finansiell rapportering. Sida kommer därför under 2018 att följa hur väl Oxfam GB åtgärdar brister inom dessa områden.

Med anledning av de uppmärksammade fallen där Oxfam GB’s personal varit inblandade i sexuellt utnyttjande och andra brott mot organisationens etiska principer, har Sida efterfrågat detaljerad information om de åtgärder Oxfam GB vidtagit sedan dessa händelser ägde rum år 2010, inklusive en detaljerad redogörelse för hur de vidtagna åtgärderna fungerat i praktiken. De erhållna svaren visar att Oxfam GB tagit frågan på stort allvar och att man sedan år 2010 har etablerat verkningsfulla regler och rutiner, som man under år 2018 dessutom planerar att skärpa ytterligare. Sida bedömer att de svar som erhållits är tillräckliga för att Sida ska kunna ingå ett nytt treårsavtal med Oxfam GB.

Vidare bedömer Sida att samtliga medel för projekten ska utbetalas omgående för att möjliggöra planering och uppstart av projekten till 1 april 2018. Detta för att på bästa sätt möjliggöra omedelbar uppstart av de humanitära aktiviteterna. Ett avsteg från Sidas vanliga rutiner om uppdelade betalningar bedöms motiverat.

Bedömningspromemorian har skrivits på engelska med anledning av att engelskspråkig personal i fält är delaktig i beredning och uppföljning av insatsen, i enlighet med Generaldirektörens beslut om Sidas språkvalsmatris med tillämpningsanvisningar från den 1 mars 2013. | Fewer women, men and children will die or suffer from a loss of dignity through insecurity and deprivation by reducing the impact of natural disasters and conflict and strengthening the resilience of communities and local partners.

results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | Over 1,393,031 affected women, men, girls and boys have been reached through 38
projects in 20 countries under the 2018-2021 HPA with activities in Water, Sanitation
and Hygiene (WASH), Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods (EFSVL),
Gender and Protection. Women and girls represented more than 50% of the
beneficiaries.

As mentioned in the previous section, during the HPA II, Oxfam implemented five
multiyear projects; six annual planned projects and method and capacity development
projects in CAR and the global Cash Learning project named CaLP. Oxfam also
implemented 27 RRM responses.

Through RRM responses, Oxfam reached more than 724,000 people with a total of
97,600,062 SEK. Sida funded Oxfam Rapid Emergency Responses in Bangladesh,
Syria, Senegal, Mauritania, Somaliland (x2), CAR (x2), Afghanistan (x2), Niger, Burkina,
Malawi, Mozambique, Sudan Sudan (x2), Kenya (x3), Chad (x3), Western Sahara, Iraq,
Colombia, Honduras, Guatemala.

Oxfam used nearly 80% of the RRM projects to respond to natural disasters such as:
floods, cyclones, locust infestations, droughts and the COVID-19 pandemic. Two RRM
projects responded to political crises: the Venezuela migrant crisis in Colombia and the
closure of refugee camps in Iraq. Five RRM responses were conflict related (Syria, CAR
(x2), Niger and Burkina Faso). More than half of the RRM projects (16), Oxfam
implemented together with local humanitarian partners in alignment with the Grand
Bargain and Charter for Change Commitments to localisation.

Examples of some of the concrete results achieved in the past agreement period include:
- In CAR 12 water points were rehabilitated providing access to water for 7,000 people
and also preventing spread of waterborne diseases.
- In the first year of the HPA agreement in Syria, through the supply of water pumps and
rehabilitation of wells and water points, 129,789 people displaced by conflict in Dar'a,
Syria, have got access to adequate and safe water.
- In Somaliland, 12,000 vulnerable drought affected persons received two rounds of
unconditional cash transfers providing them access to basic requirements such as food,
clothing and medication, as part of re-establishing their livelihoods base.
- In Niger, following attacks on several villages causing widespread displacement, Oxfam
revitalized community protection mechanisms in 12 IDP sites and improved the
protection of particularly women and children.
- In Algeria in 2020, 133,672 vulnerable Sahrawi refugees were supported with improved
food security during COVID-19-related restrictions on movement and impacts on
markets through the distribution of 2.5 kg of fresh produce over 3 months. A final year
evaluation of the project in Algeria showed that approximately 81% of the agricultural
production realised through the establishment of communal gardens was used for
commercial purposes and 19% for household consumption. The proceeds from resale
went towards buying other types of food, buying seeds and agricultural inputs or
improvements of overall living conditions of the household.
- In CAR Paoua, the multiyear project showed a significant reduction in the number of
recorded protection cases, including 73% of rapes were recorded before and 63% at the
end; 72% of physical violence before and 40.80% at the end, 36% of abductions before
and 10.20% at the end.
- For the project in Chad in 2020, 44,593 people were reached through information on
protection, the construction of 12 community protection spaces, distribution of 100 solar
lamps to women and girls and other protection services. Community structures and
committees and the creation of dialogue between them and the local authorities and
training sessions have contributed considerably to reducing protection risks, and
improving knowledge and the actions taken in this respect: 98.33% of male and female
protection committee members took positive actions against protection threats and risks
during the project. There was also a 23.69% reduction in protection cases and threats compared with last year and 93.22% of protection incidents referred to the authorities
were resolved.
- In both the multi-year projects in Chad and CAR, capacity building and advocacy
around protection made noticeable progress because of the extended duration of the
projects. Protection Committees are playing a more active role in victims referrals and
coordination with other protection actors is stronger.
- With regards to the CaLP project, 98% of respondents felt that CaLPs work has
improved CVA coordination a great deal, a lot or a moderate amount and 88% of
respondents reported that CaLP research, tools or guidance increased the quality of their
organizations programming. | Not applicable | No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published

CaLP är ett nätverk som arbetar med lärande, kunskapsdelning, nätverkande och koordination gällande kontantbaserat stöd. Mot bakgrund av att Sida i samband med World Humanitarian Summit och Grand Bargain åtagit sig att stärka arbetet med kontantbaserat stöd, rekommenderas i denna beredning att inkludera stöd till CaLP. Detta stöd ingår i beredningen av Oxfam GB eftersom CaLP inte är en egen juridisk person utan återfinns inom Humanitarian Department of Oxfam House.

Sida föreslår även att finansiera Oxfam GB’s programhanteringskostnader till en total kostnad av 2 MSEK för 2018. Programhanteringskostnaderna täcker en programkoordinator (100%), en finansiell funktion (75%), en programansvarig (100%), tekniskt rådgivande stöd (inom exempelvis tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning och skydd) samt fältuppföljning och externa revisionskostnader. Sida bedömer att programhanteringskostnaderna är nödvändiga för att säkra kvaliteten på hanteringen av Sida-medlen eftersom delar av de administrativa kostnaderna på 7% vidarebefordras till andra delar av Oxfams federation och därmed inte kommer Oxfam GB till del.

För detaljerad överblick och fördelning av Sidas stöd hänvisas till avtalets bilaga VII (Budget summary).

Även om Sida bedömer att Oxfam GB har god kapacitet att implementera humanitära projekt har Sida under tidigare samarbeten noterat vissa svagheter vad gäller intern styrning och kontroll, framförallt vad gäller revision, vidareförmedling samt finansiell rapportering. Sida kommer därför under 2018 att följa hur väl Oxfam GB åtgärdar brister inom dessa områden.

Med anledning av de uppmärksammade fallen där Oxfam GB’s personal varit inblandade i sexuellt utnyttjande och andra brott mot organisationens etiska principer, har Sida efterfrågat detaljerad information om de åtgärder Oxfam GB vidtagit sedan dessa händelser ägde rum år 2010, inklusive en detaljerad redogörelse för hur de vidtagna åtgärderna fungerat i praktiken. De erhållna svaren visar att Oxfam GB tagit frågan på stort allvar och att man sedan år 2010 har etablerat verkningsfulla regler och rutiner, som man under år 2018 dessutom planerar att skärpa ytterligare. Sida bedömer att de svar som erhållits är tillräckliga för att Sida ska kunna ingå ett nytt treårsavtal med Oxfam GB.

Vidare bedömer Sida att samtliga medel för projekten ska utbetalas omgående för att möjliggöra planering och uppstart av projekten till 1 april 2018. Detta för att på bästa sätt möjliggöra omedelbar uppstart av de humanitära aktiviteterna. Ett avsteg från Sidas vanliga rutiner om uppdelade betalningar bedöms motiverat.

Bedömningspromemorian har skrivits på engelska med anledning av att engelskspråkig personal i fält är delaktig i beredning och uppföljning av insatsen, i enlighet med Generaldirektörens beslut om Sidas språkvalsmatris med tillämpningsanvisningar från den 1 mars 2013. | In 2018-2021, Oxfam GB plans to reach over 280,000 people in Algeria, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Iraq and Chad. The contribution will consist of four components focusing on emergency life-saving activities; multi-year resilience building projects; the possibility to respond to sudden onset or deteriorating humanitarian emergencies during the year through the Rapid Response Mechanism; as well as support to method development of cash-based programming.In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Oxfam will provide support to an INGO forum with 100 NGO members with the aim of increasing the effectiveness of humanitarian interventions through improved coordination. In Iraq, Sida will support a project focusing on first line emergency response. The projects will target 9,600 people and include activities of food distribution as well as distribution of non-food items and hygiene materials.Five 3-year projects are proposed to be funded with a total of 28 MSEK for 2018, 19 MSEK for 2019 and 16 MSEK for 2019 with the following breakdown:In Algeria, 126 600 Sahrawi refugees will be supported in a project focusing on improving dietary diversity and strengthening of small-scale agriculture with the aim of increasing food security in the refugee camps. To reach the planned goals of the project, Oxfam will distribute fresh vegetables and flour, conduct trainings and awareness sessions on agricultural production and introduce drought-resistant crops.In the Central African Republic, Oxfam will target 17,500 people with food, protection and WASH activities, together with resilience building through recovery of productive assets and strengthening of communities’ conflict management capabilities. The proposed activities include distribution of agricultural kits, awareness-raising on food diversification, protection and gender themes as well as strengthening of community protection committees.The project in Chad will target 49,087 people in a project aiming to improve access to basic social services, protection, and the restoration of livelihoods. The project activities include borehole drilling, trainings of water management committees, latrine construction and hygiene promotion. The project will also highlight issues of protection and gender-based violence through awareness raising, establishment of protection committees, mapping of care services for victims of abuses and violations and awareness raising sessions on protection issues.In Iraq, Sida will support a project focusing on capacity building of local humanitarian leadership with the aim of strengthening the local humanitarian response capacity. The projects will target local humanitarian actors as well as a number of local NGOs. Moreover, it is further proposed that Sida contributes with 25 million within the Rapid Response Mechanism, RRM, to enable Oxfam GB to respond to sudden onset or deteriorating humanitarian emergencies throughout the year.Moreover, in addition to funding provided directly to Oxfam GB, Sida will also support the Cash Learning Partnership (CaLP) in a 3-year intervention with a total funding of 9 MSEK (4+3+2 MSEK). CaLP is a network based on learning, knowledge sharing, networking and coordination around the appropriate and timely use of cash transfer programming (CTP) in humanitarian response. CaLP does not deliver cash transfer programmes directly. The vision of CaLP is that humanitarian assistance creates the greatest value, choice and dignity for people in crisis. | Fewer women, men and children will die or suffer from a loss of dignity through insecurity and deprivation by reducing the impact of natural disasters and conflict and strengthening the resilience of communities and local partners.

title: CSUDP - Transition Phase
description:
Sweden has supported CSUDP since 2009 in two phases – the initial phase and the current ”Transition Phase”. The current phase is meant support the ongoing transition in urban management and develop CSUDP into an independent institution that carry on SCUDP work beyond Swedish support and provide a long-term platform for urban CSOs engagement and coordination. Maji na Ufanisi has proposed a 9-month project extension with a total budget of MSEK 17,7 to achieve the following objectives within the period: 1) strengthen local and national mechanisms or CSOs popular influence on national and county legislative and policy regimes, and 2) to improve the quality of life of disadvantages in Taita Taveta and Mombasa counties by increasing access to basic water and environmental sanitation services through participatory innovative solutions.  
The proposed extension is assessed to be relevant to the Kenyan urban sector and the country’s general developmental needs. It will support urban citizens’ participation in ongoing urban planning and legislative processes and thus help in the realization of constitutional principle on the right to participation. It will also empower urban communities through Local Urban Forums (LUFs) to effectively engage the county governments on their own development and governance and build capacity of selected county governments on urban development issues. In addition, CSUDP will, within this period, continue with strategies to upscale innovations developed with the programme’s support. Maji na Ufanisi, on its part will promote effective county domestication of national legislation and policy and support the work of the Kenya Water and Sanitation Network (KEWASNET) in the urban areas of two counties in the coast region. Moreover, Sweden will support the transformation process of CSUDP into an independent entity during the period. | Sverige har i två faser stött CSUDP sedan 2009 – den initiala fasen och den nuvarande "övergångsfasen". Den nuvarande fasen går ut på att stödja den pågående omvandlingen av den urbana samhällsstyrningen i Kenya samt utveckla CSUDP till en oberoende institution som kan fortsätta bedriva CSUDP:s arbete efter att det svenska stödet avslutats och då vara en långsiktig plattform för urbana civila samhällsorganisationer samt för koordination. Maji na Ufanisi har föreslagit en 9 månader lång förlängning av projektet med en ökning av bugdeten med MSEK 17,7 för att följande mål ska nås under perioden: 1) att stärka lokala och nationella mekanismer eller de civila samhällsorganisationernas möjlighet att påverka nationell och regional lagstiftning och politik, och 2) att förbättra livskvaliteten för utsatta i regionerna Taita Taveta och Mombasa genom att öka tillgången till grundläggande vatten- och sanitetstjänster genom ökad delaktighet och innovativa lösningar. Den föreslagna förlängningen bedöms vara relevant för den kenyanska urbana sektorn och för de allmänna utvecklingsbehov som finns i landet. Den kommer att stödja urbana medborgares delaktighet i urban planering och lagstiftningsprocesser, och därigenom bidra till att den grundlagsstadgade principen om rätten till delaktighet förverkligas. Urbana intressegrupper kommer också att få en starkare röst genom lokala urbana forum (LUF), vilka kan påverka regionstyrelserna att verka för utveckling och kapacitetsuppbyggande för att kunna hantera urbana frågor. Under denna period kommer CSUDP även att gå vidare med strategin att skala upp de innovationer som utvecklats med stöd av programmet. Maji na Ufanisi kommer för sin del att arbeta för att anpassa nationella lagar och policyer till regionala bestämmelser samt stödja det arbete som Kenya Water and Sanitation Network (KEWASNET) utför i de urbana områdena i de två kustregionerna. Under perioden kommer Sverige även att stödja processen med att omforma CSUDP till en oberoende institution.

results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The outcome objectives of the project are “Vibrant, dignified and secure urban living environments” through “strengthened and coordinated partnerships for inclusive governance and improved service delivery in programme areas”.  Overall, progress is positive and CSUDP is an Active and important actor in urban development, bringing in a civil society perspective. 
An infrastructure for enhanced citizen participation in urban governance and service delivery has been established through a network of 14 Local Urban Forums that are spearheading dialogue and citizen participation in selected municipalities.
Legislation and policy have been reviewed with the aim of making urban governance and service delivery more pro-poor. County subsidiary legislations in two counties have been enacted. Two national urban policies – the National Urban Development Policy and the National Slum Upgrading Policy were enacted. The dignity bill that gives effect to constitutional requirements for social, economic and cultural right was enacted with CSUDP support.   
For innovations developed through CSUDP support have been scaled and are being implemented by service providers. The innovations are improving the targeting of the urban poor by national and county as well as private sector and CSO service providers.
Urban CSO stakeholders are more coordinated and have strengthened capacity to influence reforms in the urban sector. A network of more than 1400 CSO organizations nationally has been established. | Not applicable | No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published

In the community of Makaror, Wajir town, DAWN plans to distribute food (unimix) to 300 vulnerable people such as lactating mothers, malnourished children and elderly people. 15 Farmers will be assisted with generators, which will support their irrigation systems and enable food production. | The current drought in the Horn of Africa also affects Wajir county. The Somali conflict has led to high food prices and pastoralists face problems with available water and pasture. Figures from the National Drought Management Authority report are alarming. Livestock is producing very little milk, affecting the purchasing power of the owners. The percentage of young children at risk of malnutrition is increasing (moving above 20%). The long rains (April-May) were expected to bring relief, but rain has been below average until now. FEWS NET (famine early warning systems net) expects more households to move into IPC phase 3 (crisis). 

Welzijn Wajir foundation has worked with Wajir for more than 20 years and supports in health and education through DAWN, the Development Agency Wajir Netherlands.

title: UNFPA MHTF 2019-2024
description:
UNFPA är FN:s befolkningsprogram för sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa. Organisationen bildades 1969 och verkar idag i över 150 länder.

Insatsen innefattar ett öronmärkt stöd till UNFPA:s Maternal and Newborn Health Thematic Fund (MHTF) fas III, om 305 MSEK för avtalsperioden 2019-2022. Sida har tidigare gett stöd till MHTF för fas I (2008–2013) respektive fas II (2014–2017). 

MHTF lanserades 2008 som ett flaggskepsprogram för att stärka nationella system för mödrahälsovård i syfte att minska mödra- och barnadödligheten i de länder som låg längst ifrån att uppnå MDG 5. MHTF:s affärsplan (business plan) 2019-2022 är helt i linje med UNFPA:s Strategiska Plan 2018-2021. Det unika med MHTF är att det är en global fond som bidrar med katalytiska medel till UNFPA:s olika landkontor. "Katalytisk" inom fonden innebär bl. a. att medel som kanaliseras genom MHTF skall bidra till att initiera/starta igång initiativ för att uppmärksamma gap/problem inom uppsatta/överenskomna mål relaterat barn- och mödrahälsa. Det kan också betyda att ta fram evidens som saknas för att länderna skall kunna gå vidare med implementering av initiativ i större omfattning (scale up). Tanken är att initiativen skall generera finansiering från regeringar, olika givare och finansieringsmekanismer (t. ex. GFF) på landnivå. Initiativ finansierade genom MHTF är således inga projekt och/eller program. 

Sida:s erfarenhet av fonden är att den har bidragit till att synliggöra vikten av mödra- och barnhälsa, stärkt utbildning för barnmorskor och deras roll samt förbättrad vård och behandling inom obstetrik och gynekologi. MHTF har också bidragit till att många av UNFPA:s landkontor har stärkt sin kapacitet inom mödra- och barnhälsa. Dessa framsteg bekräftas i den utvärdering som Sida gjorde 2017. 

Målet med MHTF fas III är att stödja länder med hög mödra- och barndödlighet, i säkerställandet av kvinnors, flickors och nyföddas rätt till överlevnad och god hälsa. Fonden innefattar fyra fokusområden för att bidra till att:
1) Stärka utbildning av barnmorskor liksom stärka deras roll/proffession; 
2) Tillhandahålla akut obstetrik och neonatal vård; 
3) Stärka och utveckla uppföljnings- och åtgärdssystem kring mödra- och spädbarnsdöd; 
4) Bidra till tillgång av obstretisk behandling av fistula och andra dödliga skador i samband med graviditet och förlossning. 

Fokusområdena är integrerade med varandra, bland annat genom att stöd till utbildning av barnmorskor och stärkande av nationella hälsosystem bidrar till ökad tillgång till rättighetsbaserade sexuella- och reproduktiva hälsotjänster. 

Som nämnts ovan är MHTF:s affärsplan helt i linje med UNFPA:s strategiska plan 2018-2021 men bidrar särskilt till målet; 1) att nå ut till fler kvinnor och ungdomar, framförallt de mest utsatta och sårbara, med integrerad SRH service, samt 2) att alla ungdomar är berättigade till SRHR. Jämlik tillgång till information och hälsoservice, kvalitet samt ansvarsutkrävande är tre principer som genomsyrar MHTF.

Fas III innebär att UNFPA anammar ett brett perspektiv på sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) som inkluderar tillgång till säker abort, abortvård och ett tydligt fokus på unga människors sexuella och reproduktiva hälsa och rättigheter. Detta anses av Sida vara av särskild vikt att stödja då det är avgörande för att minska den globala mödradödligheten. UNFPA:s starkare uttryck att arbeta mer med säkra aborter ser Sida som ett viktigt momentum. Sverige/Sida för en kontinuerlig dialog med UNFPA om integrering av mänskliga rättigheter inkl. säkra aborter och jämställdhet i UNFPA:s verksamhet och MHTF är en ingång för en fortsatt sådan dialog. 

Fonden riktar sig till länder med den högsta mödra- och barnadödligheten i världen.  För fas III har trettiotvå länder (Bangladesh, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Chad, Congo Brazzaville, Elfenbenskusten, DRC, Etiopien, Ghana, Guinea Conarky, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Kenya, Laos, Liberia, Madagaskar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mocambique, Nepal, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan, Timor-Leste, Togo, Uganda, Zambia) identifierats utifrån behov och prestationsförmåga. UNFPA:s respektive landkontor tillsammans med landet, kommer att utveckla en flerårig arbetsplan som innehåller de mål och indikatorer som är fastställda i resultatramverket för MHTF. Varje land har möjlighet att själva välja indikatorer som är mest relevanta för deras landkontext. Teamet som arbetar med MHTF vid UNFPA:s huvudkontor i New York (UNFPA-HK) kvalitetsgranskar planerna och ser till att länderna svarar upp emot hela SRHR/MHTF-agendan. 

MHTF är en fond som avser att vara katalytisk, bidra till innovation liksom skapa kunskap och intresse för investeringar inom mödra- och barnhälsa. Merparten (ca 70%) av budgeten är avsedd för landkontoren och deras partners. Varje landkontor får ett relativt begränsat bidrag från MHTF-budgeten med syfte att fonden skall generera finansiellt stöd på landnivå. Detta förväntas, enligt UNFPA, skapa ett större ägarskap för initiativet jämfört med fullfinansierade projekt/program. 

UNFPA:s regionala kontor skall ge tekniskt stöd till länderna. De har också en viktig roll i planering, uppföljning och rapportering av MHTF. Givarna kommer att ingå i MHTF:s rådgivande kommittee tillsammans med enhets- och avdelningschefer vid UNFPA-HK, de regionala kontoren, och hälsoministerierna. Newborn Health Thematic Fund (MHTF). MHTF is a thematic fund aiming at improving maternal and newborn health and wellbeing in countries with high burden of maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity by supporting the strengthening of the countries health systems. The goal of the MHTF in Phase III is to support countries to ensure the health, survival and rights of every woman, adolescent girl and newborn. The fund assists countries with high burdens of maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity in strengthening health systems to provide equitable and accountable access to quality sexual, reproductive, maternal and newborn health care. Sida has supported Phase I (2008-2013) and Phase II (2013-2017) of MHTF and this contribution refers to Phase III (2019-2022) and part of UNFPA’s strategic plan (2018-2021). Phase III is driven by a more comprehensive SRHR agenda and inclusion of newborn health. Further, Phase III of MHTF has a more pronounced
focus on adolescents reproductive and sexual health and rights, access to safe abortion
and post-abortion care, and support throughout women and girl’s lifespan. | MHTF is a thematic fund aiming at improving maternal and newborn health and well being in countries with high burden of maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity by strengthening of national health systems. 
The vision of the third phase of the fund is to support countries to ensuring the health, survival, and rights of every woman, adolescent girl and newborn, by supporting countries to strengthen their health systems for providing equitable and accountable access to quality sexual and reproductive and newborn health care.
The fund is set up to provide strategic directions and technical assistance for the development, implementation and monitoring of maternal and newborn health interventions. The fund focuses on four key intervention areas: midwifery, comprehensive SRH in Emergency Obstetric and Newborn care (EmONC) facilities, obstetric fistula and other obstetric morbidities and Maternal (and Perinatal) Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR).
MHTF, will contribute to UNFPA's Strategic Plan 2018-2021, in particular on:
outcome 1: "Every woman, adolescent and youth everywhere, especially those furthest behind, has utilized integrated sexual and reproductive health services and exercised reproductive rights, free of coercion, discrimination and violence" and
outcome 2: "Every adolescent and youth, in particular adolescent girls, is empowered to have access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights, in all contexts".
Through the following programme specific outcomes;
Outcome 1  midwifery: Every woman and adolescent girl can access right based quality sexual and reproductive health information and services delivered by midwives and that are women centered, equitable and accountable. The objective of phase III is to further accelerate the delivery of quality midwifery care. Phase III will also support midwives to address the needs of SRHR of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged women and adolescent girls.
Outcome 2  emergency obstetric and newborn care (EmONC): Every woman, adolescent girl and newborn in need of emergency obstetric and newborn care can access a referral maternity facility, staffed with skilled attendants at birth and monitored to deliver quality essential sexual and reproductive healthcare, including EmONC. In phase III there will be emphasis on implementing monitoring and quality improvement process for EmONC and SRH more broadly.
Outcome 3  maternal (and perinatal) death surveillance and response (MPDSR): Causes of maternal and perinatal deaths are identified and addressed through MPDSR programmes. The objective of phase III are to improve notification of maternal deaths, increase the number and quality of maternal death reviews, and implement multisectoral responses to address root causes of maternal and perinatal deaths. 
Outcome 4  obstetric fistula and other obstetric morbidities: Every woman and adolescent girl can access quality sexual and reproductive health information and services to prevent and, if needed, to treat them from obstetric fistula and other obstetric morbidities. In phase III, MHTF will further strengthening national programmes for ending fistula and other obstetric morbidities.

According to UNFPA, WASH is an integral part of quality and availability of services and care for women and girls. It is addressed through the program from different angels through quality assurance work, policies, implementation plans and in facilities. It is also addressed in training programs. However, UNFPA's role is generally to alert UNICEF if the water is not available in the maternity facility that falls under UNFPA support.

results_text:
Results achieved | Uppnådda resultat | UNFPA/ Maternal Health Thematic Fund has had a strong focus on promoting equity in access, universal health coverage and improving accountablity and quality of care.

MHTF has supported 32 high-priority countries to ensure an integration of SRHR in national Health Systems.The MHTF supported 32 countries with some of the highest rates of maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity across five regions (the Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, East and Southern Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and West and Central Africa. (From the annual report 2023 and UNFPA/MHTF Input to Sidas Multilateral Support 2023 MHTF HIGHLIGHTS IN SELECT COUNTRIES 2023)

2.8 million pregnant women have received safer delivery care, 180 000 midwives were trained (pre-service and in-service) and 53 midwifery schools were accredited to provide higher standard of education. The report also reflects that MHTF is an important resource for global priority setting, advocacy, research and knowledge management, to improve maternal and newborn health. It plays a convening and coordinating role for global efforts internally at UNFPA and externally. The activities of the MHTF are diverse and the report shows that the MHTF develops, uses and shares new and innovative approaches, technology and actively engages with different partners, in the public, academic and private sector.

The MHTF has worked to ensure alignment on UN system technical support on maternal and newborn health national action plans in countries and to shape global targets for a coherent and harmonized approach to tracking progress on MNH. UNFPA developed what is now a global target to secure that more than half of population has access to emergency obstetric care within 2 hours of travel, which the UN agencies are now jointly tracking together. 

950 policymakers, health managers, and healthcare providers from 13 countries to improve maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response committees, in country and through South to South learning (two regional trainings and dedicated study tour on confidential enquiry into maternal deaths by Zambia MoH delegation to South Africa). This collaboration has improved maternal and newborn death reviews and surveillance and strengthened responses to maternal deaths through the development of context-specific action plans and interventions to address the underlying causes of death

96 EmONC facilities received post-abortion care training in Kenya and in the DRC, the MHTF has enhanced three midwifery schools' capabilities in comprehensive healthcare by upgrading the skills of educators.

In DRC the Panzi Hospital has been supported in implementing a holistic birth model, providing 60 women who experienced gender-based violence with tailored medical, psychosocial, and socio-economic support. The network of Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care facilities enabling 138,760 safe deliveries by qualified health workers, based on developed tools developed by UNFPA as a global public good. DRC has also been supported to enact a law defining the legal status of midwives in the public health sector formalising the role of midwives for the first time in the country. | Not applicable | No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published | Maternal Health Thematic Fund/ UNFPA Agreement and decision | Decision MHTF 2019-2022
